formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: The following sections of this Ordinance shall apply to the estates of such persons only as shall die after the proclamation of this Ordinance
why_relevant: Fixes the scope of Part III. Every death in this matter (1990, 1995, 2022, 2023) is long after the proclamation of the Ordinance, so the Part III intestacy rules apply to each estate.
temporal_note: In force from 1876 and unamended in the corpus text; in force at the matter reference date 2026-04 and at each relevant death.
verifier_note: The excerpt stops at 'proclamation of this Ordinance' and drops the second limb of section 20, that the deceased must have been unmarried at death or married after the proclamation; that limb is satisfied on these facts but the map should state it.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: Inheritance ab interstate to the immovable property in Sri Lanka of a person deceased shall be governed and regulated by the following provisions of this Ordinance wherever such person may have or have had his actual or matrimonial domicile.
why_relevant: Lot A is immovable property in Sri Lanka, so the intestate devolution of the shares of Suresh, Rakitha and Muditha is governed by this Ordinance irrespective of the domicile of any heir, including Samantha, who lives in the United States of America.
temporal_note: In force from 1876 and unamended in the corpus text; in force at the matter reference date 2026-04 and at each relevant death.
verifier_note: Section 21(1) makes the domicile of the deceased irrelevant to inheritance to immovable property in Sri Lanka; it says nothing about the domicile or citizenship of an heir, so the map's extension of it to Samantha is not sourced from this text.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: When any person shall die intestate as to any of his or her property, leaving a spouse surviving, the surviving spouse shall inherit one-half of the property of such person.
why_relevant: Gives Kanthi one-half of Suresh's share on his intestate death in 1995 and gives Ann one-half of Rakitha's share on his intestate death in 2022.
temporal_note: In force from 1876 and unamended in the corpus text; in force at each relevant death and at 2026-04.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: Subject to the right of the surviving spouse in the preceding section mentioned, the right of inheritance is divided in the following order as respects (a) descendants, (b) ascendants, (c) collaterals.
why_relevant: Sets the order in which the remaining half of each intestate estate is taken: descendants first, then ascendants, then collaterals. It orders the moves from section 24 to section 25 in this matter.
temporal_note: In force from 1876 and unamended in the corpus text; in force at each relevant death and at 2026-04.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: Children, grandchildren, and remoter descendants are preferent to all others in the estate of the parents; all the children take equally per capita, but the children or remoter issue of a deceased child take per stirpes or by representation.
why_relevant: Divides the half of Suresh's estate not taken by Kanthi equally among his three children, Samantha, Rakitha and Muditha, per capita. It is also the provision that makes Samantha, a child of Suresh's first marriage, an heir of Suresh at all.
temporal_note: In force from 1876 and unamended in the corpus text; in force on 10 December 1995 when Suresh died and at 2026-04.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: The children and remoter descendants failing, the inheritance of the deceased goes to his father and mother in case they are both alive; but if only one of the parents be alive, the surviving parent takes half, and the brothers and sisters of the deceased of the full blood, and the issue of any deceased brother or sister of the full blood, by representation, and the brothers and sisters of the half-blood who are related to the intestate by the side of the deceased parent, and the issue of any such deceased brother or sister of the half-blood, by representation, take the other half.
why_relevant: Governs both Rakitha's estate (2022) and Muditha's estate (2023): each died without descendants, their father Suresh had predeceased them and their mother Kanthi survived, so Kanthi takes half and the surviving siblings, including the half-blood sister Samantha who is related through the deceased parent Suresh, take the other half.
temporal_note: In force from 1876 and unamended in the corpus text; in force on 2 July 2022 and 5 June 2023 and at 2026-04.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: if there are only half-brothers and sisters or such issue of one side, the full brothers and sisters and the issue of deceased full brothers and sisters by representation, take then in the first place one-half of the property, and divide the other half with the half-brothers and sisters and their issue by representation.
why_relevant: Fixes how the sibling half under section 25 is split when the only half-blood sibling is on one side. On Rakitha's death the full sister Muditha takes one-half of the sibling portion first and shares the balance with the half-sister Samantha. On Muditha's death there is no surviving full sibling and no issue of the deceased full sibling, so the sibling portion is taken by Samantha alone.
temporal_note: In force from 1876 and unamended in the corpus text; in force on 2 July 2022 and 5 June 2023 and at 2026-04.
verifier_note: Correct for Rakitha's estate, where a full sister survived, but section 27 does not govern Muditha's estate, where no full brother or sister and no issue of one survived; section 29 governs that case and is added as PROV-M001-901.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: In all questions relating to the distribution of the property of an intestate, if the present Ordinance is silent, the rules of the Roman-Dutch law as it prevailed in North Holland are to govern and be followed.
why_relevant: The Ordinance itself directs that where it is silent the Roman-Dutch law applies. It is the reason the life interest steps in this pedigree cannot be resolved from the corpus alone, and it is why question one is classified as needing non-statutory authority.
temporal_note: In force from 1876 and unamended in the corpus text; in force at 2026-04.

formal_title: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance No. 7 of 1840
relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property, and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object, or for establishing any security, interest, or incumbrance affecting land or other immovable property
why_relevant: Background for the form of the two deeds in the chain: Deed of Gift No. 515 of 1986 and Deed of Revocation of Life Interest No. 525 of 1991 were both notarially attested, which is the statutory form requirement for instruments affecting an interest in land.
temporal_note: The corpus text is the consolidated section as amended in 1947, 2022 and 2024, so the wording shown is later than the 1986 and 1991 deeds. The notarial attestation requirement itself is unchanged in substance, but the excerpt is not the text as it stood in 1986. Treated as background only for that reason.
verifier_note: Background only: the corpus holds the consolidated section as amended in 1947, 2022 and 2024, so the form of the 1986 and 1991 deeds cannot be tested against it, and the section does not name gift or donation among the dispositions it catches.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: The provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into operation with effect from January 1, 2013.
why_relevant: Fixes the temporal reach of the Act. Suresh died on 10 December 1995, so the Act cannot touch the devolution of his estate; the deaths of Rakitha in 2022 and Muditha in 2023 fall inside the operative period.
temporal_note: In force from 2014, deemed operative from 1 January 2013; in force at 2026-04.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary in any other written law, the transfer of title of any land situated in Sri Lanka, shall be prohibited if such transfer is- (a) to a foreigner;
why_relevant: The prohibition Samantha would have to escape. It bites only on a transfer of title of land to a foreigner and is expressly subject to the exemptions in section 3.
temporal_note: In force from 2014, deemed operative from 1 January 2013; unamended by Act No. 21 of 2018; in force at 2026-04.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: any land the title of which is transferred by intestacy, gift or testamentary disposition to a next of kin (who is a foreigner) of the in accordance with the applicable law of succession of Sri Lanka;
why_relevant: The decisive exemption. Title passing on intestacy to a next of kin who is a foreigner, under the Sri Lankan law of succession, is taken out of section 2 altogether. Samantha's entitlement arises exactly this way.
temporal_note: Section 3 was amended by Act No. 21 of 2018 with effect from 1 April 2018, but that amendment touched paragraphs (b) and (h) and added a new paragraph (i). Paragraph (d) is unchanged and was in the Act from its operative date of 1 January 2013.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: any land the title of which is transferred to a dual citizen of Sri Lanka within the meaning of the Citizenship Act;
why_relevant: An independent exemption that would apply if Samantha holds Sri Lankan citizenship as well as United States citizenship. The scenario says only that she is a citizen of the United States of America, which does not settle whether she is also a citizen of Sri Lanka.
temporal_note: Unchanged by Act No. 21 of 2018; in force at 2026-04.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: means a person who is not a citizen of Sri Lanka;
why_relevant: Defines the class the section 2 prohibition targets. Whether Samantha is a foreigner turns on Sri Lankan citizenship, not on her United States citizenship.
temporal_note: In force from 2014, deemed operative from 1 January 2013; in force at 2026-04.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: means any sale, donation, gift or any conveyance by or under which the title of such land passes to another person;
why_relevant: Defines the act section 2 prohibits. The listed acts are voluntary dispositions; devolution by operation of law on an intestacy is not obviously a sale, donation, gift or conveyance, which is a second and independent reason the prohibition does not reach Samantha.
temporal_note: In force from 2014, deemed operative from 1 January 2013; in force at 2026-04.
verifier_note: The definition is quoted correctly, but the inference drawn from it, that an intestate devolution falls outside the word transfer, is contradicted by section 3(1)(d), which exempts land transferred by intestacy, and by the section 2(1)(b) proviso on shares devolving on a next of kin; it is not a second independent ground.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: Any alienation of land effected in contravention of the provisions of this Act, shall be void and shall have no effect in law.
why_relevant: States the consequence Samantha would face if section 2 applied and no exemption were available. Because section 3(1)(d) applies, this section is not engaged.
temporal_note: In force from 2014, deemed operative from 1 January 2013; in force at 2026-04.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) (Amendment) Act No. 21 of 2018
relevant_excerpt: This Act may be cited as the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) (Amendment) Act, No. 21 of 2018 and shall be deemed to have come into operation on April 1, 2018.
why_relevant: Fixes when the amendment named in the question took effect, which matters because Rakitha died in 2022 and Muditha in 2023, both after that date.
temporal_note: Deemed operative from 1 April 2018; in force at 2026-04.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) (Amendment) Act No. 21 of 2018
relevant_excerpt: is hereby amended in subsection (1) - (a) by the repeal of paragraph (b) of that subsection and the substitution therefor of the following paragraph:-
why_relevant: Shows the reach of the 2018 amendment to section 3. It substitutes paragraph (b), alters paragraph (h) and adds a new paragraph (i). It does not disturb the intestacy exemption in paragraph (d) that Samantha relies on.
temporal_note: Deemed operative from 1 April 2018; in force at 2026-04. The corpus text of this section is truncated: the substituted paragraph (b) and the new paragraph (i) are not reproduced in the body.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: In case all the half-brothers and sisters, their children and remoter issue, are related to the intestate on one side only, they take the whole of the inheritance
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. On Muditha's death on 5 June 2023 no full brother or sister and no issue of a deceased full brother or sister survived, so the last limb of section 27, which gives the full siblings one-half of the sibling portion in the first place, has nothing to operate on. Section 29 is the provision that disposes of the sibling portion where the only half-blood siblings are on one side: the half-sister Samantha takes the whole of it. The section carries an express exception where a grandparent or higher ascendant on the other side survives, which the scenario does not address.
temporal_note: In force from 1876 and unamended in the corpus text; in force on 5 June 2023 and at 2026-04.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier because the map anchored the decisive step in Muditha's estate on section 27, which on its terms presupposes surviving full-blood siblings.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: Where the transfer of title of a land is effected in terms of this section, the provisions of this Act shall also apply to every subsequent transfer of title of such land or part thereof.
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. The gold conclusion to M001-Q03 and claim CL-M001-Q03-013 assert that any later disposition by Samantha would still be tested against section 2 because the Act applies to every subsequent transfer of exempted land. That proposition comes from section 3(4), which the map cited in prose but carried no provision entry for.
temporal_note: In force from 2014, deemed operative from 1 January 2013; untouched by Act No. 21 of 2018; in force at 2026-04.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier to close a citation gap in the M001-Q03 conclusion.

relevant_excerpt: Before any deed or instrument (other than a will or codicil) affecting any interest in land or other immovable property is drawn by him, he shall search or cause to be searched the registers in the land registry to ascertain the state of the title in regard to such land and whether any prior deed affecting any interest in such land has been registered
why_relevant: This is the primary statutory source of the notary's pre-purchase document check: before drawing the deed of transfer the notary must search the land registry registers to establish the vendor's title and any prior registered deed.
temporal_note: Section 31 stands as substituted and amended by Act No. 47 of 2011, Act No. 31 of 2022 and Act No. 6 of 2024, all before the April 2026 matter date, so the consolidated text is the text in force.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and the rule is correctly stated, but the corpus body of section 31 prints this rule without its number, so the subsection label follows conventional numbering and cannot be confirmed against the corpus text. The excerpt also omits the proviso at the end of the rule, under which the search is not compulsory if the parties authorise the notary in writing to dispense with it; that proviso is added as PROV-M002-901.

relevant_excerpt: he shall obtain from the Registrar of the relevant Land Registry the certified extract of the folio containing the last entry pertaining to such land or immovable property containing the ownership and the registered encumbrances relating to such land or immovable property
why_relevant: Names the specific document the notary must obtain: the certified folio extract showing ownership and registered encumbrances of the Galle land.
temporal_note: Inserted by the 2011, 2022 and 2024 amendments to section 31; in force well before April 2026.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and the rule is correctly stated, but the corpus body of section 31 prints this rule without its number, so the subsection label follows conventional numbering and cannot be confirmed against the corpus text.

relevant_excerpt: if a party to any deed or instrument is a corporate body he shall retain a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation or other instrument establishing such corporate entity and details of board of directors
why_relevant: The purchaser is a private limited company, so the notary must call for and retain a certified copy of its certificate of incorporation and the particulars of its board of directors.
temporal_note: Part of the amended section 31 text in force at April 2026.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and the rule is correctly stated, but the corpus body of section 31 prints this rule without its number, so the subsection label follows conventional numbering and cannot be confirmed against the corpus text.

relevant_excerpt: Where the executant is a body corporate, he shall attach a copy of the board resolution authorizing the executant to sign such deed or instrument to the protocol of such deed or instrument.
why_relevant: Requires the notary to obtain the board resolution authorising the person who signs for the company, and to attach a copy to the protocol.
temporal_note: Substituted by Act No. 6 of 2024; in force before April 2026.

relevant_excerpt: When a deed transferring any immovable property is executed or acknowledged before a notary, he shall use his best endeavours to obtain the title deed, if any, of such property
why_relevant: Obliges the notary to obtain the vendor's title deed itself, not merely the registry extract, and to endorse the new transaction on it.
temporal_note: Long-standing rule; unaffected on this point by the 2011 to 2024 amendments.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument, other than a will or codicil, affecting land or other immovable property, unless the deed or instrument embodies therin or in a Schedule annexed therto an accurate and clear description of the said land or other property affected thereby, showing its boundaries, extent, situation
why_relevant: The notary can only produce the required accurate description by checking the survey plan and the descriptions in the prior deeds, which makes the plan and the prior deeds documents he must call for.
temporal_note: Text as amended before April 2026.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and the rule is correctly stated, but the corpus body of section 31 prints this rule without its number, so the subsection label follows conventional numbering and cannot be confirmed against the corpus text.

relevant_excerpt: If he attest any deed or instrument executed before him by means of an attorney, he shall preserve a true copy of the power of attorney with his protocol, and shall forward a like copy with the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands.
why_relevant: Where the vendor signs through an attorney, the power of attorney becomes a document the notary must obtain, copy and forward.
temporal_note: Long-standing rule in force at April 2026.

relevant_excerpt: An instrument executed or made on or after the 1st day of January, 1864, whether before or after the commencement of this Ordinance shall, unless it is duly registered under this Chapter
why_relevant: Explains why the registry search matters: priority between competing deeds turns on registration, so the purchaser must see the registered chain before paying.
temporal_note: Unamended since 1927.

relevant_excerpt: all duplicates and copies and all books and indexes kept under this Ordinance may be searched and examined by any person claiming to be interested therein or by his attorney-at-law or agent duly authorized thereto in writing, and certified copies of or extracts from any such duplicate, copy, or book may be obtained if required
why_relevant: Gives the notary the statutory right of access to the registry books and to certified copies and extracts, which is the mechanism by which the section 31 search is carried out.
temporal_note: Unamended since 1927.

relevant_excerpt: shall bind a purchaser, unless and until the lis pendens is duly registered under this Chapter.
why_relevant: A registered lis pendens binds the purchaser, so the search must extend to registered lis pendens entries against the land.
temporal_note: The 1947 amendment predates the matter date. The corpus text of subsection (1) carries an OCR artefact, rendering the opening words as 'No Us pendens'.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim but the excerpt begins mid-sentence and drops the opening negative (no lis pendens shall bind a purchaser unless registered), so read alone it inverts the rule; the claim built on it states the rule correctly.

relevant_excerpt: may present for registration a caveat in the prescribed form requiring to be served with notice of the presentation for registration of any instrument affecting the land described in the caveat.
why_relevant: Registered caveats are a further class of registry entry the notary must look for, because a caveator can move to have the transfer rectified or cancelled.
temporal_note: Unamended since 1927.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim but the temporal note is wrong: the corpus edition is the 1990 consolidation, and Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022 s.2(1) repealed and substituted subsection (1) (and s.2(5) substituted sixty days for thirty in subsection (5)), so this is not the text in force at April 2026, although the caveat mechanism it describes survives.

relevant_excerpt: Every instrument (except a will) presented for registration shall contain embodied therein, or in a schedule annexed thereto, an accurate and clear description of the land affected thereby, its boundaries, extent, and situation
why_relevant: Registration will be refused unless the description is accurate, which is a second reason to obtain the survey plan and the prior deeds before drafting.
temporal_note: Subsections (5A) and (5B) were added before the matter date and do not affect subsection (1).
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim but the temporal note is wrong: subsection (1) was repealed and substituted by Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 48 of 2011 s.2, which is in the corpus; the 1990 consolidation held here is the superseded text, although the description requirement it states survives the substitution.

relevant_excerpt: the transfer of title of any land situated in Sri Lanka, shall be prohibited if such transfer is- (a) to a foreigner; or (b) to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act where any foreign shareholding in such company, either direct or indirect, is fifty per cent or above; or (c) to a foreign company, unless exempted as provided in section 3.
why_relevant: The purchaser is a Sri Lankan incorporated company, so the notary must establish from the company's own records what proportion of its shares is held directly or indirectly by foreigners.
temporal_note: Section 2 as amended by Act No. 3 of 2017 and Act No. 21 of 2018, both before April 2026.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim but the temporal note misattributes the amendment history: in the corpus, Act No. 3 of 2017 inserts section 5A and Act No. 21 of 2018 amends sections 3 and 5A, and the corpus row for section 2 records no amendment events, so section 2 is not shown to have been amended by either Act.

relevant_excerpt: Where the title of a land is transferred to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act, with less than fifty per cent of foreign shareholding, it shall be the duty of the Registrar of Lands to confirm himself whether the foreign shareholding of such company is less than fifty per cent, by requiring the secretary of such company to submit documentary proof to the effect that the foreign shareholding of such company is less than fifty per cent of the total number of shares issued for the time being.
why_relevant: Identifies the exact document the notary must have ready before registration: the company secretary's documentary proof of the foreign shareholding percentage.
temporal_note: In force from 2014 and unaffected on this point by the 2017 and 2018 amendments.

relevant_excerpt: Any alienation of land effected in contravention of the provisions of this Act, shall be void and shall have no effect in law.
why_relevant: Sets the consequence that makes the shareholding check indispensable rather than merely prudent.
temporal_note: Unamended and in force at April 2026.

relevant_excerpt: Provided further, where the transferee is a corporate body and where the Board of Directors of such corporate body is unable to be present and execute the deed or instrument, such Board shall authorise in writing, any other person to sign such deed or instrument on his behalf, who shall comply with the requirements set out in subsection (1).
why_relevant: The transferee company must itself execute the deed, so the notary must hold the board's written authorisation for whoever signs for the company.
temporal_note: Section 2 as amended by Act No. 30 of 2022 and Act No. 4 of 2024, both before April 2026.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim but the subsection label should be (2)(a): the excerpt is the second proviso to paragraph (a) of subsection (2), not free-standing text of subsection (2).

relevant_excerpt: Every power of attorney executed in Sri Lanka or any other country shall be registered with the Registrar General.
why_relevant: If the vendor signs through an attorney, the notary must see that the power of attorney is one registered with the Registrar-General.
temporal_note: Section 3 as substituted by Act No. 28 of 2022; in force before April 2026.

relevant_excerpt: (a) examine the relevant volumes and folios in the Registrar General's department; (b) be satisfied that the power of attorney has not been revoked or cancelled and shall state such fact in his attestation: and (c) retain the copies of the National Identity Card or the driving license or the bio page of the passport, as the case may be, of the grantor and the attorney, and a copy of the power of attorney.
why_relevant: Where the transfer is signed under a power of attorney the notary must check the Registrar-General's volumes and folios for a revocation, and retain identity documents of grantor and attorney.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 28 of 2022, in force before the April 2026 matter date.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but the duty in section 3B(1) applies only to a transaction referred to in section 3A; that gateway is missing from the map and is added as PROV-M002-902.

relevant_excerpt: A certificate of incorporation issued under this section in-respect of any company, shall be conclusive evidence of the fact that- (a) all the requirements under this Act relating to the incorporation of a company have been complied with; and (b) the company has been incorporated under this Act on the date specified in such certificate of incorporation.
why_relevant: Explains what the certificate of incorporation the notary retains actually proves about the purchaser's existence and capacity to hold land.
temporal_note: The 2019 amendment does not touch section 5(3).

relevant_excerpt: Proof of the undisturbed and uninterrupted possession by a defendant in any action, or by those under whom he claims, of lands or immovable property, by a title adverse to or independent of that of the claimant or plaintiff in such action
why_relevant: Paper title alone is not enough: ten years of adverse possession can defeat it, so the notary must also examine possession on the ground and not rely on the deeds in isolation.
temporal_note: Section 3 unamended; Act No. 26 of 2014 did not alter it.

relevant_excerpt: Where the Minister decides that land in any area is needed for any public purpose, he may direct the acquiring officer of the district in which that area lies to cause a notice in accordance with subsection (2) to be exhibited in some conspicuous places in that area.
why_relevant: Background for the check on whether an acquisition notice affects the area, since land under acquisition is of no use to the company for a hotel.
temporal_note: In force at April 2026; the 1969, 1979 and 1986 amendments do not affect section 2(1).
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and the background role is right, but section 2 concerns a preliminary investigation notice exhibited in the area; it creates nothing registrable, so it does not support a check made through registry entries.

relevant_excerpt: Subject to the provisions of subsection (2), no permit-holder shall execute or effect any disposition of the land alienated to him on the permit.
why_relevant: Background for tracing the root of title back to any State grant or permit, because a disposition by a permit-holder is null and void.
temporal_note: In force at April 2026.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but the nullity relied on in why_relevant is in subsection (3), not the excerpted subsection (1).

relevant_excerpt: no Government agency or any other person shall carry out or engage in any development activity in any development area or part thereof, except under the authority, and in accordance with the terms and conditions, of a permit issued in that behalf by the Authority
why_relevant: The only development-permit regime in this corpus. It is recorded as background context for the coastal-zone question; it is not the coastal-zone approval the question asks about, and whether the Galle land lies in a declared development area is not stated.
temporal_note: In force at April 2026.

relevant_excerpt: the provisions of the Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982, relating to the Imposition of Stamp Duty (other than any instrument relating to the transfer of immovable property, the transfer of motor vehicles or documents filed in Court), Exemptions and any other provision in the aforesaid Act, shall, in so far as the same are inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, have no operation and the provisions of this Act shall prevail.
why_relevant: Places the deed of transfer of immovable property outside the 2006 Act's displacement of the 1982 Act, so the 1982 regime is the one to look to for a deed of transfer.
temporal_note: In force at April 2026.

relevant_excerpt: a stamp duty at the prescribed rate. Different rates may be prescribed in respect of different classes or categories of instruments.
why_relevant: Shows that the charging provision fixes no figure: the rate is prescribed elsewhere, which is precisely what this corpus does not contain.
temporal_note: In force at April 2026.

relevant_excerpt: Where any property is conveyed by an instrument, the stamp duty with which such instrument is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property conveyed.
why_relevant: Establishes the base on which any rate would be applied, namely the value of the property conveyed.
temporal_note: In force at April 2026.

relevant_excerpt: in the case of a conveyance or agreement to convey, by the grantee, or intended grantee;
why_relevant: Identifies the purchasing company as the party liable for the duty, which is the part of the stamp duty question this corpus can answer.
temporal_note: In force at April 2026.

relevant_excerpt: Provided that if the parties to the transaction authorize the notary in writing to dispense with the search, the search shall not be compulsory, but he shall before the deed or instrument is tendered for registration write at the head thereof the reference to the previous registration, if any.
why_relevant: The exception to the search duty relied on in PROV-M002-001: the parties may authorise the notary in writing to dispense with the search, in which case he must still write the reference to the previous registration at the head of the deed. A checklist that states the search duty without its statutory exception is incomplete.
temporal_note: Part of the section 31 text as amended by Acts No. 47 of 2011, No. 31 of 2022 and No. 6 of 2024, all before April 2026.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier: proviso missing from the researcher's map.

relevant_excerpt: If a power of attorney specified in subsection (1) is executed outside Sri Lanka, it shall - (a) be duly executed before a person authorized under section 2 of this Act; (b) contain a description of the land or land parcel as the case may be with metes and bounds and the extent in the case of a land or land parcel;
why_relevant: A power of attorney granted abroad for a transaction within section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance must satisfy these execution and content requirements. It is the gateway that makes the section 3B duty in PROV-M002-018 apply, and it fixes what the notary must look for on the face of a power of attorney executed in Melbourne.
temporal_note: Inserted by Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022; not touched by Act No. 3 of 2024, which amends sections 2, 3D and 4. In force at April 2026.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier: indispensable cross-reference from section 3B, and directly engaged by the enrichment fact that the power of attorney was granted in Melbourne.

relevant_excerpt: where a deed or instrument is signed by an attorney, such attorney shall submit to the notary an affidavit affirming that the Power of Attorney is genuine and in force and the grantor is alive when executing such deed or instrument
why_relevant: Names a further document the notary must obtain where the vendor signs through an attorney: the attorney's affidavit that the power is genuine and in force and that the grantor is alive. The researcher's attorney limb stops at the power of attorney and the revocation search.
temporal_note: Part of the section 31 text as amended before April 2026. The corpus body prints this rule without its number, so the label follows conventional numbering and is not confirmable from the corpus text.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier: missing document requirement on the attorney limb.

relevant_excerpt: Every Registrar shall refuse to register an instrument, other than a will, which docs not state the particulars required by the foregoing provisions of this section.
why_relevant: Supplies the refusal consequence that claim CL-M002-Q01-007 asserts. The researcher cited only subsection (1), which states the description requirement but not the sanction.
temporal_note: In force at April 2026. The corpus edition is the 1990 consolidation; Acts No. 48 of 2011 and No. 21 of 2013 amend subsections (1) and (6) of this section and leave subsection (5) untouched. The word 'docs' is an OCR artefact for 'does'.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier so that the refusal limb of CL-M002-Q01-007 rests on a cited provision.

relevant_excerpt: it is proved to the satisfaction of the court that the instrument presented for registration is or was at the time of registration void or voidable by the caveator or fraudulent as against him or in derogation of his lawful rights the court may order the instrument to be rectified or cancelled as may be necessary to preserve the rights of the caveator
why_relevant: Supplies the rectification or cancellation consequence that claim CL-M002-Q01-005 asserts. The researcher cited only subsection (1), which creates the caveat but says nothing about the caveator's remedy.
temporal_note: The corpus edition is the 1990 consolidation. Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022 s.2(5) substituted sixty days for the thirty days in this subsection, so the time limit in the corpus text is superseded; the rectification power itself is unchanged.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier so that the rectification limb of CL-M002-Q01-005 rests on a cited provision.

relevant_excerpt: A power of attorney other than a power of attorney executed by a State institution shall be valid, only for a period of five years from the date of execution, unless the period of validity of such power of attorney is specified in such power of attorney or until such power of attorney is revoked or cancelled in accordance with the provisions of section 4.
why_relevant: The notary must check the age of the power of attorney, not only whether it has been revoked: a power is valid for five years from execution unless it states its own period. On the enriched facts the March 2024 power is still within that period, but the check belongs on the checklist.
temporal_note: Inserted by Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022; in force at April 2026.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier: validity period check missing from the attorney limb.

relevant_excerpt: there shall be charged a duty (hereinafter to be called "stamp duty") at such rate as the Minister may determine by Order published in the Gazette on every "specified instrument"- (a) executed, drawn or presented in Sri Lanka
why_relevant: The charging section. It imposes stamp duty on every specified instrument executed in Sri Lanka but fixes no rate in the Act itself: the rate is set by Ministerial Order published in the Gazette. Any calculation of the duty on the mortgage bond therefore depends on that Order.
temporal_note: In force from 1 April 2006 (s.1(2)) and unamended in the corpus edition; in force at 2026-04. The rate Order made under this section is subsidiary legislation and is not in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: (g) a bond or mortgage for any definite and certain sum of money and affecting any property;
why_relevant: Brings the mortgage bond within the class of 'specified instrument' chargeable under s.3. The bond secures a definite and certain sum (Rs. 10,000,000) and affects immovable property, so it falls within paragraph (g).
temporal_note: In force from 1 April 2006; no amendment events recorded in the corpus; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: (e) in all other cases, by the person drawing, making or executing such instrument.
why_relevant: Identifies the person liable. A mortgage bond is not within the specific paragraphs (a) to (ddd), so the residual paragraph (e) applies and the duty falls on the person executing the bond, that is the mortgagor Herath, unless there is an agreement to the contrary with the bank.
temporal_note: Amended by the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) (Amendment) Act No. 10 of 2008 (paragraphs (dd) and (ddd) inserted). The consolidated text reflects that amendment and is in force at 2026-04; the residual paragraph (e) relied on here is original.

relevant_excerpt: Stamp duty payable on any specified instrument relating to a mortgage or lease of any immovable property may be paid, prior to, or at the time of, the execution of the specified instrument, to a prescribed bank.
why_relevant: Answers the 'where do you pay' limb directly for a mortgage of immovable property: payment is made to a prescribed bank, before or at execution (or within seven days where payment beforehand was impossible), and the bank issues a certificate in the prescribed form which is affixed to the instrument.
temporal_note: Section 8 was replaced by Act No. 10 of 2008 s.3; the corpus consolidated text is the post-2008 text, in force well before and at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: All stamp duty payable to a Provincial Council in respect of documents and instruments referred to in List I of the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution, shall be paid to the respective Provincial Council within whose limits the instrument was executed or the property situated as the case may be
why_relevant: Directs where duty that is a devolved Provincial Council revenue must be paid: to the Provincial Council within whose limits the instrument was executed or the property is situated. The land is in Anuradhapura, so this points to the Provincial Council for the province in which Anuradhapura lies.
temporal_note: In force from 1 April 2006, no amendment events in the corpus; in force at 2026-04. Whether a mortgage bond is within List I of the Ninth Schedule cannot be checked here because the Constitution is not in the corpus.
verifier_note: Wording verbatim, but the section bites only on duty that is already payable to a Provincial Council in respect of instruments referred to in List I of the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution, and the Constitution is not in the corpus; role reduced from supporting to background for Q01, because on corpus text it is s.8(2) and not s.9 that answers the 'where do you pay' limb.

relevant_excerpt: A bond or mortgage for the payment or repayment of money to be lent, advanced, or paid shall be charged, where the total amount secured or to be ultimately recoverable is in any way limited, with the same stamp duty as on a bond or mortgage for the amount so limited.
why_relevant: Supplies the measure of the charge for a mortgage: where the amount secured is limited, duty is charged on that limited amount. It supports computing the duty on the stated Rs. 10,000,000 rather than on some larger notional sum.
temporal_note: Enacted 1982, no amendment events in the corpus. Its continued operation is qualified by s.13 of Act No. 12 of 2006, which displaces the imposition provisions of the 1982 Act so far as they are inconsistent with the 2006 Act. Treated as supporting, not indispensable, for that reason.
verifier_note: Wording verbatim, but s.13 of the 2006 Act disapplies the imposition provisions of the 1982 Act so far as inconsistent, and its carve-out covers transfers of immovable property, motor vehicles and documents filed in Court, not mortgages; s.16 therefore cannot be relied on for the measure of the charge on a mortgage bond and its role is reduced from supporting to background for Q01.

relevant_excerpt: the provisions of the Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982, relating to the Imposition of Stamp Duty (other than any instrument relating to the transfer of immovable property, the transfer of motor vehicles or documents filed in Court), Exemptions and any other provision in the aforesaid Act, shall, in so far as the same are inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, have no operation and the provisions of this Act shall prevail.
why_relevant: Background on which enactment governs. It explains why the 2006 Act, not the 1982 Act, is the charging statute for a mortgage bond, and why s.16 of the 1982 Act can only be used so far as it is not inconsistent with the 2006 Act.
temporal_note: In force from 1 April 2006; no amendment events in the corpus; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless he has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided.
why_relevant: The notary attesting the mortgage bond may not attest it unless satisfied that the required stamp duty has been provided, which is why the duty must be settled before or at execution.
temporal_note: Section 31 was substituted in several respects by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 and the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024; the corpus consolidated text carries changes down to 2024 and is in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Ordinance or any other written law, any stamp duty which is required to be paid in respect of every deed or instrument executed under any written law, shall be paid by the notary; (b) The stamps or the original receipt received from the relevant bank as proof of such payment shall be affixed to the duplicate of the deed or instrument by the notary;
why_relevant: Puts the mechanics of payment on the notary: the notary pays the stamp duty and affixes the stamps, or the original bank receipt, to the duplicate of the instrument. It confirms the practical answer to 'where do you pay', namely at the relevant bank, with the receipt going onto the duplicate.
temporal_note: This lettered clause follows rule (7) in the corpus text of s.31 and carries no subsection number of its own in that text, so the subsection field is left null. Section 31 was amended down to 2024 and is in force at 2026-04. The verifier should confirm the correct rule number against the Government Printer text.
verifier_note: Excerpt verbatim and the role is right, but the subsection field should read 'rule (7A)': Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(5) inserted this rule immediately after rule (7) without numbering it, and Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(2) names it 'rule (7A)'. That 2024 amendment also substituted 'every deed or instrument' for 'any deed or instrument relating to a transfer, a gift or an exchange', which is the only reason the rule reaches a mortgage bond at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: (b) dispose of such holding except with the prior approval of the Government Agent. (7) Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph (b) of subsection (6), the approval of the Divisional Secretary shall not be required when mortgaging such holding to a licenced commercial bank, the State Mortgage and Investment Bank, the Development Finance Corporation of Ceylon, the National Development Bank of Sri Lanka, the National Housing Development Authority, the Housing Development Finance Corporation Bank of Sri Lanka, any registered society or other prescribed institution.
why_relevant: This is the provision the question turns on. Subsection (6)(b) makes every grant subject to a condition that the owner shall not dispose of the holding except with prior approval; subsection (7) then removes that approval requirement where the disposition is a mortgage in favour of a licensed commercial bank or another listed institution.
temporal_note: Section 19 carries amendment events down to the Land Development (Amendment) Act No. 11 of 2022, which is the amendment named in the question, so subsection (7) is in force at the matter date of 2026-04. The corpus edition is consolidated to 2022 and no later change is recorded.
verifier_note: Excerpt verbatim and the role as the decisive provision is confirmed, but the temporal note overstates the corpus: both amendment events for Act No. 11 of 2022 on s.19 are recorded only as 'unknown', so the corpus does not show that the 2022 Act produced subsection (7). Separately, subsection (6)(b) requires the prior approval of the Government Agent while subsection (7) lifts the approval of the Divisional Secretary, and the Ordinance never reconciles the two offices.

relevant_excerpt: The Owner of a holding- (a) shall not lease such holding to any other person except in such circumstances as may be prescribed; and (b) shall not mortgage such holding to any person other than a licensed commercial bank
why_relevant: Sets the closed list of permissible mortgagees for the owner of a holding. It confirms that a mortgage to a licensed commercial bank is a permitted transaction under the Ordinance, which is the premise on which the exemption in s.19(7) operates.
temporal_note: In force in its present form from 1993 (insertion by Act No. 22 of 1993) as amended in 1996; both precede the matter date, so it is in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: means land alienated by grant under this Ordinance, and includes any part thereof or interest therein
why_relevant: Defines 'holding' as land alienated by grant. Sections 19(6) to (7) and 43 speak of a 'holding', so they apply only if Herath holds under a grant rather than a permit. The definition is what makes the grant and permit distinction decisive.
temporal_note: Section 2 carries amendment events down to 2022. The definition relied on is long-standing and is in force at 2026-04. In the corpus text of s.2 the defined terms are listed separately from the bodies of the definitions, so this excerpt appears without its headword.

relevant_excerpt: means a licensed commercial bank within the meaning of the Banking Act, No. 30 of 1988
why_relevant: Defines the class of mortgagee that triggers the exemption in s.19(7) and the permission in s.43(b). Whether the intended mortgagee is a licensed commercial bank under the banking legislation is what decides the question.
temporal_note: Definition introduced by amendment and reflected in the consolidated text; in force at 2026-04. The Banking Act, No. 30 of 1988 is not in the corpus, so the content of that external definition cannot be checked here.

relevant_excerpt: 'disposition' with its grammatical variations and cognate expressions means any transaction of whatever nature affecting land or the title thereto and includes any conveyance, devise, donation, exchange, lease, mortgage or transfer of land
why_relevant: Confirms that a mortgage is a 'disposition', so the prohibition in s.19(6)(b) and the prohibition in s.46(1) both reach a mortgage. Without it the general approval condition would not obviously bite on a mortgage at all.
temporal_note: Long-standing definition in the consolidated text; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: (1) Subject to the provisions of subsection (2), no permit-holder shall execute or effect any disposition of the land alienated to him on the permit. (2) With the written consent of the Government Agent, a permit-holder may mortgage his interest in the land alienated to him on the permit to any registered society of which he is a member.
why_relevant: The contrasting regime. If Herath held on a permit rather than a grant, he could not mortgage to a commercial bank at all: the only permitted mortgage would be to a registered society of which he is a member, and only with the written consent of the Government Agent. It marks the boundary of the answer.
temporal_note: Substituted by Act No. 16 of 1969; unchanged since in the corpus edition and in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: Nothing in the preceding provisions of this chapter shall be deemed to prohibit the seizure and sale, by a licensed commercial bank
why_relevant: Context on why the Ordinance permits bank mortgages of a holding: the general bar on seizure and sale of alienated land does not prevent a licensed commercial bank enforcing a mortgage over land alienated on a grant. It shows the bank's security is enforceable, though it is not needed to answer the approval question.
temporal_note: In force in its present form from 1993 as substituted in 1996; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: means the owner of a holding whose title thereto is derived from or under a grant issued under this Ordinance and includes a permit- holder who has paid all sums which he is required to pay under subsection (2) of section 19 and has complied with all the other conditions specified in the permit
why_relevant: Sections 19(6), 19(7) and 43 all fasten their conditions on 'the owner' of a holding, so neither the approval condition nor its exemption can be applied to Herath without this definition. It also does independent work on these facts: it extends 'owner' to a permit-holder who has paid every sum due under s.19(2) and complied with the conditions of his permit, so Herath is within the class even on the footing that the grant had not yet issued to him.
temporal_note: Long-standing definition carried in the consolidated s.2 text, whose latest recorded change year is 2022; in force at 2026-04.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier. Excerpt checked verbatim against 19-1935/s2.

relevant_excerpt: No written law (other than this Ordinance) which provides for succession to land upon an intestacy and no other law relating to succession to land upon an intestacy shall have any application in respect of any land alienated under this Ordinance.
why_relevant: Excludes the general law of intestate succession from land alienated under the Ordinance, so the devolution of Herath's land is governed by Chapter VII of the Ordinance and by the Third Schedule alone.
temporal_note: In force from 1935; corpus records the latest change as Act No. 16 of 1969 s.84. No later amendment event is recorded, so the text stands at the matter date 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: means the owner of a holding whose title thereto is derived from or under a grant issued under this Ordinance and includes a permit- holder who has paid all sums which he is required to pay under subsection (2) of section 19 and has complied with all the other conditions specified in the permit;
why_relevant: Fixes who counts as the owner of a holding whose death triggers the succession rules in sections 48B, 49 and 72. Herath must fall inside this definition (grant-derived title, or a permit-holder who has paid up) for Chapter VII devolution to apply.
temporal_note: Section 2 carries an amendment event from Act No. 11 of 2022 (operation recorded as 'unknown' in the corpus), so the consolidated text is at least partly post-2022 and applies at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: In this Chapter 'successor', when used with reference to any land alienated on a permit or a holding, means a person who is entitled under this Chapter to succeed to that land or holding upon the death of the permit-holder or owner thereof, if that permit-holder or owner died without leaving behind his or her spouse, or, if that permit-holder or owner died leaving behind his or her spouse, upon the failure of that spouse to succeed to that land or holding or upon the death of that spouse.
why_relevant: Defines 'successor' for Chapter VII, and locates the Third Schedule class after the surviving spouse in the order of devolution.
temporal_note: In force from 1935; substituted by Act No. 16 of 1969 s.22. No later amendment event recorded, so applicable at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: (1) Upon the death of the owner of a holding, the spouse of that owner shall be entitled to succeed to that holding subject to the following conditions:- (a) upon the marriage of such spouse, title to the holding shall devolve on the nominated successor of the deceased owner or, if there was no such nomination, on the person who was entitled to succeed under rule 1 of the Third Schedule;
why_relevant: Gives the surviving spouse of a deceased owner priority over the Third Schedule class, and confirms that where there was no nomination the holding goes to the person entitled under rule 1 of the Third Schedule. Whether the Third Schedule group takes at all depends on whether Herath left a spouse.
temporal_note: In force from 1935 (inserted by Act No. 16 of 1969 s.23 per the corpus event list); no later amendment event recorded, so applicable at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: a person nominated as successor by such permit- holder or owner shall succeed to that land or holding.
why_relevant: States the primary route, devolution on a nominated successor. Herath made no nomination, so this route fails and section 72 is reached.
temporal_note: In force from 1935; substituted by Act No. 16 of 1969 s.24 and amended by Act No. 27 of 1981 s.5. No later amendment event recorded, so applicable at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: No person shall be nominated by the owner of a holding or a permit- holder as his successor unless that person is the spouse of such owner or permit-holder, or belongs to one of the groups of relatives enumerated in rule 1 of the Third Schedule.
why_relevant: Uses the exact phrase the question asks about, the groups of relatives enumerated in rule 1 of the Third Schedule, and confirms that the Third Schedule defines the eligible class by groups of relatives. The corpus does not carry the Schedule itself.
temporal_note: In force from 1935; the corpus records no amendment event for this section, so the text stands at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: If no successor has been nominated, or if the nominated successor fails to succeed, or if the nomination of a successor contravenes the provisions of this Ordinance, the title to the land alienated on a permit to a permit-holder who at the time of his or her death was paying an annual instalment by virtue of the provisions of section 19* or to the holding of an owner shall, upon the death of such permit-holder or owner without leaving behind his or her spouse, or, where such permit- holder or owner died leaving behind his or her spouse, upon the failure of such spouse to succeed to that land or holding, or upon the death of such spouse, devolve as prescribed in rule 1 of the Third Schedule.
why_relevant: The operative gateway. Where no successor has been nominated, title to the holding devolves as prescribed in rule 1 of the Third Schedule. It answers how the land devolves but not to whom, because rule 1 is not in the corpus.
temporal_note: In force from 1935; substituted by Act No. 16 of 1969 s.43 and amended by Act No. 27 of 1981 s.5. The corpus records no amendment event from Act No. 11 of 2022 on this section, so the extracted text is as at 1981; whether Act No. 11 of 2022 touched section 72 or rule 1 of the Third Schedule cannot be checked in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: Title to a land alienated on a permit or to a holding shall be deemed to have devolved on any person entitled to succeed to the land or holding under the provisions of section 72 as from the date of the death of the permit-holder or owner of the holding if such permit-holder or owner died without leaving behind his or her spouse
why_relevant: Fixes the date on which title devolves on the person entitled under section 72, the date of the owner's death where no spouse survives. Relevant to Herath's 2023 death.
temporal_note: In force from 1935; substituted by Act No. 16 of 1969 s.44. No later amendment event recorded, so applicable at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: It is and shall be the duty of every notary strictly to observe and act in conformity with the following rules
why_relevant: Makes the rules in section 31 mandatory duties of the notary personally, so a notary cannot treat any of them as optional because of an employer's instruction or urgency.
temporal_note: Section 31 is in force from 1907; the consolidated text used here carries the amendments up to Act No. 6 of 2024. The chapeau itself was not altered by those amendments and is in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: Before any deed or instrument (other than a will or codicil) affecting any interest in land or other immovable property is drawn by him, he shall search or cause to be searched the registers in the land registry to ascertain the state of the title in regard to such land and whether any prior deed affecting any interest in such land has been registered
why_relevant: The provision that directly answers the question: the notary must search the land registry registers before drawing a deed affecting an interest in land, and must do so before the deed is drawn, not merely before it is registered.
temporal_note: Rule (17) of section 31 in the consolidated text reflects the substitutions made by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 and Act No. 6 of 2024, both of which precede 2026-04, so this text is in force at the matter date.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and the rule is in force at 2026-04, but the temporal note is corrected: paragraph (a) of rule (17) was not touched by Act No. 31 of 2022 (s.16(10) repealed and replaced only paragraph (b) and added paragraphs (c) to (e)) or by Act No. 6 of 2024 (s.3(6) altered only paragraph (b)(iii) and paragraph (c)), so the search duty stands in its pre-2022 form.

relevant_excerpt: Provided that if the parties to the transaction authorize the notary in writing to dispense with the search, the search shall not be compulsory, but he shall before the deed or instrument is tendered for registration write at the head thereof the reference to the previous registration, if any.
why_relevant: The only statutory route by which the search may lawfully be omitted. The answer turns on this exception, so it must be recorded and tested against the facts.
temporal_note: Appears in the consolidated rule (17) as amended to 2024; in force at 2026-04.
verifier_note: Excerpt verbatim and the proviso is carried at rule (17) level in the corpus (1-1907/s31/sub-17/pro-39), but the temporal note is corrected: neither Act No. 31 of 2022 nor Act No. 6 of 2024 amended the proviso; it is the original text, and by its terms it dispenses only with the search, not with the certified-folio-extract duty in paragraph (b)(i).

relevant_excerpt: he shall obtain from the Registrar of the relevant Land Registry the certified extract of the folio containing the last entry pertaining to such land or immovable property containing the ownership and the registered encumbrances relating to such land or immovable property
why_relevant: Shows what the required investigation of title consists of in concrete terms, so that inspecting a copy of an earlier deed handed over by a client or employer does not discharge the duty.
temporal_note: Inserted into rule (17) by the amendments consolidated up to 2024; in force at 2026-04.
verifier_note: Excerpt verbatim; role corrected from supporting to indispensable because the gold conclusion (CL-M005-Q01-012) requires the certified folio extract, and the temporal note is corrected: paragraph (b) was repealed and substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(10)(a), and Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(6)(a) touched only sub-paragraph (iii), not (i).

relevant_excerpt: When a deed transferring any immovable property is executed or acknowledged before a notary, he shall use his best endeavours to obtain the title deed, if any, of such property
why_relevant: A further title-related duty owed on a deed of transfer, which supports the conclusion that the Ordinance does not leave title investigation to the notary's convenience. Not indispensable: rule (17) alone decides the question.
temporal_note: Long-standing rule in section 31, not identified as altered by the 2011, 2022 or 2024 amendment events listed for the section; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: any other rule set out in section 31, shall be guilty of an offence, and shall, on conviction after summary trial before a Magistrate, be liable to a fine not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, in addition to any civil liability he may incur thereby.
why_relevant: Supplies the consequence of breaching rule (17). Rule (17) is not listed in section 34(1)(a) or (b), so it falls within the residual paragraph (c).
temporal_note: Section 34 was substituted by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022, which precedes the matter date of 2026-04; the substituted text is the one in force.

relevant_excerpt: No instrument shall be deemed to be invalid by reason only of the failure of any notary to observe any provision of any rule set out in section 31 in respect of any matter of form
why_relevant: Context only: it limits the effect of a breach on the validity of the instrument, and only for matters of form. It says nothing about the notary's own liability, so it does not make the search optional.
temporal_note: In force from 1907 and carrying no amendment events in the corpus; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: shall be entitled, on an application to a warrant authorizing him to practice as notary in the language in which he has passed the examination in conveyancing, within the judicial zone in which he resides.
why_relevant: Fixes what a notary's warrant authorises: practice in a stated language and within the judicial zone in which he resides. This is the source of the two limits (area and language) that rule (22) of section 31 enforces, and it identifies Saman's authorised area as the Judicial Zone of Colombo.
temporal_note: In force from 1907; the consolidated text records substitution by Act No. 20 of 1976 s.3 and by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.2, both before the matter date of 2026-04, so the text relied on is the operative text at that date.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any area other than that in which he is authorized to practice, nor in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice nor authenticate or attest any deed or instrument drawn in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice.
why_relevant: The operative prohibition. It restricts the area in which the notary may perform the act of attestation and the language of the instrument. It says nothing about where the land affected by the deed is situated, which is the point of the question.
temporal_note: Section 31 is in force from 1907 and the corpus edition is consolidated to 2024 (amendment events recorded for 1976, 2011, 2022 and 2024). No amendment event is recorded against the text of rule (22) itself; treated as in force at 2026-04.
verifier_note: Excerpt and role confirmed against 1-1907/s31 rule (22); read Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3 directly in the corpus (it is present as act 6-2024, contrary to the third recorded corpus gap) and it does not touch rule (22), so the consolidated text is the text in force at 2026-04; note that rule (23) of the same section treats "area" and "zone" as capable of differing, so the equation of Saman's "area" with the Judicial Zone of Colombo runs through s.9 ("the area specified in his warrant") and s.3(1) rather than through a defined term.

relevant_excerpt: shall on or before the fifteenth day of the month next following that in which the same was executed (besides transmitting the duplicate in manner aforesaid) deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which such land shall be situated a copy thereof certified by him as correct
why_relevant: Shows on the face of the Ordinance that a notary may lawfully attest a deed affecting land in a district other than his own: the statute does not forbid it, it regulates it by adding a duty to transmit a certified copy and a list to the Registrar of Lands of the district where the land is situated. This is the provision that answers the Kurunegala point.
temporal_note: Part of section 31, in force from 1907; the consolidated edition carries amendments to 2024 and records no amendment event for rule (29). Treated as in force at 2026-04.
verifier_note: Verified; note that the trigger for rule (29) is the district in which the notary resides, whereas the enriched facts fix only the district of his office, so the duty is engaged by inference from s.3(1) and s.9 rather than by a stated fact.

relevant_excerpt: Provided that, where such deed or instrument is required to be registered outside the jurisdiction in which he is practicing, he shall submit such deed or instrument for registration before the expiry of sixty days from the date of attestation.
why_relevant: Confirms again that attesting a deed registrable outside the notary's own jurisdiction is contemplated and permitted, and sets the longer sixty-day registration deadline that applies to Saman if he attests this deed in Colombo for registration in Kurunegala.
temporal_note: Rule (30A) sits within section 31 of the consolidated edition (consolidated to 2024) and is referred to in section 34(1)(b) as substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022. In force at 2026-04.
verifier_note: Verified; the temporal note is imprecise in saying only that rule (30A) "sits within" section 31 - it was inserted by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(14), and section 34(1)(b) lists rule (30A), both confirmed in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: Every notary shall be bound to have his office within the area specified in his warrant; and any notary infringing this provision shall be liable to have his warrant withdrawn by the Minister.
why_relevant: Supports the reading that the Ordinance regulates where the notary is based and operates, not where the subject land lies. Saman's office must be in the Colombo zone, which is where he proposes to attest the deed.
temporal_note: In force from 1907 with no amendment event recorded in the consolidated edition. In force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: any other rule set out in section 31, shall be guilty of an offence, and shall, on conviction after summary trial before a Magistrate, be liable to a fine not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, in addition to any civil liability he may incur thereby.
why_relevant: Gives the consequence if Saman were to attest the deed outside his zone: rule (22) is not listed in paragraph (a) or (b) of section 34(1), so a breach falls within the residual paragraph (c). It shows the territorial limit is penal, not merely directory.
temporal_note: Substituted by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.17; the substituted text is the operative text at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: If he is a legal officer working in any organization, entity or company, he shall specify the registered address of such organization, entity or company
why_relevant: Background: the Ordinance expressly contemplates a notary who is a legal officer of a company and regulates that position by a disclosure requirement on the face of the deed rather than by disqualification. It is why Saman's employment does not by itself bar him from attesting.
temporal_note: Part of the rule (17) block of section 31 as restructured by Act No. 47 of 2011 s.3 and amended by Acts No. 31 of 2022 and No. 6 of 2024, all before the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: The Minister may on application made in that behalf grant to a notary, having a warrant authorizing him to practice within a judicial zone, a fresh warrant authorizing him to practice within another judicial zone.
why_relevant: Identifies the only route by which Saman could lawfully attest the deed in Kurunegala itself: a fresh warrant for that judicial zone. It also confirms that the zone limit attaches to the warrant and is changed only by the Minister.
temporal_note: Substituted by Act No. 20 of 1976 s.5; that text stands in the consolidated edition and is in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: Every instrument presented for registration shall be registered in the book allotted to the division in which the land affected by the instrument is situated
why_relevant: Background: registration follows the situation of the land, not the zone of the attesting notary. It explains why the deed, though attested in Colombo, must be registered in the Kurunegala land registry division, and so why the extra duties in rules (29) and (30A) exist.
temporal_note: In force from 1927, last recorded change 1974. In force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument to which he is a party.
why_relevant: The one disqualification that Saman's employment could have triggered. On the enriched facts he is not a party to the deed, so it is not engaged; it is recorded because it is the rule a verifier should test the employment fact against.
temporal_note: Part of section 31, in force from 1907, no amendment event recorded for rule (13). In force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless the person executing the same and the witnesses shall have signed the same in his presence and in the presence of one another, and unless he shall have signed the same in the presence of the executant and of the attesting witnesses.
why_relevant: This is the section 31 rule that the enriched facts show Saman broke. It is the rule whose subject matter is duplicated by the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2(1)(a), so breaking it is not merely a notarial default but also non-compliance with another written law, which is what takes the deed outside the protection of s.33.
temporal_note: Rule (12) is part of the original 1907 text of s.31 and is not among the rules substituted or inserted by Acts No. 47 of 2011, No. 31 of 2022 or No. 6 of 2024; it was in force at the matter reference date of 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: he shall write on the front page of the deed his name with initials, number assigned to the notary, address of his office and telephone number.
why_relevant: Supplies the contrasting defect: a section 31 requirement about how the face of the deed is to be completed, unconnected with any other written law. It is what allows the answer to show that some section 31 breaches leave the deed intact, which is the first half of the required explanation.
temporal_note: Rule (17) was restructured by Act No. 47 of 2011 and paragraph (c) reflects the substitutions made by Acts No. 31 of 2022 and No. 6 of 2024, including the sentence requiring a notary who is a legal officer of an organisation to give that organisation's registered address. All of those changes commenced before 2026-04, so the consolidated text applies to a deed attested in 2026.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim and the paragraph is correctly identified as rule (17)(c) (inserted by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(10)(b) and amended by Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(6)(b), which substituted "name with initials" for "full name"), but the temporal note is wrong to say rule (17) was restructured by Act No. 47 of 2011: that Act amended only rules (16) and (26); the excerpt also stops before the sentence on a notary who is a legal officer of an organisation, on which claim CL-M007-Q01-005 relies.

relevant_excerpt: No instrument shall be deemed to be invalid by reason only of the failure of any notary to observe any provision of any rule set out in section 31 in respect of any matter of form: Provided that nothing hereinbefore contained shall be deemed to give validity to any instrument which may be invalid by reason of non-compliance with the provisions of any other written law.
why_relevant: The provision that answers the question directly. Its main limb denies invalidity where the notary's default is a matter of form only; its proviso withholds that protection where the instrument is invalid under some other written law. Both limbs are needed, because the enriched facts contain one defect of each kind.
temporal_note: Section 33 carries in_force_from_year 1907 and no amendment events in the corpus; it stands in its original form at the matter reference date.

relevant_excerpt: shall be in force or avail in law unless - (a) the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary
why_relevant: This is the "other written law" that the proviso to Notaries Ordinance s.33 preserves. It makes the same simultaneous-presence requirement a condition of the deed of transfer having any force in law, so the defect in Saman's attestation attacks the deed itself and not merely his conduct.
temporal_note: Section 2 was renumbered as subsection (1) and paragraph (a) was substituted by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 4 of 2024 s.2; the corpus body is the post-2024 consolidated text, which is the text in force in April 2026. The earlier changes recorded are by Act No. 60 of 1947 and Act No. 30 of 2022.
verifier_note: Verbatim and temporally correct; note only that the excerpt begins mid-sentence, so the opening words of s.2(1) that confine the provision to land and other immovable property - the words claims CL-M007-Q01-004 and CL-M007-Q01-010 depend on - sit outside the quoted text.

relevant_excerpt: any other rule set out in section 31, shall be guilty of an offence, and shall, on conviction after summary trial before a Magistrate, be liable to a fine not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, in addition to any civil liability he may incur thereby.
why_relevant: Shows that the sanction the Ordinance itself attaches to a breach of section 31 is penal and personal to the notary, with civil liability preserved, and says nothing about the standing of the instrument. It supports the point that breach of section 31 and invalidity of the deed are separate questions, but the answer to the question asked does not depend on it.
temporal_note: Section 34 was substituted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.17, which commenced before the matter reference date; the fine levels quoted are those of the 2022 text.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any area other than that in which he is authorized to practice
why_relevant: Context only. The background states that Saman's licence is for the Judicial Zone of Colombo, and the added facts place the execution at his Colombo office, so this rule is satisfied and no question of invalidity arises from the place of attestation. Recorded so that the verifier can see the point was considered and closed.
temporal_note: Rule (22) is part of the original 1907 text of s.31 and is not among the rules substituted by the 2011, 2022 or 2024 amendments; read with s.4A, a licence for a judicial division is a licence for the corresponding judicial zone.

relevant_excerpt: The Commissioner of Title Settlement shall cause an investigation to be conducted in order to determine the genuinness or otherwise of claims made in response to a Notice under section 12.
why_relevant: The question begins 'after the investigations made by the Commissioner of Title settlement'. This is the investigation stage that triggers the section 14 determination, and it fixes the officer and the moment at which the class of title is settled.
temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. In force at the matter reference date 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: where the Commissioner of Title Settlement is of the view that a claimant to a land parcel has a title of Absolute Ownership, he shall declare such claimant eligible to be registered with a First Class Title of Absolute Ownership
why_relevant: This is the higher class of title and the alternative that has to be ruled out before the answer can settle on a Second Class Title. It conditions the First Class declaration on the claimant having a title of Absolute Ownership, which Kamal cannot show on possession alone.
temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. In force at the matter reference date 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: where the Commissioner of Title Settlement is of the view that a claimant does not qualify for a First Class Title of Absolute Ownership but the claimant is in bonafide possession of the land parcel, he may declare the claimant eligible to be registered with a Second Class Title of Ownership with the right, at the end of a period of uninterrupted and unchallenged possession of ten years from the date of registration in such capacity, to have such Second Class Title converted to a registration with First Class Title of Absolute Ownership
why_relevant: This is the operative provision for a claimant whose case rests on long possession rather than documentary title. It supplies both the class of title Kamal is eligible for and the conversion right that completes the answer.
