temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. In force at the matter reference date 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: A person registered with a Second Class Title of Ownership or a person claiming title through him shall at the end of a period of ten years from such registration, and if there has been no action under section 29 against such registration during the intervening period, be eligible for the conversion of his registration to one of First Class Title of Absolute Ownership.
why_relevant: Spells out the conversion right that section 14(b) refers to, and adds the condition that no section 29 action has been filed in the intervening ten years. Supports, but does not itself decide, the class Kamal is first eligible for.
temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. In force at the matter reference date 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: proof of such undisturbed and uninterrupted possession as herein before explained, by such plaintiff or intervenient, or by those under whom he claims, shall entitle such plaintiff or intervenient to a decree in his favour with costs
why_relevant: The background says Kamal occupies 'by long and prescriptive rights'. This section shows what prescriptive possession does in statute: it entitles the possessor to a decree in an action. Without such a decree or any instrument of title, Kamal has no established title of Absolute Ownership to put before the Commissioner under section 14(a).
temporal_note: In force from 1871; section 3 itself is unamended in the corpus. The Prescription (Amendment) Act No. 26 of 2014 amends the Ordinance but replaces section 15 only, so the text of section 3 applicable at the matter reference date 2026-04 is the text quoted.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim and section 3 is unamended, but two corrections are needed: the Prescription Ordinance is amended in the corpus by the Prescription (Amendment) Act No. 26 of 2014, which replaces section 15 only, so the temporal note's 'no amendment events recorded in the corpus' is wrong at Act level though harmless for section 3; and the quoted limb stops short of the words 'by a title adverse to or independent of that of the claimant', which describe the possessor as holding a title and therefore cut against the inference the map draws from this section, so its role is reduced from indispensable support for excluding section 14(a) to context on how prescription is litigated.

relevant_excerpt: The Prescription Ordinance (Chapter 68) shall not apply to lands or interests in land registered under this Act with a First Class Title of Absolute Ownership or a Second Class Title of Ownership.
why_relevant: Closes the loop on prescription: once the parcel is registered under either class, further prescriptive claims are shut out. Context for what Kamal gains on registration, not a step in choosing the class.
temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. In force at the matter reference date 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: Any person aggrieved by the registration of title of a person with a Second Class Title of Ownership to any land parcel may with in a period of ten years from the date of such registration, file action for the amendment of the register, in the District Court
why_relevant: Qualifies the conversion right: the ten-year period must run unchallenged, and this is the challenge route. Explains why a Second Class Title is provisional for ten years.
temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. In force at the matter reference date 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: Any person may, on application made in the prescribed form and on payment of the prescribed fee inspect during office hours, any title register and any cadastral map maintained under the provisions of this Act.
why_relevant: Directly answers the inspection half of the question. The right is given to 'any person', so no proprietary interest, retainer or written authority has to be shown; the only conditions are the prescribed form, the prescribed fee and office hours.
temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. In force at the matter reference date 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: Any, person shall, on application made to the relevant Registrar of Title and on payment of the prescribed fee, be entitled to receive an extract of such Title Register certified by such Registrar of Title.
why_relevant: Answers the certified-copy half for the Title Register and identifies the officer who must be applied to and who certifies. The wording is an entitlement ('shall ... be entitled'), not a discretion.
temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. In force at the matter reference date 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: Any person on application made to the relevant Superintendent of Surveys, shall on payment of the prescribed fee be entitled to receive a copy of an extract of a cadastral map used for registration of title, certified on behalf of the Surveyor-General.
why_relevant: Answers the certified-copy half for the cadastral map, and shows that this copy comes from a different officer (the Superintendent of Surveys, certifying on behalf of the Surveyor-General) rather than from the Registrar of Title.
temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. In force at the matter reference date 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: means any person appointed as Registrar of Title under this Act; means a land parcel the title to which is registered under this Act;
why_relevant: Definitions of 'Registrar of Title' and 'registered land'. The answer turns on applying to the correct statutory officer for the certified register extract, so the defined term is part of the reasoning.
temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. In force at the matter reference date 2026-04. The corpus rendering of section 75 strips the defined terms out of the body and lists them separately, so the excerpt reads as bare 'means ...' clauses.

relevant_excerpt: Every document purporting to be certified by a Registrar of Title shall in all proceedings be presumed to have been so certified and shall be accepted as prima facie evidence of the matter to which it relates without any further proof of such matter.
why_relevant: Explains why the certified copies are worth obtaining: they carry evidential weight without further proof. Useful for a Notary advising a client, but not needed to decide whether she may obtain them.
temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. In force at the matter reference date 2026-04.
verifier_note: Wording of section 35(1) is verbatim, but the subsection cited is incomplete for the use made of it: the gold answer covers certified copies of both documents, and it is section 35(2) that gives the same prima facie status to a copy of an extract of a cadastral map certified by or on behalf of the Surveyor-General, so the entry should read 35(1) and (2).

relevant_excerpt: (g) the forms required for the purposes of this Act; (h) the fees payable under the Act.
why_relevant: Section 34 conditions both inspection and certified copies on a 'prescribed form' and a 'prescribed fee'. This is the regulation-making power under which those forms and fees are prescribed.
temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. In force at the matter reference date 2026-04. The regulations themselves are not in the corpus, so the actual form and fee cannot be stated.

relevant_excerpt: means any person performing the functions of a Superintendent of Surveys in the Survey Department; means the Title Register under the provisions of this Act.
why_relevant: Definitions of 'Superintendent of Surveys' and 'Title Register'. The answer separates the two certified documents by the officer who issues them, so this definition is part of the reasoning chain.
temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. In force at the matter reference date 2026-04. Same corpus rendering caveat as PROV-M008-011.

formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
relevant_excerpt: Any instrument attested in terms of section 44 together with the Certificate of Title pertaining to the title of the vendor shall be forwarded by the Attestor working days of such attestation to the Registrar of Title within whose area of jurisdiction the land parcel dealt with in such instrument is situate.
why_relevant: This is the provision that fixes the period within which an attesting notary must forward an attested instrument, with the vendor's Certificate of Title, to the Registrar of Title. It answers the second limb of the question. The corpus body is defective: the numeral before 'working days' is missing from the extracted text, so the period is recoverable only from the section heading in the corpus record, 'Attestor to forward instruments attested within seven days.'
temporal_note: in_force_from_year 1998, no amendment_events recorded for this section; in force at 2026-04. The gap in the extracted text is an extraction defect, not an amendment.
verifier_note: Re-extract section 45(1)(a) from a Government Printer edition and confirm the missing numeral before 'working days' before this question can be released as gold.

formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
relevant_excerpt: Failure to forward the attested instrument within the stipulated period shall be an offence punishable with the prescribed penalty.
why_relevant: Makes the forwarding duty in subsection (1)(a) mandatory rather than directory, and is the provision under which the notary's default is penalised.
temporal_note: in_force_from_year 1998, no amendment_events recorded; in force at 2026-04. The 'prescribed penalty' depends on regulations made under section 67, which are not in the corpus.

formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
relevant_excerpt: No person acquiring an interest in any land parcel registered under the provisions of this Act shall be entitled to such title or interest unless such title or interest is registered under the provisions of this Act.
why_relevant: First limb of the question: registration is not optional. A donee of a registered land parcel gets no title unless the interest is registered.
temporal_note: in_force_from_year 1998, no amendment_events recorded; in force at 2026-04.

formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
relevant_excerpt: No land parcel, title to which has been registered under this Act, or any interest therein shall be transferred or dealt with except in accordance with the provisions of this Act, and every disposition otherwise effected shall be void.
why_relevant: Supplies the sanction for the mandatory character of registration: a disposition of a registered parcel made otherwise than under the Act is void.
temporal_note: in_force_from_year 1998, no amendment_events recorded; in force at 2026-04.

formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
relevant_excerpt: An instrument pertaining to land executed in accordance with the provisions of this Act shall take effect on registration, of such instrument under the provisions of this Act.
why_relevant: Registration is constitutive: until the gift instrument is registered it has no operative effect, which is the practical reason registration is mandatory.
temporal_note: in_force_from_year 1998, no amendment_events recorded; in force at 2026-04.

formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
relevant_excerpt: A Notary Public attesting an instrument in terms of this Act shall- (a) satisfy himself regarding the identity of whosoever of the parties to the transaction and the witnesses, as are not known to him, by reference to their official identity cards or such other means as may reliably reveal their identity;
why_relevant: Section 45(1)(a) is triggered only by an instrument 'attested in terms of section 44', so this section is the condition precedent to the forwarding duty and identifies the notary as the Attestor on whom the duty falls.
temporal_note: in_force_from_year 1998, no amendment_events recorded; in force at 2026-04.

formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
relevant_excerpt: means a document having the effect of conveying title to and interest in any land parcel in the prescribed form
why_relevant: The answer turns on the defined term 'instrument'; the deed of gift is an instrument only if it conveys title to a land parcel in the prescribed form, which is what brings sections 38, 39, 45 and 49 into play.
temporal_note: in_force_from_year 1998, no amendment_events recorded; in force at 2026-04. The corpus rendering of section 75 has lost the defined terms from the run of text, but the corpus records 'instrument' among the section's defined_terms.
verifier_note: Confirm that the quoted words are the definition of 'instrument' and not of an adjacent term; the extracted body drops the term labels.

formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
relevant_excerpt: Instruments prepared under the provisions of subsection (1) shall be signed by the parties to the transaction and two witnesses and attested by a Notary Public
why_relevant: Explains why a notary is involved at all and why the gift deed had to be attested before the forwarding duty could arise.
temporal_note: in_force_from_year 1998, no amendment_events recorded; in force at 2026-04.

formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
relevant_excerpt: An instrument for conveying interest in a land parcel may be presented for title registration under this Act to the Registrar of Title by- (a) any person claiming any interest or benefit thereunder;
why_relevant: Shows that presentation for registration is not confined to the notary: the donee may also present, which matters when the notary has defaulted.
temporal_note: in_force_from_year 1998, no amendment_events recorded; in force at 2026-04.

formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
relevant_excerpt: for the purpose of priority the time of presentation shall be taken as the time of registration
why_relevant: Gives the practical consequence of delay in forwarding: priority runs from presentation, so every day of a notary's delay exposes the donee to a competing instrument.
temporal_note: in_force_from_year 1998, no amendment_events recorded; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: It shall be the duty of every notary to submit for registration to the Registrar, every deed or instrument attested by him before the expiry of thirty days from the date of attestation thereof
why_relevant: The general notarial registration duty under the deeds system, offered as a contrast: the period there is thirty days, which is not the period that applies to a land parcel registered under the Registration of Title Act. A candidate who answers 'thirty days' has applied the wrong enactment.
temporal_note: Section 31 shows latest_change_year 2024; subsection (30A) appears in the consolidated text and is reproduced in Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16. In force at 2026-04. The verifier should confirm that Act No. 6 of 2024 did not touch (30A).

formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
relevant_excerpt: no entries shall be made in respect of transactions relating to land parcels registered under this Act in the Land Registers maintained under the Registration of Documents Ordinance
why_relevant: Context: once a parcel is on the Title Register the deeds registers are closed to it, so registration under this Act is the only route available for the gift.
temporal_note: in_force_from_year 1998, no amendment_events recorded; in force at 2026-04.

formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
relevant_excerpt: such Certificate of Title shall form conclusive evidence of the title to such interest
why_relevant: Context for the Certificate of Title that must accompany the instrument when it is forwarded, and for the title certificate Kamal wanted.
temporal_note: in_force_from_year 1998, no amendment_events recorded; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: It shall be lawful for any person who has reached the age of eighteen years and residing within or outside Sri Lanka to execute a will bequeathing and disposing any movable and immovable property and all and every estate, right, share or interest in any property which belong to him at the time of death
why_relevant: Gives Martin Perera, an adult resident in Sri Lanka, the statutory power to execute a will disposing of his house, which is immovable property belonging to him at the time of death.
temporal_note: Section 2 was repealed and substituted by Wills Ordinance (Amendment) Act No. 29 of 2022 (corpus amendment_events: repeal_and_substitute by 29-2022 s.2). The substituted text is in force well before 2026-04 and is the text applied here.

relevant_excerpt: Every testator shall have full power to make such testamentary disposition as he shall feel disposed, and in the exercise of such right to exclude any child, parent, relative, or descendant, or to disinherit or omit to mention any such person, without assigning any reason for such exclusion, disinheritance, or omission
why_relevant: This is the direct answer to Q01: the testator may exclude or omit a child without assigning any reason, and no contrary law, usage or custom can be set up against him.
temporal_note: Substituted by Act No. 29 of 2022; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: No will, testament, or codicil containing any devise of land or other immovable property, or any bequest of movable property, or for any other purpose whatsoever, shall be valid unless it shall be in writing and executed subject to the provisions specified in subsection (2); (2) The testator shall - (a) sign; and (b) affix his left or right thumb impression, at the foot or end of the will, testament or codicil referred to in subsection (1), before a notary public and two witnesses who shall be present at the same time
why_relevant: Freedom of testation is exercisable only through a formally valid will. The devise of Martin's house is valid only if the will is in writing and he signs and places his thumb impression at the end of it before a notary public and two witnesses present at the same time.
temporal_note: Section 4 was amended by Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 30 of 2022 (corpus amendment_events: 30-2022 s.3), the source of the present thumb-impression and notary-plus-two-witnesses wording. It is in force before 2026-04 and applies to a will executed in 2024.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim and the amendment trail is right (corpus edge 30-2022/s3 -> 7-1840/s4); the excerpt stops before the proviso allowing another finger or toe impression where the thumb impression cannot be obtained, which does not affect the claims drawn from it.

relevant_excerpt: such devise, legacy, estate, interest, gift, disposition, or appointment shall, so far only as concerns such person attesting the execution of such will, testament, or codicil, or the wife or husband of such person, or any person claiming under such person or wife or husband, be utterly null and void
why_relevant: Qualifies the way the will must be attested: if Siripala or his spouse were to attest the will, the bequest of the house to him would be void although the will itself would stand. It matters here because the beneficiary is a member of the household.
temporal_note: No amendment event recorded in the corpus; in force since 1840 and at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: Children, grandchildren, and remoter descendants are preferent to all others in the estate of the parents; all the children take equally per capita
why_relevant: Context only: the preferential right of children on which the children might rely sits in Part III, which governs inheritance ab intestato. It shows their claim arises only over property not validly disposed of by will.
temporal_note: No amendment event recorded in the corpus; in force at 2026-04.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and the background role is right, but section 24 does not itself confine the children's preferential right to intestacy; that limitation is in section 21(1) of the same Part, now added as PROV-M010-901, and the claims drawn from section 24 have been re-cited to it.

relevant_excerpt: whenever the words 'landed property' are used they shall be construed to extend to houses and buildings erected on the same, condominium parcel or any land parcel
why_relevant: Background: confirms that a house is within the property the Ordinance contemplates being disposed of by will.
temporal_note: Amended by Act No. 29 of 2022 (corpus amendment_events: 29-2022 s.6); the amended text is in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: every such will, testament, or codicil shall, after the decease of the testator or testatrix, be duly proved and recorded in the District Court empowered by law to grant probate or administration in such case
why_relevant: States the general obligation that follows Martin's death: the will has to be proved and recorded in the District Court before it can operate.
temporal_note: No amendment event recorded in the corpus; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: the person in of whose keeping or custody it shall have been deposited, or who shall find such will after the testator's death, shall produce the same to the District Court of the district in which such depository or finder resides, or to the District Court of the district in which the testator shall have died, as soon as reasonably may be after the testator's death
why_relevant: First step for Nihal: as the person who finds and holds the will he must produce it to the District Court as soon as reasonably possible after the death, with an affidavit verifying the time and place of death and the property left.
temporal_note: Chapter XXXVIII was replaced by Act No. 14 of 1993 (corpus amendment_events: 14-1993 s.4); the current text is in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: any person appointed executor therein may apply to the District Court of the district within which he resides, or within which the testator resided at the time of his death, or within which any land belonging to the testator's estate is situate, within the time limit and in the manner specified in section 524, to have the will proved and to have probate thereof granted to him
why_relevant: Nihal's standing and forum: as the executor named in the will he may apply to the District Court of his own residence, of the testator's residence, or where the land lies, to have the will proved and probate granted to him.
temporal_note: Current text from Act No. 14 of 1993; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: In every case where a will is deposited in court after the coming into operation of this Chapter, and no application has been made by any person to have the will proved and probate granted in respect thereof, the court shall in accordance with the procedure set out in respect of the grant of probate or letters of administration on application made thereto, proceed to grant probate of the will, to the executor or executors named in such will
why_relevant: Shows that proving the will is not optional once it is deposited: if Nihal does not apply, the court itself proceeds to grant probate to the named executor or administration to another person.
temporal_note: Current text from Act No. 14 of 1993; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: Every application to the District Court to have the will of a deceased person proved, shall be made within a period of three months from the date of finding of the will, and shall be made by way of petition and affidavit and such petition shall set out in numbered paragraphs- (a) the fact of the making of the will; (b) the details and the situation of the deceased's property; (bb) the heirs of the deceased to the best of the petitioner's knowledge; (c) the grounds upon which the petitioner is entitled to have the will proved
why_relevant: Fixes the form, contents and three-month time limit of Nihal's petition, including naming the heirs (Martin's children) though they take nothing, producing the will, proving due execution and tendering the charges for the section 529 notice.
temporal_note: Substituted by Act No. 11 of 2010 (corpus amendment_events: substitute by 11-2010 s.4, and earlier 14-1993 s.4, 38-1998 s.2); the substituted text is in force at 2026-04 and governs a death in 2026.

relevant_excerpt: The notice published under subsection (2), shall call upon persons having objections to the making of an order declaring any will proved, or the grant of probate or of letters of administration with or without the will annexed, or the issue of certificates of heir ship to any person specified in the application made under section 524 or 528, to submit their written objections, if any, supported by affidavit
why_relevant: Explains what happens to Nihal's petition after filing: the Probate Officer publishes notice in Sinhala, Tamil and English and objectors, who could include Martin's children, may file written objections supported by affidavit.
temporal_note: Amended by Act No. 11 of 2010 (corpus amendment_events: 11-2010 s.8(1) and s.8(2)); in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: if the court is satisfied that the evidence adduced is sufficient to afford prima facie proof as to the due making of the will and the character of the petitioner, it shall make order declaring the will to be proved and if the applicant claims- (i) as the executor or one of the executors of the will, and asks that probate thereof be granted to him the order shall declare that he is executor, and shall direct the grant of probate to him accordingly
why_relevant: The order Nihal is working towards where no objection is filed: a declaration that the will is proved and a direction that probate issue to him as executor.
temporal_note: Current text from Act No. 14 of 1993; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: that the prima facie proof of the material averments in the application have not been rebutted, the court shall forthwith make order for the grant of probate or letters of administration with the will annexed or grant of administration only subject to the conditions hereinafter prescribed
why_relevant: Covers the alternative route if Martin's children object: issues are framed, the matter goes to a final hearing, and probate is granted if the prima facie proof is not rebutted.
temporal_note: Current text from Act No. 14 of 1993; in force at 2026-04.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but section 534 presupposes rather than creates the contested route: section 532(1) is what sends an opposed application to a final hearing and section 533 what provides for framing issues. PROV-M010-903 (section 532) has been added and the claims about the contested route re-cited to it.

relevant_excerpt: it shall be the duty of the said person, executor or administrator, in whose favour such order is made, to take within fifteen days of the making of such order, the oath of an executor or administrator as set out in form No. 92 in the First Schedule, and thereafter to file in court within a period of one month from the date of taking of the oath, an inventory of the deceased person's property and effects, with a valuation of the same
why_relevant: The steps between the order and the actual grant: Nihal must take the executor's oath within fifteen days of the order and file an inventory and valuation within one month of the oath, after which the court grants probate.
temporal_note: Current text from Act No. 14 of 1993; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: the power of administration, which is authenticated by the grant of probate, or is conveyed by the grant of letters of administration, extends to every portion of the deceased person's property, movable and immovable, within Sri Lanka
why_relevant: Background: once probate issues without limitation, Nihal's authority covers the house and the bank balance until the estate is fully administered.
temporal_note: Current text from Act No. 14 of 1993; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: Every executor and administrator shall file in the District Court, on or before the expiration of twelve months from the date upon which probate or grant of administration issued to him, or within such further time as the court may allow, a true and final account of his executor ship or administration, as the case may be, verified on oath or affirmation, with all receipts and vouchers attached
why_relevant: The closing step Nihal must take: a true and final account verified on oath, with receipts and vouchers, within twelve months of the issue of probate unless the court extends the time or the parties consent to dispense with it.
temporal_note: Current text from Act No. 14 of 1993; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: If any executor or administrator shall fail to pay over to the creditors, heirs, legatees, or other persons the sums of money to which they are respectively entitled within one year after probate or administration is granted, such executor or administrator shall be liable to pay interest out of his own funds
why_relevant: Puts a personal sanction on delay, which is why the distribution to Siripala should be completed within a year of the grant.
temporal_note: Current text from Act No. 14 of 1993; in force at 2026-04.

relevant_excerpt: Inheritance ab interstate to the immovable property in Sri Lanka of a person deceased shall be governed and regulated by the following provisions of this Ordinance
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. It is section 21(1), not section 24, that confines Part III of the Ordinance to inheritance ab intestato. Without it the claim that the children's preferential right cannot defeat a valid will rests on no provision that says so, because the text of section 24 is unqualified on its face.
temporal_note: No amendment event recorded in the corpus; in force since 1876 and at 2026-04.
verifier_note: Excerpt checked verbatim against 15-1876/s21 by the verifier; section 21 sits in the same Part III INHERITANCE as section 24.

relevant_excerpt: No person shall effect any transfer of any property movable or immovable, in Sri Lanka, belonging to or included in, the estate or effects of any person dying testate or intestate in or out of Sri Lanka within five years prior to the effecting of the transfer, unless grant of probate has been issued in the case of a person dying testate
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. The answer to Q02 has Nihal transferring the house to Siripala in terms of the will, but no provision the researcher cited makes the grant of probate a condition of that transfer. Section 545 does, and it is what makes the probate sequence a necessary step for Siripala to get the house rather than a formality.
temporal_note: Substituted by Act No. 11 of 2010 (corpus amendment_events: substitute by 11-2010 s.11, and earlier 14-1993 s.4); the substituted text is in force at 2026-04 and governs a death on 14 February 2026.
verifier_note: Excerpt checked verbatim against 2-1889/s545 by the verifier.

relevant_excerpt: If any objections are received in relation to any application under section 524 or 528 in response to a notice published under section 529, on or before the date specified in such notice in respect of such application, the court shall proceed to hear, try and determine such application in accordance with the procedure herein provided and may for such purpose name a day for final hearing and disposal of such application
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. Section 532(1) is the provision that turns objections filed in answer to the section 529 notice into a final hearing; the researcher's claims about the contested route rested on section 534, which only states the orders that may be made once that hearing has happened.
temporal_note: Current text from Act No. 14 of 1993 (corpus amendment_events: unknown by 14-1993 s.4); in force at 2026-04.
verifier_note: Excerpt checked verbatim against 2-1889/s532 by the verifier; corpus edges show 2-1889/s532 procedurally_requires 2-1889/s524, on the same footing as section 531.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: means not having a husband or wife living ; all words expressive of relationship shall apply to a child in the womb at the time in question who is afterwards born alive.
why_relevant: Defines 'unmarried' for the Ordinance. Sunali is said to have died unmarried and issueless, so on this definition she left no surviving spouse able to take under s 22 and her share falls wholly to collaterals.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event on this section. In force at 2025-10 and at each death in the scenario.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: The following sections of this Ordinance shall apply to the estates of such persons only as shall die after the proclamation of this Ordinance, and shall be then unmarried or (if married) shall have been married after the proclamation of this Ordinance.
why_relevant: Gates the whole of Part III. Every death in the scenario and every marriage in it postdate the 1876 proclamation, so Part III applies to each of the three intestate estates.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event on this section.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: Inheritance ab interstate to the immovable property in Sri Lanka of a person deceased shall be governed and regulated by the following provisions of this Ordinance wherever such person may have or have had his actual or matrimonial domicile.
why_relevant: The subject matter is a fifteen perch allotment at Nugegoda, immovable property in Sri Lanka. This is the choice of law hinge that makes the general law of intestate succession, and not a personal law, govern each devolution in the chain.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event. The corpus text reads 'ab interstate', an evident transcription of 'ab intestato'; quoted verbatim as it stands in the corpus.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: When any person shall die intestate as to any of his or her property, leaving a spouse surviving, the surviving spouse shall inherit one-half of the property of such person.
why_relevant: Gives the surviving spouse one half off the top of each intestate estate. It is the first step in Prabash's intestacy, if Linda was his lawful surviving spouse, and in Brian's intestacy, where Sara survived him.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event on this section.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: the right of inheritance is divided in the following order as respects (a) descendants, (b) ascendants, (c) collaterals.
why_relevant: Sets the order of classes that decides which of ss 24 to 32 applies to each intestacy: descendants for Prabash, ascendants and collaterals for Brian, collaterals only for Sunali.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event on this section.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: Children, grandchildren, and remoter descendants are preferent to all others in the estate of the parents; all the children take equally per capita, but the children or remoter issue of a deceased child take per stirpes or by representation.
why_relevant: Governs the half of Prabash's intestate estate that does not pass to a surviving spouse: his four children Sunali, Bimali, Brian and Rian take that half equally per capita, with no distinction between the children of the first and of the second marriage.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event on this section.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: The children and remoter descendants failing, the inheritance of the deceased goes to his father and mother in case they are both alive; but if only one of the parents be alive, the surviving parent takes half, and the brothers and sisters of the deceased of the full blood, and the issue of any deceased brother or sister of the full blood, by representation, and the brothers and sisters of the half-blood who are related to the intestate by the side of the deceased parent, and the issue of any such deceased brother or sister of the half-blood, by representation, take the other half.
why_relevant: Governs Brian's intestacy. Brian died childless in 2021, his father Prabash having died in 2019 and his mother Linda surviving. After Sara's spousal half, the surviving parent Linda takes half of the residue and the balance goes to Brian's full brother Rian together with the half-blood siblings related through the deceased parent Prabash, namely Sunali and Bimali.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event on this section.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: Father and mother both failing, the property of the intestate goes to his brothers and sisters, whether of the whole or balf-blood, and their children and other issue by representation.
why_relevant: Governs Sunali's intestacy in 2023. Both her parents, Prabash and Sheela, had died by then, so her share passes to her siblings of the whole and of the half blood, that is Bimali and Rian, Brian having already died issueless.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event. The corpus text reads 'balf-blood' for 'half-blood'; quoted verbatim as it stands in the corpus.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: but if there are only half-brothers and sisters or such issue of one side, the full brothers and sisters and the issue of deceased full brothers and sisters by representation, take then in the first place one-half of the property, and divide the other half with the half-brothers and sisters and their issue by representation.
why_relevant: Supplies the arithmetic wherever full and half siblings compete. In both Brian's and Sunali's estates the half-blood siblings stand on one side only, so the full sibling first takes one half and then shares the other half with the half-blood siblings.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event on this section.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: if all those who succeed to the inheritance are equally near in degree to the intestate, they take per capita, and not per stirpes.
why_relevant: Confirms that Prabash's four children, all in the same degree, take per capita, and that surviving siblings in the later intestacies take per capita except where s 27 expressly provides otherwise for the half blood.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event on this section.

formal_title: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876
relevant_excerpt: In all questions relating to the distribution of the property of an intestate, if the present Ordinance is silent, the rules of the Roman-Dutch law as it prevailed in North Holland are to govern and be followed.
why_relevant: The Ordinance says nothing about a reserved life interest or about a prohibition against alienation coupled with a gift over. Section 36 refers those questions out to Roman-Dutch common law, which is not in the corpus. It marks the point at which the statutory chain of reasoning runs out and is the textual basis for treating this matter as needing non-statutory authority.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event on this section.

relevant_excerpt: a trust does not include a *fideicommissum;(* Abolished by Act No. 20 of 1972.)
why_relevant: Recorded as background only. It is the clearest in-corpus signal that fideicommissa were dealt with by Act No. 20 of 1972, an enactment absent from this corpus. It shows the missing authority exists; it does not state its terms and cannot by itself decide the effect of the 2018 deed.
temporal_note: Section 3 in force from 1917 and repealed and substituted in part by Act No. 6 of 2018; the consolidated text is in force at 2025-10. The parenthetical referring to Act No. 20 of 1972 is an editorial footnote carried into the consolidated text, not operative language, and is not relied on as a rule.

relevant_excerpt: Nothing contained in the preceding provisions of this section shall affect or be deemed to affect any transfer made by a fiduciary of his interest in any agricultural land to a fideicommissary in accordance with the provisions of the Abolition of Fideicommissa and Entails Act.
why_relevant: Background only, and on unrelated subject matter. It is recorded because it names the Abolition of Fideicommissa and Entails Act by title, which is the missing authority this matter turns on. Its own operation is confined to agricultural land ceilings and it has no application to a fifteen perch residential allotment at Nugegoda.
temporal_note: In force from 1972; the corpus records no amendment event on s 13.

relevant_excerpt: In relation to a transfer deed - (a) both the transferor and the transferee shall affix their signatures and thumb impressions as required by subsection (1): Provided however, where the transferee is unable to be present and execute the deed or instrument, he shall authorise in writing, any other person to sign such deed or instrument on his behalf, who shall comply with the requirements set out in subsection (1)
why_relevant: This is the subsection inserted by the latest amendment (Act No. 4 of 2024). It is the provision the question turns on: it now requires the transferee, as well as the transferor, to sign and place a thumb impression on a transfer deed, and it gives the transferee who cannot be present the one statutory escape route - a written authorisation to another person to sign on her behalf. Wimala is the transferee and cannot be present.
temporal_note: Subsection (2) was added to section 2 by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 4 of 2024 (corpus amendment_events for 7-1840/s2 record 'unknown by 4-2024 s.2 (2024)'). 2024 precedes the matter date of 2025-10, so the subsection applies. The corpus records the year only, not the date of operation.

relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property, and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object, or for establishing any security, interest, or incumbrance affecting land or other immovable property (other than a lease at will, or for any period not exceeding one month), nor any contract or agreement for the future sale or purchase of any land or other immovable property
why_relevant: Fixes the transaction Wimala proposes - a purchase and transfer of land - inside section 2, so that the formality requirements and the subsection (2) route for an absent transferee apply to her deed at all.
temporal_note: Section 2 has stood since 1840 and was last recast in 2022 and 2024; the opening words quoted here are the operative text at 2025-10.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim but stops short of the operative words "shall be in force or avail in law unless", which are the very words claim CL-M013-Q01-001 and the conclusion rest on; the excerpt should be extended to carry them.

relevant_excerpt: the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary; and (b) the left or right thumb impression of every such executant or where both thumbs of such executant are missing, the impression of any other finger or the toe impression as the case may be, is affixed above or besides the signature to the original, duplicate and the protocol of the relevant deed or instrument, in the presence of such notary public and the witnesses
why_relevant: States the formalities the authorised signatory must satisfy, because subsection (2) sends the transferee's nominee back to subsection (1). Paragraph (a), as substituted in 2024, is also the provision that expressly recognises signature 'by any person duly authorised by such executant', which is what makes the attorney route effective rather than a nullity.
temporal_note: Paragraph (a) was substituted and paragraph (b) amended by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 4 of 2024, on the base text substituted by Act No. 30 of 2022. Both precede 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: Section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance (Chapter 70) is hereby amended as follows: - (1) by the renumbering of that section as subsection (1); (2) in the renumbered subsection (1) thereof- (a) by the repeal of paragraph (a), and the substitution therefor of the following:- "(a) the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary; and"
why_relevant: The amending Act itself. The question asks for advice 'according to the latest amendments', so the answer has to identify Act No. 4 of 2024 as the source of the renumbering, of the 'duly authorised' wording in paragraph (a), and of the new subsection (2) that governs an absent transferee.
temporal_note: Enacted 2024, before the matter date of 2025-10. The corpus records no date of operation, only the year.

relevant_excerpt: Section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance (Chapter 70) (hereinafter referred to as the "principal enactment") is hereby amended by the repeal of all the words from "shall be of force" to the end of that section
why_relevant: Background only. Act No. 30 of 2022 is the amendment immediately preceding the 2024 Act; it introduced the thumb impression requirement into section 2 but said nothing about an absent transferee. It explains why the 2024 Act, not the 2022 Act, is the operative 'latest amendment' for Wimala's problem.
temporal_note: Enacted 2022; its text was itself partly recast by Act No. 4 of 2024, so it is cited for the history of section 2 rather than as operative law.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and the background role is right, but the temporal note is wrong to say the 2022 Act's own text was recast by Act No. 4 of 2024: the 2024 Act amends section 2 of the principal Ordinance, not Act No. 30 of 2022.

relevant_excerpt: (a) if it is executed in Sri Lanka, executed before two witnesses and attested by a notary public; or (b) if it is executed outside Sri Lanka, executed before an Ambassador, or a High Commissioner, or a Diplomatic Officer or a Consular Officer within the meaning of the Consular Functions Act, No. 4 of 1981 or a person who is authorized to attest such power of attorney according to the law of that country
why_relevant: Defines how the written authorisation contemplated by Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2(2) must itself be executed. Because Wimala is outside Sri Lanka, paragraph (b) tells her before whom she may sign - a diplomatic or consular officer of Sri Lanka, or a person competent to attest under the law of the country she is in.
temporal_note: The definition was substituted by the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022 and further amended by Act No. 3 of 2024; both precede 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: A power of attorney granted to be used for the purpose of a transaction which falls within the scope of section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance (Chapter 70) shall be executed subject to the provisions specified in subsection (2) or (3), as the case may be.
why_relevant: Links the two enactments. Wimala's authorisation is granted for a transaction inside Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2, so the ordinary form of power of attorney is not enough; the special requirements of s.3A(2) or (3) are engaged.
temporal_note: Section 3A was inserted by the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022, before the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: If a power of attorney specified in subsection (1) is executed outside Sri Lanka, it shall - (a) be duly executed before a person authorized under section 2 of this Act; (b) contain a description of the land or land parcel as the case may be with metes and bounds and the extent in the case of a land or land parcel;
why_relevant: The operative checklist for Wimala, who will sign abroad: execution before a s.2 officer, a metes-and-bounds description of the Galle land, the volume and folio of its prior registration, and the certified passport and identity copies. If the instrument omits these the notary in Galle cannot safely act on it.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 28 of 2022; in force well before 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: contain a reference to the volume and folio in which the land or land parcel or condominium parcel relating to the transaction, is registered, in the case of a land or land parcel or condominium parcel with prior registration; and (e) be accompanied with a copy of the bio page of the passport of the grantor signed by such grantor and a copy of the bio page of the passport, National Identity Card or driving license of the attorney of such power of attorney certified by a notary public.
why_relevant: The remaining two requirements for a power of attorney executed abroad: the prior registration reference for the Galle land, and the signed passport bio page of the grantor together with certified identity documents of the attorney.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 28 of 2022; in force before 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: (a) Every power of attorney executed in Sri Lanka or any other country shall be registered with the Registrar General. (b) Every power of attorney holder (hereinafter referred to as the "attorney") shall submit his power of attorney for registration, if it is executed in Sri Lanka within one month and if it is executed outside Sri Lanka within three months, from the date of execution of the power of attorney together with – (i) a copy thereof certified by a notary public to be a true copy; and (ii) an affidavit made as specified in Schedule I hereto.
why_relevant: Registration is compulsory and time-limited. Wimala's power of attorney will be executed outside Sri Lanka, so her attorney must lodge it with the Registrar-General within three months of execution, with a notarially certified copy and the Schedule I affidavit. This also creates the register the attesting notary must search.
temporal_note: Section 3 was replaced by the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022; the replacement text is the law at 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: A power of attorney other than a power of attorney executed by a State institution shall be valid, only for a period of five years from the date of execution, unless the period of validity of such power of attorney is specified in such power of attorney or until such power of attorney is revoked or cancelled in accordance with the provisions of section 4.
why_relevant: Practical advice point: the authorisation Wimala grants will lapse five years from execution unless it states its own period, so the deed must be executed while it is still current.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 28 of 2022; in force before 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: Every notary public who attests a deed or instrument in terms of the Notaries Ordinance in respect of a transaction referred to in section 3A of this Act, shall – (a) examine the relevant volumes and folios in the Registrar General's department; (b) be satisfied that the power of attorney has not been revoked or cancelled and shall state such fact in his attestation
why_relevant: Explains what the notary in Galle must do before attesting a deed signed by Wimala's attorney, and why the power of attorney must be registered first - the notary has to be able to find it and certify in the attestation that it is unrevoked.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 28 of 2022; in force before 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: where a deed or instrument is signed by an attorney, such attorney shall submit to the notary an affidavit affirming that the Power of Attorney is genuine and in force and the grantor is alive when executing such deed or instrument;
why_relevant: A further condition on the attorney route: the person signing for Wimala must give the notary an affidavit that the power is genuine, in force, and that Wimala is alive at the date of the deed.
temporal_note: This rule was inserted into section 31 by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 and section 31 was further amended by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024; both precede 2025-10.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but the label "rule (16)(c)" is wrong: Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(5) refers to this block as "rule (15A)", so the citation is Notaries Ordinance s.31, rule (15A)(c).

relevant_excerpt: If he attest any deed or instrument executed before him by means of an attorney, he shall preserve a true copy of the power of attorney with his protocol, and shall forward a like copy with the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands.
why_relevant: Completes the paper trail: the notary keeps a true copy of the power of attorney with the protocol and sends a copy with the duplicate to the Land Registry, so Wimala should expect to supply an additional certified copy.
temporal_note: Long-standing rule in section 31; not affected by the 2022 or 2024 amendments in a way the corpus records.

relevant_excerpt: Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary in any other written law, the transfer of title of any land situated in Sri Lanka, shall be prohibited if such transfer is- (a) to a foreigner;
why_relevant: Background. A purchaser who is living abroad raises the question whether the transfer is prohibited at all. Because Wimala is a Sri Lankan citizen, the prohibition does not bite and the advice can rest on the execution formalities alone; the provision is recorded so the verifier can see the point was considered rather than missed.
temporal_note: In force from 2014; unaffected by any amendment recorded in the corpus for this section.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument to which at least two witnesses have not subscribed their signatures in letters.
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. The map and the gold answer both say the attorney must sign before the notary and "the two witnesses", but Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2(1)(a) as substituted in 2024 speaks only of "the witnesses" and fixes no number. Rule (8) of Notaries Ordinance s.31 is the provision that supplies the minimum of two witnesses.
temporal_note: Rule (8) of section 31 stands in the consolidated text at 2025-10; the corpus records no amendment to this rule by Act No. 31 of 2022 or Act No. 6 of 2024. Excerpt checked verbatim against 1-1907/s31.

relevant_excerpt: Before any deed or instrument (other than a will or codicil) affecting any interest in land or other immovable property is drawn by him, he shall search or cause to be searched the registers in the land registry to ascertain the state of the title in regard to such land and whether any prior deed affecting any interest in such land has been registered;
why_relevant: This is the express statutory duty to search the land registry before the deed is drawn, which is the first step the notary must take.
temporal_note: Rule (17) was substituted by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16 and further amended by Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3; the consolidated text relied on is in force at 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: he shall obtain from the Registrar of the relevant Land Registry the certified extract of the folio containing the last entry pertaining to such land or immovable property containing the ownership and the registered encumbrances relating to such land or immovable property;
why_relevant: Fixes the form the search must take: a certified folio extract from the relevant Land Registry showing ownership and registered encumbrances.
temporal_note: Inserted in its present form by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16 and amended by Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3; in force at 2025-10.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but the corpus text of rule (17) runs "(a) Before any deed ... registered; (i) he shall obtain ..." with no "(b)" marker, so the subsection label (17)(b)(i) is a reconstruction of the numbering rather than something the corpus shows.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument, other than a will or codicil, affecting land or other immovable property, unless the deed or instrument embodies therin or in a Schedule annexed therto an accurate and clear description of the said land or other property affected thereby, showing its boundaries, extent, situation specifying the district
why_relevant: The deed cannot be attested unless the schedule gives an accurate description with boundaries, extent and administrative situation, so those particulars must be obtained before drafting.
temporal_note: Rule (16) as amended by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16 and Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3; in force at 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: if such property consist of a share of a land or other property, the deed shall state whether it is a divided or undivided share, and the fractional part which it is of the whole. If it be a divided share, such share shall be clearly and accurately defined by its particular boundaries and extent;
why_relevant: Sarath is buying a portion only. A divided share must be defined by its particular boundaries and extent, which requires a survey and plan of the portion before the deed is drafted.
temporal_note: Rule (16)(b) in force at 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any area other than that in which he is authorized to practice, nor in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice nor authenticate or attest any deed or instrument drawn in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice.
why_relevant: The notary is licensed for Colombo. The territorial limit attaches to the place of attestation and to the language, not to the situation of the land, so he may act for Kurunegala land if execution takes place within his area.
temporal_note: Rule (22) unamended in substance and in force at 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which such land shall be situated a copy thereof certified by him as correct
why_relevant: Because the land lies outside the district in which the Colombo notary resides, he must plan for the further duty of transmitting a certified copy to the Registrar of Lands of the district where the land lies.
temporal_note: Rule (29) in force at 2025-10.
verifier_note: Rule (29) is triggered by the land lying in a district other than that in which the attesting notary shall reside, and neither the matter nor the enrichment states where the notary resides; s.9 fixes the location of his office, not his residence, so the trigger is assumed rather than shown.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless he has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided.
why_relevant: The notary must satisfy himself before execution that the stamp duty on the transfer is provided, which requires the value of the portion to be established beforehand.
temporal_note: Rule (6) as substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16; in force at 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless one of the executants to the deed or instrument or the two attesting witnesses be known to notary or by the identity of the executants to a deed or instrument is established by such notary by inspection of the national identity card, bio-page of the passport or the driving licence of such executants;
why_relevant: Identification of vendor and purchaser must be arranged before the deed is drawn so that the names and particulars in the deed are correct.
temporal_note: Rule (9) as amended by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16; in force at 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: It shall be the duty of every notary to endeavour to ascertain the true and full consideration for the execution of any deed, and to insert and set forth the same in such deed.
why_relevant: The notary must ascertain the true and full consideration from the parties before drafting, since it has to be set out in the deed.
temporal_note: Substituted by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.18; in force at 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: to endeavour to ascertain the true legal nature of the transaction between the parties and execute the deed or instrument for the true transaction; and (b) specifically, and expressly explain to the executants the true nature of every deed or instrument before any executant signs such deed or instrument.
why_relevant: Before drafting, the notary must take instructions sufficient to establish that the transaction really is an outright sale and not a disguised mortgage or conditional transfer.
temporal_note: Inserted by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024 s.4; in force from 2024 and therefore applicable at 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: Every appointment to the office of notary shall be by warrant granted by the Minister, and shall specify the area within which, and the language or languages in which, the person appointed is authorized to practice.
why_relevant: Identifies the source of the Colombo notary's territorial and language authority, which rule (22) then confines him to.
temporal_note: In force since 1907 and unamended in substance at 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: Every notary shall be bound to have his office within the area specified in his warrant
why_relevant: Confirms that the notary's office, at which the deed would be executed, must be within the area of his warrant.
temporal_note: In force since 1907; unamended at 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary
why_relevant: Supplies the reason a notarial deed is required at all for a sale of land and frames the notary's role in the transaction.
temporal_note: Substituted by Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Acts No. 30 of 2022 and No. 4 of 2024; the consolidated text is in force at 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: be void as against all parties claiming an adverse interest thereto on valuable consideration by virtue of any subsequent instrument which is duly registered under this Chapter
why_relevant: Explains what the pre-drafting search is directed at: an unregistered instrument loses priority to a later registered one, so the folio search establishes what registered interests bind the portion.
temporal_note: In force since 1927; unamended at 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: If the land consists of a divided portion of a land or allotment, such portion shall be clearly and accurately defined by its particular boundaries and extent.
why_relevant: Registration law imposes the same requirement as notarial rule (16)(b) for a divided portion, reinforcing the need for a survey of the portion before drafting.
temporal_note: Amended by Act No. 50 of 1982; in force at 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: Every Registrar shall refuse to register an instrument, other than a will, which docs not state the particulars required by the foregoing provisions of this section.
why_relevant: Registration will be refused if the description of the portion is deficient, so the description has to be settled before the deed is drawn.
temporal_note: In force at 2025-10. The corpus text carries an obvious typographical error, 'docs' for 'does'.
verifier_note: The excerpt of s.13(5) is verbatim, but s.13(5A) and (5B) qualify it: a refusal may be appealed to the Registrar-General, who may reverse it where the description is sufficient to identify the land with reasonable certainty, so the refusal is not the absolute bar the why_relevant implies.

relevant_excerpt: acquiring or proposing to acquire for valuable consideration from any other person (in this section called the “ transferor”) any interest or benefit in any land may before the execution of the instrument by the transferor with his written consent, or after the execution of the instrument by the transferor without such consent, present for registration a notice (in this Ordinance called a “ priority notice ”) of his intention to register the instrument.
why_relevant: A step open to the notary before execution: register a priority notice to protect the purchaser against an intervening registration between search and registration.
temporal_note: In force since 1927; unamended at 2025-10.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: The transfer of ownership of a tea or rubber estate on or after the appointed day shall, subject to the provisions of subsections (2) and (3), be null and void unless- (a) a certificate of consent of the Board to such transfer has been previously obtained by the transferor, and (b) such transfer is effected in accordance with the conditions, if any, subject to which such consent has been granted.
why_relevant: Read with the 2005 amendment this makes a transfer of a portion of a coconut estate null and void unless the transferor has previously obtained a certificate of consent of the Board, so the notary must verify the certificate before drafting.
temporal_note: In force since the appointed day, 11 December 1957. The corpus holds the Act as enacted; the extension to coconut estates is made by Act No. 20 of 2005 and is recorded in the corpus as a substitution not applied to the stored text.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: Where a certificate of consent to the transfer of ownership of a tea or rubber estate is issued by the Board, such certificate shall be attached to the deed by which such transfer is effected, and the notary attesting such deed shall in his attestation state that such certificate has been issued in respect of such transfer and specify the number, if any, and the date of issue of such certificate.
why_relevant: Places a direct duty on the notary: the certificate must be in his hands to attach to the deed and its number and date must go into the attestation, so it must be obtained before drafting.
temporal_note: In force at 2025-10, read with Act No. 20 of 2005 s.3 for coconut estates.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: means a coconut estate of not less than four hectares in extent which, under the Coconut Development Act, No. 46 of 1971, is or is deemed to be an estate registered under that Act ;
why_relevant: Sets the threshold that decides whether the fragmentation control applies at all: four hectares and registration under the Coconut Development Act. The notary must ascertain the extent of the estate and its registration status.
temporal_note: Definition inserted by Act No. 20 of 2005 s.10(a); in force at 2025-10.
verifier_note: The definition text is verbatim in the corpus, but its operative limb is registration under the Coconut Development Act, No. 46 of 1971, which is not in the corpus, so whether this estate is an estate registered under that Act cannot be checked here; the enrichment fact speaks of registration with the Coconut Cultivation Board, which is not the same thing as the statutory limb.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: with reference to any tea or rubber estate, means the transfer of ownership of such estate or any portion thereof by sale, exchange or gift other than a gift by a testamentary disposition.
why_relevant: Brings the sale of a portion of the estate, and not merely of the whole, within the consent requirement; this is what makes the control bite on Sarath's purchase.
temporal_note: In force at 2025-10; the words 'tea or rubber estate' are to be read as 'tea, rubber or coconut estates' by Act No. 20 of 2005 s.3(1)(c).

formal_title: Tea And Rubber Estates (Control Of Fragmentation) (Amendment)
relevant_excerpt: for the words "tea or rubber estate", of the words "tea, rubber or coconut estates".
why_relevant: This is the provision that extends the fragmentation control in Act No. 2 of 1958 to coconut estates; without it sections 3 and 25 would not touch a coconut estate.
temporal_note: In force since 2005 and therefore applicable at 2025-10.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: Where on an application made to the Board it is decided by the Board to consent to the transfer of ownership of the tea or rubber estate to which such application relates, or the partition by deed of such estate, or the institution of a partition action in respect of such estate, the Secretary of the Board shall prepare four copies of the Board's certificate of such consent
why_relevant: Shows how the consent is applied for and issued, which is what the notary must advise the vendor to obtain before the deed is drawn.
temporal_note: In force at 2025-10.

relevant_excerpt: the maximum extent of agricultural land which may be owned by any person, in this Law referred to as the " ceiling ", shall (a) if such land consists exclusively of paddy land, be twenty-five acres; or (b) if such land does not consist exclusively of paddy land, be fifty acres
why_relevant: A coconut estate is agricultural land, so the notary should check the purchaser's existing agricultural holdings against the fifty acre ceiling before drafting.
temporal_note: Amended by Act No. 39 of 1981; the fifty acre ceiling is in force at 2025-10.
verifier_note: Excerpt verbatim and the fifty acre ceiling is the operative text in the corpus, but the temporal note misattributes it: Act No. 39 of 1981 s.2 amends only subsections (4) and (5) of s.3 and leaves the ceiling in subsection (1) untouched.

relevant_excerpt: Where after the date of commencement of this Law any person becomes the owner of agricultural land in excess of the ceiling, any such land owned by such person in excess of the ceiling shall as from that date- (a) be deemed to vest in the Commission; and (b) be deemed to be held by that person under a statutory lease from the Commission.
why_relevant: Gives the consequence of exceeding the ceiling by purchase: the excess vests in the Commission. This is why the check belongs before drafting.
temporal_note: Amended by Act No. 39 of 1981 and Act No. 14 of 1986; in force at 2025-10.
verifier_note: Excerpt verbatim; note that Act No. 39 of 1981 s.3 works by inserting s.5(2) on marriage and inheritance and leaves s.5(1) as enacted.

relevant_excerpt: Provided that if the parties to the transaction authorize the notary in writing to dispense with the search, the search shall not be compulsory, but he shall before the deed or instrument is tendered for registration write at the head thereof the reference to the previous registration, if any.
why_relevant: The proviso to rule (17) is the express exception to the pre-drafting search duty relied on as the first step: the parties may authorise the notary in writing to dispense with the search, in which case he must instead write the reference to the previous registration at the head of the deed before it is tendered for registration.
temporal_note: Part of rule (17) as it stands in the consolidated text in force at 2025-10.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier: the map states the search duty without its proviso, and a complete statement of the step has to include the written dispensation and the substitute obligation.

relevant_excerpt: When a deed transferring any immovable property is executed or acknowledged before a notary, he shall use his best endeavours to obtain the title deed, if any, of such property, and make an endorsement thereon stating the number and date of the deed executed before him and the nature of the transaction and attach his signature thereto
why_relevant: This is the statutory source for calling for the vendor's title deed, which the gold conclusion lists as a step but which no cited provision supported.
temporal_note: Rule (33) of s.31 in the consolidated text in force at 2025-10.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier to support the examination of the vendor's title deeds step in the conclusion; note the duty is framed around execution or acknowledgment, so it is a step the notary arranges for rather than one the Ordinance in terms places before drafting.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: The Board shall grant its consent- (a) to the transfer of ownership of a tea or rubber estate which does not involve the division of such estate into a number of lots; (b) to the transfer of ownership of a tea or rubber estate which involves the division of such estate into a number of lots
why_relevant: Sarath is buying a portion, so the transfer involves division of the estate into lots and falls under paragraph (b), where consent is not automatic but depends on the conditions in (b)(i) to (iii). The notary advising on the consent step needs this, because it is what decides whether the certificate is likely to issue at all.
temporal_note: In force at 2025-10; read with s.3(1)(c) of Act No. 20 of 2005 for coconut estates.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier: the map treats the certificate of consent as a formality to be produced and never reaches the criteria on which the Board grants or withholds it for a transfer that divides the estate into lots.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: (1) Any person (in this Ordinance called a "caveator") may present for registration a caveat in the prescribed form requiring to be served with notice of the presentation for registration of any instrument affecting the land described in the caveat.
why_relevant: The original test of standing: "any person" could lodge a caveat. It is the text the question contrasts with ("the Registration of Documents Ordinance which is amended"), and it shows what the 2022 substitution changed.
temporal_note: Repealed and substituted by section 2(1) of Act No. 32 of 2022. The corpus copy of the Ordinance is the 1990 consolidation and therefore still carries the pre-2022 wording. Not in force in this form at 2025-10; recorded as background contrast only.

formal_title: Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022
subsection: (1) inserting section 32(1)(a) of the principal enactment
relevant_excerpt: A person (hereinafter referred to as the "caveator") who (i) has a right, title or interest; or (ii) claims to have a right, title or interest, to a land, an undivided land, a land parcel or a condominium parcel (hereinafter in this section referred to as the "land") may present for registration a caveat substantially in Form VIII of the Second Schedule hereto requiring him to be served a notice of the presentation for registration of any instrument affecting such land.
why_relevant: The operative substituted section 32(1)(a). It states who may present a caveat: a person who has, or claims to have, a right, title or interest in the land. Romani's entitlement stands or falls on this provision.
temporal_note: Act No. 32 of 2022 was enacted in 2022 and is in force at the matter reference date 2025-10. Corpus in_force_from_year = 2022; no later amendment to section 32 appears in the corpus (Act No. 18 of 2024 does not touch section 32).

formal_title: Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022
subsection: (1) inserting section 32(1)(c)(i) of the principal enactment
relevant_excerpt: "caveator" includes a body of persons, a beneficiary under any trust affecting a land, the lawful guardian or the next friend of a minor or of a person of unsound mind or mentally deficient person, an attorney of a person, a judgement creditor, an executor or an administrator of an estate of a deceased, or a legal heir, or an intended purchaser who has entered into an agreement with the owner of a land or a developer of a land
why_relevant: The extended definition of "caveator". It answers the second limb of the question directly by listing the classes of person who may lodge a caveat beyond the registered owner, and it covers an attorney acting for an owner who is abroad.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 32 of 2022, in force at 2025-10.

formal_title: Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022
subsection: (1) inserting section 32(1)(b)(i) of the principal enactment
relevant_excerpt: Every caveat presented for registration shall- (i) be in duplicate and accompanied by an affidavit of the caveator together with a certificate issued by an Attorney-at-law substantiating the right, title or interest in the land or claims to a right, title or interest in the land of the caveator;
why_relevant: Standing alone is not enough: the substituted section makes the caveat conditional on duplicate lodgement, an affidavit and an attorney-at-law's certificate substantiating the claimed right, title or interest. Removing it would leave the answer stating an unconditional right.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 32 of 2022, in force at 2025-10.

formal_title: Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022
subsection: (1) inserting section 32(1)(b)(iv) of the principal enactment
relevant_excerpt: contain the name, signature and the National Identity Card number or the passport number or the driving licence number and address of the caveator in Sri Lanka at which notices relating to the caveat shall be served, the date of the caveat, the names and addresses of the persons to whom the notice of the caveat shall be sent where the caveator is not the owner, the right, title or interest in the land claimed by the caveator, grounds in support of the claim and the description of the land
why_relevant: Prescribes the mandatory contents, including an address of the caveator in Sri Lanka for service. This is the condition that bites on a caveator who is leaving the country, so it is necessary to a complete answer for Romani.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 32 of 2022, in force at 2025-10.

formal_title: Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022
subsection: (1) inserting section 32(1)(c)(iii) of the principal enactment
relevant_excerpt: "interest" includes an interest arising from an unregistered deed or instrument relating to a land which is incapable of immediate registration, a trust, an inheritance either by testate or intestate succession, instruments relating to a mortgage or an agreement to sell, co-ownership, an ownership arising from a condominium parcel or the estate of a minor, or of a person of unsound mind or mentally deficient person.
why_relevant: Defines "interest" for the standing test, showing how far short of full ownership a caveator may be. It supports the second limb of the question but is not needed for Romani, who is an owner.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 32 of 2022, in force at 2025-10.
