formal_title: Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022
subsection: (1) inserting section 32(1)(b)(iii) of the principal enactment
relevant_excerpt: be accompanied by a certified copy of the original of the Power of Attorney duly registered with the Registrar General or the Registrar of the relevant Land Registry or the Registrar of Title (hereinafter in this section referred to as the "Registrar") where the caveator is a holder of a Power of Attorney
why_relevant: Where the caveat is lodged by an attorney rather than the owner personally, a certified copy of a duly registered power of attorney must accompany it. Relevant because Romani proposes to act through an attorney once she is abroad.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 32 of 2022, in force at 2025-10.

formal_title: Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022
subsection: (3) substituting section 32(3) of the principal enactment
relevant_excerpt: by the repeal of subsection (3) thereof and the substitution therefor of the following subsection: - (3) A caveat shall be in force for a maximum period of two years.
why_relevant: Fixes the life of a caveat at two years. Material practical advice for a client who will be out of the country for longer, but not part of the standing test.
temporal_note: Substituted by Act No. 32 of 2022; replaces the earlier period tied to the fee paid. In force at 2025-10.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: (2) The Registrar shall on receiving a caveat register it in the same manner as other instruments, but shall retain the caveat.
why_relevant: The registration duty that follows a properly lodged caveat, and part of the surviving framework of section 32 that the 2022 Act left untouched. Explains what filing actually achieves.
temporal_note: Subsection (2) was not amended by Act No. 32 of 2022 and remains in force at 2025-10. Note that subsections (1), (3), (4) and (5) of the same corpus section carry pre-2022 text.

formal_title: Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022
subsection: (5) substituting words in section 32(5) of the principal enactment
relevant_excerpt: in subsection (5) thereof, by the substitution for the words "a competent court within thirty days" of the words "a competent court within sixty days".
why_relevant: Extends to sixty days the window in which a caveator who receives notice must commence action to have the offending instrument rectified or cancelled. Explains the protective value of the caveat Romani wants.
temporal_note: Substituted by Act No. 32 of 2022; the corpus consolidation of section 32(5) still shows 'thirty days'. In force at 2025-10.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: In this Ordinance, unless the context otherwise requires, " land " includes things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth and any estate or interest in land, and a mortgage of or charge on land.
why_relevant: The Ordinance definition of "land", which brings Romani's Battaramulla allotment and the house on it within the subject matter of a caveat.
temporal_note: Unamended since 1927 apart from the repeal of section 2A by Law No. 4 of 1974; in force at 2025-10.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and the section is in force, but the temporal note is wrong in form: the words about section 2A are a consolidation footnote carried in the body of section 3, not an amendment of section 3, which is itself unamended.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: (1) An instrument may be presented for registration by" (a) any person executing the instrument; (b) any person claiming any interest or benefit thereunder; (c) any person having any interest in or charge on any property affected thereby; or (d) the agent of any such person or a attorney-at-law or notary acting on behalf of any such person.
why_relevant: Confirms that a notary may present an instrument for registration on behalf of an entitled person, which is how the notary consulted by Romani would lodge the papers.
temporal_note: Unamended in the corpus text; in force at 2025-10.
verifier_note: Wording verbatim, but the role is inferential rather than confirmatory: section 25 defines "instrument" for that Chapter as an instrument affecting land or a pledge, mortgage or bill of sale, which does not plainly cover a caveat, so the notary route is better supported by Form VIII as substituted by section 5(1) of Act No. 32 of 2022 (PROV-M015-901), which is signed by the caveator, his Attorney-at-Law or notary, or his attorney. Demoted to supporting weight.

formal_title: Powers of Attorney Ordinance No. 4 of 1902
relevant_excerpt: (a) Every power of attorney executed in Sri Lanka or any other country shall be registered with the Registrar General.
why_relevant: A power of attorney relied on by an attorney-caveator must be registered. Supports the route open to Romani after she leaves the country.
temporal_note: Section 3 was repealed and substituted by section 3 of Act No. 28 of 2022; the substituted text is what the corpus carries and it is in force at 2025-10.
verifier_note: Wording verbatim and in force, but the citation should be section 3(1)(a): the corpus body of 4-1902/s3 drops the "(1)" marker while its subsection (2) refers back to the power of attorney referred to in subsection (1).

formal_title: Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022
subsection: (2) inserting section 33(1)(a) of the principal enactment
relevant_excerpt: A caveat may be withdrawn or cancelled, as the case may be, at the request in writing - (i) by the caveator; (ii) by an attorney; (iii) upon the death of a caveator, by an executor, administrator, or a legal heir;
why_relevant: Shows the mirror image of the standing question: who may take a caveat off the register. Context only for this question.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 32 of 2022, in force at 2025-10.
verifier_note: Wording verbatim, but the subsection label is wrong: section 3(2) of Act No. 32 of 2022 adds a new subsection immediately after section 33(1) whose paragraphs are lettered (a) and (b); it does not insert a "section 33(1)(a)". Section 3(1) of the same Act also deletes the word caveat from section 33(1), so withdrawal of a caveat now runs only through the new subsection.

formal_title: Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022
subsection: (1) substituting Form VIII of the Second Schedule to the principal enactment
relevant_excerpt: by the repeal of Form VIII thereof, and the substitution therefor, of the following new Form:- Take notice that, I, ............ (full name and the address of the caveator) bearing (NIC/passport/ driving licence) no.................. require to be served with notice of the presentation for registration of any instrument affecting land........ (owned by me / owned by other- specify the right/ title/ or interest) referred to in the Schedule hereto. And I further declare that I present this caveat in my behalf/ in behalf of ........................ (where the caveator is not the owner) on the following ground/s. Title under deed no............. Under the last will of............ Other (specify) ........................................... And I appoint (the address in Sri Lanka) as the place at which notices relating hereto shall be sent. ............................ (Signature of the caveator/his Attorney-at-Law or notary/attorney)
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. Section 32(1)(a) as substituted requires the caveat to be substantially in Form VIII of the Second Schedule, and the gold answer's conclusion turns on lodging in Form VIII, but no provision in the map carried the Form. The substituted Form also shows on its face that it may be signed by the caveator's Attorney-at-Law or notary or attorney, which is the direct authority for the notary limb of the answer that PROV-M015-012 could only reach by inference.
temporal_note: Substituted by section 5(1) of Act No. 32 of 2022; in force at 2025-10. Act No. 18 of 2024 amends only the First Schedule (its section 8), not Form VIII.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked verbatim against 32-2022/s5.

formal_title: Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022
subsection: (2) inserting section 32(1A) of the principal enactment
relevant_excerpt: (1A) The Registrar, on being satisfied that all required documents and information referred to in paragraph (b) of subsection (1) are provided by the caveator, shall acknowledge the receipt of such caveat and record the prescribed particulars referred to in subsection (1) of section 27.
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. This is the provision that makes the paragraph (b) requirements operative: acceptance of the caveat depends on the Registrar being satisfied that all of them are met. The map relied on that step in the enrichment counterfactual for FACT-M015-Q01-002 and in CL-M015-Q01-010 without citing any provision for it.
temporal_note: Inserted by section 2(2) of Act No. 32 of 2022; in force at 2025-10.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked verbatim against 32-2022/s2.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: (5) If, while a caveat is in force, an instrument affecting the land described in the caveat is presented for registration, and in an action commenced by the caveator in a competent court within thirty days from posting of the notice required by subsection (4) it is proved to the satisfaction of the court that the instrument presented for registration is or was at the time of registration void or voidable by the caveator or fraudulent as against him or in derogation of his lawful rights the court may order the instrument to be rectified or cancelled as may be necessary to preserve the rights of the caveator, and may order the necessary correction to be made in the register.
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. CL-M015-Q01-008 asserts a sixty-day window running from the posting of the notice, but PROV-M015-010 carries only the amending words substituting sixty days for thirty days and PROV-M015-009 quotes only subsection (2); nothing in the map carried the host subsection that supplies the trigger, the running point and the relief.
temporal_note: The corpus copy is the 1990 consolidation and still reads thirty days. Read with section 2(5) of Act No. 32 of 2022 (PROV-M015-010), the period is sixty days at 2025-10; the rest of the subsection is unamended.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked verbatim against 23-1927/s32. The quoted thirty days is superseded, see temporal_note.

formal_title: Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022
subsection: (1) inserting section 32(1)(b)(ii) of the principal enactment
relevant_excerpt: be accompanied by such number of copies of the notice set out in Form X of the Second Schedule hereto together with stamped envelopes, to be served on the owners of the land whose names and addresses are given in the relevant volume and folio in which such land is registered, where the caveator is not the owner
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. CL-M015-Q01-012 and the gold answer say the Form X notices to other owners do not arise because Romani is the owner, and the gold answer cites section 32(1)(b)(ii) by number, but no provision in the map carried it.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: If, while a caveat is in force, an instrument affecting the land described in the caveat is presented for registration, and in an action commenced by the caveator in a competent court within thirty days from posting of the notice required by subsection (4) it is proved to the satisfaction of the court that the instrument presented for registration is or was at the time of registration void or voidable by the caveator or fraudulent as against him or in derogation of his lawful rights the court may order the instrument to be rectified or cancelled
why_relevant: This is the provision that fixes the time limit the question asks about: the caveator must commence the action in a competent court within the stated number of days from the posting of the notice of presentation.
temporal_note: In force since 1927. The corpus text is the 1990 consolidation and still reads 'thirty days'; that figure was replaced by 'sixty days' by Act No. 32 of 2022, s.2(5), so at the matter date (2025-10) subsection (5) must be read with sixty days substituted. The rest of the subsection is unchanged.

formal_title: Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022
relevant_excerpt: (5) in subsection (5) thereof, by the substitution for the words "a competent court within thirty days" of the words "a competent court within sixty days".
why_relevant: Supplies the number the question asks for. It substitutes sixty days for thirty days in section 32(5) of the Ordinance, so a caveator notified in 2025 has sixty days, not thirty.
temporal_note: Enacted 2022, before the October 2025 matter date. The corpus copy carries no commencement section (32-2022/s1 is the short title only), so the amendment is taken to operate from certification in 2022; see corpus_gaps.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim in 32-2022/s2 and the substitution of sixty for thirty days is exactly as stated, but the corpus copy of Act No. 32 of 2022 has no date-of-operation clause (s 1 is short title only, unlike 21-2013/s1 and 18-2024/s1 which are headed 'Short title and date of operation'), so operation before June 2025 is inferred from the absence of a deferred-commencement clause and the corpus in_force_from_year of 2022, not proved from the corpus.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: (4) The notice to be given to the caveator shall be in the prescribed form and shall be sent by registered letter to the address mentioned in the caveat.
why_relevant: Identifies the notice from whose posting the period runs. Without it the time limit in subsection (5) has no starting point, so the answer cannot be stated without it.
temporal_note: In force since 1927; the opening words were replaced by Act No. 32 of 2022, s.2(4), which changed the description of the notice but not the fact that a notice is given to the caveator and posted to the address in the caveat.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim in the 1990 consolidation but is the pre-2022 text: 32-2022/s2(4) replaced the opening words 'The notice to be given to the caveator shall be in the prescribed form', so only the surviving tail 'and shall be sent by registered letter to the address mentioned in the caveat' is the operative support at the matter date.

formal_title: Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022
relevant_excerpt: (4) in subsection (4) thereof, by the substitution for the words "The notice to be given to the caveator shall be in the prescribed form", of the words and figures "Where an instrument affecting the same land described in the caveat has been subsequently presented for registration, a notice shall be given to the caveator in Form XI of the Second Schedule hereto"

temporal_note: Enacted 2022, before the matter date; same commencement caveat as PROV-M016-002.

formal_title: Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 32 of 2022
relevant_excerpt: (3) by the repeal of subsection (3) thereof and the substitution therefor of the following subsection: - (3) A caveat shall be in force for a maximum period of two years.
why_relevant: Background only: it fixes the maximum currency of a caveat, which is what makes the scenario premise that the caveat was still in force when the instrument was presented a coherent one.
temporal_note: Enacted 2022, before the matter date; replaces the earlier rule that the caveat ran for the period specified in it.

relevant_excerpt: there shall be charged a duty (hereinafter to be called "stamp duty") at such rate as the Minister may determine by Order published in the Gazette on every "specified instrument"- (a) executed, drawn or presented in Sri Lanka
why_relevant: The charging provision for stamp duty on the lease agreement, an instrument to be executed in Sri Lanka. It is also the provision that shows why the amount cannot be computed from the Act: the rate is not in the Act, it is set by Ministerial Order in the Gazette.
temporal_note: In force from 2006 with no amendment events recorded on this section, so the same text applies at the stated 2020 execution and at the October 2025 reference date.

relevant_excerpt: (h) a promissory note; (i) a lease or hire of any property; (j) a receipt or discharge given for any money or other property;
why_relevant: Defines "specified instrument" for the purposes of section 3 and brings a lease of any property within the charge. Without it the lease between Mala and Sheela is not shown to be chargeable at all.
temporal_note: In force from 2006, no amendment events recorded on this section.

relevant_excerpt: in cases where there is an agreement to the contrary, stamp duty shall be payable:- (a) in the case of a policy of insurance, by the person effecting the insurance; (b) in the case of a transfer or assignment of any share, by the transferee or assignee of such share; (c) in the case of a lease, by the lessee;
why_relevant: Identifies Sheela, as lessee, as the person liable for the stamp duty on the lease, subject to any agreement to the contrary between the parties.
temporal_note: In force from 2006; amended in 2008 by Act No. 10 of 2008 s.2, which inserted paragraphs (dd) and (ddd). That amendment predates both the 2020 execution and the October 2025 reference date, and paragraph (c) on leases is unaffected by it.

relevant_excerpt: Stamp duty payable on any specified instrument relating to a mortgage or lease of any immovable property may be paid, prior to, or at the time of, the execution of the specified instrument, to a prescribed bank.
why_relevant: Governs how and when the duty on a lease of immovable property is paid and evidenced. It bears on the practical answer to a 'stamp duty payable' question even though it does not supply the rate.
temporal_note: Substituted in 2008 by Act No. 10 of 2008 s.3; the substituted text is the one in force at both the 2020 execution and the October 2025 reference date.

relevant_excerpt: the provisions of the Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982, relating to the Imposition of Stamp Duty (other than any instrument relating to the transfer of immovable property, the transfer of motor vehicles or documents filed in Court), Exemptions and any other provision in the aforesaid Act, shall, in so far as the same are inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, have no operation
why_relevant: Settles which of the two stamp duty statutes in the corpus governs a lease executed after 2006: the imposition provisions of the 1982 Act give way to Act No. 12 of 2006, so the rate must be found in an Order under section 3 of the 2006 Act.
temporal_note: In force from 2006, no amendment events recorded on this section.

relevant_excerpt: or for establishing any security, interest, or incumbrance affecting land or other immovable property (other than a lease at will, or for any period not exceeding one month)
why_relevant: A lease of a house for two years is outside the one-month exclusion, so the agreement must be in writing and notarially executed and attested. This fixes the form of the instrument that will carry the covenants asked for in Q03, and the instrument on which stamp duty is charged.
temporal_note: Section 2 carries amendment events in 1947, 2022 and 2024. The 2022 and 2024 amendments concern the thumb impression and transfer deed requirements in subsections (1) and (2); the exclusion of leases at will or for not more than one month relied on here is long-standing. The 2020 execution predates the 2022 and 2024 amendments, so a verifier should confirm which text governs the instrument as against the October 2025 reference date.

relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property, and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object, or for establishing any security, interest, or incumbrance affecting land or other immovable property (other than a lease at will, or for any period not exceeding one month)
why_relevant: Fixes the scope question. A two-year lease of the Colombo house is an agreement establishing an interest affecting immovable property, and the only leases carved out are a lease at will or a lease for a period not exceeding one month. The proposed lease therefore falls inside section 2 and cannot be made by an informal writing.
temporal_note: Section 2 has been in force since 1840; the consolidated text carries amendment events by Act No. 60 of 1947, Act No. 30 of 2022 and Act No. 4 of 2024, all before the October 2025 reference date. The lease is still only intended, so no earlier version can be in issue.

relevant_excerpt: the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary
why_relevant: This is the provision that makes execution by an attorney possible at all: the deed may be signed either by the executant herself or by 'any person duly authorised by such executant'. It also states the formality that any route Mala chooses must satisfy, namely signature before two witnesses and a licensed notary, all present together, and notarial attestation.
temporal_note: Present text is the consolidated text as at 2024, in force at the October 2025 reference date.

relevant_excerpt: means any written power or authority other than that given to an attorney at law for the purpose of appearing as an attorney at law on behalf of such person, given by one person to another, to represent him, to perform any work, do any act, or carry on any trade or business, and - (a) if it is executed in Sri Lanka, executed before two witnesses and attested by a notary public
why_relevant: Defines the instrument by which one person may be 'duly authorised' under Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2(1)(a). It also shows that a power of attorney is an authority to do the acts it specifies, which is why the acts covered by the 2017 instrument matter, and it sets the execution formality for a fresh power granted by Mala while she is still in Sri Lanka.
temporal_note: The definition was repealed and substituted by Act No. 28 of 2022 s.2 and further amended by Act No. 3 of 2024 s.2. The text quoted is the version in force at October 2025. The 2017 instrument was executed under the earlier definition, which is not in the corpus, so its formal validity cannot be tested against the text quoted here.

relevant_excerpt: (b) if it is executed outside Sri Lanka, executed before an Ambassador, or a High Commissioner, or a Diplomatic Officer or a Consular Officer within the meaning of the Consular Functions Act, No. 4 of 1981 or a person who is authorized to attest such power of attorney according to the law of that country
why_relevant: Gives Mala a route if she has already left for Australia: she can execute a power of attorney there before the Sri Lankan High Commission or a consular officer, or before a person authorised to attest such a power under Australian law.
temporal_note: Paragraph (b) as substituted by Act No. 3 of 2024 s.2, in force before the October 2025 reference date.

relevant_excerpt: (1) A power of attorney granted to be used for the purpose of a transaction which falls within the scope of section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance (Chapter 70) shall be executed subject to the provisions specified in subsection (2) or (3), as the case may be.
why_relevant: Links the two enactments. Because the two-year lease falls within Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2, any power of attorney used to execute it must satisfy the additional requirements of s.3A(2) if granted in Sri Lanka, or s.3A(3) if granted abroad, including a description of the land by metes and bounds, the volume and folio of prior registration, the grantor's thumb impression, and certified copies of the identity documents of grantor and attorney.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 28 of 2022 s.4, in force from 2022 and so applicable at the October 2025 reference date. It was not in force in 2017 when the Special Power of Attorney to sell was granted, so the 2017 instrument cannot have been drawn to comply with it.

relevant_excerpt: (a) Every power of attorney executed in Sri Lanka or any other country shall be registered with the Registrar General. (b) Every power of attorney holder (hereinafter referred to as the "attorney") shall submit his power of attorney for registration, if it is executed in Sri Lanka within one month and if it is executed outside Sri Lanka within three months, from the date of execution of the power of attorney
why_relevant: Any power of attorney Mala grants, whether here or in Australia, must be registered with the Registrar General, and the attorney must submit it within one month of execution in Sri Lanka or three months if executed abroad, with a notary-certified copy and the Schedule I affidavit. This is a step in the advice on how to execute the lease in Mala's absence.
temporal_note: Section 3 was repealed and substituted by Act No. 28 of 2022 s.3; the substituted text is in force at October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: A power of attorney other than a power of attorney executed by a State institution shall be valid, only for a period of five years from the date of execution, unless the period of validity of such power of attorney is specified in such power of attorney or until such power of attorney is revoked or cancelled in accordance with the provisions of section 4.
why_relevant: Raises a second and independent obstacle to using the 2017 instrument in or after October 2025: unless that instrument specified its own period of validity, a five-year limit measured from the date of execution would have run out in 2022. It also tells Mala that a fresh power will itself lapse after five years unless it states a period.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 28 of 2022 s.4, in force from 2022. Whether it applies to an instrument executed in 2017, and if so from what date the five years run, is not settled by anything in the corpus; see corpus_gaps.

relevant_excerpt: every power of attorney executed prior to the date of commencement of this Act which has been registered under the provisions of section 3 of the principal enactment and has not been revoked or cancelled on or prior to the date of commencement of this Act, shall, continue to be valid and effectual until revoked or cancelled under section 4 of this Act
why_relevant: The transitional rule for instruments granted before the 2022 amendment, which is the class the 2017 Special Power of Attorney falls into. A pre-2022 power that was already registered continues to be valid and effectual until revoked or cancelled; one that was not registered had to be submitted within six months of commencement and is deemed null and void if it was not. Whether the 2017 instrument survives therefore depends on facts about its registration that the scenario does not give.
temporal_note: Enacted 2022; the six-month window it opens closed in 2023, well before the October 2025 reference date.

relevant_excerpt: Every notary public who attests a deed or instrument in terms of the Notaries Ordinance in respect of a transaction referred to in section 3A of this Act, shall
why_relevant: The attesting notary must examine the relevant volumes and folios at the Registrar General's department, satisfy himself that the power of attorney has not been revoked or cancelled, state that fact in the attestation, and retain identity documents and a copy of the power. This is a practical check the notary will apply to whichever power Visaka produces.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 28 of 2022 s.4, in force from 2022 and applicable at October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: where a deed or instrument is signed by an attorney, such attorney shall submit to the notary an affidavit affirming that the Power of Attorney is genuine and in force and the grantor is alive when executing such deed or instrument
why_relevant: If Visaka signs the lease as attorney she must give the notary an affidavit that the power is genuine and in force and that Mala is alive at the time of execution. She cannot swear that the power is 'in force' for a leasing transaction if the power on its face authorises only a sale, which is why this rule bears directly on the first limb of the question.
temporal_note: Rule (16) as inserted or substituted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 and further amended by Act No. 6 of 2024; the quoted text is in force at October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: If he attest any deed or instrument executed before him by means of an attorney, he shall preserve a true copy of the power of attorney with his protocol, and shall forward a like copy with the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands.
why_relevant: Completes the procedural picture for execution by an attorney: the notary keeps a certified copy of the power with his protocol and sends a copy with the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands, so the power itself becomes part of the notarial and registry record of the lease.
temporal_note: Rule (30) as amended by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3, in force at October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: (22) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any area other than that in which he is authorized to practice, nor in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice
why_relevant: This is the territorial bar that creates the problem. The notary instructed holds a licence to practise in Colombo, so he cannot lawfully attest the signature of the co-owner who is in Tangalle by travelling there; any solution must work around this rule rather than through it.
temporal_note: Rule (22) of section 31 is part of the Ordinance as enacted in 1907 and was not touched by the 2011, 2022 or 2024 amending Acts recorded against section 31. In force at October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: (12) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless the person executing the same and the witnesses shall have signed the same in his presence and in the presence of one another, and unless he shall have signed the same in the presence of the executant and of the attesting witnesses.
why_relevant: Fixes what a valid signing event requires: the executant and the witnesses must sign in the presence of the attesting notary and of one another. It is why the Tangalle co-owner cannot simply post her signature to Colombo, and why whichever notary takes her signature must be physically with her.
temporal_note: Original 1907 rule; no amendment event recorded against it. In force at October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: (25) Where any deed or instrument is executed or acknowledged before more than one notary- (a) the notary who first attests such deed or instrument shall comply with all the requirements of rule (20), and every other notary attesting such deed or instrument shall comply with the requirements of paragraphs (a) to (e) of the aforesaid rule
why_relevant: The central enabling provision. It shows that one and the same deed may be executed before more than one notary, which allows the three Colombo parties to sign before the Colombo notary and the Tangalle party to sign before a notary licensed for the area in which she is, and it sets out how each notary attests and keeps a protocol.
temporal_note: Rule (25) was restructured by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 47 of 2011 s.3 and stands in the consolidated text relied on. In force well before October 2025.
verifier_note: Rule (25)(a) confirmed verbatim; paragraphs (b) and (c) of the same rule, on which the answer also relies, are added by the verifier as PROV-M020-902.

relevant_excerpt: (2) In the case of any deed or instrument which is to be executed by two or more parties, both or all of whom, as the case may be, do not sign the deed or instrument at the same time and place-
why_relevant: Confirms that the Ordinance contemplates a multi-party deed whose parties do not all sign at the same time and place, and adjusts the operation of rules (6), (7), (18), (19), (20), (23) and (25) accordingly. Without it the staggered signing of the partition deed would have no statutory footing.
temporal_note: Original 1907 section, no recorded amendment events. In force at October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary
why_relevant: The deed of partition affects immovable property, so its validity depends on this section. It supplies both the strict requirement (every executant signs before a licensed notary and witnesses) and the opening for the alternative route, since it expressly allows signature by a person duly authorised by the executant.
temporal_note: Section 2 in its present form reflects amendments by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 30 of 2022 and No. 4 of 2024, both in force before October 2025.
verifier_note: Wording confirmed, but section 2(1) is expressed by reference to a sale, purchase, transfer, assignment or mortgage and to agreements affecting land and does not name a deed of partition, and other corpus statutes (Stamp Duty Act s.5(11); Western Province Financial Statute s.106) treat a deed of partition of land held in common as distinct from a transfer, so the premise that the section governs this deed rests on characterisation rather than on the words of the section.

relevant_excerpt: a warrant authorizing him to practice as notary in the language in which he has passed the examination in conveyancing, within the judicial zone in which he resides
why_relevant: Supplies the content of the area referred to in rule (22): the warrant of an attorney-at-law notary is confined to the judicial zone in which he resides. It is what makes the Colombo licence a limit rather than a description.
temporal_note: Section 3 was replaced by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.2; the replacement text is quoted and was in force before October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: Every warrant issued to a notary under the provisions of section 3* or section 4* authorizing him to practice as a notary in any judicial division in which he resides, shall be deemed to authorize him to practice as a notary in the judicial zone in which he resides.
why_relevant: Widens an older division-based warrant to the whole judicial zone. It matters because it fixes the outer limit of the Colombo notary's authority: the zone, and no further. It does not reach a property or a party in Tangalle.
temporal_note: Inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Law No. 20 of 1976 s.4; in force from 1976.
verifier_note: Wording confirmed, but section 4A operates only on a warrant issued under section 3 or section 4 for a judicial division, and section 3 as substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022 already grants a zone warrant, so for a warrant issued at the matter date section 4A is of historic effect and is supporting rather than load-bearing.

relevant_excerpt: (ii) where any such deed or instrument is not signed by all the parties thereto before the expiry of a period of three months from the date on which it is first signed by one of such parties
why_relevant: Puts a practical outer limit on the staggered-signing route: if the deed is not signed by all parties within three months of the first signature, the notary may be required to deliver the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands. It shapes the advice on timing.
temporal_note: Part of rule (27) as it stands in the consolidated text; no amendment event recorded against this sub-paragraph. In force at October 2025.
verifier_note: Wording confirmed, but the corpus text carries this group without the rule (26), rule (27) and paragraph (c) labels, and the provision imposes no three-month deadline: it obliges the notary to deliver the duplicate only if called upon by written notice, and the duplicate is returnable on demand within two years for completion of the deed.

relevant_excerpt: (28) Where any deed or instrument other than a will or codicil shall be executed or acknowledged by two or more parties before more than one notary, the duplicate of such deed or instrument shall be delivered or transmitted by the notary who first attests such deed or instrument to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which he resides
why_relevant: Allocates the duty to transmit the duplicate where two notaries attest the same deed, so the advice can say which notary carries the post-execution obligation and that the second notary need not duplicate it.
temporal_note: Consolidated text; no amendment event recorded against rule (28). In force at October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which such land shall be situated a copy thereof certified by him as correct, together with a list in duplicate in the Form F 1 in the Second Schedule
why_relevant: The land lies in a district other than that in which the Colombo notary resides, so a certified copy must also go to the Registrar of Lands for the district in which the Tangalle land is situated. It confirms that the Ordinance already anticipates a notary attesting a deed about land outside his own district.
temporal_note: Consolidated text; no amendment event recorded against rule (29). In force at October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: means any written power or authority other than that given to an attorney at law for the purpose of appearing as an attorney at law on behalf of such person, given by one person to another, to represent him, to perform any work, do any act, or carry on any trade or business, and - (a) if it is executed in Sri Lanka, executed before two witnesses and attested by a notary public
why_relevant: Definition of a power of attorney. The alternative route turns on this defined term: the person duly authorised under the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance must hold an instrument answering this definition, which itself has to be executed before two witnesses and attested by a notary.
temporal_note: Section 2 reflects amendments up to the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 3 of 2024; in force before October 2025.
verifier_note: The dropped lemma is resolved from the corpus row's defined_terms, which lists attorney, power of attorney and Registrar General in the order in which the three limbs appear, so the quoted words are the definition of power of attorney.

relevant_excerpt: (2) If a power of attorney specified in subsection (1) is executed in Sri Lanka, it shall - (a) be duly attested by a notary public in accordance with the Notaries Ordinance (Chapter 107) and the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance;
why_relevant: A power of attorney used for a transaction within section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, which a deed of partition of land is, must satisfy this section: notarial attestation, a description of the land with metes and bounds and extent, the registration reference, the grantor's thumb impression and identity copies. It sets the conditions the Tangalle party's authority would have to meet.
temporal_note: Section 3A was inserted in 2022 (Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022) and is recorded in the corpus as in force from 2022, before October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: shall submit his power of attorney for registration, if it is executed in Sri Lanka within one month and if it is executed outside Sri Lanka within three months, from the date of execution of the power of attorney
why_relevant: Registration of the power of attorney with the Registrar-General within one month of execution. Relevant to whether the attorney route can be completed in time and in order.
temporal_note: Section 3 reflects the 2022 amendment; in force before October 2025.
verifier_note: Wording confirmed but the subsection is section 3(1)(b), not section 3(1) as a whole; paragraph (a) of the same subsection carries the general obligation to register.

relevant_excerpt: (b) be satisfied that the power of attorney has not been revoked or cancelled and shall state such fact in his attestation
why_relevant: If the Tangalle party signs through an attorney, the notary attesting the partition deed must check the registers and state in the attestation that the power is unrevoked. It is a step the answer has to name for the attorney route to be practicable advice.
temporal_note: Inserted in 2022; corpus records in force from 2022, before October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: (30) If he attest any deed or instrument executed before him by means of an attorney, he shall preserve a true copy of the power of attorney with his protocol, and shall forward a like copy with the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands.
why_relevant: The notarial record-keeping obligation that attaches when a party signs through an attorney, completing the attorney route.
temporal_note: Consolidated text; no amendment event recorded against rule (30). In force at October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: (c) where a deed or instrument is signed by an attorney, such attorney shall submit to the notary an affidavit affirming that the Power of Attorney is genuine and in force and the grantor is alive when executing such deed or instrument;
why_relevant: A further condition on the attorney route added by recent amendment: the attorney must give the notary an affidavit that the power is genuine, in force and the grantor alive at execution.
temporal_note: This paragraph sits in the group inserted into section 31 by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 and amended by No. 6 of 2024; in force before October 2025. The corpus text does not carry a rule number for this group, which follows rule (15); it is cited here as rule (15A)(c) and the numbering should be checked against the printed amendment.
verifier_note: Wording confirmed verbatim, but the corpus carries this paragraph in an unnumbered group immediately after rule (15) and gives it no rule number, so the citation rule (15A)(c) cannot be confirmed from the corpus and should be checked against the printed amending Acts No. 31 of 2022 and No. 6 of 2024.

formal_title: Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance
relevant_excerpt: be valid and effectual, so far as relates to the execution thereof, if the same be signed by the party making the same or by some person lawfully authorized by him, and by two or more witnesses present at the same time, in the presence of some District Judge or Commissioner of a Court of Requests* for the district in which the party making such writing, deed, or instrument, or the person signing the same as such attorney, resides
why_relevant: A third statutory route that meets the facts squarely: a deed which section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance would otherwise require to be notarially executed is valid if executed before the District Judge for the district in which that party resides. The Tangalle co-owner resides in that district, so she could execute there without a notary and without anyone travelling to Colombo.
temporal_note: The Ordinance dates from 1852 and the corpus records no amendment or repeal of section 2. The reference to a Commissioner of a Court of Requests is marked in the corpus text as an obsolete office; only the District Judge limb is relied on. Whether the section remains in practical use at October 2025 could not be confirmed from this corpus.
verifier_note: Wording confirmed and the corpus records no repeal, but the section is keyed to a District Judge or Commissioner of a Court of Requests, an office abolished by court-structure legislation outside this corpus, and the corpus does not show whether one party of four may execute before the officer while the others execute before notaries, so the availability of this route at October 2025 cannot be resolved here.

formal_title: Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance
relevant_excerpt: nor until the same shall have been read over and explained to the party making the same, and to the witnesses thereto, by or in the presence of such Judge, Commissioner, or Justice as aforesaid, nor unless the same, and the duplicate thereof, shall be legibly written or engrossed, without erasures therein
why_relevant: Sets the conditions the officer must satisfy before certifying: proper stamping, reading over and explanation, legible engrossment without erasures, and identification of the party. It is what the third route costs in practice.
temporal_note: Original 1852 section; no amendment event recorded. Availability depends on the same question raised for section 2.
verifier_note: Wording confirmed; availability depends entirely on PROV-M020-017, which is unresolved.

formal_title: Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance
relevant_excerpt: Provided that every such writing, deed, or instrument shall be executed in duplicate, which duplicate shall be delivered or transmitted by such Judge, Commissioner, or Justice to the Registrar of Lands
why_relevant: Duplicate and registration mechanics for the third route, so that the deed reaches the Land Registry as a notarial deed would.
temporal_note: Original 1852 section; no amendment event recorded.
verifier_note: Wording confirmed; availability depends entirely on PROV-M020-017, which is unresolved. Section 5, which prescribes the form of the officer's certificate, was not mapped.

relevant_excerpt: (c) any other rule set out in section 31, shall be guilty of an offence, and shall, on conviction after summary trial before a Magistrate, be liable to a fine not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, in addition to any civil liability he may incur thereby.
why_relevant: Gives the consequence of the Colombo notary going to Tangalle to attest in breach of rule (22): an offence punishable by a fine of up to fifty thousand rupees, besides civil liability. It shows the territorial bar is not merely directory.
temporal_note: Penalty amounts in section 34 reflect later amendment; the consolidated text relied on was in force at October 2025.
verifier_note: Confirmed: rule (22) is not listed in section 34(1)(a) or (b), so a breach of it falls under the residual paragraph (c).

relevant_excerpt: Every notary shall be bound to have his office within the area specified in his warrant
why_relevant: Background on how tightly the Ordinance ties a notary to his area; it explains the scheme in which rule (22) sits but is not needed for any step of the reasoning.
temporal_note: Original 1907 section; no amendment event recorded.

relevant_excerpt: No instrument shall be deemed to be invalid by reason only of the failure of any notary to observe any provision of any rule set out in section 31 in respect of any matter of form
why_relevant: Background: a breach of a section 31 rule in a matter of form does not by itself invalidate the instrument, but the proviso preserves invalidity under other written law, so it gives no comfort against a breach of section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance.
temporal_note: Original 1907 section; no amendment event recorded.

relevant_excerpt: (20) He shall without delay duly attest every deed or instrument which shall be executed or acknowledged before him, and shall sign and seal such attestation. In such attestation he shall state- (a) that the said deed or instrument was signed by the party and the witnesses thereto in his presence and in the presence of one another;
why_relevant: The attestation rule itself. Rule (25) allocates compliance with rule (20) between the first attesting notary and every other attesting notary, and the answer turns on that allocation, so rule (20) has to be in the map for the two-notary route to be traceable to text.
temporal_note: Rule (20) stands in the consolidated text as amended by Act No. 31 of 2022 and Act No. 6 of 2024, both before October 2025.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier: relied on throughout the researcher's answer but absent from the provision list.

relevant_excerpt: (b) every notary attesting the deed or instrument shall number such deed or instrument in accordance with the provisions of rule (23); (c) the notary who first attests such deed or instrument shall preserve as his protocol the draft or copy referred to in rule (24), and shall comply with the requirements of that rule, and every other notary attesting such deed or instrument shall supply himself with a certified copy of the deed or instrument, which shall be deemed to be his protocol for the purposes of that rule;
why_relevant: Supplies the separate numbering and the certified-copy protocol that the answer attributes to the second notary. PROV-M020-003 quotes only paragraph (a) of rule (25), so without this entry those steps of the advice have no cited text.
temporal_note: Rule (25) was restructured by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 47 of 2011 s.3; paragraphs (b) and (c) stand in the consolidated text at October 2025.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier to carry the numbering and protocol steps asserted in CL-M020-Q01-005 and CL-M020-Q01-014.

relevant_excerpt: until the whole of such deed or instrument shall have been written or engrossed thereon, and in any event no signature or affixing of the left or right thumb impression or any other finger impression or toe impression of such executant shall be obtained for any deed or instrument on a blank paper or in any incomplete form.
why_relevant: The rule that forbids taking any signature before the deed is fully engrossed. The answer and the enrichment both rely on the deed being engrossed before the first signature; rule (3), not rule (12), is the provision that requires it.
temporal_note: Rule (3) stands in the consolidated text as amended before October 2025; no later amendment event affects the quoted words.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier because FACT-M020-Q01-008 activates PROV-M020-002 (rule (12)) for engrossment, which is the wrong rule.

relevant_excerpt: A power of attorney other than a power of attorney executed by a State institution shall be valid, only for a period of five years from the date of execution, unless the period of validity of such power of attorney is specified in such power of attorney or until such power of attorney is revoked or cancelled in accordance with the provisions of section 4.
why_relevant: Caps the life of the power of attorney relied on in the second route at five years unless a shorter period is stated in it. It belongs with sections 3, 3A and 3B in any advice on that route and was missing from the map.
temporal_note: Inserted by the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022; the corpus records the section as in force from 2022, before October 2025.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier as a missing condition on the attorney route.

relevant_excerpt: It shall be lawful for any person who has reached the age of eighteen years and residing within or outside Sri Lanka to execute a will bequeathing and disposing any movable and immovable property
why_relevant: This is the operative age rule. As substituted in 2022 it fixes eighteen completed years as the age at which a person becomes competent to execute a will, and it covers persons residing within or outside Sri Lanka and both movable and immovable property.
temporal_note: In force from 1844; the present text was substituted by Act No. 29 of 2022 (latest_change_year 2022), so it was in force well before the matter reference date of October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: Section 2 of the Wills Ordinance (Chapter 60) (hereinafter referred to as the "principal enactment") is hereby repealed and the following section is substituted therefor
why_relevant: The question asks for the age limit according to the latest amendments. This is the amending provision that repealed and replaced section 2 of the Wills Ordinance with the present eighteen-year rule, and Act No. 29 of 2022 is the most recent amendment to that Ordinance in the corpus.
temporal_note: Enacted in 2022, before the October 2025 matter reference date. No later amendment to the Wills Ordinance appears in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: Section 3 of the principal enactment is hereby repealed.
why_relevant: Section 3 of the Wills Ordinance was the provision that invalidated wills made by persons below the prescribed age. Its repeal in 2022 means the age question is now answered solely by the substituted section 2, with no separate invalidating provision surviving in the Ordinance.
temporal_note: Enacted 2022, in force before October 2025. The corpus table of sections for the Wills Ordinance confirms the effect: it runs s.1, s.2, then s.5 to s.9, with ss.3 and 4 absent.
verifier_note: Excerpt and effect confirmed; the description of what the repealed s.3 said is carried by PROV-M021-004, since the pre-2022 text of s.3 is not in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: Section 3 of the Wills Ordinance is hereby amended by the substitution for the words " No will made by any male under the age of twenty-one years, or by any female under the age of eighteen years,", of the words "No will made by any person under the age of eighteen years,"
why_relevant: Background only. It records the earlier statutory position, twenty-one years for males and eighteen for females, equalised at eighteen in 1993, which the 2022 amendment has now superseded, and it shows where the old age rule sat in the Ordinance.
temporal_note: Enacted 1993. It amended section 3 of the Wills Ordinance, which was repealed outright by Act No. 29 of 2022, so it has no operative effect at the October 2025 matter date and is used here only to explain the history.
verifier_note: Correctly recorded as historical background with applicable_to_matter_date false; the amended s.3 was itself repealed by 29-2022 s.3.

relevant_excerpt: No will, testament, or codicil containing any devise of land or other immovable property, or any bequest of movable property, or for any other purpose whatsoever, shall be valid unless it shall be in writing and executed subject to the provisions specified in subsection (2); (2) The testator shall - (a) sign; and (b) affix his left or right thumb impression, at the foot or end of the will, testament or codicil referred to in subsection (1), before a notary public and two witnesses who shall be present at the same time
why_relevant: This is the core of the procedure the testator must follow. The will must be in writing; the testator must sign and affix his thumb impression at the foot or end of the instrument, and must do so before a notary public and two witnesses all present at the same time. The proviso allows another finger impression or a toe impression where the thumb impression cannot be obtained.
temporal_note: Section 4 was renumbered and expanded by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 30 of 2022 (latest_change_year 2022), so this text was in force before October 2025.
verifier_note: Wording and role are right, but the proviso permitting another finger impression or a toe impression, which the gold answer and CL-M021-Q01-005 rely on, sits in 7-1840/s4 outside the recorded relevant_excerpt; the excerpt should be extended to the end of subsection (2) so the quoted text carries the whole rule relied on.

relevant_excerpt: by the addition immediately after subsection (1) of that section, the following new subsection: - "(2) The testator shall – (a) sign; and (b) affix his left or right thumb impression, at the foot or end of the will, testament or codicil referred to in subsection (1), before a notary public and two witnesses who shall be present at the same time
why_relevant: Shows that the thumb impression requirement for wills is itself a recent statutory change, introduced in 2022 alongside the Wills Ordinance amendment. It supports the temporal claim that the execution formalities stated in the answer are the current ones.
temporal_note: Enacted 2022, in force before the October 2025 matter date.
verifier_note: Excerpt is a verbatim substring of 30-2022/s3; note that search_corpus.py check reports FAIL for it from a Windows console because the en dash in 'The testator shall -' is mangled in argv, not because the text differs.

relevant_excerpt: in the case of a will- (i) set out in the attestation of the will that the testator was in good and sound mind to execute the will; and (ii) enter in the deed register maintained by him, the number assigned to such will, the date and the name of the testator.
why_relevant: This is the will-specific notarial duty and the point at which the chronic illness in the scenario bites procedurally: the attesting notary must state in the attestation that the testator was of good and sound mind when he executed the will, and must enter the will's number, its date and the testator's name in his deed register.
temporal_note: Rule (20)(h) was added to section 31 by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022; section 31 was further amended by Act No. 6 of 2024, which did not disturb paragraph (h). Both changes precede October 2025.
verifier_note: Rule (20)(h) confirmed as inserted by 31-2022 s.16(11)(d) and untouched by 6-2024 s.3(7), which reached only paragraph (g).

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless the person executing the same and the witnesses shall have signed the same in his presence and in the presence of one another, and unless he shall have signed the same in the presence of the executant and of the attesting witnesses.
why_relevant: Reinforces the simultaneous-presence requirement from the notary's side: the testator and the witnesses must sign in the notary's presence and in the presence of one another, and the notary must sign in their presence.
temporal_note: Long-standing rule in section 31, not altered by the 2022 or 2024 amending Acts. In force at October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument to which at least two witnesses have not subscribed their signatures in letters.
why_relevant: Fixes the minimum of two attesting witnesses subscribing in letters, matching the two witnesses the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance requires for a will.
temporal_note: In force at October 2025; not amended by Act No. 31 of 2022 or Act No. 6 of 2024.

relevant_excerpt: in the case of a deed of transfer or a deed of gift, or deed of exchange or a will, he shall affix to the protocol of such instrument passport size photographs of the signatories, other than the witnesses, to which the notary has affixed his seal and shall keep copies of national identity card, passport or driving licence of such signatories attached to the protocol
why_relevant: A current, will-specific step in the notarial procedure: the notary must attach a sealed passport size photograph of the testator and a copy of his identity document to the protocol of the will.
temporal_note: This text of rule (17)(b)(iii) was substituted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024, in force before October 2025.
verifier_note: Subsection label (17)(b)(iii) confirmed against 6-2024 s.3(6)(a), which substituted that sub paragraph and moved the photographs from the original to the protocol.

relevant_excerpt: If any person shall attest the execution of any will, testament, or codicil to whom or to whose wife or husband any beneficial devise, legacy, estate, interest, gift, disposition, or appointment of or affecting any immovable or movable property
why_relevant: A practical constraint on the choice of the two witnesses: a benefit given by the will to an attesting witness, or to that witness's spouse, is void so far as that witness is concerned, although the witness remains competent to prove the will.
temporal_note: In force since 1840, with no amendment recorded in the corpus. Applicable at October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: Every deed or other instrument, except any will, testament, or codicil required by this Ordinance to be executed or acknowledged before or to be attested by a notary, shall be executed, acknowledged, or attested in triplicate.
why_relevant: Wills are expressly excepted from the triplicate execution rule that applies to other notarially attested instruments, so the procedure for this will does not include execution in triplicate.
temporal_note: Section 16 carries a 2022 change made through the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 30 of 2022; the text relied on was in force at October 2025.
verifier_note: Confirmed, including that the word triplicate in the excerpt is the text as substituted by 30-2022 s.5 for the former word duplicate.

relevant_excerpt: Every will, testament, or codicil executed in manner herein before required shall be valid without any other publication thereof: Provided always that every such will, testament, or codicil shall, after the decease of the testator or testatrix, be duly proved and recorded in the District Court empowered by law to grant probate or administration
why_relevant: Background. Once executed in the required manner the will needs no further publication during the testator's lifetime; proof of the will is a step for the District Court after his death, not part of what the testator must do now.
temporal_note: In force since 1840 with no recorded amendment. Applicable at October 2025.

relevant_excerpt: Whenever in this Ordinance the word 'will' is used it shall be construed to extend to a testament and to a codicil, and to any other testamentary disposition
why_relevant: The interpretation section. It fixes the meaning of 'will' in the Ordinance, so the eighteen-year rule in section 2 governs codicils and other testamentary dispositions as well as the will itself.
temporal_note: Amended by Act No. 29 of 2022, which extended the definition of 'landed property' to condominium and land parcels. The definition of 'will' relied on here is unchanged and in force at October 2025.
verifier_note: Confirmed; the 2022 change made by 29-2022 s.6 touched only the 'landed property' limb, not the definition of 'will' relied on.

relevant_excerpt: he shall satisfy himself, before accepting them as witnesses, that they are persons of good repute and that they are well acquainted with the executant and know his proper name, occupation, and residence, and the witnesses shall sign a declaration at the foot of the deed or instrument that they are well acquainted with the executant and know his proper name, occupation, and residence.
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. Rule (9) is a mandatory step in the execution procedure that the map omitted: the notary must establish the identity of the executant (by acquaintance or by inspecting the national identity card, passport bio page or driving licence), must satisfy himself that the two witnesses are of good repute and well acquainted with the testator, and the witnesses must sign a declaration to that effect at the foot of the instrument. The enriched facts put two neighbours forward as witnesses, so the rule is squarely engaged.
temporal_note: Rule (9) in its present form was substituted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(6) and further amended by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(3); both precede the October 2025 matter reference date.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked verbatim against 1-1907/s31.

relevant_excerpt: (1) He shall not divulge the secrets confided to him or of which he becomes possessed in the execution of his office, unless with the express permission of his employer or when required to do so by law.
why_relevant: This is the notary's statutory duty of secrecy and the only provision that decides the question. It covers both secrets 'confided to him' and secrets 'of which he becomes possessed in the execution of his office', which is how a notary learns that a will exists and what it says. It also states the only two exceptions - the express permission of his employer (here the testator, who instructed and employed him) and a legal compulsion to disclose.
temporal_note: Rule (1) is original 1907 text and is in force at 2025-10. Section 31 as a whole has been amended many times (latest change year 2024), but the corpus text of Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16 begins its substitutions at rule (3), and No. 6 of 2024 s.3 contains no reference to rule (1); neither touches rule (1). Section 34 as substituted in 2022 still lists rule (1), which confirms rule (1) survives in the consolidated text.

relevant_excerpt: and he shall keep a register thereof with a convenient index for the purpose of easy reference; and every such register shall be substantially in the form F in the Second Schedule, but in the case of wills and codicils only the number and date of the instrument shall be inserted in the register.
why_relevant: Shows that the Ordinance itself treats a will as confidential where the register of other instruments is fuller: for wills and codicils the notary records only the number and date, not the parties or the contents. Supports reading the existence and contents of a will as a secret within rule (1) rather than as ordinary notarial information.
temporal_note: In force at 2025-10. Rule (24) is listed in the 2022 substitution of section 34 as a rule still in existence; the corpus consolidated text carries the wills-and-codicils qualification.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim and rule (24) is in force at 2025-10, but the inference in why_relevant that the Ordinance keeps the parties out of the notary's register no longer holds generally: rule (20)(h)(ii), inserted by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(11)(d), now requires the notary to enter in his deed register the number, the date and the name of the testator of a will; role remains supporting only.

relevant_excerpt: the duplicate of every deed or instrument (except wills and codicils) executed or acknowledged before or attested by him during the preceding month, together with a list in duplicate, signed by him, of all such deeds or instruments, which list shall be substantially in the Form F 1 in the Second Schedule: Provided, however, that in the case of wills and codicils only the number and date of the document shall be inserted in such list;
why_relevant: A second indication of the same legislative policy: unlike other instruments, the duplicate of a will is not transmitted to the Registrar of Lands and only its number and date appear in the monthly list, so the contents of a will are not put into any public channel during the testator's lifetime.
temporal_note: In force at 2025-10; the corpus consolidated text of rule (27) carries the wills-and-codicils exception and the proviso.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim and in force, but the subsection label is wrong: this text is rule (26)(a)(i) (47-2011 s.3 renumbered rule (26)(a) as (26)(a)(i) and inserted the (a)(ii) certified-copy paragraph that immediately follows it in the corpus text, and 6-2024 s.3(8) substituted 'Form F 1' in rule (26)(a)(i)); rule (27) was repealed outright by 31-2022 s.16(12) and no longer exists at 2025-10, so the citation in the map and in the gold answer prose must be corrected to rule (26)(a)(i).

relevant_excerpt: (a) rules (1), (31) or (32) set out in section 31, shall be guilty of an offence, and shall, on conviction after summary trial before a Magistrate, be liable to a fine not exceeding five thousand rupees, in addition to any civil liability he may incur thereby;
why_relevant: Attaches the sanction to a breach of rule (1) and so answers the 'discuss' element: divulging is not merely improper, it is an offence triable summarily before a Magistrate, and the fine is expressly in addition to any civil liability the notary may incur.
temporal_note: Section 34 was substituted by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.17; the substituted text, in force well before 2025-10, is the text quoted and is the version applicable at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: the documents specified in paragraph (a) of subsection (1) (not being wills or codicils, or drafts, minutes, or copies of the same)
why_relevant: Background only. Even when notarial records change hands on death, retirement or sale of a notarial practice, wills and codicils and their drafts and copies are carved out of what may be transferred. Context for the confidential status of a will; it does not itself bear on a request made during the testator's lifetime.
temporal_note: In force at 2025-10; section 41 was substituted by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.20 and the corpus consolidated text carries subsection (4) with the wills-and-codicils carve-out.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim and subsection (4) is correct, but why_relevant overstates it: the wills-and-codicils carve-out appears only in s.41(4) (transfer to a notary who has purchased the goodwill of the practice); s.41(2) and s.41(3) let a continuing partner or a principal retain the same paragraph (1)(a) documents with no wills exception, so this is weaker evidence of a general legislative policy than stated; background role is correct.

relevant_excerpt: The following sections of this Ordinance shall apply to the estates of such persons only as shall die after the proclamation of this Ordinance
why_relevant: Fixes the temporal scope of Part III. All the deaths relied on (2008, 2011, 2012, 2015) occurred long after the proclamation of the Ordinance, so Part III applies to each estate.
temporal_note: Corpus shows in_force_from_year 1876 with no recorded amendment events; the consolidated text is in force at the matter reference date 2025-04 and was equally in force at each of the deaths in 2008, 2011, 2012 and 2015.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but why_relevant states only one limb of s.20: the section also requires the deceased to have been unmarried at death or, if married, to have married after the proclamation of the Ordinance; both limbs are in fact satisfied for Kapila, Anusha and Prema, and the provision remains background rather than operative.

relevant_excerpt: Inheritance ab interstate to the immovable property in Sri Lanka of a person deceased shall be governed and regulated by the following provisions of this Ordinance
why_relevant: The subject matter is immovable property (Lot 1, 40 perches, at Battaramulla). This subsection makes Part III of the Ordinance the governing law for intestate succession to it, whatever the deceased's domicile.
temporal_note: Corpus shows in_force_from_year 1876 with no recorded amendment events; the consolidated text is in force at the matter reference date 2025-04 and was equally in force at each of the deaths in 2008, 2011, 2012 and 2015.

relevant_excerpt: When any person shall die intestate as to any of his or her property, leaving a spouse surviving, the surviving spouse shall inherit one-half of the property of such person.
why_relevant: Gives Champa one-half of Kapila's estate and Hasitha Perera one-half of Anusha's estate. It is the first deduction made in each intestacy before the blood relations take.
temporal_note: Corpus shows in_force_from_year 1876 with no recorded amendment events; the consolidated text is in force at the matter reference date 2025-04 and was equally in force at each of the deaths in 2008, 2011, 2012 and 2015.

relevant_excerpt: Subject to the right of the surviving spouse in the preceding section mentioned, the right of inheritance is divided in the following order as respects (a) descendants, (b) ascendants, (c) collaterals.
why_relevant: Sets the order of classes that structures each of the three intestacies: descendants first, then ascendants, then collaterals. It shows why Anusha's and Prema's estates move down the order once they die issueless.
temporal_note: Corpus shows in_force_from_year 1876 with no recorded amendment events; the consolidated text is in force at the matter reference date 2025-04 and was equally in force at each of the deaths in 2008, 2011, 2012 and 2015.

relevant_excerpt: Children, grandchildren, and remoter descendants are preferent to all others in the estate of the parents; all the children take equally per capita, but the children or remoter issue of a deceased child take per stirpes or by representation.
why_relevant: Divides the half of Kapila's estate not taken by his widow equally among his four surviving children, Anusha, Prema, Rupa and Seetha, per capita.
temporal_note: Corpus shows in_force_from_year 1876 with no recorded amendment events; the consolidated text is in force at the matter reference date 2025-04 and was equally in force at each of the deaths in 2008, 2011, 2012 and 2015.

relevant_excerpt: if only one of the parents be alive, the surviving parent takes half, and the brothers and sisters of the deceased of the full blood, and the issue of any deceased brother or sister of the full blood, by representation, and the brothers and sisters of the half-blood who are related to the intestate by the side of the deceased parent, and the issue of any such deceased brother or sister of the half-blood, by representation, take the other half.
why_relevant: Governs Prema's estate: she left no descendants, her father Kapila had predeceased her and her mother Champa survived, so Champa takes half and the surviving siblings take the other half.
temporal_note: Corpus shows in_force_from_year 1876 with no recorded amendment events; the consolidated text is in force at the matter reference date 2025-04 and was equally in force at each of the deaths in 2008, 2011, 2012 and 2015.

relevant_excerpt: Father and mother both failing, the property of the intestate goes to his brothers and sisters, whether of the whole or balf-blood, and their children and other issue by representation.
why_relevant: Governs Anusha's estate: she left no descendants and both her parents (Sandya and Kapila) had predeceased her, so the residue passes to her half-sisters Prema, Rupa and Seetha.
temporal_note: Corpus shows in_force_from_year 1876 with no recorded amendment events; the consolidated text is in force at the matter reference date 2025-04 and was equally in force at each of the deaths in 2008, 2011, 2012 and 2015.

relevant_excerpt: In case all the half-brothers and sisters, their children and remoter issue, are related to the intestate on one side only, they take the whole of the inheritance, unless there be a grandfather or grandmother or higher ascendant yet alive, related to the intestate on the other side
why_relevant: Anusha's only surviving siblings are half-sisters on her father's side. This section lets them take the whole collateral share, subject to the exception for a surviving ascendant on the mother's side, which the facts do not raise.
temporal_note: Corpus shows in_force_from_year 1876 with no recorded amendment events; the consolidated text is in force at the matter reference date 2025-04 and was equally in force at each of the deaths in 2008, 2011, 2012 and 2015.

relevant_excerpt: if all those who succeed to the inheritance are equally near in degree to the intestate, they take per capita, and not per stirpes.
why_relevant: Confirms per capita division among the three half-sisters in Anusha's estate and among the two full sisters in Prema's estate, all being equally near in degree.
temporal_note: Corpus shows in_force_from_year 1876 with no recorded amendment events; the consolidated text is in force at the matter reference date 2025-04 and was equally in force at each of the deaths in 2008, 2011, 2012 and 2015.
verifier_note: The excerpt drops the section's opening qualifier 'Except when otherwise expressly provided', so s.30 supplies per capita division only inside a class that ss.25 and 27 have not already divided; on these facts that is the sibling half in each of Anusha's and Prema's estates, so the result is unchanged but the qualifier must be stated.

relevant_excerpt: In all questions relating to the distribution of the property of an intestate, if the present Ordinance is silent, the rules of the Roman-Dutch law as it prevailed in North Holland are to govern and be followed.
why_relevant: The Ordinance's own residual clause. It is the statutory acknowledgement that any step the Ordinance does not cover, such as the effect of a reserved life interest, falls to Roman-Dutch common law, which is outside this corpus.
temporal_note: Corpus shows in_force_from_year 1876 with no recorded amendment events; the consolidated text is in force at the matter reference date 2025-04 and was equally in force at each of the deaths in 2008, 2011, 2012 and 2015.

relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property
why_relevant: Background for the 2006 Deed of Gift: a disposition of immovable property has no force in law unless notarially executed and attested. Deed of Gift No 925 was attested by a notary public.
temporal_note: Corpus records amendment events for this section in 1947, 2022 and 2024; the text shown is the current consolidated text and is in force at 2025-04, but its present subsections (1) and (2) post-date the 2006 deed. Used only as background, not as an operative rule for the deed's validity.
verifier_note: Corpus records amendment events on this section in 1947, 2022 and 2024, so the corpus does not hold the wording in force when Deed of Gift No 925 was executed on 11 March 2006; usable only as background and not as authority on that deed's validity, which is how the map already confines it.

relevant_excerpt: means not having a husband or wife living
why_relevant: Defines 'unmarried' for the Ordinance. Prema is described as having died unmarried, so no share of her estate is deducted for a surviving spouse under section 22.
temporal_note: Corpus shows in_force_from_year 1876 with no recorded amendment events; the consolidated text is in force at the matter reference date 2025-04 and was equally in force at each of the deaths in 2008, 2011, 2012 and 2015.

relevant_excerpt: if there are only half-brothers and sisters or such issue of one side, the full brothers and sisters and the issue of deceased full brothers and sisters by representation, take then in the first place one-half of the property, and divide the other half with the half-brothers and sisters and their issue by representation.
why_relevant: The division rule that qualifies section 26 where half-blood siblings are involved. It is examined and found not to alter the result in Anusha's estate, because she left no full siblings at all, so section 29 rather than section 27 supplies the division.
temporal_note: Corpus shows in_force_from_year 1876 with no recorded amendment events; the consolidated text is in force at the matter reference date 2025-04 and was equally in force at each of the deaths in 2008, 2011, 2012 and 2015.

relevant_excerpt: includes land, incorporeal tenements, and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything which is attached to the earth, and any interest in land except that of a mortgagee
why_relevant: Defines 'immovable property' for the Ordinance. Section 21(1) makes Part III the governing law for inheritance ab intestato to immovable property in Sri Lanka, and Lot 1 is land, so this definition is what brings the subject matter inside s.21(1).
