temporal_note: Corpus shows in_force_from_year 1876 with no recorded amendment events and no amending Act to 15-1876 in the corpus; in force at the matter reference date 2025-04 and at each of the deaths in 2008, 2011, 2012 and 2015.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier: `edges 15-1876/s21` records a defines-link to 15-1876/s3 for the term 'immovable property', and the map excerpted s.3 only for 'unmarried'. Excerpt confirmed verbatim with `check`.

relevant_excerpt: (other than a lease at will, or for any period not exceeding one month)
why_relevant: Fixes the scope of the notarial-execution requirement for leases. Only a lease at will or a lease for a period not exceeding one month is carved out of section 2, so a two-year lease is inside it.
temporal_note: Section 2 records amendment events in 1947, 2022 and 2024; all precede April 2025 and the corpus holds the consolidated text. The one-month carve-out appears unchanged in that text.

relevant_excerpt: signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary
why_relevant: States the execution formality that governs how this lease must be signed: signature by each executant, or by a person duly authorised by the executant, and by the witnesses, all present at the same time and in one another's presence before a notary, followed by notarial attestation. It also supplies the statutory basis for signature through an attorney.
temporal_note: This is the wording as substituted by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Acts of 2022 and 2024, both in force before April 2025, so the reference to a person duly authorised by the executant applies to this matter.

relevant_excerpt: (12) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless the person executing the same and the witnesses shall have signed the same in his presence and in the presence of one another, and unless he shall have signed the same in the presence of the executant and of the attesting witnesses.
why_relevant: Casts the same simultaneous-presence requirement on the notary as a professional duty, which rules out the parties simply posting the instrument between Colombo and Galle and signing it away from the notary.
temporal_note: Rule (12) is not among the rules recorded as substituted, inserted or repealed by the Notaries (Amendment) Acts No. 47 of 2011, No. 31 of 2022 or No. 6 of 2024; the consolidated text is in force at April 2025.

relevant_excerpt: (22) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any area other than that in which he is authorized to practice
why_relevant: Explains why the Colombo notary cannot simply travel to Galle and attest there. A notary may not attest outside the area in which she is authorised to practise, which is what forces either a second notary or an attorney.
temporal_note: Rule (22) is not among the rules recorded as substituted or repealed by the 2011, 2022 or 2024 amending Acts; in force at April 2025.

relevant_excerpt: shall be deemed to authorize him to practice as a notary in the judicial zone in which he resides
why_relevant: Identifies the area referred to in rule (22) as the judicial zone in which the notary resides, so a notary practising in Colombo is authorised for the Colombo zone and not for Galle.
temporal_note: Inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Law No. 20 of 1976, long before April 2025.
verifier_note: Wording and effect confirmed, but section 4A keys the authorised area to the judicial zone in which the notary resides, and the facts state only that Malani Silva practises in Colombo, so the step from Colombo practice to Colombo residence is an assumption rather than a corpus fact.

relevant_excerpt: In the case of any deed or instrument which is to be executed by two or more parties, both or all of whom, as the case may be, do not sign the deed or instrument at the same time and place
why_relevant: Expressly recognises a deed executed by two or more parties who do not sign at the same time and place, and adjusts the operation of rules (6), (7), (18), (19), (20), (23) and (25) accordingly. This is the provision that makes split execution lawful.
temporal_note: Section 32 carries no amendment events in the corpus; in force since 1907 and at April 2025.

relevant_excerpt: (25) Where any deed or instrument is executed or acknowledged before more than one notary- (a) the notary who first attests such deed or instrument shall comply with all the requirements of rule (20), and every other notary attesting such deed or instrument shall comply with the requirements of paragraphs (a) to (e) of the aforesaid rule
why_relevant: Sets out how attestation works when the same instrument is executed before more than one notary, which is the mechanism that lets Rupa Perera sign in Galle before a Galle notary while Gamini Sirisene signs in Colombo before Malani Silva.
temporal_note: Rule (25) is not among the rules recorded as substituted or repealed by the 2011, 2022 or 2024 amendments; in force at April 2025.

relevant_excerpt: (ii) where any such deed or instrument is not signed by all the parties thereto before the expiry of a period of three months from the date on which it is first signed by one of such parties
why_relevant: Shows that split execution is treated by the Ordinance as a time-limited process and fixes the three-month point at which the notary may be called on to deliver the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands. A practical constraint on the split-execution route rather than a condition of validity.
temporal_note: Rule (27) as consolidated is in force at April 2025; no amendment event in the corpus records its repeal.
verifier_note: The excerpt is verbatim and the supporting role is right, but the corpus text of section 31 carries this paragraph in an unlabelled block between rules (26) and (28) with no printed "(27)" or "(c)" marker, so the subsection label "rule (27)(c)(ii)" is a reconstruction rather than something the corpus states.

relevant_excerpt: given by one person to another, to represent him, to perform any work, do any act, or carry on any trade or business, and - (a) if it is executed in Sri Lanka, executed before two witnesses and attested by a notary public
why_relevant: Defines the instrument by which Rupa Perera could authorise someone else to sign for her and fixes its own form: a written authority executed before two witnesses and notarially attested.
temporal_note: The definition was substituted by the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022 and further amended by Act No. 3 of 2024, both before April 2025.

relevant_excerpt: shall be executed subject to the provisions specified in subsection (2) or (3), as the case may be. (2) If a power of attorney specified in subsection (1) is executed in Sri Lanka, it shall - (a) be duly attested by a notary public in accordance with the Notaries Ordinance (Chapter 107) and the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance
why_relevant: Because a two-year lease is a transaction within section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, any power of attorney used for it must meet the extra requirements in this section, including notarial attestation, a description of the land and the grantor's thumb impression.
temporal_note: Inserted by the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022, in force before April 2025.

relevant_excerpt: Every power of attorney executed in Sri Lanka or any other country shall be registered with the Registrar General.
why_relevant: Makes registration with the Registrar General compulsory, and paragraph (b) fixes one month from execution for a power executed in Sri Lanka. A necessary step if the attorney route is taken.
temporal_note: Section 3 was repealed and substituted by the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022, in force before April 2025.

relevant_excerpt: (30) If he attest any deed or instrument executed before him by means of an attorney, he shall preserve a true copy of the power of attorney with his protocol, and shall forward a like copy with the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands.
why_relevant: Fixes what the attesting notary must do when the instrument is signed by an attorney rather than by the principal, which is the notary-side counterpart of the power of attorney route.
temporal_note: Rule (30) is not recorded as substituted or repealed by the 2011, 2022 or 2024 amendments to section 31; in force at April 2025.

relevant_excerpt: (h) a promissory note; (i) a lease or hire of any property; (j) a receipt or discharge given for any money or other property;
why_relevant: Brings a lease of property within the class of specified instruments on which stamp duty is charged, so the lease agreement in this matter is a chargeable instrument.
temporal_note: Section 4 carries no amendment events in the corpus and has been in force since 2006.

relevant_excerpt: there shall be charged a duty (hereinafter to be called "stamp duty") at such rate as the Minister may determine by Order published in the Gazette on every "specified instrument"- (a) executed, drawn or presented in Sri Lanka
why_relevant: Is the charging provision, and shows that the rate sits not in the Act but in a Ministerial Order published in the Gazette. This is why the money value of the duty cannot be derived from the statutes in the corpus.
temporal_note: Section 3 carries no amendment events in the corpus and has been in force since 2006.

relevant_excerpt: Otherwise than in cases where there is an agreement to the contrary, stamp duty shall be payable:- (a) in the case of a policy of insurance, by the person effecting the insurance; (b) in the case of a transfer or assignment of any share, by the transferee or assignee of such share; (c) in the case of a lease, by the lessee
why_relevant: Identifies the lessee as the person liable for duty on a lease unless the parties agree otherwise, so the burden falls on Gamini Sirisene in the absence of contrary agreement.
temporal_note: Section 6 was amended by Act No. 10 of 2008; paragraph (c) on leases appears in the consolidated text in force at April 2025.

relevant_excerpt: Stamp duty payable on any specified instrument relating to a mortgage or lease of any immovable property may be paid, prior to, or at the time of, the execution of the specified instrument, to a prescribed bank.
why_relevant: Gives the manner and timing of payment for a lease of immovable property: payment to a prescribed bank before or at execution, with the bank certificate affixed to the instrument.
temporal_note: Subsection (2) was substituted by Act No. 10 of 2008; the consolidated text is in force at April 2025.

relevant_excerpt: (6) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless he has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided.
why_relevant: Makes the correct stamp duty the attesting notary's concern, which is why the notary in this matter has to settle the duty before attesting.
temporal_note: Rule (6) is not recorded as substituted or repealed by the amendments to section 31; in force at April 2025.

relevant_excerpt: (a) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Ordinance or any other written law, any stamp duty which is required to be paid in respect of every deed or instrument executed under any written law, shall be paid by the notary; (b) The stamps or the original receipt received from the relevant bank as proof of such payment shall be affixed to the duplicate of the deed or instrument by the notary;
why_relevant: Places the mechanics of paying the duty and affixing proof of payment on the notary, alongside the lessee's liability for the duty under the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act.
temporal_note: Rule (7) paragraphs (a) to (d) were inserted or substituted by the Notaries (Amendment) Acts No. 31 of 2022 and No. 6 of 2024, both before April 2025.

formal_title: Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance
relevant_excerpt: signed by the party making the same or by some person lawfully authorized by him, and by two or more witnesses present at the same time, in the presence of some District Judge or Commissioner of a Court of Requests* for the district in which the party making such writing, deed, or instrument, or the person signing the same as such attorney, resides
why_relevant: Supplies a third lawful mode of execution for an instrument caught by section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance: signature before two or more witnesses in the presence of a District Judge for the district in which the party resides, or of a Justice of the Peace for that district specially authorised by the Minister of Justice, with a certificate of execution at the foot of the instrument. Added by the verifier because the map treats notarial execution as the only route and concludes that signature outside the presence of a notary is not open to the parties.
temporal_note: The corpus records in_force_from_year 1852 with no amendment events and no repeal, so the section stands as at April 2025. The corpus marks "Commissioner of a Court of Requests" with an asterisk, that court no longer existing, so the live officers are the District Judge and a specially authorised Justice of the Peace. Sections 3 and 4 add execution in duplicate, transmission to the Registrar of Lands, and proper stamping.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier. Excerpt checked verbatim against 17-1852/s2; the cross-reference to Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 is confirmed by the corpus edge graph.

relevant_excerpt: (8) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument to which at least two witnesses have not subscribed their signatures in letters.
why_relevant: Fixes the number of attesting witnesses. Section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance speaks of "the witnesses" without a number, and the answer asserts that Rupa Perera signs before two witnesses without citing anything for the figure. Rule (8) is the provision that supplies it.
temporal_note: Rule (8) appears in the consolidated text of section 31 and is not among the rules recorded as substituted, inserted or repealed by the 2011, 2022 or 2024 amending Acts; in force at April 2025.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier. Excerpt checked verbatim against 1-1907/s31.

relevant_excerpt: (c) where a deed or instrument is signed by an attorney, such attorney shall submit to the notary an affidavit affirming that the Power of Attorney is genuine and in force and the grantor is alive when executing such deed or instrument;
why_relevant: Completes the power of attorney route on the notary's side. Where the lease is signed by an attorney rather than by Rupa Perera, the attorney must give the notary an affidavit that the power is genuine and in force and that the grantor is alive. The map cited rule (30) for the notary's protocol duty but omitted this condition on the attorney.
temporal_note: This paragraph sits in the block inserted into section 31 by the Notaries (Amendment) Acts No. 31 of 2022 and No. 6 of 2024, both in force before April 2025.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier. Excerpt checked verbatim against 1-1907/s31.

relevant_excerpt: Inheritance ab interstate to the immovable property in Sri Lanka of a person deceased shall be governed and regulated by the following provisions of this Ordinance wherever such person may have or have had his actual or matrimonial domicile.
why_relevant: The subject matter is immovable property in Sri Lanka (the land and premises bearing Assessment No.45, Colombo Road, Pugoda). This subsection is the gateway provision: it makes Part III of the Ordinance the governing law for every intestate devolution in the chain, irrespective of the domicile of Kasun, Thilak or Sarathi.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event for this section, so the same text governed the deaths in 2013, 2017 and 2018 and is in force at 2024-10.

relevant_excerpt: this Ordinance shall not apply to Kandyans or Muslims, or to Tamils of the Northern Province who are or may become subject to the Tesawalamai.
why_relevant: Fixes the outer limit of the general law of inheritance. Nothing in the background places any of the parties within Kandyan law, Muslim law or the Thesawalamai, so the general law in Part III of this Ordinance applies rather than a special personal law. Recorded as background because the exclusion is not engaged on the facts as given.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; no amendment event recorded in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: When any person shall die intestate as to any of his or her property, leaving a spouse surviving, the surviving spouse shall inherit one-half of the property of such person.
why_relevant: Governs the share of Sena, the surviving husband of Sarathi, who died intestate on 8 August 2018. It also explains why nothing passes to a spouse out of the estates of Kasun (who died unmarried) and Thilak (no surviving spouse disclosed).
temporal_note: In force from 1876; no amendment event recorded in the corpus, so the same text applied at Sarathi's death in 2018 and at 2024-10.

relevant_excerpt: Subject to the right of the surviving spouse in the preceding section mentioned, the right of inheritance is divided in the following order as respects (a) descendants, (b) ascendants, (c) collaterals.
why_relevant: Sets the order in which the remaining half (or the whole, where there is no surviving spouse) is taken, and makes clear that the spouse's half under s.22 is carved out first. It is the ordering rule that sends each of the three intestate estates in this matter past the descendant class, which is empty in every case.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; no amendment event recorded in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: Children, grandchildren, and remoter descendants are preferent to all others in the estate of the parents; all the children take equally per capita, but the children or remoter issue of a deceased child take per stirpes or by representation.
why_relevant: Governs the devolution of Thilak's half share on his intestate death on 3 March 2017: his surviving children Sunil and Lalith are preferent to all others and take equally per capita. It also shows that Kasun, who predeceased his father in 2013 without issue, leaves nobody to take by representation.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; no amendment event recorded in the corpus, so the same text applied at Thilak's death in 2017 and at 2024-10.

relevant_excerpt: The children and remoter descendants failing, the inheritance of the deceased goes to his father and mother in case they are both alive; but if only one of the parents be alive, the surviving parent takes half, and the brothers and sisters of the deceased of the full blood, and the issue of any deceased brother or sister of the full blood, by representation, and the brothers and sisters of the half-blood who are related to the intestate by the side of the deceased parent, and the issue of any such deceased brother or sister of the half-blood, by representation, take the other half.
why_relevant: The central operative rule. It governs Kasun's estate (no descendants; mother Kamala predeceased in 2011, father Thilak surviving, so Thilak takes half and the half-blood brothers and sisters on the deceased mother's side take the other half) and, on the footing that Namal Silva is Sarathi's father and survives her, the non-spousal half of Sarathi's estate. Its restriction of half-blood siblings to those related through the deceased parent is what excludes Sunil and Lalith, who are related to Kasun through his surviving father.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; no amendment event recorded in the corpus, so the same text applied at Kasun's death in 2013, at Sarathi's death in 2018 and at 2024-10.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and the reading of "by the side of the deceased parent" is right, but the excerpt stops before the second sentence of s.25 ("In case there is no full or half-brother or sister alive at the death of the deceased, the surviving parent inherits the whole, although there may be children or other issue of deceased brothers or sisters"), which has to be read with the first: it is only because Sarathi and Amal were alive at Kasun's death that Thilak took a half and not the whole.

relevant_excerpt: Except when otherwise expressly provided, if all those who succeed to the inheritance are equally near in degree to the intestate, they take per capita, and not per stirpes.
why_relevant: Supplies the mode of division within the sibling half of Kasun's estate: Sarathi and Amal are equally near in degree to Kasun (both half-sisters and half-brothers on the mother's side), so they take that half per capita, one-quarter of the land each.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; no amendment event recorded in the corpus.
verifier_note: Excerpt verbatim, but s.30 opens "Except when otherwise expressly provided" and s.27 (added as PROV-M025-901) is the express provision on dividing among half-blood brothers and sisters; s.30 supplies the per capita division here only because s.25 confines the takers of the sibling half to the deceased mother's side, so no father's-side against mother's-side split under s.27 arises.

relevant_excerpt: means not having a husband or wife living
why_relevant: Defines "unmarried" for the purposes of the Ordinance. The background records that Kasun died "intestate and unmarried", which on this definition means he left no surviving spouse, so s.22 gives no half share out of his estate and the whole of it falls to be divided under s.25.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; no amendment event recorded in the corpus. The corpus text of this interpretation section has lost its defined-term lead-ins in extraction, so the excerpt reads as a bare definition body; the corpus row records "unmarried" among the section's defined terms.
verifier_note: The excerpt is a verbatim substring of s.3 but the corpus extraction has dropped the defined-term lead-ins, so the words "means not having a husband or wife living" cannot be tied to "unmarried" from the excerpt alone; defs 15-1876 unmarried confirms s.3 defines that term, and the provision should be cited as s.3 sv "unmarried".

relevant_excerpt: The following sections of this Ordinance shall apply to the estates of such persons only as shall die after the proclamation of this Ordinance
why_relevant: Temporal scope of Part III. Every death in this matter (2011, 2013, 2017, 2018) is long after the proclamation of the Ordinance, so the inheritance sections apply to each estate. Recorded as background because the condition is plainly satisfied.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; no amendment event recorded in the corpus.
verifier_note: Excerpt verbatim but truncated: s.20 continues "and shall be then unmarried or (if married) shall have been married after the proclamation of this Ordinance", a second condition the map does not record; it is satisfied on these facts because every marriage and death in the chain is long after 1876.

relevant_excerpt: the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary
why_relevant: Explains why the three notarially attested instruments in the chain (Deed of Transfer No.2778, Deed of Gift No.5634 and Administrator's Conveyance No.6231) are effective to move title in immovable property. Recorded as background: the background states that each was attested by a named notary, so the requirement is met and no issue turns on it.
temporal_note: In force at 2024-10, but the corpus text is the version as amended by Act No. 30 of 2022 and Act No. 4 of 2024. The deeds in this matter were executed in 2011 and 2014, before those amendments, so the corpus wording (thumb impressions, transferee execution) is not the text that governed their execution. Used only as background for the general notarial-writing requirement, which predates the amendments.
verifier_note: Excerpt verbatim, but the corpus holds only the text as amended by Act No. 30 of 2022 and Act No. 4 of 2024, so the version that governed Deed of Transfer No.2778 (2011), Deed of Gift No.5634 (2011) and Administrator's Conveyance No.6231 (2014) is not in the corpus; the provision can be relied on only for the notarial-writing requirement common to both versions, which is how the map uses it (background).

relevant_excerpt: make order for the issue of a certificate of heir ship in form No. 87A in the First Schedule, to each of the heirs mentioned in the application, stating also the share of the estate which each heir is entitled to receive, if agreed to by the heirs
why_relevant: Frames the testamentary proceeding No.1589/2013/T in the District Court of Pugoda: on an intestacy the court either grants letters of administration or issues certificates of heirship stating each heir's share. It supports the step in which Kasun's heirs and their shares were identified in that proceeding before the administrator conveyed the land to them.
temporal_note: In force from 1889, last changed in 1993 (Act No. 14 of 1993 s.4) per the corpus amendment events, so the corpus text was already in force when the testamentary proceeding ran in 2013 and 2014 and remains in force at 2024-10.
verifier_note: Excerpt verbatim, but the subsection cited is the wrong limb: s.531(1)(b)(ii) is the certificate-of-heirship route, whereas the background says Kasun's estate was "duly administered" and Thilak executed the conveyance as Administrator, which is the grant of letters of administration under s.531(1)(b)(i); the section supports the identification of heirs in the testamentary proceeding, but not on the limb quoted.

relevant_excerpt: establishing that the entire estate has been duly administered and distributed, the court may grant him a discharge and enter an order that the estate has been fully administered.
why_relevant: Supports the statement in the background that the testamentary proceeding was terminated on 10 February 2014: termination follows distribution of the estate to those entitled. It anchors the Administrator's Conveyance No.6231 of 21 March 2014 as the distribution step rather than an independent disposition.
temporal_note: In force from 1889, last changed in 1977 (Act No. 20 of 1977 s.108) per the corpus amendment events, so the corpus text governed the 2014 termination and is in force at 2024-10.
verifier_note: Excerpt verbatim but cut mid-sentence: it drops the antecedent condition in s.724B(1) ("Where an executor or administrator files with his final account a receipt and discharge in the form No. 119A ... signed by the devisees, legatees, trustees, heirs, creditors or other persons entitled to or having an interest in the estate"), so as quoted it does not itself show that discharge follows distribution to those entitled.

relevant_excerpt: The division however in the case of half-brothers and sisters is as follows: - The inheritance is divided into two parts ; the one-half the full brothers and sisters and the issue of such as are deceased by representation divide with the half-brothers and sisters of the father's side and the issue of such as are deceased by representation ; and the other half they divide with those of the mother's side and the issue of such as are deceased by representation
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. Section 27 is the express provision on how an inheritance is divided where half-blood brothers and sisters take, and s.30 applies only "Except when otherwise expressly provided", so s.27 has to be checked before s.30 is used on the sibling half of Kasun's estate. It does not change the result: s.25 admits only the half-blood brothers and sisters related to Kasun through his deceased mother, so there is no father's-side share to set against a mother's-side share and no full brother or sister to take a preferential half. Sarathi and Amal therefore divide the sibling half equally under s.30.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event for this section, so the same text applied at Kasun's death in 2013 and is in force at 2024-10.

relevant_excerpt: Father and mother both failing, the property of the intestate goes to his brothers and sisters, whether of the whole or balf-blood, and their children and other issue by representation.
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. Both gold answers cite s.26 by number in their conclusions as the alternative outcome if no parent of Sarathi was alive on 8 August 2018, but the researcher's map carried no entry for it, so that citation was unanchored. On that alternative the non-spousal half of Sarathi's share goes to her brothers and sisters whether of the whole or half-blood, which on these facts is Amal alone, Kasun having predeceased her without issue.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; no amendment event recorded in the corpus. The corpus body carries an OCR corruption, "balf-blood" for "half-blood"; the excerpt is quoted as the corpus holds it.

relevant_excerpt: In all questions relating to the distribution of the property of an intestate, if the present Ordinance is silent, the rules of the Roman-Dutch law as it prevailed in North Holland are to govern and be followed.
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. Both questions are classified statute_only on the footing that the Ordinance is not silent on any step in this chain; s.36 is the provision that makes that footing load-bearing, because it is the only route by which non-corpus Roman-Dutch law could be reached. Recorded as background: on these facts ss.20 to 30 cover every devolution, so s.36 is not engaged.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; no amendment event recorded in the corpus.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: be void as against all parties claiming an adverse interest thereto on valuable consideration by virtue of any subsequent instrument which is duly registered under this Chapter
why_relevant: Priority between competing instruments turns on due registration, so the purchaser's lawyer must call for the vendor's title deeds together with a certified extract of the land registry folio to see what has in fact been registered against the land and in what order. It is the reason the search covers registered instruments and not only the deeds the vendor chooses to produce.
temporal_note: In force from 1927; the corpus records no amendment event on this section, and it stands in the consolidated 1990 edition. In force in October 2024.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: all duplicates and copies and all books and indexes kept under this Ordinance may be searched and examined by any person claiming to be interested therein or by his attorney-at-law or agent duly authorized thereto in writing, and certified copies of or extracts from any such duplicate, copy, or book may be obtained if required
why_relevant: This is the statutory authority for the central document of any title examination: the certified extract of the land registry folio, obtained by the purchaser's attorney-at-law. It also authorises certified copies of registered duplicates where an original deed in the chain has been lost.
temporal_note: In force from 1927; no amendment event recorded on this section. In force in October 2024.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: Every instrument presented for registration shall be registered in the book allotted to the division in which the land affected by the instrument is situated
why_relevant: Registration counts only if it is in the correct folio or a folio opened in continuation of it with cross references. The extract called for must therefore be of the folio in which the first registered instrument affecting the land was registered and of every connected folio, otherwise the search misses registrations that still take priority.
temporal_note: In force from 1927, amended in 1974 (Act No. 14 of 1974). The amended text long predates the matter date and is the text relied on.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: affecting or relating to land instituted on or after the 9th day of November, 1917, shall bind a purchaser, unless and until the lis pendens is duly registered under this Chapter
why_relevant: A registered lis pendens binds a purchaser for valuable consideration. The search of the folio must therefore extend to registered lis pendens entries, and the purchaser must call for particulars of any pending action disclosed, because the company would take subject to the outcome of that action.
temporal_note: In force from 1927, amended in 1947. The text relied on is the consolidated text, which stood unchanged in October 2024.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim but begins after the opening negative of s.11(1) ("No lis pendens ... shall bind a purchaser, unless and until the lis pendens is duly registered"), so standing alone it states the opposite of the section; the section as a whole does support why_relevant, and the corpus OCR renders "lis" as "Us" in subsections (1) and (7).

formal_title: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance No. 7 of 1840
relevant_excerpt: shall be in force or avail in law unless - (a) the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary
why_relevant: No sale or transfer of immovable property avails in law unless it is in writing and notarially attested. Every link in the chain the vendor produces must therefore be a notarially executed deed (or its registered duplicate or a certified copy), which is why the lawyer calls for the deeds themselves and inspects the attestations rather than accepting a schedule of title.
temporal_note: In force from 1840; the section was replaced by Act No. 30 of 2022 and further amended by Act No. 4 of 2024, so the text quoted is the text in force in October 2024. The notarial requirement itself has stood since 1840, so the older deeds in the chain were subject to an equivalent requirement in the text then in force. A verifier should confirm the commencement date of Act No. 4 of 2024 against the matter date.

formal_title: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance No. 7 of 1840
relevant_excerpt: Provided further, where the transferee is a corporate body and where the Board of Directors of such corporate body is unable to be present and execute the deed or instrument, such Board shall authorise in writing, any other person to sign such deed or instrument on his behalf
why_relevant: The purchaser here is a corporate body. The transferee must sign and place a thumb impression, and where the board cannot attend, a written board authority in favour of a named signatory is required. That written authorisation, together with proof of the board's constitution, is a document that must be in hand before the transfer is executed.
temporal_note: This proviso is part of the section as it stood in October 2024, following the 2022 and 2024 amendments. It has no bearing on the older deeds in the chain, which were executed before it was introduced.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and is the text the corpus now prints, but subsection (2) with the corporate-transferee proviso was inserted only by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 4 of 2024, which carries no commencement provision beyond its short title; the corpus records no certification date, so applicability at the October 2024 matter date cannot be established from the corpus and rests on the inference that an Act numbered 4 of 2024 was certified early in that year.

relevant_excerpt: Proof of the undisturbed and uninterrupted possession by a defendant in any action, or by those under whom he claims, of lands or immovable property, by a title adverse to or independent of that of the claimant or plaintiff in such action
why_relevant: Ten years of undisturbed adverse possession can defeat a paper title, so a deed chain alone does not settle title. The purchaser must also call for documents that evidence possession over at least that period: rates and assessment receipts, utility bills, tenancy or lease agreements and receipts for rent, and where the building is let, the tenancy records.
temporal_note: In force from 1871; the corpus records no amendment event on this section (Act No. 26 of 2014 amended the Ordinance but the corpus records no change to s.3). In force in October 2024.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: the transfer of title of any land situated in Sri Lanka, shall be prohibited if such transfer is- (a) to a foreigner; or (b) to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act where any foreign shareholding in such company, either direct or indirect, is fifty per cent or above; or (c) to a foreign company, unless exempted as provided in section 3.
why_relevant: The purchaser is a company incorporated in Sri Lanka. A transfer to it is prohibited outright if direct or indirect foreign shareholding is fifty per cent or above, and s.2(2)(a) requires that the shareholding stay below that level for twenty consecutive years after the transfer. This makes the purchaser's own corporate documents part of the title examination: the share register, the latest annual return and the shareholder particulars needed to establish direct and indirect foreign holding.
temporal_note: In force from 2014; the corpus records no amendment event on s.2 itself (the 2017 and 2018 amending Acts touched other sections, and s.3 was amended in 2018). In force in October 2024.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: The provisions of section 2 shall not apply to- (a) any land the title of which is transferred to a Diplomatic Mission of another State within the meaning of the Diplomatic Privileges Act
why_relevant: The exemptions qualify the prohibition, so if the purchaser were to rely on one (for instance listing on the Colombo Stock Exchange under paragraph (i)) the documents evidencing that exemption would have to be called for as well. On the facts no exemption is relied on, which is why the shareholding documents remain the operative check.
temporal_note: In force from 2014, amended by Act No. 21 of 2018. The amended text is the text in force in October 2024.

relevant_excerpt: A certificate of incorporation issued under this section in-respect of any company, shall be conclusive evidence of the fact that- (a) all the requirements under this Act relating to the incorporation of a company have been complied with
why_relevant: Both parties are companies, so their existence and identity must be proved by the document the Act treats as conclusive: the certificate of incorporation. Certified copies of the certificate, the articles and the form recording the current directors and registered office are called for to show that the vendor company exists, that the persons signing for it are its directors, and that the purchaser company itself is validly incorporated.
temporal_note: In force from 2007; subsections were substituted by the Companies (Amendment) Act No. 13 of 2019. The 2019 text is the text in force in October 2024.

relevant_excerpt: A company shall not enter into any major transaction, unless such transaction is- (a) approved by special resolution; (b) contingent on approval by special resolution; (c) consented to in writing by all the shareholders of the company; or (d) a transaction which the company is expressly authorised to enter into by a provision in its articles
why_relevant: A major transaction includes the acquisition of assets worth more than half the value of the company's assets before the acquisition. If the purchase price crosses that threshold for the purchaser, the transaction requires a special resolution, written consent of all shareholders or express authority in the articles. The certified special resolution or shareholders' consent, and the articles, must therefore be called for on the purchaser's side; the same test is applied to the vendor company's disposal of the building.
temporal_note: In force from 2007; the corpus records no amendment event on this section. In force in October 2024.
verifier_note: Excerpt stops at "a provision in its articles" and omits the closing words of s.185(1)(d), "which was included in it at the time the company was incorporated", so the articles limb is stated more widely in the map and in the gold rule than the section allows.

relevant_excerpt: Registration of a charge under this Part shall constitute notice to all persons of the particulars of the charge entered on the register of charges under this section, but not of the contents of the instrument which creates or is evidence of the charge
why_relevant: Because registration of a charge is notice to all persons, the purchaser cannot claim ignorance of a charge registered against a corporate vendor. A search of the Registrar's register of charges, and the certificate of registration and instrument creating any subsisting charge, must be called for in addition to the land registry search, together with a letter of release or vacation of the mortgage on completion.
temporal_note: In force from 2007; no amendment event recorded. In force in October 2024.

relevant_excerpt: Where a company creates a charge to which this section applies, it shall be the duty of the company within the time specified in subsection (3), to cause a copy of the instrument by which the charge is created or evidenced, to be delivered to the Registrar for registration under this Act.
why_relevant: A charge on land or on any interest in land created by a company registered in Sri Lanka is registrable, so the register of charges is the right place to look for a mortgage granted by a corporate vendor. It tells the lawyer which company filings to call for.
temporal_note: In force from 2007; no amendment event recorded. In force in October 2024.

formal_title: Western Province Financial Statute No. 6 of 1990
relevant_excerpt: No instrument chargeable with stamp duty shall be received or admitted in evidence by any person having by law or consent of parties authority to receive evidence or registered or authenticated or acted upon by any person or by any officer in a public office or corporation or bank or approved credit agency unless such instrument is duly stamped
why_relevant: The land is in Colombo, in the Western Province. An instrument that is not duly stamped cannot be registered or acted upon, so each deed in the chain must be inspected for the stamp or the endorsement of payment, and the stamp duty receipts and endorsements must be called for with the deeds.
temporal_note: In force from 1990; no amendment event recorded on this section in the corpus. A verifier should note that the corpus holds no later Western Province statute, so only the admissibility rule and not the current rate is relied on.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but s.60 carries a proviso under which such an instrument may still be admitted in evidence and, where the duty chargeable is Rs. 5,000 or less, acted upon by the Registrar-General on payment of the proper duty and a penalty; why_relevant and the gold rule state the bar as absolute.

relevant_excerpt: No plan or map or copy or tracing of a plan or map shall be receivable in evidence in any court in Sri Lanka unless such plan or map has been prepared
why_relevant: Ten perches has to be identified on the ground and matched to the description in the deeds. Only a plan prepared or certified by the Surveyor-General, an authorised registered surveyor or a registered licensed surveyor is receivable in evidence, so the survey plan and, where the identity of the land is in doubt, a fresh survey by a registered licensed surveyor must be called for.
temporal_note: In force from 2002; no amendment event recorded. In force in October 2024.

relevant_excerpt: No building constructed after the date of the commencement of this Ordinance shall be occupied, except by a caretaker, until the Council has given a certificate that such building, as regards construction, drainage, and other respects conforms to the provisions of this Ordinance and to the by-laws made thereunder.
why_relevant: The subject of the purchase is an office building in a Municipality. It cannot lawfully be occupied without the Council's certificate of conformity, so the approved building plan and the certificate of conformity are documents the purchaser must call for before parting with the price.
temporal_note: In force from 1947, amended in 1986. The amended text long predates the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: be a first charge on the premises in respect of which the same are incurred or made, and shall be paid to the Council by the owner of such premises and his successors in title
why_relevant: Council expenses of this kind rank with the rates as a first charge on the premises and are payable by successors in title, so they pass to the purchaser. Rates and assessment receipts to date and a Council statement showing that nothing is outstanding must therefore be called for.
temporal_note: In force from 1947; no amendment event recorded on this section. In force in October 2024.

formal_title: Urban Development Authority Law No. 41 of 1978
relevant_excerpt: no Government agency or any other person shall carry out or engage in any development activity in any development area or part thereof, except under the authority, and in accordance with the terms and conditions, of a permit issued in that behalf by the Authority
why_relevant: If the premises are in a declared development area, the building had to be put up under a permit and in conformity with it. The permit, the approved plan and any clearance about street lines and building limits are called for both to confirm the building is authorised and to see what the company may lawfully do with the premises afterwards.
temporal_note: In force from 1978, amended in 1982. The amended text long predates the matter date.

formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
relevant_excerpt: shall apply to such Province, Administrative District or Administrative Division as the Minister may from time to time, by Order published in the Gazette, specify as an area to which this Act shall apply
why_relevant: Title registration applies only to areas declared by Order, so the first thing the lawyer establishes is which system governs the land. If the land is in a declared area the documents called for change; on these facts the land is on the deeds register, which is why the deed chain and folio extract are the operative documents.
temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment event recorded. In force in October 2024.

formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
relevant_excerpt: Any person, having a Title of Ownership or other interest in a land parcel registered under this Act, may on payment of the prescribed fee, obtain a Certificate of Title in respect of such Ownership or interest, from the appropriate Registrar of Title.
why_relevant: Where the land parcel is registered under the title system the Certificate of Title is conclusive evidence of title, and it, rather than the deed chain, is the document to be called for. Recorded as background because on these facts the land is not in a declared area.
temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment event recorded. In force in October 2024.

formal_title: Powers of Attorney Ordinance No. 4 of 1902
relevant_excerpt: Every power of attorney executed in Sri Lanka or any other country shall be registered with the Registrar General.
why_relevant: One deed in the chain was signed by an attorney and not by the owner. The power of attorney under which he acted, its registration particulars and evidence that it had not been revoked at the date of that deed must be called for, because a deed signed without a subsisting authority breaks the chain.
temporal_note: The section was repealed and substituted by the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022, so the text quoted is the text in force in October 2024. The 1994 deed in the chain was governed by the earlier text, which a verifier should check separately before treating the current registration duty as applicable to that deed.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but s.3 in this form is the substitution made by the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022 and cannot be applied directly to the 1994 deed; the transitional and validation provisions that govern a pre-2022 power at the matter date (28-2022 s.8 and 3-2024 s.6) were missing and have been added as PROV-M026-902 and PROV-M026-903. The corpus body also carries the subsection (1) marker only as "(a)", an OCR loss.

relevant_excerpt: Where the Minister considers that a particular land is suitable for a public purpose, or that a particular servitude over a particular land should be acquired for a public purpose, he shall direct the acquiring officer of the district in which that land is situated to cause a notice in accordance with subsection (3) to be given to the owner or owners of that land
why_relevant: Land in Colombo may be under notice of intended acquisition, and the notice goes to the owner. The purchaser must therefore call on the vendor to produce any notice received and obtain confirmation from the acquiring officer that no acquisition proceeding affects the land, since an acquisition would defeat the purpose of the purchase.
temporal_note: In force from 1950, amended in 1964. The amended text long predates the matter date.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and supports the point that a notice of intended acquisition is given to the owner, but s.4 creates no right to obtain confirmation from the acquiring officer that no acquisition proceeding affects the land, which is the document the answer actually calls for; that step is conveyancing practice, not this section.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: it shall be the duty of the Registrar of Lands to confirm himself whether the foreign shareholding of such company is less than fifty per cent, by requiring the secretary of such company to submit documentary proof
why_relevant: This is the provision that actually puts the purchaser company's shareholding documents on the list. The Registrar of Lands may not register a transfer caught by s.2 unless satisfied that it complies with the Act, and where the transferee is a Sri Lankan company with foreign shareholding below fifty per cent the Registrar must require the company secretary to produce documentary proof of that shareholding. The map cited only ss.2 and 3, which state the prohibition and the exemptions but require no document.
temporal_note: In force from 2014; the corpus records no amendment event on s.4. In force in October 2024.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier: the link between the foreign shareholding prohibition and the documents called for on the purchaser's side.

formal_title: Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022
relevant_excerpt: every power of attorney executed prior to the date of commencement of this Act which has not been registered under the provisions of section 3 of the principal enactment and which has not been revoked or cancelled on or prior to the date of commencement of this Act, shall, within a period of six months from the date of commencement of this Act, be submitted for registration to the Registrar General
why_relevant: The chain contains a 1994 deed signed under a power of attorney. The registration duty in s.3 of the Ordinance is the 2022 substitution and does not apply of its own force to a power granted in 1994; this transitional provision is what carries an unregistered pre-2022 power into the current regime, and subsection (2) deems it null and void if it was not submitted for registration in time. It is the provision that tells the purchaser's lawyer what to ask about that power and what the answer costs.
temporal_note: In force from 2022; the Act carries only a short title, so it operated from the date it became an Act. Its effect on pre-25 October 2022 powers is modified by the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 3 of 2024 s.6, recorded as PROV-M026-903.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier: the temporal bridge PROV-M026-021 needed for the 1994 deed.

formal_title: Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 3 of 2024
relevant_excerpt: every power of attorney executed prior to October 25, 2022 and which has not been registered on or prior to the date of commencement of this Act shall be deemed to be valid for a period of two years from October 25, 2022, and be submitted for registration to the Registrar General within such period of two years
why_relevant: This fixes the deadline that matters on these facts. An unregistered power executed before 25 October 2022 is deemed valid only for two years from that date, that is until 25 October 2024, and is null and void afterwards. Completion is intended for October 2024, so whether the 1994 power was registered, and when, is a question the purchaser's lawyer must put and document before that date rather than a formality.
temporal_note: In force from 2024; the Act carries only a short title, so it operated from the date it became an Act. The two-year period it creates runs from 25 October 2022 and expires in the month of the matter reference date.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier: decisive temporal provision for the power of attorney limb at an October 2024 completion.

formal_title: Powers of Attorney Ordinance No. 4 of 1902
relevant_excerpt: submit such document referred to in paragraph (b) to the Registrar General, to register the same in the relevant volume and folio with cross reference to the volume and folio in which such power of attorney was registered
why_relevant: The answer calls for evidence that the power of attorney had not been revoked when the 1994 deed was signed, an element no cited provision supported. This is the provision that makes such evidence obtainable: a revocation or cancellation must be executed before a notary and registered in the relevant volume and folio with a cross reference to the folio in which the power was registered, so the registry search is where the absence of a revocation is established.
temporal_note: The section was substituted by Act No. 28 of 2022 and amended again by Act No. 3 of 2024, so the text quoted is the text in force in October 2024; the revocation regime in 1994 was different and a lawyer should check the position for that deed separately.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier: supports the 'unrevoked at that date' element of CL-M026-Q01-021.

relevant_excerpt: shall be in force or avail in law unless - (a) the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary;
why_relevant: A lease of an apartment for three years is an agreement affecting immovable property outside the 'lease at will or for any period not exceeding one month' exclusion, so it is of no force in law unless it is in writing, signed by every executant or by a person duly authorised by the executant, together with the witnesses, in the presence of a licenced notary and attested by that notary. This both compels notarial execution and supplies the route by which Shantha may sign through an authorised person.
temporal_note: Section 2 was last amended in 2024 (Act No. 4 of 2024) and in 2022 (Act No. 30 of 2022); the corpus text is the consolidated version. Commencement dates are not in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: (12) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless the person executing the same and the witnesses shall have signed the same in his presence and in the presence of one another, and unless he shall have signed the same in the presence of the executant and of the attesting witnesses.
why_relevant: Fixes the core execution requirement: the executant and the witnesses must sign in the notary's presence and in the presence of one another. This is why Shantha cannot simply post a signed agreement to Kanthi.
temporal_note: Section in the consolidated Notaries Ordinance text; the corpus records the latest change as 2024 (Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024). The corpus carries years only, not commencement dates, so the verifier should confirm that the 2024 text was in force by October 2024.

relevant_excerpt: (22) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any area other than that in which he is authorized to practice, nor in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice nor authenticate or attest any deed or instrument drawn in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice.
why_relevant: A notary may not attest a deed in any area other than the area in which she is authorised to practise. Kanthi practises in Colombo, so if the Negombo area lies outside her authorised area she cannot travel to Negombo and attest Shantha's signature there.
temporal_note: Section in the consolidated Notaries Ordinance text; the corpus records the latest change as 2024 (Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024). The corpus carries years only, not commencement dates, so the verifier should confirm that the 2024 text was in force by October 2024.

relevant_excerpt: (25) Where any deed or instrument is executed or acknowledged before more than one notary- (a) the notary who first attests such deed or instrument shall comply with all the requirements of rule (20), and every other notary attesting such deed or instrument shall comply with the requirements of paragraphs (a) to (e) of the aforesaid rule
why_relevant: Expressly contemplates a deed or instrument executed or acknowledged before more than one notary and allocates the attestation duties between the first attesting notary and every other attesting notary. This is the statutory basis for Shantha signing before a notary where he is and Ananda signing before Kanthi in Colombo.
temporal_note: Section in the consolidated Notaries Ordinance text; the corpus records the latest change as 2024 (Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024). The corpus carries years only, not commencement dates, so the verifier should confirm that the 2024 text was in force by October 2024.

relevant_excerpt: (2) In the case of any deed or instrument which is to be executed by two or more parties, both or all of whom, as the case may be, do not sign the deed or instrument at the same time and place- (i) the deed or instrument shall, for the purposes of the application of rules (6), (7), (23) and (25) set out in section 31, be deemed to be executed or acknowledged at the time when it is first signed by a party, or by two or more parties at the same time and place;
why_relevant: Deals in terms with a deed to be executed by two or more parties who do not sign at the same time and place, and fixes when the instrument is deemed executed for the purposes of rules (6), (7), (23) and (25). It confirms that split execution is lawful and tells Kanthi which date governs stamping and numbering.
temporal_note: Unamended 1907 text in the corpus; no amendment event recorded, so in force at October 2024.

relevant_excerpt: (30) If he attest any deed or instrument executed before him by means of an attorney, he shall preserve a true copy of the power of attorney with his protocol, and shall forward a like copy with the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands.
why_relevant: If the agreement is executed by an attorney under a power of attorney, the attesting notary must keep a true copy of the power with her protocol and forward a like copy with the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands.
temporal_note: Section in the consolidated Notaries Ordinance text; the corpus records the latest change as 2024 (Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024). The corpus carries years only, not commencement dates, so the verifier should confirm that the 2024 text was in force by October 2024.

subsection: rule (15A), paragraph (c) (inserted by Act No. 31 of 2022; rule number taken from the corpus provision ids for section 31, which label this block sub-15A)
relevant_excerpt: (c) where a deed or instrument is signed by an attorney, such attorney shall submit to the notary an affidavit affirming that the Power of Attorney is genuine and in force and the grantor is alive when executing such deed or instrument;
why_relevant: Where an attorney signs, that attorney must give the notary an affidavit that the power of attorney is genuine and in force and that the grantor is alive at the time of execution. A step Kanthi must take if the power-of-attorney route is used.
temporal_note: Consolidated Notaries Ordinance text; latest recorded change 2022 (Act No. 31 of 2022), before the October 2024 matter date. The corpus carries years only, not commencement dates.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim and the substance is right, but the rule number is recoverable after all: the corpus provision ids for section 31 label this block 1-1907/s31/sub-15A/sub-1/par-c, and section 32(1) independently identifies rule (16) as the boundaries rule, so this is rule (15A), paragraph (c), not an unnumbered rule.

relevant_excerpt: means any written power or authority other than that given to an attorney at law for the purpose of appearing as an attorney at law on behalf of such person, given by one person to another, to represent him, to perform any work, do any act, or carry on any trade or business, and - (a) if it is executed in Sri Lanka, executed before two witnesses and attested by a notary public;
why_relevant: Defines the instrument by which Shantha can authorise another person to sign for him, and requires that a power executed in Sri Lanka be executed before two witnesses and attested by a notary public.
temporal_note: Definition substituted by Act No. 28 of 2022 and amended by Act No. 3 of 2024; the corpus text is the consolidated version. Commencement dates are not in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: (b) Every power of attorney holder (hereinafter referred to as the "attorney") shall submit his power of attorney for registration, if it is executed in Sri Lanka within one month and if it is executed outside Sri Lanka within three months, from the date of execution of the power of attorney
why_relevant: A power of attorney executed in Sri Lanka must be submitted to the Registrar-General for registration within one month of execution, with a notarially certified copy and an affidavit. A dated step in the power-of-attorney route.
temporal_note: Section 3 was repealed and substituted by Act No. 28 of 2022, before the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: (1) A power of attorney granted to be used for the purpose of a transaction which falls within the scope of section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance (Chapter 70) shall be executed subject to the provisions specified in subsection (2) or (3), as the case may be.
why_relevant: A power of attorney granted for a transaction within section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance - which this three-year lease is - must satisfy the additional formal requirements in section 3A(2) or (3), including a description of the condominium parcel and the prior registration reference.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 28 of 2022, before the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: (a) examine the relevant volumes and folios in the Registrar General's department; (b) be satisfied that the power of attorney has not been revoked or cancelled and shall state such fact in his attestation:
why_relevant: Puts a personal duty on the attesting notary to examine the Registrar-General's volumes and folios, to satisfy herself that the power of attorney has not been revoked or cancelled, and to say so in the attestation.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 28 of 2022, before the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: (30A) It shall be the duty of every notary to submit for registration to the Registrar, every deed or instrument attested by him before the expiry of thirty days from the date of attestation thereof: Provided that, where such deed or instrument is required to be registered outside the jurisdiction in which he is practicing, he shall submit such deed or instrument for registration before the expiry of sixty days from the date of attestation.
why_relevant: The registration deadline: every deed attested must be submitted for registration within thirty days of attestation, or sixty days where it has to be registered outside the jurisdiction in which the notary practises. The apartment is in Negombo and Kanthi practises in Colombo, so the sixty-day limb is the one in issue.
temporal_note: Consolidated Notaries Ordinance text; latest recorded change 2022 (Act No. 31 of 2022), before the October 2024 matter date. The corpus carries years only, not commencement dates.

relevant_excerpt: (i) He shall deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which he resides the following documents, so that they shall reach the registrar on or before the fifteenth day of every month, namely, the duplicate of every deed or instrument (except wills and codicils) executed or acknowledged before or attested by him during the preceding month, together with a list in duplicate, signed by him, of all such deeds or instruments, which list shall be substantially in the Form F 1 in the Second Schedule
why_relevant: Requires the duplicate of every deed attested during a month, with a signed list in duplicate in Form F1, to reach the Registrar of Lands of the district in which the notary resides on or before the fifteenth day of the following month. Rule (26) is identified by number in section 21(1)(d) and section 34(2).
temporal_note: Section in the consolidated Notaries Ordinance text; the corpus records the latest change as 2024 (Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024). The corpus carries years only, not commencement dates, so the verifier should confirm that the 2024 text was in force by October 2024.

relevant_excerpt: such notary, or in case such deed or instrument is attested by two or more notaries, then the notary upon whom is cast the duty of transmitting to the Registrar of Lands the duplicate of such deed or instrument, shall on or before the fifteenth day of the month next following that in which the same was executed (besides transmitting the duplicate in manner aforesaid) deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which such land shall be situated a copy thereof certified by him as correct
why_relevant: Where the deed affects land in a district other than the district in which the attesting notary resides, a certified copy must also be sent to the Registrar of Lands of the district where the land is situated by the fifteenth of the following month. Kanthi resides and practises in Colombo; the apartment is in Negombo.
temporal_note: Unamended 1907 text in the corpus; no amendment event recorded, so in force at October 2024.

formal_title: Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross Ingratitude Act
relevant_excerpt: An irrevocable deed of gift may be revoked on the ground of gross ingratitude, only on an Order made by a competent court, in an action filed by the donor of such deed against the donee to have the said deed revoked.
why_relevant: States the only statutory ground on which an irrevocable deed of gift can be revoked (gross ingratitude) and the only route (an order of a competent court in an action by the donor against the donee). It rules out unilateral revocation by the father where the deed is irrevocable.
temporal_note: In force from 2017; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. Applies at the matter reference date 2024-10. The deed in the enriched scenario was executed in 2019, after the Act came into operation.

formal_title: Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross Ingratitude Act
relevant_excerpt: Court shall not entertain an action referred to in section 2, unless it is filed within a period of ten years from the date of the execution of such deed of gift and within two years from the date on which the cause of action arose.
why_relevant: Imposes two cumulative time bars on the revocation action. Even a good ground of gross ingratitude fails if either limit has passed, so the father's ability to revoke turns on it.
temporal_note: In force from 2017; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. Applies at 2024-10.

formal_title: Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross Ingratitude Act
relevant_excerpt: The plaintiff in an action instituted under the provisions of this Act shall file or cause to be filed in court with the plaint, an application for registration of lis pendens
why_relevant: Mandatory procedural step for the donor who sues to revoke: the lis pendens application must be filed with the plaint, addressed to the Registrar of Lands of the district where the deed is registered or, if unregistered, where the land lies.
temporal_note: In force from 2017; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. Applies at 2024-10.

formal_title: Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross Ingratitude Act
relevant_excerpt: Every action filed under the provisions of this Act shall be proceeded with and regulated by the procedure provided for in the Civil Procedure Code (Chapter 101).
why_relevant: Confirms that the revocation claim is an ordinary civil action governed by the Civil Procedure Code, so the father must prove the ground in a regular trial rather than by an administrative or notarial act.
temporal_note: In force from 2017; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. Applies at 2024-10.

formal_title: Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross Ingratitude Act

why_relevant: The Act's only interpretation section. It defines 'Registrar of Lands' and 'land' and defines no other term; in particular it gives no statutory meaning to 'gross ingratitude', which is why the content of the ground has to be found outside the Act.
temporal_note: In force from 2017; no amendment events recorded in the corpus. Applies at 2024-10. The corpus text of this section is lightly garbled (the defined terms are carried in a defined_terms field rather than inline), so the verifier should read it against the Gazette text.

relevant_excerpt: shall bind a purchaser, unless and until the lis pendens is duly registered under this Chapter
