temporal_note: In force from 1927, latest recorded change 1947; in force at 2024-10.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary in any other written law, the transfer of title of any land situated in Sri Lanka, shall be prohibited if such transfer is- (a) to a foreigner; or (b) to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act where any foreign shareholding in such company, either direct or indirect, is fifty per cent or above; or (c) to a foreign company, unless exempted as provided in section 3.
why_relevant: This is the operative prohibition. It bars the very transaction the client proposes - the transfer of title of private land in Sri Lanka to a person who is not a citizen - and it is the provision on which the whole advice turns. It also fixes the alternative transferee route (a Sri Lankan company with less than fifty per cent foreign shareholding) and points to the section 3 exemptions.
temporal_note: Section 2 has been in force since the Act commenced in 2014 and carries no amendment event in the corpus consolidation, so the text applies at the matter reference date of October 2024.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: means a person who is not a citizen of Sri Lanka; means a company or a body of persons incorporated under the laws of any country other than Sri Lanka;
why_relevant: The prohibition in section 2 operates on the defined term 'foreigner'. The definition is purely negative - anyone who is not a citizen of Sri Lanka - so the client's nationality, and not his residence, visa status or business purpose, decides whether section 2 catches him. Without this definition the prohibition cannot be applied to him.
temporal_note: Section 25 has been in force since 2014 with no amendment event recorded in the corpus, so it applies at October 2024. Caveat for the verifier: in the corpus text of section 25 the defined terms themselves have been dropped in extraction, so the excerpt reads as two bare 'means ...' clauses; in the printed Act these are the definitions of 'foreigner' and 'foreign company' respectively.
verifier_note: Verified: the corpus metadata for 38-2014/s25 lists twenty defined terms in the same order as the twenty 'means/includes' clauses in the body, and the ninth and tenth clauses are 'foreigner' and 'foreign company', so the label loss noted by the researcher does not affect the mapping.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: means any State or private land and includes- (a) any interest in the land; (b) any land covered with water; and (c) any house or building stands on that land; means the Minister to whom the subject of Finance has been assigned; means any sale, donation, gift or any conveyance by or under which the title of such land passes to another person;
why_relevant: The two other defined terms the prohibition depends on. 'Land' covers private as well as State land and extends to any interest in the land and to buildings on it, so a private bare-land purchase for an apartment development is within the Act. 'Transfer' covers any sale or conveyance passing title, which is exactly the deed the client wants attested.
temporal_note: Same section and same commencement as PROV-M030-002; in force at October 2024. The extraction has again dropped the term labels, so the excerpt runs the definitions of 'land', 'Minister' and 'transfer' together.
verifier_note: Verified on the same clause-to-term alignment as PROV-M030-002: clauses fifteen, sixteen and seventeen of 38-2014/s25 are 'land', 'Minister' and 'transfer'.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: (1) The provisions of section 2 shall not apply to- (a) any land the title of which is transferred to a Diplomatic Mission of another State within the meaning of the Diplomatic Privileges Act or to an International, Multilateral or Bilateral Organization recognized in terms of that Act; (b) a condominium parcel specified under the Apartment Ownership Law: Provided that, the entire value shall be paid upfront through an inward foreign remittance prior to the execution of the relevant deed of transfer;
why_relevant: The exception the advice must be checked against. Paragraph (b) is the one route by which a foreigner may take freehold title in an apartment context - a condominium parcel under the Apartment Ownership Law, and then only if the entire value is remitted from abroad before the deed is executed. The remaining paragraphs (dual citizens, next of kin, banks, listed companies) are the exhaustive list against which the client's position must be tested before advising that section 2 bites.
temporal_note: Section 3(1) was amended by the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) (Amendment) Act, No. 21 of 2018, section 2, which substituted paragraph (b) and added paragraph (i). The corpus text is the consolidated post-2018 text, which is the text in force at October 2024. The verifier should note that the corpus body of 21-2018 section 2 is truncated and does not itself show the substituted paragraph (b).

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: (a) For the purpose of maintaining the legal validity of a transfer of land to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act, with less than fifty per cent of foreign shareholding, the foreign shareholding of such company shall remain less than fifty per cent, for a minimum period of consecutive twenty (20) years from the date of such transfer.
why_relevant: Qualifies the corporate route. If the client is advised to acquire through a Sri Lankan company, the sub-fifty per cent foreign shareholding is not a one-off test at the date of the deed; it must be held for twenty consecutive years, failing which the transfer becomes void. This is the most important warning to give a client who is told he may buy through a local company.
temporal_note: Part of section 2, in force from 2014, unamended in the corpus consolidation; applies at October 2024.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but two corrections: the corpus body of 38-2014/s2 carries no '(2)' subsection marker before this paragraph, and the voidness consequence relied on in why_relevant sits in paragraph (b), not paragraph (a), and is subject to provisos allowing a company to cure a breach within twelve months (listed) or six months (unlisted); no excerpt of paragraph (b) is in the map.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary in any other written law, the leasing of a land- (a) to a foreigner; or (b) to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act, where any foreign shareholding in such company, either direct or indirect, is fifty per cent or above; or (c) to a foreign company, shall be effected subject to the payment of the Land Lease Tax imposed under section 6: Provided however, the maximum tenure of any such lease shall not exceed ninety nine years.
why_relevant: The principal lawful alternative. A foreigner who cannot take title may take a lease, capped at ninety-nine years, which is long enough to support an apartment development. This is the constructive half of the advice.
temporal_note: In force from 2014 and unamended in the corpus consolidation, but it must be read with section 5A, which has since removed the Land Lease Tax from leases executed on or after 1 January 2016.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: the provisions relating to the Land Lease Tax shall not apply to a lease of any land- (a) to a foreigner; or (b) to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act, where any foreign shareholding in such company, either direct or indirect, is fifty per cent or above; or (c) to a foreign company, under and indenture of lease executed on or after January 1, 2016
why_relevant: Removes the cost objection to the lease route. The Land Lease Tax referred to in section 5(1) is not charged on an indenture of lease executed on or after 1 January 2016, so a lease taken in 2024 attracts no Land Lease Tax.
temporal_note: Section 5A was inserted by the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) (Amendment) Act, No. 3 of 2017, section 2 and further amended by Act, No. 21 of 2018, section 3. It is in force from 2017, before the matter reference date of October 2024, and it operates on leases executed on or after 1 January 2016.
verifier_note: Verified including the temporal chain: section 5A was inserted by 3-2017 s.2 with effect from January 8, 2017 and that date was substituted by 21-2018 s.3 with January 1, 2016, so the corpus text is the text in force at October 2024.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: Any alienation of land effected in contravention of the provisions of this Act, shall be void and shall have no effect in law.
why_relevant: The consequence that makes the advice urgent. A deed of transfer taken in the teeth of section 2 is not merely unregistrable; it is void, so the client would pay the price and acquire nothing. This is what the attorney and notary must tell the client before any deed is drawn.
temporal_note: In force from 2014 and unamended in the corpus consolidation; applies at October 2024.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: The Registrar of Lands shall not register an instrument effecting any transfer of title referred to in section 2, under the provisions of the Registration of Documents Ordinance, unless such registrar of lands is satisfied that such transfer is in compliance with the provisions of this Act.
why_relevant: The practical bar at the registry. Even if a deed were executed, the Registrar of Lands must refuse registration unless satisfied that the transfer complies with the Act, so the client would also be left with an unregistrable instrument.
temporal_note: In force from 2014 and unamended in the corpus consolidation; applies at October 2024.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: Any land transferred or leased to a person or a company referred to in section 2(1) or 5(1), after the date on which the certificate of the speaker is endorsed in respect of this Act, shall not for any purpose be been mortgaged or pledged to any bank licensed under the Banking Act
why_relevant: A funding constraint the client must be warned about if he takes the lease route or acquires through a company with fifty per cent or more foreign shareholding: the land cannot be mortgaged or pledged to a licensed bank for five years from execution of the instrument, which matters to an apartment developer relying on construction finance.
temporal_note: In force from 2014 and unamended in the corpus consolidation; applies at October 2024. The corpus body of this section is visibly corrupted by extraction ('shall not for any purpose be been mortgaged ... for leased to a foreign a period of five years'); the excerpt has been kept short and the five-year period should be confirmed against the printed Act.
verifier_note: The five-year bar and its running from execution of the instrument are legible in the corrupted corpus body and the excerpt is verbatim, but the role is narrower than why_relevant states: section 11(1) bites only on land transferred or leased to a person or company 'referred to in section 2(1) or 5(1)', which does not include a Sri Lankan company whose foreign shareholding is below fifty per cent, so the bar does not reach the corporate route the map recommends.

relevant_excerpt: (4) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other law but subject to the provisions of this Law, after the registration of a Condominium Plan, or Semi Condominium Plan, any condominium parcel depicted therein together with the common elements appurtenant thereto may be held and dealt with in the same manner and form as any land.
why_relevant: Explains what the condominium exemption in section 3(1)(b) of the 2014 Act actually gives a foreign buyer: once a Condominium Plan is registered, each condominium parcel with its share of the common elements may be held and dealt with as land. It also shows why the exemption does not help a purchase of bare land over which no Condominium Plan has been registered.
temporal_note: Section 9 has been in force since 1973 and was last amended in 2003, before the matter reference date of October 2024.
verifier_note: Verified; role raised from supporting to indispensable, because ruling out the section 3(1)(b) condominium exemption is a necessary step in the answer rather than a supporting one.

formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, No. 38 of 2014
relevant_excerpt: (2) The Minister may in consultation with the Minister to whom the subject of lands has been assigned and with the prior written approval of the Cabinet of Ministers, by Order published in the Gazette, exempt any foreign entity engaged in the banking, financial, insurance, maritime, aviation, advanced technology or infrastructure development project identified as a Strategic Development Project, in terms of the provisions of the Strategic Development Projects Act, No. 14 of 2008, from the application of the provisions of section 2.
why_relevant: The discretionary exemption route. It is worth putting to the client, but it is confined to listed sectors and to a project identified as a Strategic Development Project, and it requires a Ministerial Order in the Gazette with prior Cabinet approval, so an ordinary private apartment venture cannot rely on it.
temporal_note: Subsection (2) was not touched by the 2018 amendment, which amended subsection (1) only; in force at October 2024.
verifier_note: Verified; note that section 3 also carries a third Ministerial exemption, in subsection (3), for a foreign company engaged in international commercial operations, which the map does not record.

relevant_excerpt: means a defined space which is shown as an independent parcel on a condominium plan or semi condominium plan or provisional condominium plan and which is designed for independent use consisting of one or more rooms whether occupying the entirety or part of one or more storeys in a building of more than one storey and which is shown as a separate condominium parcel
why_relevant: The exemption in section 3(1)(b) of Act, No. 38 of 2014 is expressed in the term 'condominium parcel specified under the Apartment Ownership Law', and this is the definition of that term. It is what makes the exclusion of bare land determinate: a condominium parcel is a defined space shown as an independent parcel on a condominium plan, semi condominium plan or provisional condominium plan, so an allotment of bare land over which no such plan has been registered cannot be a condominium parcel and the exemption cannot be reached.
temporal_note: Section 26 is the interpretation section of the Apartment Ownership Law; the corpus records it as in force from 1973 with its latest change in 2003, both before the matter reference date of October 2024.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier. The research notes rejected 11-1973 s.26 as garbled, but the clause the researcher read as the definition of 'condominium parcel' ('a parcel intended for separate ownership...') is in fact the definition of 'accessory parcel'; the corpus defined-term order places 'condominium parcel' immediately after 'Condominium Plan', and that clause is clean and verbatim.

relevant_excerpt: Before any deed or instrument (other than a will or codicil) affecting any interest in land or other immovable property is drawn by him, he shall search or cause to be searched the registers in the land registry to ascertain the state of the title in regard to such land and whether any prior deed affecting any interest in such land has been registered
why_relevant: Imposes the notary's core pre-drafting duty on a purchase: search the land registry to establish the state of the vendor's title and prior registered dealings.
temporal_note: Section 31 stands in the corpus in its consolidated form. The rules relied on here were last substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022, in force before April 2024. Act No. 6 of 2024 also touched section 31, but only in points of detail not relied on here; the corpus records amendment years only, so the exact commencement of Act No. 6 of 2024 relative to April 2024 is unverified.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but the corpus body of section 31 does not print the rule number: 'rule (17)(a)' is reconstructed from the section's structure, and the duty is subject to a proviso allowing the parties to dispense with the search in writing, now recorded as PROV-M032-901.

relevant_excerpt: he shall obtain from the Registrar of the relevant Land Registry the certified extract of the folio containing the last entry pertaining to such land or immovable property containing the ownership and the registered encumbrances relating to such land or immovable property
why_relevant: Specifies the documentary output of the search: a certified folio extract showing ownership and registered encumbrances, which is how the mortgage over the estate would surface.
temporal_note: Section 31 stands in the corpus in its consolidated form. The rules relied on here were last substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022, in force before April 2024. Act No. 6 of 2024 also touched section 31, but only in points of detail not relied on here; the corpus records amendment years only, so the exact commencement of Act No. 6 of 2024 relative to April 2024 is unverified.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument, other than a will or codicil, affecting land or other immovable property, unless the deed or instrument embodies therin or in a Schedule annexed therto an accurate and clear description of the said land or other property affected thereby, showing its boundaries, extent, situation specifying the district, pattu, korale, Divisional Secretary's Division, local authority division and the Grama Niladari Division
why_relevant: Governs the schedule to the conveyance: the thirty-acre estate must be described by boundaries, extent and administrative situation, which is why a survey plan is called for.
temporal_note: Section 31 stands in the corpus in its consolidated form. The rules relied on here were last substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022, in force before April 2024. Act No. 6 of 2024 also touched section 31, but only in points of detail not relied on here; the corpus records amendment years only, so the exact commencement of Act No. 6 of 2024 relative to April 2024 is unverified.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and the role is right, but the label 'rule (16)(a)' is reconstructed from the section's structure and why_relevant overstates the rule: it requires boundaries, extent and administrative situation but does not itself require a survey plan.

relevant_excerpt: When a deed transferring any immovable property is executed or acknowledged before a notary, he shall use his best endeavours to obtain the title deed, if any, of such property, and make an endorsement thereon stating the number and date of the deed executed before him and the nature of the transaction and attach his signature thereto,
why_relevant: Requires the notary to call for and endorse the vendor's title deed on a transfer, which is the statutory anchor for taking the prior deeds into his hands.
temporal_note: Section 31 stands in the corpus in its consolidated form. The rules relied on here were last substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022, in force before April 2024. Act No. 6 of 2024 also touched section 31, but only in points of detail not relied on here; the corpus records amendment years only, so the exact commencement of Act No. 6 of 2024 relative to April 2024 is unverified.

relevant_excerpt: It shall be the duty of every notary to endeavour to ascertain the true and full consideration for the execution of any deed, and to insert and set forth the same in such deed.
why_relevant: Requires the true purchase price, including any advance already paid, to be ascertained and stated in the deed.
temporal_note: In force since 1907; the fine in subsection (2) reflects later increases. Unaffected by the 2024 amendment.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless he has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided.
why_relevant: Bars attestation until stamp duty on the conveyance is provided for, making stamp duty one of the notary's pre-execution steps.
temporal_note: Section 31 stands in the corpus in its consolidated form. The rules relied on here were last substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022, in force before April 2024. Act No. 6 of 2024 also touched section 31, but only in points of detail not relied on here; the corpus records amendment years only, so the exact commencement of Act No. 6 of 2024 relative to April 2024 is unverified.

relevant_excerpt: any stamp duty which is required to be paid in respect of every deed or instrument executed under any written law, shall be paid by the notary
why_relevant: Places the mechanics of paying and evidencing stamp duty on the notary himself.
temporal_note: Rule (7A) was inserted by Act No. 31 of 2022; paragraph (a) was widened by Act No. 6 of 2024 from transfers, gifts and exchanges to every deed. A deed of transfer is caught either way, but the corpus records only amendment years, so the April 2024 wording is unverified.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but the label 'rule (7A)(a)' is not printed in the corpus body (the paragraph runs on directly after rule (7)), and the 'every deed or instrument' wording is attributed to Act No. 6 of 2024, whose commencement relative to April 2024 cannot be established from the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless one of the executants to the deed or instrument or the two attesting witnesses be known to notary or by the identity of the executants to a deed or instrument is established by such notary by inspection of the national identity card, bio-page of the passport or the driving licence of such executants
why_relevant: Requires the notary to establish the identity of the vendor and purchaser and to satisfy himself about the witnesses before attesting.
temporal_note: Section 31 stands in the corpus in its consolidated form. The rules relied on here were last substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022, in force before April 2024. Act No. 6 of 2024 also touched section 31, but only in points of detail not relied on here; the corpus records amendment years only, so the exact commencement of Act No. 6 of 2024 relative to April 2024 is unverified.

relevant_excerpt: He shall without delay duly attest every deed or instrument which shall be executed or acknowledged before him, and shall sign and seal such attestation.
why_relevant: Fixes the attestation step and, in its paragraphs, the matters the attestation must record, including whether consideration was paid in the notary's presence.
temporal_note: Section 31 stands in the corpus in its consolidated form. The rules relied on here were last substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022, in force before April 2024. Act No. 6 of 2024 also touched section 31, but only in points of detail not relied on here; the corpus records amendment years only, so the exact commencement of Act No. 6 of 2024 relative to April 2024 is unverified.

relevant_excerpt: It shall be the duty of every notary to submit for registration to the Registrar, every deed or instrument attested by him before the expiry of thirty days from the date of attestation thereof
why_relevant: Sets the post-execution step and its deadline: lodging the conveyance for registration within thirty days.
temporal_note: Section 31 stands in the corpus in its consolidated form. The rules relied on here were last substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022, in force before April 2024. Act No. 6 of 2024 also touched section 31, but only in points of detail not relied on here; the corpus records amendment years only, so the exact commencement of Act No. 6 of 2024 relative to April 2024 is unverified.
verifier_note: Wording and thirty-day deadline are verbatim, but the excerpt omits the proviso extending the period to sixty days where the deed must be registered outside the jurisdiction in which the notary practises; on these facts the land and the notary are both in Kurunegala, so thirty days is correct.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any area other than that in which he is authorized to practice, nor in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice
why_relevant: Limits which notary may attest the deed; the notary must confirm the transaction falls inside his authorised area and language before accepting the retainer.
temporal_note: Section 31 stands in the corpus in its consolidated form. The rules relied on here were last substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022, in force before April 2024. Act No. 6 of 2024 also touched section 31, but only in points of detail not relied on here; the corpus records amendment years only, so the exact commencement of Act No. 6 of 2024 relative to April 2024 is unverified.

relevant_excerpt: deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which such land shall be situated a copy thereof certified by him as correct
why_relevant: Background: had the notary resided outside the district in which the estate lies, he would additionally have to transmit a certified copy to the Kurunegala land registry. On the enriched facts he practises in that district, so the rule is not engaged.
temporal_note: Section 31 stands in the corpus in its consolidated form. The rules relied on here were last substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022, in force before April 2024. Act No. 6 of 2024 also touched section 31, but only in points of detail not relied on here; the corpus records amendment years only, so the exact commencement of Act No. 6 of 2024 relative to April 2024 is unverified.

relevant_excerpt: the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary
why_relevant: Explains why a notary is needed at all: a sale of land has no force in law unless it is in writing, signed before and attested by a notary.
temporal_note: Section 2 was renumbered and paragraph (a) substituted by Act No. 4 of 2024; the requirement of notarial writing and attestation is unchanged since 1840. The corpus records years only, so the precise April 2024 wording is unverified; the substance relied on predates 2024.
verifier_note: Subsection (1)(a) is verbatim and correctly placed, but the map omits section 2(1)(b) (thumb impressions) and section 2(2)(a), which requires the transferee as well as the transferor to sign a transfer deed; that paragraph is added as PROV-M032-905. Section 2 was also touched by Act No. 4 of 2024, whose commencement relative to April 2024 cannot be established from the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: be void as against all parties claiming an adverse interest thereto on valuable consideration by virtue of any subsequent instrument which is duly registered under this Chapter
why_relevant: Supplies the reason the search and prompt registration matter: priority between competing instruments turns on registration, not on date of execution.
temporal_note: In force since 1927 and unamended in the corpus for the point relied on.

relevant_excerpt: all duplicates and copies and all books and indexes kept under this Ordinance may be searched and examined by any person claiming to be interested therein or by his attorney-at-law or agent duly authorized thereto in writing, and certified copies of or extracts from any such duplicate, copy, or book may be obtained if required
why_relevant: Gives the notary, as the purchaser's agent, the right of access to the registry books and to the certified extracts that rule (17) obliges him to obtain.
temporal_note: In force since 1927; no amendment recorded in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: A priority notice shall remain in force for six weeks from the date of registration of the notice
why_relevant: Supports the protective step of lodging a priority notice between the search and execution, so that an instrument later registered relates back to the notice.
temporal_note: In force since 1927; no amendment recorded in the corpus.
verifier_note: Subsection (5) is verbatim but supplies only the six-week currency of the notice; the relation-back the answer relies on is in section 30(2), added as PROV-M032-904.

relevant_excerpt: if such land does not consist exclusively of paddy land, be fifty acres, so however that the total extent of any paddy land, if any, comprised in such fifty acres shall not exceed the ceiling on paddy land specified in paragraph (a)
why_relevant: Sets the ceiling the notary must test the purchase against, because a purchase pushing the buyer's agricultural holding over the ceiling would vest the excess in the Commission.
temporal_note: In force since 1972, last amended in 1981; well before the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: Every grant issued under subsection (4) shall contain the conditions that the owner of the holding shall not (a) dispose of a divided portion, or an undivided share of the holding which is less in extent than the unit of the sub-division or the minimum fraction specified in the grant; and (b) dispose of such holding except with the prior approval of the Government Agent.
why_relevant: Identifies the statutory restriction the notary must exclude: if the estate were held on a state grant, the vendor could not convey without prior approval.

relevant_excerpt: there shall be charged a duty (hereinafter to be called "stamp duty") at such rate as the Minister may determine by Order published in the Gazette on every "specified instrument"- (a) executed, drawn or presented in Sri Lanka
why_relevant: Background: the charging provision behind the notary's stamping duties. The rate itself is fixed by Ministerial Order, which is not in the corpus.
temporal_note: In force since 2006; no amendment recorded in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: to endeavour to ascertain the true legal nature of the transaction between the parties and execute the deed or instrument for the true transaction
why_relevant: Requires the notary to satisfy himself that an outright purchase is what the parties really intend, and to explain the deed to them before signature.
temporal_note: Section 38A was inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 6 of 2024. The corpus records the year only, so it cannot be confirmed that it was in force in April 2024. Treated as supporting and not relied on as indispensable.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: The transfer of ownership of a tea or rubber estate on or after the appointed day shall, subject to the provisions of subsections (2) and (3), be null and void unless- (a) a certificate of consent of the Board to such transfer has been previously obtained by the transferor
why_relevant: Background: the consent regime for a plantation transfer is confined to tea and rubber, so a coconut estate needs no Board certificate. Recorded so the verifier can see the point was checked, not missed.
temporal_note: In force since 1958; no amendment recorded in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: Provided that if the parties to the transaction authorize the notary in writing to dispense with the search, the search shall not be compulsory, but he shall before the deed or instrument is tendered for registration write at the head thereof the reference to the previous registration, if any.
why_relevant: The exception to the pre-drafting search duty the map relied on: the search is not compulsory if the parties authorise the notary in writing to dispense with it, in which case he must instead write the reference to the previous registration at the head of the deed. Added by the verifier because an indispensable duty was stated without its proviso.
temporal_note: Part of the consolidated section 31; the proviso is of long standing and is not attributed to the 2024 amendment in the corpus.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked verbatim against 1-1907/s31.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument to which at least two witnesses have not subscribed their signatures in letters.
why_relevant: Supplies the two-witness requirement that the gold answer's execution step asserts; the map had cited only rule (9), which deals with identity and the repute of witnesses, not with their number.
temporal_note: Rule (8) is of long standing in the consolidated section 31 and is not attributed to the 2024 amendment in the corpus.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked verbatim against 1-1907/s31.

relevant_excerpt: unless and until he shall have read over and explained the same, or caused the same to be explained, in the presence and hearing of such person and, except in the case of wills and codicils, in the presence of the attesting witnesses.
why_relevant: Supplies the reading-over step the gold answer asserts. The duty is conditional: it bites where the executant is or professes to be unable to read the deed or requires the notary to read it over. Rule (20)(d) separately requires the attestation to state whether the deed was read over.
temporal_note: Rule (11) is of long standing in the consolidated section 31 and is not attributed to the 2024 amendment in the corpus.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked verbatim against 1-1907/s31. Note the duty is conditional, so the gold answer's flat 'read over and explain the deed' is wider than the rule.

relevant_excerpt: such instrument shall, for the purposes of this Ordinance, be deemed to have been registered at the time of registration of the priority notice.
why_relevant: Supplies the relation-back effect of a priority notice that the answer relies on; PROV-M032-016 (subsection (5)) gives only the six-week currency of the notice.
temporal_note: In force since 1927; no amendment recorded in the corpus.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked verbatim against 23-1927/s30.

relevant_excerpt: both the transferor and the transferee shall affix their signatures and thumb impressions as required by subsection (1)
why_relevant: On a transfer deed the purchaser as well as the vendor must sign and affix a thumb impression. The map recorded only section 2(1)(a), which is framed around the executants generally; this paragraph is what puts the notary's client, the buyer, on the deed.
temporal_note: Subsection (2) stands in the consolidated section 2. Section 2 was touched by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act, No. 4 of 2024, whose commencement relative to April 2024 cannot be established from the corpus.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked verbatim against 7-1840/s2. Its wording may be post-2024, which is the temporal doubt already recorded for PROV-M032-013.

relevant_excerpt: Where after the date of commencement of this Law any person becomes the owner of agricultural land in excess of the ceiling, any such land owned by such person in excess of the ceiling shall as from that date- (a) be deemed to vest in the Commission; and (b) be deemed to be held by that person under a statutory lease from the Commission.
why_relevant: This, not section 3(2), is the vesting consequence for a buyer who exceeds the ceiling by a purchase made after 1972; it is what makes the notary's ceiling check worth doing on this transaction.
temporal_note: In force since 1972, last amended in 1986; well before the matter date.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked verbatim against 1-1972/s5.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: There shall be charged on- (a) every instrument relating to a transfer of situated in the immovable property Western Province; (b) every document presented or filed, in proceedings instituted in any Court of law established by law, in the Western Province of Sri Lanka; (c) every transfer of a motor vehicle effected in Western Province. a stamp duty at the prescribed rate. Different rates may be prescribed in respect of different classes or categories of instruments.
why_relevant: Charging provision for stamp duty on an instrument relating to a transfer of immovable property situated in the Western Province. The premises at Maradana Road, Borella are in the Colombo District of the Western Province, so the deed of gift is charged under this Statute rather than under the general stamp duty enactments. The section fixes liability but leaves the rate to be prescribed.
temporal_note: In force from 1990. The corpus records no amendment event and no later change year on this section, so the text is treated as in force at 2024-04.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: means a sale and shall include a gift or exchange or a conveyance, without consideration, by an executor or administrators of an estate of a deceased to a person beneficially entitled to such property
why_relevant: Brings a gift within the word "transfer" used in the charging section. Without this definition a deed of gift, which passes no consideration, would arguably fall outside section 37.
temporal_note: In force from 1990. No amendment event is recorded on this section in the corpus, so the definition is treated as in force at 2024-04.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: (b) to any immovable property which is gifted, beingi immovable property which was acquired by the donor on or before March 31, 1977 means - (1) the price which in the opinion of the Assessor that property would have fetched if sold in the open market on March 31, 1977 increased by an amount equal to the cost of the improvements, alterations and additions, if any, made to such property after March 31, 1977 and prior to the date of the instrument by which such property is gifted; or (ii) the price which, in the opinion of the Assessor, that property would havefetched if sold in the open market on the date of the instrument by which such property is gifted ; whichever price is the lower ;
why_relevant: Supplies the special valuation rule for gifted immovable property acquired by the donor on or before 31 March 1977. It is this paragraph, not the present market value, that fixes the base on which the duty is calculated: the 1977 open market price increased by the cost of improvements, or the open market price at the date of the deed, whichever is lower.
temporal_note: In force from 1990. No amendment event is recorded on this section in the corpus, so the definition is treated as in force at 2024-04.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: (c) any immovable property which is gifted, being immovable property which was acquired by the donor after March 31, 1977 means - the price which, in the opinion ofthe Assessor, such property would have fetched if sold in the open market on the date which such on property was acquired by the donor, increased by an amount equal to the cost of the improvements, alterations and additions, if any, made to such property after the date on which the property was acquired by the donor, and prior to the date of the instrument by which such property is gifted ; or (ii) the price which, in the opinion of the assessor, that property would have: fetched, if sold in the open market on the date of the instrument by which such property was gifted. whichever price is the lower.
why_relevant: The alternative limb, applying if the 1977 purchase was made after 31 March 1977. The scenario says only "in 1977", so it is not determinate which paragraph governs; both produce the same comparison on these facts, namely acquisition-date price plus improvements against present market value, whichever is lower.
temporal_note: In force from 1990. No amendment event is recorded on this section in the corpus, so the definition is treated as in force at 2024-04.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: means a transfer by one person to another ofany movable or immovable property made voluntarily and without consideration in money or money's worth
why_relevant: Defines a gift for the purposes of the Statute as a voluntary transfer without consideration in money or money's worth. It confirms that the intended instrument is a gift rather than a sale, and it explains why the deed carries no consideration recital.
temporal_note: In force from 1990. No amendment event is recorded on this section in the corpus, so the definition is treated as in force at 2024-04.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: (1) Where any property is conveyed by an instrument, the stamp duty with which such instrument is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property conveyed.
why_relevant: Links the charging section to the defined term: the duty is calculated on the "value" of the property conveyed, which for gifted immovable property is the artificial figure set by the definition in section 106 rather than the open market price of the day.
temporal_note: In force from 1990. No amendment event is recorded on this section in the corpus, so the text is treated as in force at 2024-04.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: Except where there is an agreement to the contrary stamp duty shall be payable; (a) in the case of an instrument of transfer by the grantee;
why_relevant: Identifies the person liable. On an instrument of transfer the duty falls on the grantee, so on this deed of gift the donee Sarathi Perera bears the duty unless the deed provides otherwise.
temporal_note: In force from 1990. No amendment event is recorded on this section in the corpus, so the text is treated as in force at 2024-04.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: The following instruments and documents shall be exempted from the payment of stamp duty:- (1) bail bond in criminal proceedings;
why_relevant: The exemption list is closed and contains no exemption for a gift between family members or for a gift of business premises, so no exemption removes the charge on this deed.
temporal_note: In force from 1990. No amendment event is recorded on this section in the corpus, so the text is treated as in force at 2024-04.

relevant_excerpt: the provisions of the Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982, relating to the Imposition of Stamp Duty (other than any instrument relating to the transfer of immovable property, the transfer of motor vehicles or documents filed in Court), Exemptions and any other provision in the aforesaid Act, shall, in so far as the same are inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, have no operation and the provisions of this Act shall prevail.
why_relevant: Explains why the 2006 Act does not govern this deed: instruments relating to the transfer of immovable property are carved out of the displacement of the earlier stamp duty regime, leaving duty on such transfers to the provincial enactment.
temporal_note: In force from 2006. Section 13 carries no amendment event in the corpus, so it is treated as in force at 2024-04.

relevant_excerpt: All stamp duty payable to a Provincial Council in respect of documents and instruments referred to in List I of the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution, shall be paid to the respective Provincial Council within whose limits the instrument was executed or the property situated as the case may be
why_relevant: Confirms that stamp duty on this class of instrument accrues to the Provincial Council within whose limits the property is situated, which supports treating the Western Province Statute as the governing enactment for property in Borella.
temporal_note: In force from 2006. No amendment event is recorded on this section in the corpus, so the text is treated as in force at 2024-04.

relevant_excerpt: (2) In relation to a transfer deed - (a) both the transferor and the transferee shall affix their signatures and thumb impressions as required by subsection (1)
why_relevant: Requires the transferee, as well as the transferor, to sign a transfer deed, which is the statutory hook for the donee joining in and subscribing the deed of gift. It does not itself prescribe the words of an acceptance clause.
temporal_note: Section 2 carries amendment events in 1947, 2022 and 2024 and subsection (2) reflects the current consolidated text. The corpus dates the 2024 amendment only to the year, so whether subsection (2) was already in force in April 2024 should be checked by the verifier. Nothing in the draft answer turns on the point beyond the donee's signature.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless the person executing the same and the witnesses shall have signed the same in his presence and in the presence of one another, and unless he shall have signed the same in the presence of the executant and of the attesting witnesses.
why_relevant: Governs how the deed, including any clause signed by the donee, must be executed before the notary. It bears on the mechanics of recording the donee's acceptance on the face of the deed but says nothing about the substance of an acceptance clause.
temporal_note: Section 31 has amendment events up to 2024. Rule (12) is not among the rules substituted in 2011, 2022 or 2024, so the quoted text is treated as in force at 2024-04.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: Every person drawing, making, executing or of attesting any instrument chargeable with stamp duty shall set out therein, the full names and addresses of the parties ofs such instrument, the consideration, the date and manner of payment and all other facts and circumstances affecting the chargeability of such instrument with stamp duty and the amount of the stamp duty with which it is chargeable.
why_relevant: Requires the deed itself to set out the parties and all facts and circumstances affecting chargeability, including the amount of duty. It shapes what the drafter must recite in a deed of gift and connects the drafting question to the valuation question.
temporal_note: In force from 1990. No amendment event is recorded on this section in the corpus, so the text is treated as in force at 2024-04.

relevant_excerpt: Save as aforesaid, this Ordinance shall not apply to Kandyans or Muslims, or to Tamils of the Northern Province who are or may become subject to the Tesawalamai.
why_relevant: Fixes the personal-law gateway. The whole devolution below assumes the family is governed by the general law and not by Kandyan law, Muslim law or the Tesawalamai. The background gives no personal-law marker beyond a Nugegoda (Western Province) land, so this is an assumption the verifier must test.
temporal_note: Part III of the Ordinance has stood in this form since 1876; the corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment events, so the text was in force at every death in the chain (2006, 2008, 2012, 2013) and at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: The following sections of this Ordinance shall apply to the estates of such persons only as shall die after the proclamation of this Ordinance
why_relevant: Temporal gateway to Part III. Every death in this chain (2006, 2008, 2012, 2013) is long after proclamation, so Part III governs each intestacy.
temporal_note: Part III of the Ordinance has stood in this form since 1876; the corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment events, so the text was in force at every death in the chain (2006, 2008, 2012, 2013) and at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: Inheritance ab interstate to the immovable property in Sri Lanka of a person deceased shall be governed and regulated by the following provisions of this Ordinance wherever such person may have or have had his actual or matrimonial domicile.
why_relevant: The subject matter is immovable property in Sri Lanka (Assessment No. 3, Alwis Road, Nugegoda), so intestate devolution of every interest in it is governed by Part III of this Ordinance.
temporal_note: Part III of the Ordinance has stood in this form since 1876; the corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment events, so the text was in force at every death in the chain (2006, 2008, 2012, 2013) and at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: When any person shall die intestate as to any of his or her property, leaving a spouse surviving, the surviving spouse shall inherit one-half of the property of such person.
why_relevant: Governs the last death in the chain: Akash died intestate leaving his wife Seena, so Seena takes one-half of Akash's share in the land.
temporal_note: Part III of the Ordinance has stood in this form since 1876; the corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment events, so the text was in force at every death in the chain (2006, 2008, 2012, 2013) and at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: Subject to the right of the surviving spouse in the preceding section mentioned, the right of inheritance is divided in the following order as respects (a) descendants, (b) ascendants, (c) collaterals.
why_relevant: Sets the order in which the remaining half devolves after the spouse's half is taken out, and confirms that the spouse's half under s.22 is carved out first.
temporal_note: Part III of the Ordinance has stood in this form since 1876; the corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment events, so the text was in force at every death in the chain (2006, 2008, 2012, 2013) and at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: Children, grandchildren, and remoter descendants are preferent to all others in the estate of the parents; all the children take equally per capita, but the children or remoter issue of a deceased child take per stirpes or by representation.
why_relevant: Governs Kamal's intestacy in 2012: his surviving children Ravi, Lalani and Akash take his half share equally per capita; Suneth, who predeceased leaving no issue, takes nothing and there is no one to represent him.
temporal_note: Part III of the Ordinance has stood in this form since 1876; the corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment events, so the text was in force at every death in the chain (2006, 2008, 2012, 2013) and at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: The children and remoter descendants failing, the inheritance of the deceased goes to his father and mother in case they are both alive; but if only one of the parents be alive, the surviving parent takes half, and the brothers and sisters of the deceased of the full blood, and the issue of any deceased brother or sister of the full blood, by representation, and the brothers and sisters of the half-blood who are related to the intestate by the side of the deceased parent, and the issue of any such deceased brother or sister of the half-blood, by representation, take the other half.
why_relevant: Governs Suneth's intestacy in 2008. He died unmarried and issueless; his mother Kanthi had predeceased him and his father Kamal survived. Kamal therefore takes one-half; the other half goes to the full-blood siblings Lalani and Akash and to the half-blood sibling related through the deceased parent Kanthi, namely Salinga. Ravi, a half-brother through the surviving parent Kamal, is excluded by the express words of the section.
temporal_note: Part III of the Ordinance has stood in this form since 1876; the corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment events, so the text was in force at every death in the chain (2006, 2008, 2012, 2013) and at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: Father and mother both failing, the property of the intestate goes to his brothers and sisters, whether of the whole or balf-blood, and their children and other issue by representation.
why_relevant: Governs the collateral half of Akash's estate in 2013: both his parents (Kanthi in 2006, Kamal in 2012) were dead, so the half not taken by his widow goes to his brothers and sisters of the whole and half blood.
temporal_note: Part III of the Ordinance has stood in this form since 1876; the corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment events, so the text was in force at every death in the chain (2006, 2008, 2012, 2013) and at the matter reference date 2023-10. The corpus body carries the transcription slip 'balf-blood' for 'half-blood'; the excerpt is reproduced verbatim.

relevant_excerpt: The inheritance is divided into two parts ; the one-half the full brothers and sisters and the issue of such as are deceased by representation divide with the half-brothers and sisters of the father's side and the issue of such as are deceased by representation ; and the other half they divide with those of the mother's side and the issue of such as are deceased by representation
why_relevant: The two-part rule that fixes how the collateral half of Akash's estate is split: half of it is shared by the full sister Lalani with the father's-side half-brother Ravi, and the other half by Lalani with the mother's-side half-brother Salinga. Without this section s.26 does not yield a numerical answer.
temporal_note: Part III of the Ordinance has stood in this form since 1876; the corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment events, so the text was in force at every death in the chain (2006, 2008, 2012, 2013) and at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: but if there are only half-brothers and sisters or such issue of one side, the full brothers and sisters and the issue of deceased full brothers and sisters by representation, take then in the first place one-half of the property, and divide the other half with the half-brothers and sisters and their issue by representation
why_relevant: The one-side proviso, applied to the sibling half of Suneth's estate. Only one half-blood sibling qualifies there (Salinga, on the deceased mother's side), so the full-blood siblings Lalani and Akash take one-half of the sibling half in the first place and divide the remainder with Salinga. This is the most contestable step in the map: it assumes the s.27 proviso governs the sibling half created by s.25 and not only the s.26 case.
temporal_note: Part III of the Ordinance has stood in this form since 1876; the corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment events, so the text was in force at every death in the chain (2006, 2008, 2012, 2013) and at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: Except when otherwise expressly provided, if all those who succeed to the inheritance are equally near in degree to the intestate, they take per capita, and not per stirpes.
why_relevant: Supplies the default equal division inside each class at each step: the children of Kamal take per capita, and the siblings sharing a fraction under ss.25 to 27 take per capita among themselves.
temporal_note: Part III of the Ordinance has stood in this form since 1876; the corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment events, so the text was in force at every death in the chain (2006, 2008, 2012, 2013) and at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: In all questions relating to the distribution of the property of an intestate, if the present Ordinance is silent, the rules of the Roman-Dutch law as it prevailed in North Holland are to govern and be followed.
why_relevant: Marks the boundary of the statutory answer. The Ordinance is silent on the effect of a deed of gift reserving a life interest and on the extinction of that life interest at the death of the life holder, so those steps rest on Roman-Dutch common law that is outside this corpus.
temporal_note: Part III of the Ordinance has stood in this form since 1876; the corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment events, so the text was in force at every death in the chain (2006, 2008, 2012, 2013) and at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: the power of administration, which is authenticated by the grant of probate, or is conveyed by the grant of letters of administration, extends to every portion of the deceased person's property, movable and immovable, within Sri Lanka
why_relevant: Supports the step formed by Testamentary Case No. 1231/2008/T and Administrator's Conveyance No. 2635: the administrator's power over Suneth's immovable property, and therefore his capacity to execute a conveyance out of that estate, is statutory.
temporal_note: In force from 1889; the corpus records a change by Act No. 14 of 1993, well before the 2008 administration and before the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: shall be in force or avail in law unless - (a) the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary
why_relevant: Background only: it explains why the two instruments in the chain (Deed of Gift No. 1663 and Administrator's Conveyance No. 2635) had to be notarially attested, which the facts confirm they were.
temporal_note: The corpus body is the consolidated text carrying the 2022 and 2024 amendments; the 2006 and 2008 deeds were executed under the earlier wording, so this provision is used for context only and nothing in the map turns on the current text.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: means a rubber estate of not less than one hundred acres in extent which, under the Rubber Control Act is or is deemed to be an estate registered under that Act
why_relevant: The consent machinery of the Act bites only on a 'rubber estate' as defined. The definition has two limbs, an extent threshold and registration under the rubber control legislation, so the first step in a rubber estate purchase is to test the subject land against both limbs.
temporal_note: Corpus edition is as_enacted (1958). Act No. 20 of 2005 s.10(b) substituted 'twenty hectares' for 'forty hectares' in this definition, and the corpus records that substitution as not applied to the body text. A 41-acre (about 16.6 hectare) estate is below the threshold on either version, so the classification of the subject land is unaffected at the matter date.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but the corpus body is the as-enacted 1958 text ('one hundred acres'); the text in force at October 2023 reads 'twenty hectares', substituted by Act No. 20 of 2005 s.10(b) for 'forty hectares', and the 16.6-hectare estate falls below either threshold so the classification is unchanged.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: The transfer of ownership of a tea or rubber estate on or after the appointed day shall, subject to the provisions of subsections (2) and (3), be null and void unless- (a) a certificate of consent of the Board to such transfer has been previously obtained by the transferor, and (b) such transfer is effected in accordance with the conditions, if any, subject to which such consent has been granted.
why_relevant: If the land answers the statutory description of a rubber estate, a transfer without the Board's prior certificate of consent is null and void, so the certificate must be obtained by the transferor before the deed is drawn.
temporal_note: In force from 1958; no amendment recorded against s.3 in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: if such land does not consist exclusively of paddy land, be fifty acres, so however that the total extent of any paddy land, if any, comprised in such fifty acres shall not exceed the ceiling on paddy land specified in paragraph (a)
why_relevant: Fixes the ceiling of fifty acres of non-paddy agricultural land per person, against which any proposed acquisition of a rubber estate has to be measured.
temporal_note: Corpus edition is consolidated; the only amendment event recorded against s.3 is Act No. 39 of 1981 s.2 (1981), long before the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: where any agricultural land is owned by a private company or co-operative society, the shareholders of such company, or society, as the case may be, shall be deemed to own such land for the purposes of section 3, in proportion to the shares held by each shareholder
why_relevant: A private company cannot be used to escape the ceiling. Agricultural land bought by a private company is attributed to its shareholders in proportion to their shareholdings, so the ceiling has to be checked shareholder by shareholder, not against the company.
temporal_note: In force from 1972; no amendment event recorded against s.8 in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: Where after the date of commencement of this Law any person becomes the owner of agricultural land in excess of the ceiling, any such land owned by such person in excess of the ceiling shall as from that date- (a) be deemed to vest in the Commission; and (b) be deemed to be held by that person under a statutory lease from the Commission.
why_relevant: This is the sanction that makes the ceiling check a real pre-purchase step: any excess created by the purchase vests in the Commission automatically, so the company would pay for land it could not keep.
temporal_note: Amendment events recorded against s.5 are Act No. 39 of 1981 s.3 and Act No. 14 of 1986 s.2, both long before the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: means land used or capable of being used for agriculture within the meaning given in this Law and shall include private lands
why_relevant: Establishes that a privately owned rubber-planted estate is agricultural land, which is what brings the ceiling provisions into play at all.
temporal_note: Amendment event recorded is Act No. 39 of 1981 s.15 (1981), before the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: the transfer of title of any land situated in Sri Lanka, shall be prohibited if such transfer is- (a) to a foreigner; or (b) to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act where any foreign shareholding in such company, either direct or indirect, is fifty per cent or above; or (c) to a foreign company, unless exempted as provided in section 3.
why_relevant: Because the purchaser is a company, the shareholding of the purchaser must be examined before the deed is drawn: at fifty per cent or more foreign shareholding, direct or indirect, the transfer is prohibited outright.
temporal_note: Corpus edition is consolidated (includes Act No. 3 of 2017 and Act No. 21 of 2018). No amendment event is recorded against s.2 after 2014.

relevant_excerpt: Where the title of a land is transferred to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act, with less than fifty per cent of foreign shareholding, it shall be the duty of the Registrar of Lands to confirm himself whether the foreign shareholding of such company is less than fifty per cent, by requiring the secretary of such company to submit documentary proof
why_relevant: Converts the shareholding question into a registration requirement: the company secretary must be in a position to give the Registrar of Lands documentary proof, and there is a continuing six-monthly reporting duty after registration.
temporal_note: In force from 2014; no later amendment event recorded against s.4.

relevant_excerpt: Any alienation of land effected in contravention of the provisions of this Act, shall be void and shall have no effect in law.
why_relevant: Supplies the consequence of getting the shareholding check wrong, which is why it is a pre-contract step rather than a post-completion formality.
temporal_note: In force from 2014; no later amendment event recorded.

relevant_excerpt: A company shall not enter into any major transaction, unless such transaction is- (a) approved by special resolution; (b) contingent on approval by special resolution; (c) consented to in writing by all the shareholders of the company; or (d) a transaction which the company is expressly authorised to enter into by a provision in its articles, which was included in it at the time the company was incorporated.
why_relevant: Where the purchase amounts to a major transaction, shareholder approval by special resolution (or unanimous written consent, or express authority in the original articles) must be secured before the company binds itself.
temporal_note: In force from 2007; Companies (Amendment) Act No. 13 of 2019 records no change to s.185 in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: (a) the acquisition of or an agreement to acquire whether contingent or not, assets of a value which is greater than half the value of the assets of the company before the acquisition
why_relevant: Gives the arithmetical test for a major transaction, so the value of the estate has to be compared with the company's asset base before advising on the resolution required.
temporal_note: In force from 2007; no amendment event recorded in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: an obligation which, if entered into by a natural person is required by law to be in writing signed by that person and be notarially attested, may be entered into on behalf of the company in writing signed under the name of the company by - (i) two directors of the company
why_relevant: Prescribes how the company itself signs a notarially attested obligation such as an agreement to sell, and therefore who must be produced before the notary on the company's side.
temporal_note: In force from 2007; no amendment event recorded in the corpus.
verifier_note: Section 19(1)(a) offers four alternative modes of execution (two directors; a sole director; any other person or class of persons if the articles so provide; or one or more attorneys appointed by the company), so the statement that the company signs 'by two directors' is only one permitted route and should be stated as such.

relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property, and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object, or for establishing any security, interest, or incumbrance affecting land or other immovable property (other than a lease at will, or for any period not exceeding one month)
why_relevant: Fixes the form requirement that governs both the agreement to sell and the transfer itself, and is the reason every link in the vendor's chain has to be a notarially executed instrument.
temporal_note: The corpus body is consolidated to 2024. The words quoted here are the opening words of the section and were not touched by Act No. 30 of 2022 or Act No. 4 of 2024. The operative conditions in force at October 2023 are those substituted by Act No. 30 of 2022 s.2, cited separately as PROV-M036-014; subsection (2), which requires the transferee also to sign, was added by Act No. 4 of 2024 and was not in force at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: shall be in force or avail in law unless – (a) the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant and attested by a notary public before two witnesses present at the same time
why_relevant: This is the text of the execution requirement that was in force in October 2023: writing, signature by every executant, attestation by a notary before two witnesses present at the same time, and thumb impressions on original, duplicate and protocol.
temporal_note: Enacted and in force in 2022, and still the operative text at the matter date. It was itself superseded by Act No. 4 of 2024, after the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: Before any deed or instrument (other than a will or codicil) affecting any interest in land or other immovable property is drawn by him, he shall search or cause to be searched the registers in the land registry to ascertain the state of the title in regard to such land and whether any prior deed affecting any interest in such land has been registered
why_relevant: The statutory duty to search the land registry before the deed is drawn. It is the source of the title investigation step and of the requirement to call for the registry material.
temporal_note: This paragraph is original text; neither Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(10) nor Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(6) altered rule (17)(a). In force at the matter date.
verifier_note: Rule (17)(a) is correctly quoted, but it is subject to the proviso at the end of rule (17) permitting the parties to authorise the notary in writing to dispense with the search; that proviso is added as PROV-M036-902 and should be stated alongside the search duty.

relevant_excerpt: he shall obtain from the Registrar of the relevant Land Registry the certified extract of the folio containing the last entry pertaining to such land or immovable property containing the ownership and the registered encumbrances relating to such land or immovable property
why_relevant: Names the specific document that must be obtained from the Land Registry: the certified folio extract showing ownership and registered encumbrances. It is the first document to call for on any examination of title.
temporal_note: Substituted by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(10)(a), in force from 2022 and unchanged by Act No. 6 of 2024, which altered only sub-paragraph (iii) of the same rule. In force at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: if a party to any deed or instrument is a corporate body he shall retain a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation or other instrument establishing such corporate entity and details of board of directors
why_relevant: Because a company is a party, the certificate of incorporation and the details of the board must be produced to the notary. This is a document to be called for on both a purchase and a title examination where a company appears in the chain.
temporal_note: Added by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(10)(b), in force from 2022 and not altered by Act No. 6 of 2024. In force at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: if an executant to any deed or instrument is a corporate body, cause to be affixed the seal of the corporate body and obtain the signatures of the board of directors or any person authorized by the board by resolution to sign such deed or instrument
why_relevant: Where a corporate body executes, the seal and the signatures of the board or of a person authorised by board resolution are required, and a copy of the resolution goes on the protocol. This governs the mechanics of execution wherever a company is an executant in the chain.
temporal_note: Substituted by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(7), in force from 2022 and not altered by Act No. 6 of 2024. In force at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: an accurate and clear description of the said land or other property affected thereby, showing its boundaries, extent, situation specifying the district, pattu, korale, Divisional Secretary's Division, local authority division and the Grama Niladari Division
why_relevant: The deed cannot be drawn without an accurate description showing boundaries, extent and situation, which is why a survey plan or figure of survey and the schedule of the vendor's deed must be called for.
temporal_note: Amended by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(9)(a) (condominium wording), in force from 2022; the words quoted here are unchanged by that amendment and by Act No. 6 of 2024. In force at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless he has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided.
why_relevant: Makes provision for stamp duty a precondition of attestation, so funds for duty must be arranged as part of the pre-completion steps.
temporal_note: Substituted by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(4), in force from 2022 and not altered by Act No. 6 of 2024. In force at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: It shall be the duty of every notary to submit for registration to the Registrar, every deed or instrument attested by him before the expiry of thirty days from the date of attestation thereof
why_relevant: Fixes the outer limit for lodging the transfer for registration, which is the step that secures the company's priority once the deed is executed.
temporal_note: Inserted by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(14), in force from 2022 and not altered by Act No. 6 of 2024. In force at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: be void as against all parties claiming an adverse interest thereto on valuable consideration by virtue of any subsequent instrument which is duly registered under this Chapter
why_relevant: The priority rule of the deeds registration system. It is why the registry folio has to be searched, why registered encumbrances bind a later purchaser, and why the company's own deed must be registered promptly.
temporal_note: Corpus edition is consolidated to 1990; no amendment event is recorded against s.7. In force at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: all duplicates and copies and all books and indexes kept under this Ordinance may be searched and examined by any person claiming to be interested therein or by his attorney-at-law or agent duly authorized thereto in writing, and certified copies of or extracts from any such duplicate, copy, or book may be obtained if required
why_relevant: Gives the attorney-at-law acting for an intending purchaser the statutory right to search the registry books and to take certified copies and extracts, which is the mechanism by which the documents called for are actually obtained.
temporal_note: No amendment event recorded against s.42; in force at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: No Us pendens affecting or relating to land instituted on or after the 9th day of November, 1917, shall bind a purchaser, unless and until the lis pendens is duly registered under this Chapter.
why_relevant: A registered lis pendens binds a purchaser, so the folio extract must be read for pending actions as well as for deeds, and any lis pendens disclosed must be investigated before the purchase proceeds.
temporal_note: No amendment event recorded against s.11; in force at the matter date. The corpus text reproduces the source transcription, which renders 'lis pendens' as 'Us pendens' in places.

relevant_excerpt: Any person (in this Ordinance called a "caveator") may present for registration a caveat in the prescribed form requiring to be served with notice of the presentation for registration of any instrument affecting the land described in the caveat.
why_relevant: A registered caveat is a warning on the folio that a third party asserts rights and will be noticed on any dealing; it is one of the entries the title examiner is looking for in the registry extract.
temporal_note: No amendment event recorded against s.32; in force at the matter date.
verifier_note: The excerpt is verbatim of the corpus body, but that body is the pre-2022 text: section 32(1) was repealed and substituted by the Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act, No. 32 of 2022 s.2(1), in force at the matter date, so the operative caveat text at October 2023 is PROV-M036-904; the substance relied on (a registered caveat entitles the caveator to notice of any instrument presented for registration) survives the substitution.

relevant_excerpt: Proof of the undisturbed and uninterrupted possession by a defendant in any action, or by those under whom he claims, of lands or immovable property, by a title adverse to or independent of that of the claimant or plaintiff in such action
why_relevant: Ten years of adverse possession can defeat a paper title, so an examination of title cannot stop at the deeds: possession has to be traced, and documents evidencing the vendor's possession must be called for.
temporal_note: Corpus edition is consolidated; Prescription (Amendment) Act No. 26 of 2014 records no change to s.3 in the corpus. In force at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: Any person, having a Title of Ownership or other interest in a land parcel registered under this Act, may on payment of the prescribed fee, obtain a Certificate of Title in respect of such Ownership or interest, from the appropriate Registrar of Title.
why_relevant: Where the land parcel has been brought under title registration, the document to call for is the Certificate of Title, which is conclusive evidence of the interest, rather than a chain of deeds. The examiner must first establish which registration system applies to the parcel.
temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment event recorded against s.37. Whether a particular parcel is registered under the Act depends on declarations made for the area, which are not in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: For the purpose of maintaining the legal validity of a transfer of land to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act, with less than fifty per cent of foreign shareholding, the foreign shareholding of such company shall remain less than fifty per cent, for a minimum period of consecutive twenty (20) years from the date of such transfer.
why_relevant: The shareholding test is not spent on completion. A Sri Lankan company that takes a transfer on the footing of less than fifty per cent foreign shareholding must keep it below fifty per cent for twenty consecutive years; if it reaches or exceeds fifty per cent the transfer of land becomes void with effect from the date of the increase, subject to a six or twelve month window to restore the position. Advising the company of that continuing condition is a step the research map omitted.
temporal_note: Part of section 2 of the consolidated corpus edition of the 2014 Act (which includes Act No. 3 of 2017 and Act No. 21 of 2018). In force at the matter date.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked verbatim against 38-2014/s2.

relevant_excerpt: Provided that if the parties to the transaction authorize the notary in writing to dispense with the search, the search shall not be compulsory, but he shall before the deed or instrument is tendered for registration write at the head thereof the reference to the previous registration, if any.
why_relevant: The search duty in rule (17)(a) is not absolute. The parties may authorise the notary in writing to dispense with the search, in which case he must instead endorse the reference to the previous registration before the deed is tendered for registration. Any statement of the search obligation has to be qualified by this proviso.
temporal_note: The proviso stands at the end of rule (17) in the corpus body of section 31 and is not touched by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(10) or Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(6). In force at the matter date.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier as the missing exception to PROV-M036-015; excerpt checked verbatim against 1-1907/s31.
