relevant_excerpt: When a deed transferring any immovable property is executed or acknowledged before a notary, he shall use his best endeavours to obtain the title deed, if any, of such property, and make an endorsement thereon stating the number and date of the deed executed before him and the nature of the transaction and attach his signature thereto
why_relevant: This is the statutory duty that most directly answers a question about what documents must be called for: the notary must use his best endeavours to obtain the vendor's title deed itself and endorse the new transaction on it. It anchors the call for the originals of the chain of deeds independently of the search and folio-extract duties in rule (17).
temporal_note: Rule (33) stands in the corpus body of section 31; no amendment event in the corpus is attributed to it by Act No. 31 of 2022 or Act No. 6 of 2024. In force at the matter date.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier as a missing document-production duty for M036-Q02; excerpt checked verbatim against 1-1907/s31.

relevant_excerpt: A person (hereinafter referred to as the "caveator") who (i) has a right, title or interest; or (ii) claims to have a right, title or interest, to a land, an undivided land, a land parcel or a condominium parcel (hereinafter in this section referred to as the "land") may present for registration a caveat substantially in Form VIII of the Second Schedule hereto requiring him to be served a notice of the presentation for registration of any instrument affecting such land.
why_relevant: This is the caveat text in force at October 2023. It replaced section 32(1) of the Registration of Documents Ordinance, narrows the class of caveators to persons who have or claim a right, title or interest, prescribes Form VIII with a supporting affidavit and an attorney-at-law certificate, and (by section 2(3)) limits a caveat to a maximum of two years. A title examiner reading a caveat on the folio must apply this text, not the 1927 text carried in the corpus body of 23-1927/s32.
temporal_note: Enacted in 2022 with no separate date-of-operation clause; in force at the matter date and not superseded before October 2023. The corpus edition of the Registration of Documents Ordinance is consolidated to 1990 and does not carry this substitution.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier to supply the in-force text behind PROV-M036-025; excerpt checked verbatim against 32-2022/s2.

relevant_excerpt: There shall be charged on- (a) every instrument relating to a transfer of situated in the immovable property Western Province; (b) every document presented or filed, in proceedings instituted in any Court of law established by law, in the Western Province of Sri Lanka; (c) every transfer of a motor vehicle effected in Western Province. a stamp duty at the prescribed rate. Different rates may be prescribed in respect of different classes or categories of instruments.
why_relevant: Charging section. Stamp duty is charged on every instrument relating to a transfer of immovable property situated in the Western Province, at the prescribed rate. The land and house are at Kadawatha, in the Gampaha District of the Western Province, so the deed of gift falls within this charge. The section fixes no rate itself; the rate is prescribed by subsidiary legislation that is not in the corpus.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1990 with no amendment events for this section, so the text is in force at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: means a sale and shall include a gift or exchange or a conveyance, without consideration, by an executor or administrators of an estate of a deceased to a person beneficially entitled to such property or to a trustee appointed under the will of the deceased, or by a trustee to a beneficiary or a conveyance, without consideration, by a trustee or the executor or administrator of a deceased trustee to a surviving trustee or to a new trustee, but does not include a deed of partition of any land held in common or an agreement to transfer.
why_relevant: Definition of "Transfer" in the interpretation section. The corpus body has lost the quoted term labels through OCR; the term is recorded in the section's defined_terms as "Transfer". The definition expressly includes a gift, which is what brings a deed of gift within the charge in section 37.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1990 with no amendment events for this section, so the text is in force at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: (1) Where any property is conveyed by an instrument, the stamp duty with which such instrument is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property conveyed.
why_relevant: Fixes the base of the calculation: duty is calculated on the value of the property conveyed, not on the consideration (a gift has none) and not automatically on the current market price.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1990 with no amendment events for this section, so the text is in force at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: (c) any immovable property which is gifted, being immovable property which was acquired by the donor after March 31, 1977 means - the price which, in the opinion ofthe Assessor, such property would have fetched if sold in the open market on the date which such on property was acquired by the donor, increased by an amount equal to the cost of the improvements, alterations and additions, if any, made to such property after the date on which the property was acquired by the donor, and prior to the date of the instrument by which such property is gifted
why_relevant: The operative valuation rule. For gifted immovable property acquired by the donor after March 31, 1977, value is the open market price at the date the donor acquired it, increased by the cost of improvements, alterations and additions made after acquisition and before the gift. The donor acquired the land in February 1980, so paragraph (c) applies and not paragraph (b).
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1990 with no amendment events for this section, so the text is in force at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: (ii) the price which, in the opinion of the assessor, that property would have: fetched, if sold in the open market on the date of the instrument by which such property was gifted. whichever price is the lower.
why_relevant: The lower-of limb of paragraph (c): the acquisition-cost-plus-improvements figure is compared with the open market price at the date of the deed of gift and the lower of the two is the value. Without this limb the present market value of Rs. 5,400,000 could not be excluded.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1990 with no amendment events for this section, so the text is in force at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: Except where there is an agreement to the contrary stamp duty shall be payable; (a) in the case of an instrument of transfer by the grantee; (b) in the case of àny other instrument by the person drawing, making or executing the instrument;
why_relevant: Identifies who must pay. On an instrument of transfer the duty is payable by the grantee, that is the donee Saranga, unless the parties agree otherwise.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1990 with no amendment events for this section, so the text is in force at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: (1) The stamp duty with which any instrument is chargeable shall be paid before or at the time of execution of the instrument except as otherwise permitted in this Statute and such payment shall be indicated on such instrument by means of adhesive stamps or impressed stamps or a Certificate of payment referred to in subsection (2) hereof. (2) Stamp duty payable on an instrument relating to a transfer ofimmovable property may be paid to a prescribed bank which shall issue a Certificate in the prescribed form of payment of the amount of Stamp duty paid and the date of payment of such duty
why_relevant: The procedure for payment: duty is paid before or at the time of execution and shown on the instrument by adhesive or impressed stamps or a certificate of payment; for an instrument transferring immovable property the duty may be paid to a prescribed bank, which issues a certificate of payment to be affixed to the instrument.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1990 with no amendment events for this section, so the text is in force at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: (2) Every notary public who attests an instrument of conveyance shall before doing SO take all reasonable steps to satisfy himself that the value on which the stamp duty is paid represents the value of the property conveyed. (3) Every notary public who attests any instrument for which adhesive stamps are used shall affix stamps of the correct description and value to such instrument and cause them tol be cancelled in the manner directed by this Statute and state in his attestation, the number and value of the stamps affixed to such instruments.
why_relevant: The notary's duties on execution: to satisfy himself that the value on which duty is paid represents the value of the property conveyed, and where adhesive stamps are used to affix, cancel and recite them in the attestation.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1990 with no amendment events for this section, so the text is in force at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: (4) When stamp duty is paid on an instrument in the manner set out in section 40(2) or 40(3) the Notary Public who attests such instrument shall certify in his attestation that the certificate of payment issued by the bank under Section 40(2) has been duly affixed to the duplicate of such instrument or that such instrument has been endorsed by the Commissioner in the manner set out in Section 40(3).
why_relevant: Completes the procedure where duty is paid to a bank under section 40(2): the attesting notary must certify in the attestation that the bank's certificate of payment has been duly affixed to the duplicate.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1990 with no amendment events for this section, so the text is in force at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: Where any instrument whether executed or not and as is whether previously stamped or not, brought to an Assessor together with a copy thereof and the person bringing it applies to have the opinion of the Assessor as to the stamp duty, if any, with which it is chargeable, and pays a fee of two hundred and fifty rupees the Assessor shall determine the stamp duty, if any with which in his opinion the instrument is chargeable and shall notify his determination to such person in writing.
why_relevant: Adjudication. Because value under section 106 turns on the Assessor's opinion, the instrument, executed or not, may be brought to an Assessor with the prescribed fee for a written determination of the duty chargeable.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1990 with no amendment events for this section, so the text is in force at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: The following instruments and documents shall be exempted from the payment of stamp duty:- (1) bail bond in criminal proceedings; conveyance or transfer of any immovable L vehicle by the Government property or motor or by a person for or on behalf of the 5 Government;
why_relevant: The exemption list. A gift of land between private individuals is not within any listed exemption, so the charge in section 37 is not displaced.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1990 with no amendment events for this section, so the text is in force at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: means a transfer by one person to another ofany movable or immovable property made voluntarily and without consideration in money or money's worth
why_relevant: Definition of "gift" (term recorded in the section's defined_terms; the label is lost in the OCR body): a voluntary transfer without consideration in money or money's worth. It confirms that the intended deed is a gift and that there is no consideration on which duty could be based.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1990 with no amendment events for this section, so the text is in force at the matter reference date 2023-10.

relevant_excerpt: From and after the date of the coming into operation of this Act, the provisions of the Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982, relating to the Imposition of Stamp Duty (other than any instrument relating to the transfer of immovable property, the transfer of motor vehicles or documents filed in Court), Exemptions and any other provision in the aforesaid Act, shall, in so far as the same are inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, have no operation and the provisions of this Act shall prevail.
why_relevant: Background on which stamp duty regime governs. The 2006 Act expressly carves out instruments relating to the transfer of immovable property, so the national Special Provisions Act does not govern this deed; duty on Western Province land transfers remains a devolved provincial charge under the Financial Statute.
temporal_note: In force from April 1, 2006; the consolidated text records no amendment to this section. In force at 2023-10.

formal_title: Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross Ingratitude Act
relevant_excerpt: An irrevocable deed of gift may be revoked on the ground of gross ingratitude, only on an Order made by a competent court, in an action filed by the donor of such deed against the donee to have the said deed revoked.
why_relevant: Directly answers the question. It establishes that a deed of gift expressed to be irrevocable is nevertheless capable of revocation, and fixes the only ground (gross ingratitude), the only mode (an order of a competent court) and the only parties (donor as plaintiff, donee as defendant). The word "only" also excludes unilateral revocation by the donor's own act or deed.
temporal_note: In force from 2017 per the corpus (in_force_from_year 2017); no amendment events recorded. In force at 2023-10.

formal_title: Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross Ingratitude Act
relevant_excerpt: Court shall not entertain an action referred to in section 2, unless it is filed within a period of ten years from the date of the execution of such deed of gift and within two years from the date on which the cause of action arose.
why_relevant: A necessary statutory condition on the section 2 remedy. Even where the ground exists, the court cannot entertain the action outside the two cumulative time limits, so whether the deed could be revoked on the facts turns on the date of execution of the deed and the date the cause of action arose.
temporal_note: In force from 2017 per the corpus; no amendment events recorded. In force at 2023-10.

formal_title: Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross Ingratitude Act
relevant_excerpt: The plaintiff in an action instituted under the provisions of this Act shall file or cause to be filed in court with the plaint, an application for registration of lis pendens
why_relevant: Explains what the donor must do when instituting the action. It is a filing requirement rather than a condition of the right, so it supports the practical answer without changing whether revocation is available.
temporal_note: In force from 2017 per the corpus; no amendment events recorded. In force at 2023-10.
verifier_note: Wording confirmed verbatim and the supporting role is right, but the excerpt stops at "an application for registration of lis pendens" and omits paragraphs (a) and (b) of section 4(1), which are the words the answer actually relies on for addressing the application to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which the deed is registered (or, if unregistered, in which the land lies); the full section text supports the claim.

formal_title: Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross Ingratitude Act
relevant_excerpt: Every action filed under the provisions of this Act shall be proceeded with and regulated by the procedure provided for in the Civil Procedure Code (Chapter 101).
why_relevant: Identifies the procedure the revocation action follows. Supporting context for the mode of revocation; it does not affect whether the deed can be revoked.
temporal_note: In force from 2017 per the corpus; no amendment events recorded. In force at 2023-10.

formal_title: Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross Ingratitude Act
relevant_excerpt: means the Registrar of Lands appointed under the Registration of Documents Ordinance (Chapter 117) and having jurisdiction over the district in which the land which forms the subject matter of an irrevocable deed of gift which is sought to be revoked is situated
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. Section 6 is the interpretation section and defines "Registrar of Lands", the term section 4(1) turns on. It is background rather than operative, but it matters because it identifies that officer by the district in which the land is situated, whereas section 4(1)(a) directs the lis pendens application to the Registrar of the district in which the deed is registered. On these facts the land and the registry are both in the Kalutara district, so the two coincide and the answer is unaffected.
temporal_note: In force from 2017 per the corpus (in_force_from_year 2017); no amendment events recorded. In force at 2023-10.
verifier_note: Excerpt checked verbatim against 5-2017/s6. Note that the corpus body of section 6 has the defined terms stripped out of the running text, so the excerpt begins at "means".

relevant_excerpt: Inheritance ab interstate to the immovable property in Sri Lanka of a person deceased shall be governed and regulated by the following provisions of this Ordinance wherever such person may have or have had his actual or matrimonial domicile.
why_relevant: Fixes this Ordinance as the governing law for intestate succession to Lot 1, immovable property situated at Kandawatta Road, Nugegoda, on each of the three intestate deaths (Pethum 2010, Sadun 2011, Rohan 2018).
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event for this section and latest_change_year is null. The text applies unchanged at the matter reference date 2023-04 and at each of the three deaths in issue (2010, 2011, 2018).

relevant_excerpt: When any person shall die intestate as to any of his or her property, leaving a spouse surviving, the surviving spouse shall inherit one-half of the property of such person.
why_relevant: Gives Sadana one-half of Pethum's interest and Roshini one-half of Sadun's interest. Rohan left no spouse, so the section is spent for his estate.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event for this section and latest_change_year is null. The text applies unchanged at the matter reference date 2023-04 and at each of the three deaths in issue (2010, 2011, 2018).

relevant_excerpt: Subject to the right of the surviving spouse in the preceding section mentioned, the right of inheritance is divided in the following order as respects (a) descendants, (b) ascendants, (c) collaterals.
why_relevant: Sets the order in which the residue after the surviving spouse's half is offered to descendants, then ascendants, then collaterals; supplies the framework in which sections 24 and 25 operate.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event for this section and latest_change_year is null. The text applies unchanged at the matter reference date 2023-04 and at each of the three deaths in issue (2010, 2011, 2018).

relevant_excerpt: Children, grandchildren, and remoter descendants are preferent to all others in the estate of the parents; all the children take equally per capita, but the children or remoter issue of a deceased child take per stirpes or by representation.
why_relevant: Gives Rohan, as Sadun's only child, the residue of Sadun's interest after Roshini's statutory half; and, because Pethum and Rohan each died issueless, exhausts the descendant class in their two estates and pushes each of those estates into section 25.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event for this section and latest_change_year is null. The text applies unchanged at the matter reference date 2023-04 and at each of the three deaths in issue (2010, 2011, 2018).

relevant_excerpt: The children and remoter descendants failing, the inheritance of the deceased goes to his father and mother in case they are both alive; but if only one of the parents be alive, the surviving parent takes half, and the brothers and sisters of the deceased of the full blood, and the issue of any deceased brother or sister of the full blood, by representation, and the brothers and sisters of the half-blood who are related to the intestate by the side of the deceased parent, and the issue of any such deceased brother or sister of the half-blood, by representation, take the other half.
why_relevant: Governs Pethum's estate: he died issueless, his father Kamal had predeceased him in 2005 and his mother Thilaka survived, so Thilaka takes half of the residue and the other half goes to his full siblings Kalum and Shanthi together with Sadun and Nadun, who are half-blood siblings related to Pethum by the side of the deceased parent, Kamal.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event for this section and latest_change_year is null. The text applies unchanged at the matter reference date 2023-04 and at each of the three deaths in issue (2010, 2011, 2018).

relevant_excerpt: In case there is no full or half-brother or sister alive at the death of the deceased, the surviving parent inherits the whole, although there may be children or other issue of deceased brothers or sisters.
why_relevant: Governs Rohan's estate: he died in 2018 unmarried, issueless and without any brother or sister, his father Sadun having predeceased him in 2011, so his surviving mother Roshini takes the whole of his interest.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event for this section and latest_change_year is null. The text applies unchanged at the matter reference date 2023-04 and at each of the three deaths in issue (2010, 2011, 2018).

relevant_excerpt: but if there are only half-brothers and sisters or such issue of one side, the full brothers and sisters and the issue of deceased full brothers and sisters by representation, take then in the first place one-half of the property, and divide the other half with the half-brothers and sisters and their issue by representation.
why_relevant: Supplies the full-blood preference inside the sibling portion of Pethum's estate. Pethum's half-blood siblings Sadun and Nadun are all on one side, the father's, so his full siblings Kalum and Shanthi first take one-half of that portion and then share the remaining half with Sadun and Nadun.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event for this section and latest_change_year is null. The text applies unchanged at the matter reference date 2023-04 and at each of the three deaths in issue (2010, 2011, 2018).

relevant_excerpt: if all those who succeed to the inheritance are equally near in degree to the intestate, they take per capita, and not per stirpes.
why_relevant: Supports the equal split inside each group under section 27: Kalum and Shanthi share the first half of the sibling portion equally, and the four siblings share the remaining half equally, none of them taking by representation.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event for this section and latest_change_year is null. The text applies unchanged at the matter reference date 2023-04 and at each of the three deaths in issue (2010, 2011, 2018).

relevant_excerpt: this Ordinance shall not apply to Kandyans or Muslims, or to Tamils of the Northern Province who are or may become subject to the Tesawalamai.
why_relevant: Records the personal-law precondition. Nothing in the background states the parties' personal law; the answer proceeds on the general law and this section is what would exclude the Ordinance if any party were Kandyan, Muslim or subject to the Tesawalamai.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event for this section and latest_change_year is null. The text applies unchanged at the matter reference date 2023-04 and at each of the three deaths in issue (2010, 2011, 2018).

relevant_excerpt: The following sections of this Ordinance shall apply to the estates of such persons only as shall die after the proclamation of this Ordinance
why_relevant: Confirms that Part III applies to estates of persons dying after the Ordinance was proclaimed, which covers all three deaths in issue.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event for this section and latest_change_year is null. The text applies unchanged at the matter reference date 2023-04 and at each of the three deaths in issue (2010, 2011, 2018).

relevant_excerpt: includes land, incorporeal tenements, and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything which is attached to the earth, and any interest in land except that of a mortgagee
why_relevant: Defines 'immovable property' for the Ordinance, so that Lot 1 and every undivided interest in it fall within section 21(1).
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event for this section and latest_change_year is null. The text applies unchanged at the matter reference date 2023-04 and at each of the three deaths in issue (2010, 2011, 2018).

relevant_excerpt: In all questions relating to the distribution of the property of an intestate, if the present Ordinance is silent, the rules of the Roman-Dutch law as it prevailed in North Holland are to govern and be followed.
why_relevant: The Ordinance's own referral clause. It is the reason the non-statutory limbs of this matter, in particular the effect of an absolute and irrevocable deed of gift subject to a reserved life interest, are answered outside the corpus and cannot be closed on statute alone.
temporal_note: In force from 1876; the corpus records no amendment event for this section and latest_change_year is null. The text applies unchanged at the matter reference date 2023-04 and at each of the three deaths in issue (2010, 2011, 2018).

relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property
why_relevant: Background only: the notarial-execution requirement for dispositions of immovable property, which Deed of Gift No.232 attested by a Notary Public satisfies on its face. It is not relied on for any share calculation.
temporal_note: The corpus text of this section is the consolidation as amended by Act No. 30 of 2022 and Act No. 4 of 2024, both later than the matter reference date 2023-04 and far later than the 2002 deed. The 1840 to 2002 wording is not in the corpus, so this provision is carried as background only and is marked not applicable to the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: Before any deed or instrument (other than a will or codicil) affecting any interest in land or other immovable property is drawn by him, he shall search or cause to be searched the registers in the land registry to ascertain the state of the title in regard to such land and whether any prior deed affecting any interest in such land has been registered;
why_relevant: Imposes the notary's first substantive step: a search of the land registry registers to ascertain the state of the title and prior registered deeds before the deed of transfer is drawn.
temporal_note: Long-standing rule, not altered by the Notaries (Amendment) Acts of 2022 or 2024, so the quoted text was in force at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: he shall obtain from the Registrar of the relevant Land Registry the certified extract of the folio containing the last entry pertaining to such land or immovable property containing the ownership and the registered encumbrances relating to such land or immovable property;
why_relevant: Requires the notary to obtain the certified folio extract showing ownership and registered encumbrances, which is how the search result and any subsisting mortgage is established.
temporal_note: Rule as substituted or inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 31 of 2022; that text was in force at April 2023. The consolidated corpus text of section 31 also carries later changes made by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 6 of 2024, but this rule was not among them.

relevant_excerpt: if a party to any deed or instrument is a corporate body he shall retain a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation or other instrument establishing such corporate entity and details of board of directors;
why_relevant: Where the purchaser is a company, the notary must call for and retain a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation and the details of the board of directors.
temporal_note: Rule as substituted or inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 31 of 2022; that text was in force at April 2023. The consolidated corpus text of section 31 also carries later changes made by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 6 of 2024, but this rule was not among them.

relevant_excerpt: if an executant to any deed or instrument is a corporate body, cause to be affixed the seal of the corporate body and obtain the signatures of the board of directors or any person authorized by the board by resolution to sign such deed or instrument and if the name of such executant or witness differs from the name given in the identification documents of such executant or witness, he shall, in his attestation of such deed or instrument, describe such executant or witness by such name and by the name written in the signature.
why_relevant: Governs how a corporate executant signs: the notary must cause the seal of the corporate body to be affixed and obtain the signatures of the board or of a person authorised by board resolution.
temporal_note: Rule as substituted or inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 31 of 2022; that text was in force at April 2023. The consolidated corpus text of section 31 also carries later changes made by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 6 of 2024, but this rule was not among them.

relevant_excerpt: Where the executant is a body corporate, he shall attach a copy of the board resolution authorizing the executant to sign such deed or instrument to the protocol of such deed or instrument.
why_relevant: Requires the board resolution authorising execution to be attached to the protocol, so the notary must call for it before execution.
temporal_note: Rule as substituted or inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 31 of 2022; that text was in force at April 2023. The consolidated corpus text of section 31 also carries later changes made by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 6 of 2024, but this rule was not among them.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument, other than a will or codicil, affecting land or other immovable property, unless the deed or instrument embodies therin or in a Schedule annexed therto an accurate and clear description of the said land or other property affected thereby, showing its boundaries, extent, situation specifying the district, pattu, korale, Divisional Secretary's Division, local authority division and the Grama Niladari Division, and the village within the District in which the land is situated
why_relevant: Requires the deed or its schedule to carry an accurate description of the estate showing boundaries, extent and administrative situation, which is why the notary must obtain the survey plan and locality particulars.
temporal_note: Rule as substituted or inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 31 of 2022; that text was in force at April 2023. The consolidated corpus text of section 31 also carries later changes made by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 6 of 2024, but this rule was not among them.

relevant_excerpt: When a deed transferring any immovable property is executed or acknowledged before a notary, he shall use his best endeavours to obtain the title deed, if any, of such property, and make an endorsement thereon stating the number and date of the deed executed before him and the nature of the transaction and attach his signature thereto,
why_relevant: Requires the notary to use his best endeavours to obtain the vendor's title deed and to endorse the new transaction on it.
temporal_note: Long-standing rule, not altered by the Notaries (Amendment) Acts of 2022 or 2024, so the quoted text was in force at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless he has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided.
why_relevant: Bars attestation until the notary is assured that the stamp duty on the transfer has been provided for.
temporal_note: Rule as substituted or inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 31 of 2022; that text was in force at April 2023. The consolidated corpus text of section 31 also carries later changes made by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 6 of 2024, but this rule was not among them.

relevant_excerpt: whether any money was paid or not in his presence as consideration or part of the consideration of the deed or instrument, and if paid, the actual amount in local currency of such payment and if the payment is made by cheque, pay order, bank draft or a banker's cheque the details of such instrument shall be set out in the attestation, in proof of such payment.
why_relevant: Requires the attestation to state whether the consideration was paid in the notary's presence and, where payment is by bank draft, the details of that instrument.
temporal_note: Rule as substituted or inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 31 of 2022; that text was in force at April 2023. The consolidated corpus text of section 31 also carries later changes made by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 6 of 2024, but this rule was not among them.

relevant_excerpt: It shall be the duty of every notary to submit for registration to the Registrar, every deed or instrument attested by him before the expiry of thirty days from the date of attestation thereof:
why_relevant: Fixes the notary's post-execution step: the attested deed must be submitted for registration within thirty days of attestation.
temporal_note: Rule 30A was inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 47 of 2011 and was in force at April 2023.
verifier_note: Wording and role confirmed, but the temporal note misattributes rule (30A): it was inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 31 of 2022 s.16(14), not by Act No. 47 of 2011, whose s.3 amended rule (26); the rule was nonetheless in force at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: It shall be the duty of every notary to endeavour to ascertain the true and full consideration for the execution of any deed, and to insert and set forth the same in such deed.
why_relevant: Obliges the notary to ascertain and set out the true and full consideration, so the notary must verify the purchase price actually agreed and paid.
temporal_note: Section 38 was last touched in 2022; subsection (1) has stood since 1907 and was in force at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property, and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object, or for establishing any security, interest, or incumbrance affecting land or other immovable property (other than a lease at will, or for any period not exceeding one month), nor any contract or agreement for the future sale or purchase of any land or other immovable property, and no notice, given under the provisions of the Thesawalamai Pre-emption Ordinance, of an intention or proposal to sell any undivided share or interest in land held in joint or common ownership, shall be in force or avail in law unless
why_relevant: Establishes that the purchase of the estate is of no force in law unless effected by a notarially attested writing, which is the source of the notary's engagement.
temporal_note: The quoted opening words have stood since 1840 and were unchanged at April 2023. The corpus body is the consolidated text and also carries subsection (2), added only by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act, No. 4 of 2024; that subsection is therefore not relied on.
verifier_note: The excerpt stops at the words “shall be in force or avail in law unless”, so the notarial-writing requirement the map relies on sits in paragraph (a), which is not quoted; those closing words come from the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act, No. 30 of 2022, not from 1840, and the subsection label “(1)” is anachronistic for April 2023 because the renumbering was made only by Act No. 4 of 2024.

relevant_excerpt: an obligation which, if entered into by a natural person is required by law to be in writing signed by that person and be notarially attested, may be entered into on behalf of the company in writing signed under the name of the company by - (i) two directors of the company; (ii) if there be only one director, by that director; (iii) if the articles of the company so provide, by any other person or class of persons; or (iv) one or more attorneys appointed by the company, and be notarially executed;
why_relevant: Prescribes how a company enters a notarially attested obligation: signed under the name of the company by two directors, a sole director, a class authorised by the articles, or an appointed attorney, and notarially executed.
temporal_note: Section 19 of the Companies Act has stood unamended since the Act came into operation and was in force at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: A company shall not enter into any major transaction, unless such transaction is- (a) approved by special resolution; (b) contingent on approval by special resolution; (c) consented to in writing by all the shareholders of the company; or (d) a transaction which the company is expressly authorised to enter into by a provision in its articles, which was included in it at the time the company was incorporated.
why_relevant: A purchase of assets worth more than half the value of the company's assets is a major transaction and cannot be entered into without shareholder approval, so the notary must call for that approval.
temporal_note: Section 185 has stood unamended since 2007 and was in force at April 2023.
verifier_note: Excerpt is subsection (1) only; the definition of “major transaction” that the answer turns on is in subsection (2)(a), which is not quoted and has been added as PROV-M041-902.

relevant_excerpt: approve a major transaction for the purpose of paragraphs (a) or (b) of subsection (1) of section 185 of this Act;
why_relevant: Fixes the form of the shareholder approval required for a major transaction: it must be exercised by special resolution.
temporal_note: Section 92 has stood unamended since 2007 and was in force at April 2023.
verifier_note: Excerpt quotes only paragraph (b) of section 92(1); the operative words “such powers shall be exercised by special resolution” are in the closing words of subsection (1) and are not in the quoted text.

relevant_excerpt: the transfer of title of any land situated in Sri Lanka, shall be prohibited if such transfer is- (a) to a foreigner; or (b) to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act where any foreign shareholding in such company, either direct or indirect, is fifty per cent or above; or (c) to a foreign company, unless exempted as provided in section 3.
why_relevant: Prohibits transfer of title to a Sri Lankan company in which direct or indirect foreign shareholding is fifty per cent or above, so the notary must establish the purchaser's shareholding before the deed is drawn.
temporal_note: Section 2 has stood since 2014; the amending Acts of 2017 and 2018 did not disturb the prohibition in subsection (1). In force at April 2023.
verifier_note: Role and temporal note confirmed, but the subsection label should be “(1)”: the excerpt is the whole of subsection (1) less its opening words, not paragraph (b) alone.

relevant_excerpt: Where the title of a land is transferred to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act, with less than fifty per cent of foreign shareholding, it shall be the duty of the Registrar of Lands to confirm himself whether the foreign shareholding of such company is less than fifty per cent, by requiring the secretary of such company to submit documentary proof to the effect that the foreign shareholding of such company is less than fifty per cent of the total number of shares issued for the time being.
why_relevant: Makes registration conditional on documentary proof from the company secretary that foreign shareholding is under fifty per cent, so the notary must have that proof ready when the deed is tendered.
temporal_note: Section 4 has stood since 2014 and was in force at April 2023.
verifier_note: The excerpt is accurate, but section 4(3) puts the duty to require the secretary's documentary proof on the Registrar of Lands; why_relevant overstates it as a step the notary must take.

relevant_excerpt: Any alienation of land effected in contravention of the provisions of this Act, shall be void and shall have no effect in law.
why_relevant: Sets the consequence of getting the shareholding question wrong: the alienation is void, which is why the check is a mandatory step rather than a formality.
temporal_note: Section 18 has stood since 2014 and was in force at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: the maximum extent of agricultural land which may be owned by any person, in this Law referred to as the " ceiling ", shall (a) if such land consists exclusively of paddy land, be twenty-five acres; or (b) if such land does not consist exclusively of paddy land, be fifty acres, so however that the total extent of any paddy land, if any, comprised in such fifty acres shall not exceed the ceiling on paddy land specified in paragraph (a).
why_relevant: Sets the fifty-acre ceiling on agricultural land other than paddy, which governs how much agricultural land the purchase may lawfully add to an owner's holding.
temporal_note: The ceiling in section 3 has applied since 1972; the 1981 amendment did not alter the fifty-acre figure. In force at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: where any agricultural land is owned by a private company or co-operative society, the shareholders of such company, or society, as the case may be, shall be deemed to own such land for the purposes of section 3, in proportion to the shares held by each shareholder of such company, or society, as the case may be.
why_relevant: Attributes agricultural land owned by a private company to its shareholders in proportion to their shares, so the ceiling has to be tested against each shareholder's total holding rather than against the company.
temporal_note: Section 8 has stood unamended since 1972 and was in force at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: Where after the date of commencement of this Law any person becomes the owner of agricultural land in excess of the ceiling, any such land owned by such person in excess of the ceiling shall as from that date- (a) be deemed to vest in the Commission; and (b) be deemed to be held by that person under a statutory lease from the Commission.
why_relevant: Sets the consequence of exceeding the ceiling on a later acquisition: the excess vests in the Land Reform Commission, which is what the notary's ceiling check is designed to avoid.
temporal_note: Subsection (1) has stood since 1972; the 1981 and 1986 amendments added subsection (2) and did not displace it. In force at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: means land used or capable of being used for agriculture within the meaning given in this Law and shall include private lands, lands alienated under the Land Development Ordinance or the State Lands Ordinance or any other enactment and includes also things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth
why_relevant: Defines the land to which the ceiling applies; a planted coconut estate is land used for agriculture, so the ceiling provisions engage.
temporal_note: The definition has stood since 1972 and was in force at April 2023.
verifier_note: The words are verbatim and, by position in the run-on interpretation section, are the definition of “agricultural land”, but the corpus text carries no defined-term label, and the excerpt stops before the exclusions in limbs (a) to (e), one of which takes out cultivated land owned by a public company; immaterial on these facts, but the excerpt should be read with them.

relevant_excerpt: shall, unless it is duly registered under this Chapter, or, if the land has come within the operation of the Land Registration Ordinance, 1877f, in the books mentioned in section 26 of that Ordinance, be void as against all parties claiming an adverse interest thereto on valuable consideration by virtue of any subsequent instrument which is duly registered under this Chapter
why_relevant: Makes an unregistered instrument void against a later registered instrument taken for value, which is the reason the notary must both search the registers and register the deed promptly.
temporal_note: Section 7 has stood unamended since 1927 and was in force at April 2023.
verifier_note: The excerpt begins mid-sentence and omits its subject, “An instrument executed or made on or after the 1st day of January, 1864”; the rule claim it supports is right, but the quotation should be extended.

relevant_excerpt: there shall be charged a duty (hereinafter to be called "stamp duty") at such rate as the Minister may determine by Order published in the Gazette on every "specified instrument"- (a) executed, drawn or presented in Sri Lanka;
why_relevant: Is the charging provision for the stamp duty the notary must see provided for on the deed of transfer.
temporal_note: Section 3 has stood since 2006 and was in force at April 2023. The applicable rate is fixed by Ministerial Order in the Gazette, which is not in the corpus.
verifier_note: The charging provision is quoted correctly, but section 4 of the same Act gives a closed list of “specified instrument” that does not include a transfer of immovable property except through a Ministerial Order under paragraph (k) which is not in the corpus, so the corpus does not establish that stamp duty is chargeable on this deed.

relevant_excerpt: Provided that if the parties to the transaction authorize the notary in writing to dispense with the search, the search shall not be compulsory, but he shall before the deed or instrument is tendered for registration write at the head thereof the reference to the previous registration, if any.
why_relevant: Qualifies the search duty in rule (17)(a): the parties may authorise the notary in writing to dispense with the search, in which case he must instead write the reference to the previous registration at the head of the deed before it is tendered for registration. The map presented the search duty as unqualified.
temporal_note: The proviso to rule (17) was not touched by the Notaries (Amendment) Acts No. 47 of 2011, No. 31 of 2022 or No. 6 of 2024, so it stood in this form at April 2023.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier: the exception to the search duty was missing from the map.

relevant_excerpt: " major transaction", means- (a) the acquisition of or an agreement to acquire whether contingent or not, assets of a value which is greater than half the value of the assets of the company before the acquisition;
why_relevant: Supplies the definition on which the major transaction limb of the answer depends: an acquisition of assets of a value greater than half the value of the company's assets before the acquisition. PROV-M041-014 quotes only section 185(1) and does not itself carry this definition.
temporal_note: Section 185 has stood unamended since the Companies Act came into operation and was in force at April 2023.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier: the definitional limb the answer relies on was referred to by subsection label only, not quoted.

relevant_excerpt: no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object, or for establishing any security, interest, or incumbrance affecting land or other immovable property (other than a lease at will, or for any period not exceeding one month)
why_relevant: A lease of the shop for a period exceeding one month creates an interest affecting immovable property and so falls inside section 2: it has no force in law unless reduced to writing, signed by the executants and the witnesses before a licensed notary and attested by him. This is why the transaction must take the form of a notarial deed at all, and it fixes the frame within which the parts of the deed are drafted.
temporal_note: The quoted opening words predate both the 2022 and the 2024 amendments and were in force in April 2023. The renumbering into subsection (1) and the new subsection (2) come from Act No. 4 of 2024, after the matter date; the subsection label here reflects the consolidated corpus text, not the April 2023 layout.

relevant_excerpt: Every deed or other instrument, except any will, testament, or codicil required by this Ordinance to be executed or acknowledged before or to be attested by a notary, shall be executed, acknowledged, or attested in triplicate.
why_relevant: Fixes the physical form in which the drafted lease must be produced: original, duplicate and protocol. It bears on how the document as a whole is described, though it says nothing about the internal parts.
temporal_note: No amendment event recorded; in force from 1840 and unchanged at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument, other than a will or codicil, affecting land or other immovable property, unless the deed or instrument embodies therin or in a Schedule annexed therto an accurate and clear description of the said land or other property affected thereby, showing its boundaries, extent, situation
why_relevant: The only provision in the corpus prescribing the descriptive content of a deed affecting immovable property, and the reason the description of the shop premises is carried in a schedule rather than in the body. The question excludes the schedule, so this is context for the operative part rather than the answer itself.
temporal_note: Rule (17)(a) in this form was substituted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 31 of 2022, in force before April 2023. The Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 6 of 2024 amended rule (17)(b)(iii) and rule (17)(c), not paragraph (a), so the quoted words were in force at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: (18) He shall correctly insert in letters in every deed or instrument executed before him the day, month, and year on which and the place where the same is executed, and shall sign the same.
why_relevant: Supplies the statutory content of the opening or introductory part of the deed: the date and place of execution, written in letters. It is the one element of the conventional premises of a lease that a corpus provision actually prescribes.
temporal_note: Rule (18) carries no recorded amendment event in the 2011, 2013, 2022 or 2024 amending Acts; in force in this form at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: (6) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless he has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided.
why_relevant: Links the drafting question to the two duty questions: the notary may not attest the lease or the bond until satisfied that the duty chargeable on it has been provided for.
temporal_note: Rule (6) in this form comes from the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 31 of 2022, in force before April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: It shall be the duty of every notary to endeavour to ascertain the true and full consideration for the execution of any deed, and to insert and set forth the same in such deed.
why_relevant: The consideration for a lease is the rent, so this is the corpus provision behind the requirement that the reddendum state the true rent of Rs.50,000 a month. It also matters to the duty questions, because an understated rent would understate the chargeable amount.
temporal_note: No amendment event recorded against section 38; in force since 1907 and unchanged at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: there shall be charged a duty (hereinafter to be called "stamp duty") at such rate as the Minister may determine by Order published in the Gazette on every "specified instrument"- (a) executed, drawn or presented in Sri Lanka
why_relevant: The charging provision for both the lease agreement and the mortgage bond. It also shows why neither amount can be computed here: the Act itself fixes no rate, and the operative rate lives in a Ministerial Order published in the Gazette which is not in the corpus.
temporal_note: In force from 2006 with no recorded amendment; unchanged at April 2023. The rate Order in force in April 2023 is a separate instrument and is not in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: (g) a bond or mortgage for any definite and certain sum of money and affecting any property; (h) a promissory note; (i) a lease or hire of any property;
why_relevant: Brings both instruments inside the charge. Paragraph (i) makes the lease of the shop a specified instrument for Q02; paragraph (g) makes a mortgage bond for the definite sum of Rs.4,000,000 a specified instrument for Q03.
temporal_note: In force from 2006 with no recorded amendment; unchanged at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: stamp duty shall be payable:- (a) in the case of a policy of insurance, by the person effecting the insurance; (b) in the case of a transfer or assignment of any share, by the transferee or assignee of such share; (c) in the case of a lease, by the lessee;
why_relevant: Identifies the payer. On the lease the duty falls on the lessee, Asela Pathirana, unless the parties agree otherwise; on the mortgage bond the residual paragraph (e) puts it on the person drawing, making or executing the instrument, the mortgagor Shantha Silva.
temporal_note: Section 6 was amended in 2008 by the insertion of paragraphs (dd) and (ddd); the corpus body reflects that and is the text in force at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: the stamp duty payable on any specified instrument shall be paid by means of affixing adhesive stamps to the required value, prior to, or at the time of, the execution of the instrument.
why_relevant: Fixes when and how the computed duty must be met, which is the practical half of a calculate-the-duty answer once the rate is known.
temporal_note: In force from 2006 with no recorded amendment; unchanged at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: (2) Stamp duty payable on any specified instrument relating to a mortgage or lease of any immovable property may be paid, prior to, or at the time of, the execution of the specified instrument, to a prescribed bank.
why_relevant: The specific route for the two instruments in this matter: duty on a lease or a mortgage of immovable property may be paid to a prescribed bank, which issues a certificate to be affixed to the instrument.
temporal_note: In force from 2006 with no recorded amendment; unchanged at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: the provisions of the Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982, relating to the Imposition of Stamp Duty (other than any instrument relating to the transfer of immovable property, the transfer of motor vehicles or documents filed in Court), Exemptions and any other provision in the aforesaid Act, shall, in so far as the same are inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, have no operation
why_relevant: Rules out the 1982 Act as the source of a rate for a lease or a mortgage bond. Neither instrument is a transfer of immovable property, a motor vehicle transfer or a court document, so the 2006 Act prevails and the figure must come from an Order under section 3 of that Act.
temporal_note: In force from 2006 with no recorded amendment; unchanged at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: the Minister may from time to time by Order published in the Gazette specify the instruments, which shall be exempt from the payment of stamp duty.
why_relevant: Shows that exemptions are also delegated to Gazette Orders. Any exemption or threshold that might apply to this lease or this mortgage bond in April 2023 is therefore outside the corpus, which compounds the rate gap.
temporal_note: In force from 2006 with no recorded amendment; unchanged at April 2023.

relevant_excerpt: shall apply to the estates of such persons only as shall die after the proclamation of this Ordinance
why_relevant: Fixes the temporal reach of Part III. Every death in this matter (2003, 2006, 2010, 2016) is long after the proclamation of the Ordinance, so the Part III intestacy rules govern each estate.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment event for this section; the text is therefore in force at the matter reference date 2022-10 and at every death in the scenario (2003, 2006, 2010, 2016).

relevant_excerpt: Inheritance ab interstate to the immovable property in Sri Lanka of a person deceased shall be governed and regulated by the following provisions of this Ordinance
why_relevant: Lot 5 at Battaramulla is immovable property in Sri Lanka, so each intestate devolution of an interest in it is governed by Part III of this Ordinance rather than by the law of any domicile.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment event for this section; the text is therefore in force at the matter reference date 2022-10 and at every death in the scenario (2003, 2006, 2010, 2016).

relevant_excerpt: When any person shall die intestate as to any of his or her property, leaving a spouse surviving, the surviving spouse shall inherit one-half of the property of such person.
why_relevant: Gives Sanatha one-half of Rikitha's interest on her intestate death in 2016. It also explains why no spouse share arises out of Piyal's estate (he died unmarried) or Kanthi's estate (her husband predeceased her).
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment event for this section; the text is therefore in force at the matter reference date 2022-10 and at every death in the scenario (2003, 2006, 2010, 2016).

relevant_excerpt: the right of inheritance is divided in the following order as respects (a) descendants, (b) ascendants, (c) collaterals
why_relevant: Sets the order in which each estate in the chain is worked out: descendants first, then ascendants, then collaterals, always subject to the surviving spouse's half.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment event for this section; the text is therefore in force at the matter reference date 2022-10 and at every death in the scenario (2003, 2006, 2010, 2016).

relevant_excerpt: Children, grandchildren, and remoter descendants are preferent to all others in the estate of the parents; all the children take equally per capita, but the children or remoter issue of a deceased child take per stirpes or by representation.
why_relevant: Governs Kanthi Gamage's intestacy in 2010: her surviving children Aruna and Leela take her estate equally per capita, and Piyal leaves no issue to represent him. Nikitha and Rikitha are not her children and take nothing from her.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment event for this section; the text is therefore in force at the matter reference date 2022-10 and at every death in the scenario (2003, 2006, 2010, 2016).

relevant_excerpt: if only one of the parents be alive, the surviving parent takes half, and the brothers and sisters of the deceased of the full blood, and the issue of any deceased brother or sister of the full blood, by representation, and the brothers and sisters of the half-blood who are related to the intestate by the side of the deceased parent, and the issue of any such deceased brother or sister of the half-blood, by representation, take the other half.
why_relevant: Governs Piyal Gamage's intestacy in 2006: he left no descendants, his father Nihal had predeceased him and his mother Kanthi survived, so Kanthi takes half and the other half goes to his full sisters Aruna and Leela together with his paternal half-sisters Nikitha and Rikitha, who are related to him through the deceased parent.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment event for this section; the text is therefore in force at the matter reference date 2022-10 and at every death in the scenario (2003, 2006, 2010, 2016).

relevant_excerpt: Father and mother both failing, the property of the intestate goes to his brothers and sisters, whether of the whole or balf-blood, and their children and other issue by representation.
why_relevant: Governs the collateral half of Rikitha's intestacy in 2016 on the footing that neither of her parents survived her: her sister Nikitha and her paternal half-sisters Aruna and Leela take. The word 'balf-blood' is the corpus text and is plainly a rendering of 'half-blood'.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment event for this section; the text is therefore in force at the matter reference date 2022-10 and at every death in the scenario (2003, 2006, 2010, 2016).

relevant_excerpt: if there are only half-brothers and sisters or such issue of one side, the full brothers and sisters and the issue of deceased full brothers and sisters by representation, take then in the first place one-half of the property, and divide the other half with the half-brothers and sisters and their issue by representation.
why_relevant: Fixes the proportions when Rikitha's collateral share is divided: her full sister Nikitha takes the first half of it and then shares the remaining half with the paternal half-sisters Aruna and Leela, there being half-blood on the father's side only.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment event for this section; the text is therefore in force at the matter reference date 2022-10 and at every death in the scenario (2003, 2006, 2010, 2016).

relevant_excerpt: if all those who succeed to the inheritance are equally near in degree to the intestate, they take per capita, and not per stirpes
why_relevant: Supplies the mode of division of the sibling half under section 25, which section 25 itself leaves unallocated: Aruna, Leela, Nikitha and Rikitha are all in the same degree to Piyal and therefore take that half in equal per capita shares.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment event for this section; the text is therefore in force at the matter reference date 2022-10 and at every death in the scenario (2003, 2006, 2010, 2016).

relevant_excerpt: In all questions relating to the distribution of the property of an intestate, if the present Ordinance is silent, the rules of the Roman-Dutch law as it prevailed in North Holland are to govern and be followed.
why_relevant: The Ordinance is the express route by which non-statutory Roman-Dutch law enters this matter. It is what carries the parts of the pedigree the corpus cannot supply: the effect of a donation reserving life interests, and the internal allocation of the sibling half under section 25 if section 30 is not accepted as the answer.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment event for this section; the text is therefore in force at the matter reference date 2022-10 and at every death in the scenario (2003, 2006, 2010, 2016).

relevant_excerpt: means not having a husband or wife living
why_relevant: Defines the term on which the absence of a spouse share out of Piyal's estate turns: he is stated to have died unmarried, so no one takes the surviving spouse's half under section 22 out of his estate.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1876 and no amendment event for this section; the text is therefore in force at the matter reference date 2022-10 and at every death in the scenario (2003, 2006, 2010, 2016).

relevant_excerpt: any heir of the deceased may apply for the issue of certificates of heir ship to each of the heirs entitled to succeed to the estate of the deceased
why_relevant: Background only. It explains the testamentary proceedings in District Court of Kaduwela Case No. 1052/2006/T in which letters of administration to Piyal's estate issued to Kanthi. Administration does not alter who the heirs are; the shares are fixed by Part III of the Ordinance, not by the grant.
temporal_note: Corpus records in_force_from_year 1889 with an amendment event in 1993 (Act No. 14 of 1993 s.4). The consolidated text is in force at the matter reference date 2022-10 and at the 2006 grant.

relevant_excerpt: (m) enter the share value of each condominium parcel in the plan in compliance with the provisions of section 20A;
why_relevant: The registered Condominium Plan is the statutory record that fixes the share value of the very parcel Neela Kumari wants to buy. It is the primary document she must inspect to know what proportion of the condominium property her purchase carries.
temporal_note: Section 5 is in force from 1973; the corpus records changes by 45-1982 s.4 and 39-2003 s.6, both well before the October 2022 reference date. Paragraph (m) as it stands is the post-2003 text.

relevant_excerpt: (h) specify the approximate floor area of each condominium parcel;
why_relevant: Floor area is the physical measure a purchaser needs before any price can be assessed, and the Condominium Plan is required to state it. It supports the share value figure rather than replacing it.
temporal_note: In force from 1973, last changed in 2003, so in force at October 2022.

relevant_excerpt: (1) The share value of each parcel (except in the case of an accessory parcel where no share value shall be allotted) shown in every plan lodged for registration as a Condominium Plan shall be taken as share parcels. (2) The determine- share parcels shall (a) the voting rights of the owners of all the parcels; (b) the quantum of the undivided share of each owner of a parcel in the common elements, and (c) the proportion payable by each owner of a parcel of contributions levied by the management corporation pursuant to section 20H.
why_relevant: This is the section that turns the share value shown on the plan into legal consequences: the size of the undivided share in the common elements that comes with the parcel, the voting strength attaching to it, and the proportion of management corporation contributions the buyer will have to bear. All three bear on what the parcel is worth. It also states that no share value is allotted to an accessory parcel, which matters where a car park bay is included in the sale.
temporal_note: In force from 1973; the corpus records changes by 45-1982 s.11 and 39-2003 s.26, both before October 2022. The corpus text of subsection (2) is garbled ('The determine- share parcels shall'), apparently an extraction artefact; the verifier should compare it with the printed consolidated text.

relevant_excerpt: (3) The share value which each owner of a condominium parcel has in the common elements shall be given according to the user of such condominium parcel whether commercial or residential or otherwise, as the case may be.
why_relevant: Share value is not allotted at large: it is tied to the user of the parcel. A purchaser reading the share value off the plan must read it with the user recorded for that parcel, because a commercial and a residential parcel of the same floor area need not carry the same share value.
temporal_note: In force from 1973, last changed by the 2003 amendment, so in force at October 2022.

relevant_excerpt: any alienation of any condominium parcel shall be deemed also to convey the undivided share of the owner in the common elements appertaining to that condominium parcel
why_relevant: It settles what is being valued. The purchase cannot be valued as the apartment alone: the undivided share in the common elements passes with it automatically, so the share value on the plan is part of what she is paying for.
temporal_note: In force from 1973; the corpus records a change by 39-2003 s.16, before October 2022.

relevant_excerpt: in respect of a condominium parcel means the share parcels determined for that condominium parcel according to its share value and shown as such in the Schedule endorsed on the Condominium Plan or Semi Condominium Plan or Provisional Condominium Plan
why_relevant: The defined term tells the purchaser exactly where to look: the Schedule endorsed on the registered Condominium Plan. Without this definition the references to share value in sections 5 and 20A do not point to a document she can inspect.
temporal_note: Interpretation section in force from 1973 and amended down to 2003; in force at October 2022.

relevant_excerpt: means a person who is a party to an agreement for sale agreeing to purchase a condominium parcel or provisional condominium parcel, from the owner of the Condominium Property
why_relevant: Fixes Neela Kumari's status once she signs an agreement for sale, and shows that the Law contemplates the price being settled at the agreement for sale stage rather than at transfer.
temporal_note: In force at October 2022.

relevant_excerpt: any condominium parcel depicted therein together with the common elements appurtenant thereto may be held and dealt with in the same manner and form as any land
why_relevant: Because the parcel is dealt with as land, the ordinary conveyancing checks on value that apply to land, including the valuation on which stamp duty is computed, apply to this purchase too.
temporal_note: In force at October 2022.

relevant_excerpt: shall be deemed to be the owner of his parcel and his share in the common elements or provisional common elements, subject to the encumbrances, if any, registered or notified in the relevant register
why_relevant: Registered encumbrances noted against the parcel reduce what the purchaser gets for her money, so the relevant register is a second document she must search alongside the plan.
temporal_note: In force from 1973, last changed in 2003; in force at October 2022.

relevant_excerpt: (1) Where any property is conveyed by an instrument, the stamp duty with which such instrument is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property conveyed.
why_relevant: The property is in Colombo, within the Western Province. Duty on the transfer is charged on the value of the property conveyed, not on whatever figure the parties choose to recite, so the value has to be arrived at independently of the bargain.
temporal_note: In force from 1990 with no later change recorded in the corpus. The corpus does not carry the interaction between this provincial statute and the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act, No. 12 of 2006, so whether this is the operative charging instrument for an October 2022 Colombo conveyance is not settled from the corpus. Treated as supporting rather than indispensable for that reason.

relevant_excerpt: (2) Every notary public who attests an instrument of conveyance shall before doing SO take all reasonable steps to satisfy himself that the value on which the stamp duty is paid represents the value of the property conveyed.
why_relevant: A practical route for the purchaser: her notary is under a statutory duty to satisfy himself that the value stamped represents the value of the property, so the notary's enquiry is itself a check on the figure she proposes to pay.
temporal_note: In force from 1990, no later change recorded. Same instrument-selection caveat as PROV-M046-010. The corpus text carries an obvious typographic artefact ('before doing SO').

relevant_excerpt: the person bringing it applies to have the opinion of the Assessor as to the stamp duty, if any, with which it is chargeable, and pays a fee of two hundred and fifty rupees the Assessor shall determine the stamp duty, if any with which in his opinion the instrument is chargeable
why_relevant: Adjudication is the one mechanism in the corpus by which a party to a conveyance can obtain an official determination bearing on value, since duty is computed on the value of the property conveyed.
temporal_note: In force from 1990, no later change recorded. Same instrument-selection caveat as PROV-M046-010; the fee figure may also have been revised by instruments outside the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: (2) Every owner or occupier of any house, building, land, or tenement, or his authorized agent, shall be permitted free of charge, to inspect any portion of the said assessment book which relates to his premises.
why_relevant: Colombo is a Municipality, so an assessment book recording the annual value of the parcel exists and gives a further reference figure. Inspection as of right belongs to the owner or occupier, so Neela Kumari would have to obtain it through the vendor. Annual value is a rating measure rather than capital value, which is why this is background rather than a route to the purchase price.
temporal_note: In force from 1947, no later change recorded in the corpus. The corpus footnote to subsection (1) records that it does not have effect in areas specified under section 2 of the Rating and Valuation Ordinance, which is not in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: There shall be charged on- (a) every instrument relating to a transfer of situated in the immovable property Western Province;
why_relevant: Provincial charging section. A Deed of Gift of a house and land at Maharagama is an instrument relating to a transfer of immovable property situated in the Western Province, so it is chargeable with stamp duty at the prescribed rate. The word order as printed in the corpus is transposed by OCR, but the sense is plain.
temporal_note: In force long before the October 2022 matter date; the corpus records no amendment event on this section.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim in 6-1990/s37 and the section charges stamp duty at the prescribed rate on every instrument relating to a transfer of immovable property in the Western Province; the corpus text transposes the words 'situated in the immovable property Western Province' as OCR damage, and the reading relied on is the only sensible one.

relevant_excerpt: means a sale and shall include a gift or exchange or a conveyance, without consideration, by an executor or administrators of an estate of a deceased to a person beneficially entitled to such property
why_relevant: The charge in s.37 bites on a transfer. The interpretation section defines Transfer to include a gift, so a Deed of Gift is within the charge even though no money passes. Without this definition the gratuitous deed would not obviously be dutiable.
temporal_note: In force long before the October 2022 matter date; the corpus records no amendment event on this section.

relevant_excerpt: (1) Where any property is conveyed by an instrument, the stamp duty with which such instrument is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property conveyed.
why_relevant: Fixes the base of the charge: duty is calculated on the value of the property conveyed, not on any consideration recited. This is what makes the value figure entered in the deed the operative amount.
temporal_note: In force long before the October 2022 matter date; the corpus records no amendment event on this section.

relevant_excerpt: (c) any immovable property which is gifted, being immovable property which was acquired by the donor after March 31, 1977 means - the price which, in the opinion ofthe Assessor, such property would have fetched if sold in the open market on the date which such on property was acquired by the donor, increased by an amount equal to the cost of the improvements, alterations and additions, if any, made to such property after the date on which the property was acquired by the donor,
why_relevant: Definitive on the first limb of the statutory value of gifted immovable property acquired after 31 March 1977: the open market price at the date the donor acquired it, increased by the cost of improvements made after acquisition. The donor bought in December 1977, so paragraph (c), not paragraph (b), governs.
temporal_note: In force long before the October 2022 matter date; the corpus records no amendment event on this section.
verifier_note: Verbatim; the corpus text of paragraph (c) has lost the '(i)' marker of the first limb through OCR, and the clean parallel in 43-1982/s71(c)(i) confirms the limb structure.

subsection: definition of "value", paragraph (c), second limb and the lower-of rule
relevant_excerpt: or (ii) the price which, in the opinion of the assessor, that property would have: fetched, if sold in the open market on the date of the instrument by which such property was gifted. whichever price is the lower.
why_relevant: Supplies the second limb (open market price at the date of the deed) and the decisive instruction that the lower of the two limbs is the statutory value. Without it the present valuation would be assumed to govern.
temporal_note: In force long before the October 2022 matter date; the corpus records no amendment event on this section.

relevant_excerpt: (c) any immovable property which is gifted, being immovable property which was acquired by the donor after March 31, 1977 means- (i) the price which, in the opinion of the Assessor, such property would have fetched if sold in the open market on the date on which such property was acquired by the donor, increased by an amount equal to the cost of the improvements, alterations and additions, if any, made to such property after the date on which the property was acquired by the donor, and prior to the date of the instrument by which such property is gifted;
why_relevant: The national Act carries the same definition in cleaner text, including the express requirement that the improvements be made before the date of the gift instrument. Cited as the parallel national formulation of the same rule and as a check on the OCR-damaged provincial wording.
temporal_note: In force long before the October 2022 matter date; the corpus records no amendment event on this section.

relevant_excerpt: the provisions of the Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982, relating to the Imposition of Stamp Duty (other than any instrument relating to the transfer of immovable property, the transfer of motor vehicles or documents filed in Court), Exemptions and any other provision in the aforesaid Act, shall, in so far as the same are inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, have no operation
why_relevant: Explains why the 1982 Act still speaks to this instrument: the 2006 Act expressly carves instruments relating to the transfer of immovable property out of the displacement of the 1982 Act, so the older valuation machinery survives for a deed of gift of land.
temporal_note: In force from 2006, before the October 2022 matter date.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim but the role claimed is overstated: s.13 speaks to the 1982 Act only and displaces it only so far as it is inconsistent with the 2006 Act, so the 1982 valuation rule survives for want of any competing 2006 valuation rule as much as by the parenthetical carve-out, and neither route makes the 1982 Act the charging Act for land in the Western Province.
