relevant_excerpt: If any person who shall attest the execution of any will, testament, or codicil shall at the time of the execution thereof, or at any time afterwards, be incompetent to be admitted a witness to prove the execution thereof, such will, testament, or codicil shall not on that account be invalid.
why_relevant: Fixes the first half of the answer: the will itself is not struck down because of a defect in an attesting witness. Without it the advice could wrongly be that the whole will fails.
temporal_note: In force from 1840; no amendment event recorded in the corpus, so the text applies at 2020-04.

relevant_excerpt: any creditor, or the wife or husband of any creditor whose debt is so charged, shall attest the execution of such will, testament, or codicil, such creditor, notwithstanding such charge, shall be admitted a witness to prove the execution of such will, testament, or codicil, or to prove the validity or invalidity thereof.
why_relevant: The added facts make the proposed witness both a devisee and a creditor whose debt is charged on the estate. Section 12 completes the exception already carved out in section 11 for charges and directions for the payment of debts: the charged debt survives the attestation and the creditor remains a competent witness.
temporal_note: In force from 1840; no amendment event recorded in the corpus, so the text applies at 2020-04.
verifier_note: Wording and temporal note confirmed verbatim against 7-1840/s12, but the role is overstated: the charge-for-debt exception is written into s.11 itself and s.12 adds only the attesting creditor's competence, so s.12 moves from indispensable to supporting.

relevant_excerpt: nor shall any executor or executrix, by reason of his or her attesting such will, forfeit the recompense or commission for his or her trouble payable by law, custom, or practice.
why_relevant: The proposed witness is also named executor. Section 13 shows that the executorship and the commission attached to it are not lost by attesting, so the loss is confined to the beneficial gift.
temporal_note: In force from 1840; no amendment event recorded in the corpus, so the text applies at 2020-04.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim, but it quotes only the second limb of s.13 (no forfeiture of recompense or commission); claim CL-M073-Q01-005 also relies on the first limb, which turns on being an executor rather than on the act of attesting.

relevant_excerpt: The testator shall - (a) sign; and (b) affix his left or right thumb impression, at the foot or end of the will, testament or codicil referred to in subsection (1), before a notary public and two witnesses who shall be present at the same time
why_relevant: Context for why two attesting witnesses are needed at all and why the notary is involved. Background only, because the corpus text is the post-2022 wording.
temporal_note: The corpus text carries the substitution made by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 30 of 2022 s.3, which is after the matter date of 2020-04. The April 2020 wording is not in the corpus, so this provision is not indispensable and no claim rests on its detail.
verifier_note: The corpus body of 7-1840/s4 carries the substitution made by Act No. 30 of 2022 s.3 and the April 2020 wording is not in the corpus, so the section's content at the matter reference date cannot be checked; it is correctly confined to background and no claim rests on it.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument to which at least two witnesses have not subscribed their signatures in letters.
why_relevant: The notary's own duty: two subscribing witnesses are required, so the testator must find a second person in any event and there is room to choose two disinterested witnesses instead of the beneficiary.
temporal_note: Section 31 as a whole was amended in 2011, 2022 and 2024, but neither the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16 nor the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3 touches rule (8), so the corpus text of rule (8) is the text in force at 2020-04.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless the person executing the same and the witnesses shall have signed the same in his presence and in the presence of one another, and unless he shall have signed the same in the presence of the executant and of the attesting witnesses.
why_relevant: Sets out how the witnesses must sign, which is the mechanical duty engaged when the client proposes a particular person as a witness.
temporal_note: Rule (12) is not amended by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16 or the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3, so the corpus text is the text in force at 2020-04.

formal_title: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance No. 7 of 1840
relevant_excerpt: shall be in force or avail in law unless - (a) the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary
why_relevant: A deed of partition transfers and extinguishes interests in land between the co-owners, so it falls within the transactions that s.2 renders of no force in law unless the instrument is in writing and notarially attested. This is the provision that makes 'execute a notarially attested deed' a legal requirement rather than a matter of practice, and it is the core of the alternative route the question asks about.
temporal_note: Section 2 has required notarial execution of instruments affecting land since 1840 and was in force at 2020-04. The corpus holds the consolidated edition; amendment_events record changes by Act No. 60 of 1947, Act No. 30 of 2022 and Act No. 4 of 2024, and the quoted paragraph (a) wording ('signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant') is post-2020. The pre-2022 text required signature by the party making the instrument in the presence of a licensed notary and two or more witnesses. The requirement relied on here - writing plus notarial attestation - is common to both texts, but the verifier should confirm the 2020 wording against a pre-2022 edition before treating the excerpt as the operative text.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument, other than a will or codicil, affecting land or other immovable property, unless the deed or instrument embodies therin or in a Schedule annexed therto an accurate and clear description of the said land or other property affected thereby, showing its boundaries, extent, situation
why_relevant: The notary may not attest the deed of partition unless it carries a schedule describing each allotment with its boundaries, extent and situation. This is what forces the co-owners to have the 45 perches surveyed and blocked out into three defined lots before the deed can be drawn, and it is therefore the first practical step in the alternative route.
temporal_note: Rule (16)(a) in this form was substituted by Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 47 of 2011 s.2 and so was in force at 2020-04. Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(9)(a) added condominium wording at the end of the paragraph only; the excerpt stops before that addition and matches the 2011 text.

relevant_excerpt: if such property consist of a share of a land or other property, the deed shall state whether it is a divided or undivided share, and the fractional part which it is of the whole. If it be a divided share, such share shall be clearly and accurately defined by its particular boundaries and extent; if it be an undivided share, the boundaries and extent shall be stated of the land of which it is a share.
why_relevant: The brothers presently hold undivided one-third shares. Rule (16)(b) is the provision that distinguishes the two states and requires that once the shares are converted into divided shares each allotment be defined by its particular boundaries and extent in the deed. It is the statutory expression of the difference between the co-owners' present position and the 'divided and defined block' the Bank wants.
temporal_note: In force at 2020-04. Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(9)(b) deleted a proviso at the end of paragraph (b); the excerpt is drawn from the opening of the paragraph and is unaffected by that deletion.

relevant_excerpt: Before any deed or instrument (other than a will or codicil) affecting any interest in land or other immovable property is drawn by him, he shall search or cause to be searched the registers in the land registry to ascertain the state of the title in regard to such land and whether any prior deed affecting any interest in such land has been registered
why_relevant: Fixes the title-search step. Before drawing the deed of partition the notary must search the Land Registry folio for the land to establish the state of title and to pick up registered encumbrances - here the Bank's mortgage over Pramuk's undivided share, and the registration of the partition decree in D.C. Ratnapura case No. 345/P through which the brothers derive title.
temporal_note: Rule (17)(a) is long-standing and was in force at 2020-04. Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(10) repealed and replaced paragraph (b) of rule (17) and added new paragraphs (c) to (e); paragraph (a) was not touched by the 2022 or 2024 amendments.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: (2) If the land consists of a divided portion of a land or allotment, such portion shall be clearly and accurately defined by its particular boundaries and extent. (3) If the land consists of an undivided share in a land, the proportion which the share bears to the entire land shall be staled, and a description of the entire land shall be given as required by subsection (1).
why_relevant: Repeats the description requirement on the registration side and, by s.13(5), obliges the Registrar to refuse registration of an instrument that does not carry the required particulars. It confirms that the survey and the schedule of boundaries are not optional if the deed of partition is to be registered.
temporal_note: In force at 2020-04; last amended in 1982 by Act No. 50 of 1982, well before the matter date. 'staled' is an OCR artefact for 'stated' in the corpus text and is reproduced verbatim.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: be void as against all parties claiming an adverse interest thereto on valuable consideration by virtue of any subsequent instrument which is duly registered under this Chapter
why_relevant: Registration is the final step and it is not merely administrative: an unregistered deed of partition is void against a later registered instrument taken for valuable consideration. Anuk's intended sale, Pramuk's mortgage and Dinuk's lease all depend on the partition deed holding priority, so registration in the Ratnapura Land Registry folio is indispensable to the alternative route.
temporal_note: In force at 2020-04; no amendment events recorded for this section in the corpus.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: all instruments, including wills, decrees and orders of any court or authority, and awards, which purport or operate to create, confer, declare, limit, assign, transfer, charge, incumber, release, or extinguish any right, title, or interest, whether vested or contingent, past, present, or future, to, in or over land
why_relevant: Establishes that a deed of partition is an instrument 'affecting land' for the purposes of Chapter II, because it declares and transfers interests in the land and extinguishes each brother's undivided interest in the other two allotments. Without this the priority rule in s.7 would not reach the deed.
temporal_note: In force at 2020-04; no amendment events recorded for this section in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: Whenever a notary has received instructions to register, and a sufficient sum to meet the necessary expense of registering, any deed drawn or attested by him, and shall in such case fail to use due diligence in effecting such registration, he shall be guilty of an offence
why_relevant: Supports the advice that the co-owners should instruct and fund the notary to register the deed of partition promptly: once instructed and put in funds the notary is under a penal duty to use due diligence in effecting registration.
temporal_note: In force at 2020-04; the only recorded change is the fine increase by the Increase of Fines Act, No. 12 of 2005 s.5, which predates the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: No plan or map or copy or tracing of a plan or map shall be receivable in evidence in any court in Sri Lanka unless such plan or map has been prepared
why_relevant: Supports the advice that the blocking-out survey be done by a registered licensed surveyor rather than informally: only a plan prepared and certified as this section requires will be receivable in evidence if the allotments are later disputed. It is supporting, not indispensable - no corpus provision makes a survey plan a condition of validity of a deed of partition.
temporal_note: In force from 2002 and applicable at 2020-04; no amendment events recorded. The corpus text of this section duplicates paragraph (a), which appears to be an extraction artefact; the excerpt is taken from the opening words only.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act No. 2 of 1958
relevant_excerpt: The partition of a tea or rubber estate effected on or after the appointed day by deed by agreement of the co-owners of such estate shall, subject to the provisions of subsection (2), be null and void unless
why_relevant: Background only. It is the clearest corpus recognition that partition of land held in common may be 'effected by deed by agreement of the co-owners' as an alternative to a partition action, which the same Act treats separately in s.6. It does not apply to this matter - a 45-perch allotment in Ratnapura is not a tea or rubber estate - and it does not confer the right to partition amicably; it presupposes it.
temporal_note: In force from 1958; no amendment events recorded for this section in the corpus. Carried as background because the Act's subject matter does not cover this land.

relevant_excerpt: He shall correctly insert in letters in every deed or instrument executed before him the day, month, and year on which and the place where the same is executed, and shall sign the same.
why_relevant: This is the statutory source of the two variable elements every testimonium clause carries: the place of execution and the date of execution, and the requirement that the date be written in letters rather than figures. A testimonium that gave the date in numerals, or omitted the place, would put the attesting notary in breach of rule (18).
temporal_note: Rule (18) was not touched by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 47 of 2011, No. 31 of 2022 or No. 6 of 2024; the text quoted is the text in force in April 2020.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless the person executing the same and the witnesses shall have signed the same in his presence and in the presence of one another, and unless he shall have signed the same in the presence of the executant and of the attesting witnesses.
why_relevant: The testimonium is the clause by which the deed itself records the act of signing that rule (12) requires: the parties setting their hands to the instrument at one place, on one date, before the notary and the witnesses. It fixes the single time and place the testimonium must recite.
temporal_note: Rule (12) was not amended by the 2011, 2022 or 2024 amending Acts; text as in force in April 2020.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument to which at least two witnesses have not subscribed their signatures in letters.
why_relevant: Explains why the execution block that immediately follows the testimonium carries two witness signature lines. It shapes the layout the testimonium leads into, but the clause itself speaks of the parties setting their hands, not of the witnesses.
temporal_note: Rule (8) unamended by the 2011, 2022 and 2024 amending Acts; in force in April 2020.

relevant_excerpt: He shall carefully preserve as his protocol a draft or copy of every deed or instrument executed or acknowledged before him, to which shall be attached his signature and those of the party and witnesses to the original deed or instrument
why_relevant: The protocol is one of the two further parts the parties sign. Together with the duplicate required by rule (26) it is the statutory reason a Sri Lankan testimonium says the parties set their hands hereto and to two others of the same tenor and date as these presents.
temporal_note: Rule (24) unamended by the 2011, 2022 and 2024 amending Acts; in force in April 2020.

relevant_excerpt: He shall deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which he resides the following documents, so that they shall reach the registrar on or before the fifteenth day of every month, namely, the duplicate of every deed or instrument (except wills and codicils) executed or acknowledged before or attested by him during the preceding month
why_relevant: Supplies the second of the two further parts. With rule (24) it accounts for the original, the duplicate and the protocol, that is three signed parts of the same tenor and date, which is what the counterpart recital in the testimonium asserts.
temporal_note: The rule stood as rule (26) in April 2020 and was in force. The only later change is Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(8), which replaced the reference to "Form F" with "Form F 1" later in the same rule; the words quoted here are unaffected.

relevant_excerpt: Every such attestation shall be substantially in the form E in the Second Schedule, and shall be legibly signed by him in the language in which the deed or instrument is written
why_relevant: Background, and a boundary marker. The one part of the end of a deed whose form is statutorily prescribed is the notary's attestation, not the testimonium. The question asks only for the testimonium, so Form E material (identification of executants, consideration paid, stamps, erasures) is kept out of the answer.
temporal_note: Rule (21) unamended by the 2011, 2022 and 2024 amending Acts; in force in April 2020. Form E itself is not held in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: an obligation which, if entered into by a natural person is required by law to be in writing signed by that person and be notarially attested, may be entered into on behalf of the company in writing signed under the name of the company by - (i) two directors of the company; (ii) if there be only one director, by that director;
why_relevant: The lessee is OMEGA (Private) Ltd, a company. A lease of immovable property must be notarially executed, so it falls within paragraph (a): the company executes by signature under the company's name by two directors (or the sole director, or a person or class of persons named in the articles, or an appointed attorney), and the deed must then be notarially executed. This is what the lessee half of the testimonium and the execution block must reflect. The 2007 Act does not require a common seal; s.12(1)(f) treats a company seal as optional.
temporal_note: Section 19 is unamended and was in force in April 2020. The Companies (Amendment) Act No. 13 of 2019 does not touch it.

formal_title: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance No. 7 of 1840
relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property, and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object, or for establishing any security, interest, or incumbrance affecting land or other immovable property (other than a lease at will, or for any period not exceeding one month)
why_relevant: Background: a lease of land for a period exceeding one month is outside the parenthetical exclusion and so must be by notarially attested writing. That is what makes this an indenture of lease attested by a notary at all, and so brings the Notaries Ordinance s.31 duties, and the testimonium's place-and-date recital, into play.
temporal_note: The words quoted are the opening words of s.2 and were in force in April 2020. Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 30 of 2022 s.2 repealed only the words from "shall be of force" to the end of the section, and Act No. 4 of 2024 s.2 then re-substituted paragraph (a); paragraphs (a) and (b) as they appear in the corpus text therefore post-date the matter and are not relied on. The duration of the proposed lease is not stated in the scenario, so the one-month exclusion cannot be conclusively ruled out on the facts as given.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument, other than a will or codicil, affecting land or other immovable property, unless the deed or instrument embodies therin or in a Schedule annexed therto an accurate and clear description of the said land or other property affected thereby, showing its boundaries, extent, situation specifying the district, pattu, korale, Divisional Secretary's Division, local authority division and the Grama Niladari Division, and the village within the District in which the land is situated
why_relevant: This is the rule that fixes what the Schedule of the deed of transfer must contain: an accurate and clear description of the land showing boundaries, extent and situation down to the Grama Niladhari Division and village, with the assessment number and street name where the land lies in a municipality, town or development area. A deed whose Schedule is blank cannot lawfully be attested.
temporal_note: Rule (16)(a) in this form was substituted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 47 of 2011, s.2, and was in force in April 2020. The consolidated corpus text of s.31 also carries later words on condominium parcels inserted by Act No. 31 of 2022, with further changes by Act No. 6 of 2024; those post-date the matter and are not relied on. The excerpt quoted here is common to the 2011 text and the consolidated text.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim in 1-1907/s31 and the rule (16)(a) description duty applied in April 2020, but the excerpt stops before the municipality, town and development area clause that why_relevant and CL-M077-Q01-002 rely on; that clause is now quoted separately as PROV-M077-901.

relevant_excerpt: if such property consist of a share of a land or other property, the deed shall state whether it is a divided or undivided share, and the fractional part which it is of the whole. If it be a divided share, such share shall be clearly and accurately defined by its particular boundaries and extent; if it be an undivided share, the boundaries and extent shall be stated of the land of which it is a share.
why_relevant: Anuk holds one of three equal shares of the 45 perch portion. This rule decides the form the Schedule must take: the deed must say whether the interest sold is divided or undivided and the fractional part it is of the whole, and where the share is undivided the Schedule must give the boundaries and extent of the entire land of which it is a share rather than of a notional block.
temporal_note: No amendment event recorded against s.31 in the corpus touches paragraph (b) of rule (16); the paragraph stood in this form well before April 2020.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but the temporal note is wrong that no amendment touches paragraph (b): Act No. 31 of 2022, s.16(9)(b) substituted the words running from "which it is a share: Provided, however" to the end of the paragraph, so the text in force in April 2020 carried a further proviso whose wording the corpus does not hold.

relevant_excerpt: (2) If the land consists of a divided portion of a land or allotment, such portion shall be clearly and accurately defined by its particular boundaries and extent. (3) If the land consists of an undivided share in a land, the proportion which the share bears to the entire land shall be staled, and a description of the entire land shall be given as required by subsection (1).
why_relevant: The registration statute imposes the same divided and undivided distinction on the description in the Schedule of the instrument presented for registration, so one description must satisfy both the notarial duty and the registration requirement.
temporal_note: Subsections (2) and (3) are the 1927 text as consolidated to 1990. No amendment event in the corpus record touches them, so they stood in this form in April 2020.

relevant_excerpt: Every Registrar shall refuse to register an instrument, other than a will, which docs not state the particulars required by the foregoing provisions of this section.
why_relevant: Supplies the consequence of a blank or insufficient Schedule: the Registrar of Lands must refuse registration, which is why the draft cannot be passed for execution as it stands.
temporal_note: Consolidated 1927 text with no amendment event recorded against subsection (5), so it applied in April 2020. Subsections (5A) and (5B) give a right of appeal to the Registrar-General and thereafter to the District Court.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and applied in April 2020, but the temporal note is wrong that no amendment event is recorded against subsection (5): the quoted subsection is the text substituted by the Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 50 of 1982, s.2(a), which also inserted (5A) and (5B).

relevant_excerpt: Every instrument (other than a will) presented for registration shall embody therein or in a Schedule annexed thereto, an accurate and clear description of the land or immovable property affected thereby, its boundaries, extent and situation specifying the District, Pattu, Korale, Divisional Secretary's Division, local authority division and the Grama Niladari Division and the village, of the District in which the land is situated
why_relevant: Gives the text of s.13(1) of the Registration of Documents Ordinance actually in force in April 2020. The corpus copy of the principal Ordinance is consolidated only to 1990 and still shows the older wording, so the amending section is cited for the operative registration standard, which matches Notaries Ordinance s.31(16)(a).
temporal_note: Enacted in 2011 and in force well before the April 2020 matter date.

relevant_excerpt: Section 31 of the Notaries Ordinance (Chapter 107) (hereinafter referred to as the "principal enactment") is hereby amended by the repeal of paragraph (a) of subsection (16) thereof and substitution therefor of the following paragraph
why_relevant: Establishes that the expanded description requirement in rule (16)(a), covering the Divisional Secretary's Division, the local authority division and the Grama Niladhari Division, was already the law in April 2020, and isolates the 2020 text from the condominium wording added in 2022.
temporal_note: Enacted in 2011 and in force well before the April 2020 matter date.
verifier_note: The excerpt quotes only the amending formula and not the paragraph substituted by it, so on its own it does not show the 2020 wording; the substituted paragraph does appear in the body of 47-2011/s2, but the corpus text of it breaks off at "section 2 of the Pradeshiya Sabha number", so the 2011 wording of the municipality and assessment number clause is only partly legible in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: Before any deed or instrument (other than a will or codicil) affecting any interest in land or other immovable property is drawn by him, he shall search or cause to be searched the registers in the land registry to ascertain the state of the title in regard to such land and whether any prior deed affecting any interest in such land has been registered
why_relevant: Explains where the description that goes into the Schedule must come from: the notary's search of the land registry folio, so that the Schedule reproduces the land as it stands registered under the partition decree rather than a description supplied by the parties.
temporal_note: The search duty in rule (17)(a) long predates the matter. Neighbouring paragraphs of rule (17) in the consolidated corpus text carry insertions made in 2022 and 2024 which post-date April 2020 and are not relied on.

subsection: (16)(a), municipality, town and development area clause
relevant_excerpt: and in case the land is situated in any municipality, town or development area, declared under section 2 of the Municipal Councils Ordinance (Chapter 252) section 2 of the Urban Councils' Ordinance (Chapter 255) and section 2 of the Pradeshiya Sabha Act, No. 15 of 1987 respectively, the assessment number and the name, if any, of the street in which it is situated
why_relevant: Carries the part of rule (16)(a) that CL-M077-Q01-002 and the rule paragraph of the gold answer depend on: where the land lies in a municipality, town or development area the Schedule must also give the assessment number and the street name. PROV-M077-001 quotes only the earlier half of the paragraph.
temporal_note: These are the closing words of rule (16)(a) as substituted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 47 of 2011, s.2. Act No. 31 of 2022, s.16(9)(a) substituted for the words "the assessment number and the name, if any, of the street in which it is situated." a longer form adding condominium parcels, which confirms that the clause quoted here stood in this form in April 2020 and that the condominium tail in the consolidated corpus text does not.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked verbatim against 1-1907/s31.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: unless it is duly registered under this Chapter, or, if the land has come within the operation of the Land Registration Ordinance, 1877f, in the books mentioned in section 26 of that Ordinance, be void as against all parties claiming an adverse interest thereto on valuable consideration by virtue of any subsequent instrument which is duly registered under this Chapter
why_relevant: This is the whole of the priority rule the Lending Institution is invoking. An earlier instrument that is not duly registered is void against a later instrument taken for valuable consideration and duly registered. It decides whether the mortgage bond can be put ahead of the Indenture of Lease.
temporal_note: In force from 1927; the corpus records no amendment to section 7, so the text applies at 2020-04.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: Registration of an instrument under this Chapter shall not cure any defect in the instrument or confer upon it any effect or validity which it would not otherwise have except the priority conferred on it by this section.
why_relevant: Limits what registration achieves. Registering the mortgage bond buys priority and nothing else, so Kamal cannot be advised that registration will cure any other defect in the bond or in his title.
temporal_note: In force from 1927; no amendment recorded in the corpus.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: all instruments, including wills, decrees and orders of any court or authority, and awards, which purport or operate to create, confer, declare, limit, assign, transfer, charge, incumber, release, or extinguish any right, title, or interest, whether vested or contingent, past, present, or future, to, in or over land
why_relevant: Brings both competing documents inside section 7. An Indenture of Lease creates an interest in land and a mortgage bond charges land, so each is an instrument affecting land and each is registrable.
temporal_note: In force from 1927; no amendment to section 8 recorded in the corpus.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: (xi) any instrument if the only interest in land created or dealt with thereby is a tenancy at will or for a period not exceeding one month or determinable by the landlord by not more than one month's notice.
why_relevant: The one exception that matters here. A tenancy at will or for a month or less is outside the registration scheme, so the priority question only arises if the Indenture of Lease is for a longer term. The scenario does not give the term.
temporal_note: In force from 1927; no amendment recorded in the corpus.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: An instrument, whether registered before or after the commencement of this Ordinance, shall not be deemed to be duly registered under this Chapter unless it is registered in accordance with the foregoing provisions of this section.
why_relevant: Supplies the content of duly registered in section 7. The bond must go into the book for the division in which the Nugegoda house lies and into the folio carrying the earlier registered instruments affecting the same land, otherwise it earns no priority at all.
temporal_note: Section 14 was last touched by Law No. 14 of 1974, long before the matter date; the corpus text applies at 2020-04.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: for the purpose of priority the time of presentation shall be taken as the time of registration
why_relevant: Fixes the moment from which priority runs. Between two competing instruments the contest is decided by the day and hour of presentation entered in the day book, which is what the Lending Institution has to win.
temporal_note: Part of the Chapter inserted by section 4 of Act No. 22 of 1958; in force well before 2020-04.
verifier_note: Wording and role confirmed, but the temporal note is wrong: 22-1958 s.4 substituted a Chapter V heading and did not insert section 27, so the bracketed marker in the corpus is a heading marker, not an insertion; the corpus records section 27 as in force from 1927 with no amendment event, which is the correct basis for holding it applicable at 2020-04.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: If, at any time while a priority notice remains in force, any instrument is registered whereby the transferee or a person deriving title under him acquires for valuable consideration from the transferor or a person deriving title under him any interest or benefit in the land described in the priority notice, such instrument shall, for the purposes of this Ordinance, be deemed to have been registered at the time of registration of the priority notice.
why_relevant: The statutory device by which a lender secures its place in the register before the bond is executed. A priority notice registered by the Lending Institution backdates registration of the bond to the date of the notice, and subsection (3) blocks registration of any instrument executed by Kamal while a notice registered with his written consent is in force.
temporal_note: Inserted by section 4 of Act No. 22 of 1958; in force at 2020-04 with no later amendment recorded in the corpus.
verifier_note: Wording and role confirmed against the full text of section 30, including subsections (3) and (5), but the temporal note is wrong for the same reason as PROV-M078-006: 22-1958 s.4 substituted a Chapter V heading and did not insert section 30; the corpus records section 30 as in force from 1927 with no amendment event.

relevant_excerpt: Before any deed or instrument (other than a will or codicil) affecting any interest in land or other immovable property is drawn by him, he shall search or cause to be searched the registers in the land registry to ascertain the state of the title in regard to such land and whether any prior deed affecting any interest in such land has been registered
why_relevant: The practical step that answers the priority question on the facts. The notary drawing the mortgage bond must search the folio for the Nugegoda land, and that search will show whether the Indenture of Lease has already been registered.
temporal_note: The corpus reproduces section 31 in its current consolidated form. The 2022 and 2024 amendments to rule (17) touched paragraphs (b)(iii) and (c) only, not the search obligation in paragraph (a), so the quoted words stand for 2020-04.
verifier_note: Temporal note independently confirmed against the amending Acts in the corpus: 31-2022 s.16(10) repealed and replaced paragraph (b) of rule (17) and added paragraphs (c) to (e), and 6-2024 s.3(6) touched paragraph (b)(iii) and paragraph (c) only; neither touched the search obligation in paragraph (a). The note omits the 2022 replacement of paragraph (b), which does not affect the quoted words.

formal_title: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance No. 7 of 1840
relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property, and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object, or for establishing any security, interest, or incumbrance affecting land or other immovable property (other than a lease at will, or for any period not exceeding one month)
why_relevant: Background only. It explains why both the Indenture of Lease and the mortgage bond are notarially executed instruments in the first place, and it draws the same line at a lease of one month that the Registration of Documents Ordinance draws.
temporal_note: The corpus carries section 2 as amended by Act No. 30 of 2022 and Act No. 4 of 2024, both after the matter date of 2020-04. The requirement of notarial execution itself long predates 2020, but the April 2020 wording is not in the corpus, so this provision is treated as background and no claim rests on it.
verifier_note: The excerpt is verbatim and was in force at the matter date, so applicable_to_matter_date=false and the matching corpus_gaps entry are too cautious: 30-2022 s.2 repealed only the words from the phrase beginning shall be of force to the end of the section, and 4-2024 s.2 renumbered the section, rewrote paragraphs (a) and (b) and added subsection (2); neither touched the opening words excerpted here, which therefore stood in April 2020. No claim rests on this provision, so nothing downstream changes.

formal_title: Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006
relevant_excerpt: there shall be charged a duty (hereinafter to be called "stamp duty") at such rate as the Minister may determine by Order published in the Gazette on every "specified instrument"- (a) executed, drawn or presented in Sri Lanka
why_relevant: The charging provision, and the reason the rate cannot be taken from the statute. The Act imposes the duty but leaves the rate to a Ministerial Order published in the Gazette, and subsection (2) allows different rates for different classes of instrument.
temporal_note: In force from 2006 and unamended in the corpus text; in force at 2020-04. The rate Order in force in April 2020 is not in the corpus.

formal_title: Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006
relevant_excerpt: (g) a bond or mortgage for any definite and certain sum of money and affecting any property;
why_relevant: Puts this mortgage bond inside the charge. The bond secures a definite and certain sum, Rs.3,000,000, and affects the Nugegoda house, so it is a specified instrument for the purposes of section 3.
temporal_note: In force from 2006 and unamended in the corpus text; in force at 2020-04.

formal_title: Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006
relevant_excerpt: Otherwise than in cases where there is an agreement to the contrary, stamp duty shall be payable:- (a) in the case of a policy of insurance, by the person effecting the insurance; (b) in the case of a transfer or assignment of any share, by the transferee or assignee of such share; (c) in the case of a lease, by the lessee;
why_relevant: The opening words make the statutory allocation of liability yield to any agreement between the parties, which is what a mortgage bond in favour of a lending institution normally contains. Paragraph (c) also shows that on the earlier Indenture of Lease the duty fell on the lessee, not on Kamal.
temporal_note: Section 6 was amended by section 2 of Act No. 10 of 2008, twelve years before the matter date; the corpus text applies at 2020-04.

formal_title: Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006
relevant_excerpt: (e) in all other cases, by the person drawing, making or executing such instrument.
why_relevant: The residual limb, and the one that catches a mortgage bond. No earlier paragraph of section 6 names a bond or mortgage, so the duty falls on the person drawing, making or executing it, that is Kamal Perera as mortgagor.
temporal_note: Section 6 was amended by section 2 of Act No. 10 of 2008; the residual limb (e) stands in the corpus text and applies at 2020-04.
verifier_note: Confirmed against the full text of section 6: paragraphs (a) to (e), including (dd) and (ddd) inserted by 10-2008 s.2, name no bond or mortgage, so the residual limb (e) is the operative one.

formal_title: Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006
relevant_excerpt: the stamp duty payable on any specified instrument shall be paid by means of affixing adhesive stamps to the required value, prior to, or at the time of, the execution of the instrument. The value of the stamp duty so paid shall be specified on the face of the instrument so executed
why_relevant: The default mode and time of payment. Unless the duty is compounded under section 7, adhesive stamps to the required value must be affixed before or at execution of the bond and the value stated on its face.
temporal_note: Section 8 was substituted by section 3 of Act No. 10 of 2008; the substituted text is the corpus text and applies at 2020-04.

formal_title: Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006
relevant_excerpt: Stamp duty payable on any specified instrument relating to a mortgage or lease of any immovable property may be paid, prior to, or at the time of, the execution of the specified instrument, to a prescribed bank. Where however, the stamp duty cannot be so paid due to reasons beyond the control of the person by whom the stamp duty is payable, the stamp duty shall be paid to the prescribed bank within seven days from the date of such execution. The bank shall thereupon issue a certificate in the prescribed form certifying that the stamp duty has been duly paid and such certificate shall be affixed to the instrument so executed.
why_relevant: The limb written for this very instrument. A mortgage of immovable property may be stamped by payment to a prescribed bank before or at execution, with a seven day fallback, and the bank certificate is then affixed to the bond. This answers to whom the duty is paid and by what procedure.
temporal_note: Substituted by section 3 of Act No. 10 of 2008; in force at 2020-04.

formal_title: Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006
relevant_excerpt: Any person executing a specified instrument shall at the time of the execution of such specified instrument which is not stamped with an impressed stamp, cancel the stamps thereon by writing or marking in ink on or across each stamp, his name or initials, thereby preventing the stamp from being used again. Further, where such specified instrument bears an adhesive stamp of the value of fifty rupees or more, such stamp shall be cancelled by the person executing a specified instrument by perforating the same by either cutting or pricking the stamp with a suitable instrument.
why_relevant: Part of the procedure if adhesive stamps are used. Kamal himself must cancel the stamps at execution, and stamps of fifty rupees or more must also be perforated.
temporal_note: Substituted by section 3 of Act No. 10 of 2008; in force at 2020-04.

formal_title: Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006
relevant_excerpt: Any specified instrument bearing an adhesive stamp which has not been cancelled in the manner set out in subsection (3) shall be deemed to be unstamped to the extent of the value of such stamp.
why_relevant: The sanction that makes cancellation part of the procedure rather than a formality. Uncancelled stamps count for nothing and leave the bond insufficiently stamped.
temporal_note: Substituted by section 3 of Act No. 10 of 2008; in force at 2020-04.

formal_title: Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006
relevant_excerpt: The Commissioner – General shall, be charged with the proper implementation and administration of this Act.
why_relevant: Identifies the revenue authority behind the duty. Read with section 14, the Commissioner-General is the Commissioner-General under the Inland Revenue Act, so the duty on this bond is central revenue collected through a prescribed bank rather than a Provincial Council receipt.
temporal_note: In force from 2006 and unamended in the corpus text; in force at 2020-04.
verifier_note: Confirmed by 12-2006 s.14, which gives Commissioner-General the meaning it has in the Inland Revenue Act.

formal_title: Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006
relevant_excerpt: Where an Assessor is of the opinion that an instrument liable to stamp duty has not been duly stamped, he shall assess the value of the stamp duty payable in respect of such instrument, by the person liable to pay such duty and forward a Notice to such person requiring him to pay the amount due thereon, within the time specified in the Notice.
why_relevant: What follows if the bond is understamped. An Assessor assesses the duty on the person liable and serves a notice to pay, which is the back end of the procedure Kamal is asking about.
temporal_note: In force from 2006 and unamended in the corpus text; in force at 2020-04.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless he has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided.
why_relevant: The notary's part in the procedure. The bond cannot be attested until the notary is satisfied that the stamp duty has been provided, which is why the duty is settled before or at execution.
temporal_note: The corpus shows rule (6) as substituted by section 16(4) of Act No. 31 of 2022, after the matter date, but the substituted wording is word for word the same as the wording it replaced, so the obligation stated here held at 2020-04. Rule (7A), which shifts payment of stamp duty on to the notary, was inserted by the same 2022 Act and widened by Act No. 6 of 2024, and is deliberately not relied on.
verifier_note: The wording is verbatim in the current corpus text and 31-2022 s.16(4) did substitute rule (6), but the amending Act does not set out the words it replaced and the pre-2022 text is not in the corpus, so the researcher's assertion that the substituted wording is word for word the same as the wording it replaced cannot be checked here; the provision is supporting only, so nothing turns on it.

formal_title: Western Province Financial Statute No. 6 of 1990
relevant_excerpt: There shall be charged on- (a) every instrument relating to a transfer of situated in the immovable property Western Province; (b) every document presented or filed, in proceedings instituted in any Court of law established by law, in the Western Province of Sri Lanka; (c) every transfer of a motor vehicle effected in Western Province. a stamp duty at the prescribed rate.
why_relevant: The Nugegoda house is in the Western Province, so the provincial charge has to be checked. Section 37 charges transfers of immovable property, court documents and motor vehicle transfers only. A mortgage bond is none of these, so the provincial statute does not charge it and the duty is the national duty under Act No. 12 of 2006.
temporal_note: In force from 1990; the corpus records no amendment, so the text applies at 2020-04.
verifier_note: Reading confirmed. Paragraph (a) of the corpus text is garbled, but on any reconstruction it charges a transfer of immovable property, and no limb of section 37 reaches a mortgage bond, so the researcher's conclusion holds.

formal_title: Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006
relevant_excerpt: All stamp duty payable to a Provincial Council in respect of documents and instruments referred to in List I of the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution, shall be paid to the respective Provincial Council within whose limits the instrument was executed or the property situated as the case may be
why_relevant: Background. It is the provision that would route the duty to the Western Provincial Council if a mortgage bond were a provincially charged instrument. Read with section 37 of the Western Province Financial Statute it is not, so the money does not go to the Provincial Council.
temporal_note: In force from 2006 and unamended in the corpus text; in force at 2020-04.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: But fraud or collusion in obtaining such subsequent instrument or in securing the prior registration thereof shall defeat the priority of the person claiming thereunder.
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. The gold answer for M078-Q01 twice states that fraud or collusion in securing the prior registration defeats the priority so obtained, and warns Kamal Perera against concealing the lease. That proposition comes from section 7(2), which no provision entry in the researcher's map carried: PROV-M078-001 is section 7(1) and PROV-M078-002 is section 7(4).
temporal_note: In force from 1927. The corpus records no amendment event on section 7, and none of the Registration of Documents amendment Acts in the corpus that predate the matter date (22-1958, 27-1969, 4-1974, 14-1974, 19-1976, 50-1982, 5-1990, 48-2011, 21-2013) amends section 7, so the text applies at 2020-04.
verifier_note: Excerpt checked verbatim against 23-1927/s7 by the verifier.

relevant_excerpt: When any person shall die intestate as to any of his or her property, leaving a spouse surviving, the surviving spouse shall inherit one-half of the property of such person.
why_relevant: Fixes the share of Kamani, the surviving spouse of Lalith Perera who died intestate on 2 March 2018, in Lot 5B (Assessment No. 3/2B) at one-half.
temporal_note: In force since 1876; the corpus records no amendment event for this section, so the text stood unchanged at the matter reference date of October 2019.

relevant_excerpt: Children, grandchildren, and remoter descendants are preferent to all others in the estate of the parents; all the children take equally per capita
why_relevant: Gives the remaining one-half of Lalith Perera's estate to his children Hasini and Kushan in equal per capita shares, and excludes Ruvini, who is not his descendant.
temporal_note: In force since 1876; no amendment event is recorded in the corpus, so the text stood unchanged at October 2019.

relevant_excerpt: Inheritance ab interstate to the immovable property in Sri Lanka of a person deceased shall be governed and regulated by the following provisions of this Ordinance wherever such person may have or have had his actual or matrimonial domicile.
why_relevant: Establishes that intestate succession to Lot 5B, immovable property in Sri Lanka, is governed by Part III of this Ordinance rather than by any other regime.
temporal_note: In force since 1876; no amendment event is recorded in the corpus for this section.

relevant_excerpt: The following sections of this Ordinance shall apply to the estates of such persons only as shall die after the proclamation of this Ordinance, and shall be then unmarried or (if married) shall have been married after the proclamation of this Ordinance.
why_relevant: Threshold condition for applying Part III: Lalith Perera died in 2018 and was married long after the 1876 proclamation, so the inheritance sections apply to his estate.
temporal_note: In force since 1876; no amendment event is recorded in the corpus for this section.

relevant_excerpt: Subject to the right of the surviving spouse in the preceding section mentioned, the right of inheritance is divided in the following order as respects (a) descendants, (b) ascendants, (c) collaterals.
why_relevant: Orders the classes of heirs and makes the children's entitlement expressly subject to the surviving spouse's one-half, linking section 22 to section 24.
temporal_note: In force since 1876; no amendment event is recorded in the corpus for this section.

formal_title: Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance
relevant_excerpt: Such woman shall, subject and without prejudice to any such trusts as aforesaid, have as full power of disposing of and dealing with such property by any lawful act inter vivos without the consent of the husband in case of movables, or with his written consent in the case of immovables, but not otherwise, or by last will without consent, as if she were unmarried.
why_relevant: A married woman subject to the Thesawalamai may dispose of immovable property inter vivos only with her husband's written consent. Mala Nadaraja sold Lot 5A by Deed No. 456 of 3 February 2015 while Mohan Nadaraja was alive, so his written consent was required; by Deed No. 789 of 5 April 2017 she was a widow and no consent was needed.
temporal_note: Section 6 was last amended by Ordinance No. 58 of 1947, well before the 2015 and 2017 deeds and before the matter reference date.
verifier_note: Wording verbatim, but section 6 governs the wife's separate estate, that is property held at marriage or acquired during marriage by gift, inheritance or conversion, whereas this map characterises Lots 5A and 5B as thediatheddam bought for valuable consideration under section 19(a), so on the corpus text the written-consent rule does not plainly reach these lots.

formal_title: Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance
relevant_excerpt: This Ordinance shall apply only to those Tamils to whom the Tesawalamai applies, and it shall apply in respect of their movable and immovable property wherever situate.
why_relevant: Application provision. It brings Mala Nadaraja, stated to be governed by the Thesawalamai, within the Ordinance and makes it bite on the Hendala land even though that land lies outside the Northern Province.
temporal_note: Last amended by Ordinance No. 58 of 1947; unchanged at the matter reference date.

formal_title: Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance
relevant_excerpt: On the death of either spouse one-half of the thediatheddam which belonged to the deceased spouse, and has not been disposed of by last will or otherwise, shall devolve on the surviving spouse and the other half shall devolve on the heirs of the deceased spouse.
why_relevant: Divides only the deceased spouse's thediatheddam. Lot 5B was Mala Nadaraja's own acquisition, not Mohan Nadaraja's, so on his death none of Lot 5B passed to his heirs and she remained sole owner when she sold to Lalith Perera in 2017.
temporal_note: Last amended by Ordinance No. 58 of 1947; unchanged at the matter reference date.

formal_title: Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance
relevant_excerpt: Property acquired by that spouse during the subsistence of the marriage for valuable consideration, such consideration not forming or representing any part of the separate estate of that spouse.
why_relevant: Defines thediatheddam. Lots 5A and 5B were bought by Mala Nadaraja for value on 1 August 2014 during her marriage, so they answer this description and section 20 governs what happened on her husband's death.
temporal_note: Last amended by Ordinance No. 58 of 1947; unchanged at the matter reference date.
verifier_note: The definition is quoted correctly, but section 19(a) excludes consideration drawn from the spouse's separate estate and the scenario says nothing about where Mala Nadaraja's purchase money came from, so the thediatheddam characterisation of Lots 5A and 5B is an inference rather than a finding on the text.

formal_title: Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance
relevant_excerpt: it shall be lawful for the wife to apply by petition to the District Court of the district in which she resides or in which the property is situated for an order authorizing her to dispose of or deal with such property without her husband's consent
why_relevant: The alternative to joining the husband in the deed: where consent cannot be had or is unreasonably withheld, a District Court order dispensing with it must be obtained before the wife executes the transfer.
temporal_note: In force since 1911; the corpus records no amendment event for this section.
verifier_note: Section 8 is not a free-standing alternative to consent: it operates only where the wife is deserted or separated, or the husband is imprisoned for over two years, of unsound mind, of unknown abode, unreasonably withholding consent, or where the interests of the wife or children require it, and no fact in the scenario brings Mala Nadaraja within any of those cases.

relevant_excerpt: Every person who shall claim a right to have charge of property in trust for a minor, under a will or deed, or by reason of nearness of kin, or otherwise, may apply to the Family Court for a certificate of curatorship; and no person shall be entitled to institute or defend any action connected with the estate of a minor, of which he claims the charge, until he shall have obtained such certificate
why_relevant: The statutory route by which charge of a minor's property is taken. Gayan Peiris was 15 when Deed No. 1234 of 1 August 2014 purported to sell his Lot 5A, so a duly certificated curator, not the minor himself, had to deal with that property.
temporal_note: Last amended by Act No. 79 of 1988; the text stood as shown in 2014 and at the matter reference date.
verifier_note: Section 582 says a claimant to charge of a minor's property 'may apply' for a certificate and bars an uncertificated person only from instituting or defending an action connected with the minor's estate; it does not say that a certificated curator must execute a conveyance of the minor's land, so the role assigned to it here is wider than the text supports.

relevant_excerpt: If there is no person so entitled, or if such person is unwilling to undertake the trust and there is any near relative of the minor who is willing and fit to be entrusted with the charge of his property, the court may grant a certificate to such relative.
why_relevant: Identifies who the court may certify as curator of the minor's property, and so who could lawfully have been joined in Deed No. 1234 on Gayan Peiris's behalf.
temporal_note: In force since 1889; the corpus records no amendment event for this section.

relevant_excerpt: If any of the heirs, legatees or beneficiaries of the deceased is a minor without a natural guardian, or person of unsound mind, without a guardian, steps shall be taken for the appointment of a guardian or manager, upon the making of an application to the District Judge, which application shall be heard in Chambers.
why_relevant: Gayan Peiris was a minor legatee in DC Negambo Case No. 456/DTS when the will was proved in 2013, so a guardian had to be appointed before the Executor's Conveyance was executed in his favour.
temporal_note: Last amended by Act No. 11 of 2010, before the 2013 testamentary proceedings and before the matter reference date.
verifier_note: Section 530 requires steps to be taken to appoint a guardian for a minor heir or legatee, but says nothing about the timing relied on here, namely that this had to happen before the Executor's Conveyance was executed.

relevant_excerpt: a minor shall be deemed to have attained majority or full age on his attaining the age of eighteen years, or on marriage, or on obtaining letters of venia aetatis.
why_relevant: Fixes eighteen as full age for the purposes of the Code's minors chapter. It confirms that Gayan Peiris at 15 was under disability in 2014 while Malika Peiris at 20 was not, though the general age of majority statute itself is not in this corpus.
temporal_note: Last amended by Act No. 12 of 1996; unchanged at the matter reference date. The section is expressed to apply 'For the purposes of this Chapter'.
verifier_note: Section 502 opens with 'For the purposes of this Chapter' and sits in the chapter on actions by and against minors, whereas sections 582 and 585 sit in the separate chapter on actions for the appointment of guardians, so section 502 does not supply the age threshold for those sections either, and the general age of majority remains uncited.

relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property, and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object, or for establishing any security, interest, or incumbrance affecting land or other immovable property (other than a lease at will, or for any period not exceeding one month)
why_relevant: Every link in this pedigree that is a sale, gift or transfer had to be notarially executed. It is also the provision that makes the identity of the executants of each deed, and therefore who had to be joined, a question of validity rather than of form.
temporal_note: The opening words quoted here are the original 1840 wording and were in force in October 2019. The corpus text is the consolidated version: paragraphs (a) and (b) were substituted by Act No. 30 of 2022 and Act No. 4 of 2024, and subsection (2), including the rule that a guardian may act for a minor transferee, was added only by Act No. 4 of 2024. Neither applies to deeds executed between 2008 and 2018.
verifier_note: The excerpt is verbatim but stops before the operative words; the notarial-execution requirement now sits in paragraph (a) as substituted by Act No. 30 of 2022 and read with Act No. 4 of 2024, so the version in force for the 2008 to 2018 deeds is not available in the corpus, and section 2 does not name a gift in its list of dealings.

relevant_excerpt: It shall be lawful for any person who has reached the age of eighteen years and residing within or outside Sri Lanka to execute a will bequeathing and disposing any movable and immovable property
why_relevant: Testamentary capacity for Last Will No. 980 of 6 April 2010 by Kusum Perera, the step in the pedigree that carried Lot 5A to Gayan Peiris and Lot 5B to Malika Peiris.
temporal_note: The corpus carries the text as repealed and substituted by Act No. 29 of 2022, which is later than both the 2010 will and the October 2019 matter reference date. The provision in force in 2010 was the earlier section 2 read with section 3 as amended by Act No. 5 of 1993. Background only; not relied on as decisive.
verifier_note: The corpus holds only the text substituted by Act No. 29 of 2022, so the testamentary capacity provision in force when Last Will No. 980 was made in 2010 cannot be checked here; correctly confined to background.

relevant_excerpt: it shall make order declaring the will to be proved and if the applicant claims- (i) as the executor or one of the executors of the will, and asks that probate thereof be granted to him the order shall declare that he is executor, and shall direct the grant of probate to him accordingly
why_relevant: The order proving Last Will No. 980 in DC Negambo Case No. 456/DTS on 10 March 2013 and appointing the executor whose conveyance is the next link in the pedigree.
temporal_note: Last amended by Act No. 14 of 1993, before the 2013 proceedings and before the matter reference date.

formal_title: Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance
relevant_excerpt: The respective matrimonial rights of every husband and wife married after the commencement of this Ordinance
why_relevant: Threshold provision for Part II. Section 6, on which the husband's written consent turns, applies only to a woman married after the commencement of the Ordinance, and section 5 is what carries the matrimonial rights of such a marriage into the Ordinance. The map relied on section 6 without citing the applicability provision that lets it bite.
temporal_note: In force since 1911; the corpus records no amendment event for this section, so it stood unchanged at the matter reference date of October 2019.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier as the missing Part II applicability provision for section 6.

formal_title: Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance
relevant_excerpt: shall apply to the estate of such persons only as shall die after the commencement of this Ordinance, and shall be then unmarried, or if married, shall have been married after the commencement of this Ordinance.
why_relevant: Threshold provision for Part III, the counterpart of Ordinance No. 15 of 1876 s.20 which the map did cite. Sections 19 and 20, on the meaning and devolution of thediatheddam, reach Mohan Nadaraja's estate only because he died after 1911 and married after it.
temporal_note: In force since 1911; the corpus records no amendment event for this section, so it stood unchanged at the matter reference date of October 2019.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier as the missing Part III applicability provision for sections 19 and 20.

formal_title: Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross Ingratitude Act
relevant_excerpt: An irrevocable deed of gift may be revoked on the ground of gross ingratitude, only on an Order made by a competent court, in an action filed by the donor of such deed against the donee to have the said deed revoked.
why_relevant: Directly answers the question. It confirms that a deed of gift expressed to be irrevocable is not beyond recall, fixes the single statutory ground (gross ingratitude), and restricts the mode of revocation to an order of a competent court in an action by the donor against the donee, so the donor cannot revoke by his own act.
temporal_note: In force from 2017 per the corpus (in_force_from_year 2017); no amendment_events recorded. The matter date is October 2019, so the section was in force, and the enriched deed date (March 2018) falls after the Act.

formal_title: Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross Ingratitude Act
relevant_excerpt: Court shall not entertain an action referred to in section 2, unless it is filed within a period of ten years from the date of the execution of such deed of gift and within two years from the date on which the cause of action arose.
why_relevant: A necessary statutory condition on the remedy in section 2. Whether the gift can in fact still be revoked depends on both limbs of this time bar being satisfied, so the answer turns on the deed date and on the date the cause of action arose.
temporal_note: In force from 2017 per the corpus; no amendment_events recorded. Applicable at October 2019.

formal_title: Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross Ingratitude Act
relevant_excerpt: The plaintiff in an action instituted under the provisions of this Act shall file or cause to be filed in court with the plaint, an application for registration of lis pendens
why_relevant: Sets the mandatory step that accompanies the plaint in a revocation action and identifies which Registrar of Lands the application is addressed to, depending on whether the deed is registered. It shapes how the remedy is pursued but does not decide whether the gift is revocable.
temporal_note: In force from 2017 per the corpus; no amendment_events recorded. Applicable at October 2019.
verifier_note: The excerpt is verbatim but stops at the lead-in of section 4(1) and omits paragraphs (a) and (b), which are the words that actually fix the addressee of the lis pendens application relied on in why_relevant and in claims CL-M080-Q01-005 and CL-M080-Q01-011; the full corpus body of 5-2017/s4 does support those claims.

formal_title: Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross Ingratitude Act
relevant_excerpt: Every action filed under the provisions of this Act shall be proceeded with and regulated by the procedure provided for in the Civil Procedure Code (Chapter 101).
why_relevant: Confirms that the revocation action is an ordinary civil action governed by the Civil Procedure Code, which is how the donor must proceed once the deed cannot be cancelled consensually.
temporal_note: In force from 2017 per the corpus; no amendment_events recorded. Applicable at October 2019.

formal_title: Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross Ingratitude Act
relevant_excerpt: means the Registrar of Lands appointed under the Registration of Documents Ordinance (Chapter 117) and having jurisdiction over the district in which the land which forms the subject matter of an irrevocable deed of gift which is sought to be revoked is situated
why_relevant: Defines Registrar of Lands, the officer to whom the lis pendens application under section 4 must be addressed, and so fixes the district in which that application is made.
temporal_note: In force from 2017 per the corpus; no amendment_events recorded. Applicable at October 2019. The corpus body of this section is a definition list whose defined terms have been stripped out of the lead-in, so the excerpt begins mid-sentence.
verifier_note: The excerpt is verbatim in the corpus but begins mid-sentence because the extraction stripped the defined term from the lead-in, and on its own words this definition fixes the Registrar of Lands by the district in which the land lies, which is not the section 4(1)(a) test (district in which the deed is registered), so it should be read as background to section 4 rather than as the source of the addressee rule.

relevant_excerpt: For the purpose of the application of the doctrine of lis pendens, an action duly registered as lis pendens shall be deemed to be pending from the time of registration notwithstanding that the summons has not been served on the defendant.
why_relevant: Background on why section 4 of the 2017 Act makes the lis pendens application compulsory: registration is what protects the donor against a disposition of the land by the donee while the revocation action is on foot.
temporal_note: In force from 1927; the corpus records a latest change in 1947 (Ordinance No. 13 of 1947), well before the October 2019 matter date. The corpus text of this section carries OCR damage (lis rendered as Us in several subsections); the excerpt used is taken from a clean subsection.
verifier_note: Subsection (6) is clean of the OCR damage that affects subsections (1), (4), (5) and (7) of the corpus text, and the latest recorded change (Ordinance No. 13 of 1947) is long before the October 2019 matter date.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: There shall be charged on- (a) every instrument relating to a transfer of situated in the immovable property Western Province; (b) every document presented or filed, in proceedings instituted in any Court of law established by law, in the Western Province of Sri Lanka; (c) every transfer of a motor vehicle effected in Western Province. a stamp duty at the prescribed rate. Different rates may be prescribed in respect of different classes or categories of instruments.
why_relevant: The charging section. A Deed of Gift of land and a house at Kohuwala is an instrument relating to a transfer of immovable property situated in the Western Province, so the Western Provincial Council's stamp duty regime, administered by its Assessors, applies. It also shows that the rate itself is 'prescribed' outside the Statute.
temporal_note: In force from 1990 per the corpus; no amendment events recorded. Assumed to be the text in force in October 2019, but the corpus holds no later Western Province amending statute against which to confirm this.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim in 6-1990/s37 and the closing words "a stamp duty at the prescribed rate" carry the charge; (a)-(c) are lettered paragraphs, not subsections, so the "subsection: (a)" label should be read as paragraph (a).

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: (1) Where any property is conveyed by an instrument, the stamp duty with which such instrument is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property conveyed.
why_relevant: Fixes the base on which duty is computed as the 'value' of the property conveyed, and so sends the Assessor to the statutory definition of 'value' rather than to the consideration or to any figure the parties choose to insert.
temporal_note: In force from 1990 per the corpus; no amendment events recorded; treated as in force in October 2019.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: (c) any immovable property which is gifted, being immovable property which was acquired by the donor after March 31, 1977 means - the price which, in the opinion ofthe Assessor, such property would have fetched if sold in the open market on the date which such on property was acquired by the donor, increased by an amount equal to the cost of the improvements, alterations and additions, if any, made to such property after the date on which the property was acquired by the donor, and prior to the date of the instrument by which such property is gifted ; or (ii) the price which, in the opinion of the assessor, that property would have: fetched, if sold in the open market on the date of the instrument by which such property was gifted. whichever price is the lower.
why_relevant: This is the operative rule the question asks about. For gifted immovable property acquired by the donor after 31 March 1977 the Assessor does not simply take present market value: he forms two opinions of open-market price, one at the date of acquisition (uplifted by the cost of post-acquisition improvements) and one at the date of the deed of gift, and takes the lower. The donor acquired in March 1978, so paragraph (c) and not paragraph (b) governs.
temporal_note: In force from 1990 per the corpus; no amendment events recorded. The 31 March 1977 cut-off is internal to the definition and is unaffected by the October 2019 matter date.
verifier_note: Verbatim, including the corpus OCR loss of the limb numeral "(i)"; paragraph (c) is the correct limb because the donor acquired in March 1978, and paragraph (b) (acquisition on or before 31 March 1977) is correctly excluded.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: means a sale and shall include a gift or exchange or a conveyance, without consideration, by an executor or administrators of an estate of a deceased to a person beneficially entitled to such property
why_relevant: Brings a Deed of Gift inside the section 37 charge on instruments 'relating to a transfer' of immovable property: 'Transfer' is defined to include a gift. Without it the charging section would not obviously reach a gratuitous deed.
temporal_note: In force from 1990 per the corpus; no amendment events recorded; treated as in force in October 2019.
verifier_note: Verbatim but the excerpt stops before the closing words of the definition, which exclude a deed of partition and an agreement to transfer; neither exclusion touches a deed of gift.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: means a transfer by one person to another ofany movable or immovable property made voluntarily and without consideration in money or money's worth
why_relevant: Establishes that the instrument Nimal Perera wants drawn is a 'gift' for the purposes of the Statute, which is the trigger for paragraphs (b) and (c) of the definition of 'value' rather than the ordinary open-market test in paragraph (a).
temporal_note: In force from 1990 per the corpus; no amendment events recorded; treated as in force in October 2019.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: Assessor" means a Provincial Assessor of Revenue appointed for the purposes of and includes a Senior Assessor of Revenue appointed for the purposes of this statute
why_relevant: Identifies the officer named in the question. An Assessor attached to the Western Provincial Council is a Provincial Assessor of Revenue appointed under this Statute, and it is his opinion that the definition of 'value' makes decisive.
temporal_note: In force from 1990 per the corpus; no amendment events recorded; treated as in force in October 2019.
verifier_note: Verbatim, including the OCR damage around "appointed for the purposes of"; s.106 separately defines "Provincial Assessor" as an Assessor of Revenue appointed under the Statute, which is consistent.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: the person bringing it applies to have the opinion of the Assessor as to the stamp duty, if any, with which it is chargeable, and pays a fee of two hundred and fifty rupees the Assessor shall determine the stamp duty, if any with which in his opinion the instrument is chargeable and shall notify his determination to such person in writing.
why_relevant: The adjudication route by which the Assessor is formally asked to value the property and determine the duty on the draft or executed Deed of Gift, and the source of the written determination.
temporal_note: In force from 1990 per the corpus; no amendment events recorded; treated as in force in October 2019. The adjudication fee figure may have been altered by later provincial instruments that are not in the corpus.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and the role is correctly supporting, but two corrections: adjudication under s.62 is optional (it runs only where the person bringing the instrument applies for the Assessor’s opinion), and the Rs.250 fee inside the excerpt cannot be confirmed as the October 2019 figure from this corpus.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: For the purpose of giving his opinion under section 62 the Assessor may require the person bringing the instrument to produce any such document or other evidence as is necessary to prove the facts relating to the chargeability of the instrument with stamp duty or the amount of the stamp duty with which it is chargeable
why_relevant: Explains how the Assessor gathers the material for his opinion: he can call for the 1978 deed of purchase, building plans, bills and receipts for the cost of construction, and evidence of current market price.
temporal_note: In force from 1990 per the corpus; no amendment events recorded; treated as in force in October 2019.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim; it stops before the proviso relieving a person who furnishes evidence from penalty, which does not affect the valuation point.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: (1) The Assessor shall certify by endorsement on any instrument brought to him under Section 62 that any stamp duty with which such instrument is chargeable has been paid or that such instrument is not chargeable with stamp duty.
why_relevant: Completes the adjudication procedure: once the value is settled and the duty paid, the Assessor endorses the instrument. Supporting context for how the Assessor's valuation is given effect.
temporal_note: In force from 1990 per the corpus; no amendment events recorded; treated as in force in October 2019.

number_and_year: Statute No. 6 of 1990 (Provincial Council, Western Province)
relevant_excerpt: Every notary public who attests an instrument of conveyance shall before doing SO take all reasonable steps to satisfy himself that the value on which the stamp duty is paid represents the value of the property conveyed.
