why_relevant: Background on why prompt registration of the original matters: an unregistered instrument is void against a later instrument taken for value and duly registered.
temporal_note: No amendment to section 7 is recorded in the corpus; the text was in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: (2) Where a notary acts in violation of or disregards or neglects to observe the provisions of rule (26) set out in section 31 the Registrar-General may, by a written notice served on him personally or sent by registered post, call upon such notary to comply with the requirements of the said rule within such further period of time as he may specify in such notice for such purpose.
why_relevant: Consequence of neglecting the duplicate rule: the Registrar-General may call on the notary to comply within a further period and, on default, the Minister may suspend him from office.
temporal_note: Section 34 as it stands in the corpus is the replacement enacted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 31 of 2022, s. 17, which postdates April 2019; it also refers to rule (30A), itself only inserted in 2022. The corpus does not hold the pre-2022 section 34, so the enforcement provision in force in April 2019 cannot be quoted. Recorded as context for the verifier only and not relied on by any claim.
verifier_note: The corpus holds only the section 34 substituted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 31 of 2022 s.17, whose subsection (1)(b) itself refers to rule (30A), inserted in 2022; the penal and suspension provisions that governed breach of rules (24), (26) and (29) in April 2019 cannot be read off the corpus, so no consequence for the duplicate duties is verifiable at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: (1) The provisions of rules (20), (23), (24), (25), and (26) set out in section 31, and of rule (16) as to the statement of the boundaries, shall not apply to any of the following deeds or instruments:-
why_relevant: The exception that has to be cleared before rules (20), (24) and (26) are applied: they do not apply to the listed classes of deeds, none of which covers a deed of transfer of land in Sri Lanka.
temporal_note: No amendment to section 32 is recorded in the corpus; the text was in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: No instrument shall be deemed to be invalid by reason only of the failure of any notary to observe any provision of any rule set out in section 31 in respect of any matter of form
why_relevant: Qualifies the consequences of default: breach of a rule in section 31 in a matter of form does not by itself invalidate the instrument, so the sanction falls on the notary rather than on the deed.
temporal_note: No amendment to section 33 is recorded in the corpus; the text was in force in April 2019.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and supports the saving, but the excerpt stops before the proviso, which preserves the invalidity of an instrument that fails to comply with any other written law; the conclusion drawn from section 33 has to be read subject to that proviso.

relevant_excerpt: (d) the agent of any such person or a attorney-at-law or notary acting on behalf of any such person. (2) Either the original or a duly attested or certified copy of the instrument may be presented for registration
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. It governs what the notary actually does with the original when he registers it: a notary acting on behalf of a party is a person who may present the instrument for registration, and the thing presented need not be the original, because a duly attested or certified copy may be presented instead. It is the provision the researcher's rule claim on the original had to clear.
temporal_note: Section 26 stands in the corpus in the 1990 consolidated edition with in_force_from_year 1927 and no recorded later change; none of the amending Acts in the corpus (Nos. 22 of 1958, 48 of 2011, 21 of 2013, 32 of 2022, 18 of 2024) touches it, so this was the text in force in April 2019.
verifier_note: Excerpt checked verbatim against 23-1927/s26 by the verifier.

relevant_excerpt: (1) After registration, the Registrar shall endorse the instrument in the prescribed manner and return it on demand to the person who presented it for registration or his agent.
why_relevant: Added by the verifier as background. It completes the account of the original: once registration is effected the Registrar endorses the instrument and returns it on demand to the person who presented it or his agent, so the original comes back to the notary who presented it and is then handed to the client, unlike the duplicate, which stays with the registrar.
temporal_note: Section 28 stands in the corpus in the 1990 consolidated edition with in_force_from_year 1927 and no recorded later change; none of the Registration of Documents amending Acts in the corpus touches it, so this was the text in force in April 2019.
verifier_note: Excerpt checked verbatim against 23-1927/s28 by the verifier.

relevant_excerpt: No will, testament, or codicil containing any devise of land or other immovable property, or any bequest of movable property, or for any other purpose whatsoever, shall be valid unless it shall be in writing and executed subject to the provisions specified in subsection (2);
why_relevant: Sets the validity condition for every will: it must be in writing and executed in the prescribed manner. It is the provision that makes the mode of execution a question of validity rather than of good practice.
temporal_note: In force from 1840. The corpus text is the version substituted by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 30 of 2022, which post-dates 2019-04; the requirement that a will be in writing and executed in the prescribed manner was, however, the substance of the section long before the matter date.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim of the current text, but the renumbering as subsection (1) and the closing words ‘subject to the provisions specified in subsection (2)’ were made by Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 30 of 2022 s.3(1)-(2); in April 2019 the section read ‘executed in the manner hereinafter mentioned’ and that repealed wording is not in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: The testator shall - (a) sign; and (b) affix his left or right thumb impression, at the foot or end of the will, testament or codicil referred to in subsection (1), before a notary public and two witnesses who shall be present at the same time
why_relevant: Fixes the three actors who must be together at one time for a valid will: the testator signing at the foot or end, a notary public, and two witnesses. This is why execution cannot happen by post, by proxy or in stages, and therefore why someone must travel to the bedridden testator.
temporal_note: The requirement of signature at the foot or end before a notary public and two witnesses present at the same time was in force in April 2019. The additional thumb-impression requirement in paragraph (b) and its proviso were introduced by Act No. 30 of 2022 and did NOT apply at the matter date; the excerpt is relied on only for the signature, notary and two-witnesses-present-together elements.
verifier_note: Confirmed against 30-2022 s.3(3): the whole of subsection (2) was added in 2022 and the pre-2022 words prescribing the manner of execution were repealed by the same section, so the April 2019 requirement of signature at the foot or end before a notary and two witnesses present together is a reconstruction that cannot be read anywhere in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any area other than that in which he is authorized to practice, nor in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice
why_relevant: The decisive constraint. A notary's competence to attest is territorial: he may not attest anywhere outside the area named in his warrant. A will attested at the testator's home outside that area is attested in breach of this rule.
temporal_note: Rule (22) is part of the original 1907 rules and is not among the rules recorded as substituted by the 2011, 2022 or 2024 amending Acts; treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless the person executing the same and the witnesses shall have signed the same in his presence and in the presence of one another, and unless he shall have signed the same in the presence of the executant and of the attesting witnesses.
why_relevant: Makes simultaneous physical presence of testator, both witnesses and the notary a notarial duty as well as a validity requirement, so the whole signing must happen in one sitting at the testator's bedside.
temporal_note: Original 1907 rule, not recorded as substituted by any amending Act in the corpus; treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument to which at least two witnesses have not subscribed their signatures in letters.
why_relevant: Requires two witnesses who sign in letters, which matches the two witnesses demanded by the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance and settles that a mark alone from a witness is not enough.
temporal_note: Original 1907 rule, not recorded as substituted by any amending Act in the corpus; treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: unless and until he shall have read over and explained the same, or caused the same to be explained, in the presence and hearing of such person and, except in the case of wills and codicils, in the presence of the attesting witnesses.
why_relevant: Governs reading over where the executant cannot read or asks for it, and carries the express exception for wills and codicils: the reading need not be done in the presence of the attesting witnesses, which protects the confidentiality of the testator's dispositions.
temporal_note: Original 1907 rule with the wills exception; not recorded as substituted by any amending Act in the corpus; treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: He shall without delay duly attest every deed or instrument which shall be executed or acknowledged before him, and shall sign and seal such attestation. In such attestation he shall state- (a) that the said deed or instrument was signed by the party and the witnesses thereto in his presence and in the presence of one another;
why_relevant: Requires the notary to draw, sign and seal an attestation recording that the testator and both witnesses signed in his presence and in the presence of one another. The attestation is the instrument's own proof that the statutory mode of execution was followed.
temporal_note: The rule (20) chapeau and paragraph (a) are long-standing; the corpus records substitutions to parts of rule (20) by Act No. 31 of 2022 and Act No. 6 of 2024, so the exact 2019 wording of the later paragraphs is uncertain and is not relied on here.

relevant_excerpt: He shall correctly insert in letters in every deed or instrument executed before him the day, month, and year on which and the place where the same is executed, and shall sign the same.
why_relevant: The notary must state the true place of execution in letters. He cannot cure a territorial problem by recording a place inside his own area when the will was in fact signed elsewhere, so this rule locks rule (22) in place.
temporal_note: Original 1907 rule, not recorded as substituted by any amending Act in the corpus; treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: The Minister may on application made in that behalf grant to a notary, having a warrant authorizing him to practice within a judicial zone, a fresh warrant authorizing him to practice within another judicial zone.
why_relevant: The only route in the corpus by which this notary himself could become competent to attest in the testator's area, and the reason the answer is either a fresh warrant or a different notary rather than a flat impossibility.
temporal_note: Substituted by the Notaries (Amendment) Law No. 20 of 1976, well before the matter date; in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: he shall satisfy himself, before accepting them as witnesses, that they are persons of good repute and that they are well acquainted with the executant and know his proper name, occupation, and residence
why_relevant: Constrains who may be used as the two witnesses at a bedside execution: people of good repute who genuinely know the testator, not whoever happens to be in the house.
temporal_note: The good-repute and acquaintance limb quoted here is long-standing. The identity-document limb of rule (9), covering the national identity card, passport bio-page and driving licence, was introduced by later amendments recorded in the corpus and is not relied on for April 2019.
verifier_note: In April 2019 the quoted duty was introduced by the words ‘and in the latter case, he shall satisfy himself’, which Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(3) replaced with ‘he shall’; at the matter date the good-repute and acquaintance duty therefore applied where the executant was known to the notary through the two attesting witnesses, not unconditionally as the excerpt now reads.

relevant_excerpt: Every such attestation shall be substantially in the form E in the Second Schedule, and shall be legibly signed by him in the language in which the deed or instrument is written
why_relevant: Prescribes the form and language of the attestation the notary must sign at the bedside.
temporal_note: Original 1907 rule, not recorded as substituted by any amending Act in the corpus; treated as in force in April 2019. Form E itself is not reproduced as a searchable section in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: He shall carefully preserve as his protocol a draft or copy of every deed or instrument executed or acknowledged before him, to which shall be attached his signature and those of the party and witnesses to the original deed or instrument
why_relevant: The protocol obligation applies to wills as well, and the same rule limits the register entry for a will to its number and date, which is how the notary's record-keeping duty is reconciled with testamentary secrecy.
temporal_note: Original 1907 rule, not recorded as substituted by any amending Act in the corpus; treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: any other rule set out in section 31, shall be guilty of an offence, and shall, on conviction after summary trial before a Magistrate, be liable to a fine not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, in addition to any civil liability he may incur thereby.
why_relevant: Shows the consequence for the notary personally if he attests outside his area: rule (22) is not in the lighter penalty lists in paragraphs (a) and (b), so it falls into the residual paragraph (c).
temporal_note: The corpus carries the consolidated text including fine levels raised by later amendments; the fine figures may differ from those in force in April 2019, so the provision is used for the fact of criminal liability, not for the amount.
verifier_note: Section 34 was repealed and replaced by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.17, so the paragraph lettering, the rule lists in paragraphs (a) and (b) and the fine levels are all 2022 text; the April 2019 section is not in the corpus, so the inference that rule (22) falls into the residual paragraph (c) cannot be read off the law in force at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: No instrument shall be deemed to be invalid by reason only of the failure of any notary to observe any provision of any rule set out in section 31 in respect of any matter of form
why_relevant: Separates the two consequences that this scenario mixes together. Breach of a section 31 rule of form does not by itself void the instrument, but the proviso keeps intact any invalidity arising under another written law, which is where the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance requirements bite.
temporal_note: Original 1907 section, not recorded as amended in the corpus; treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: If any person shall attest the execution of any will, testament, or codicil to whom or to whose wife or husband any beneficial devise, legacy, estate, interest, gift, disposition, or appointment of or affecting any immovable or movable property (other than and except charges and directions for the payment of any debt or debts) shall be thereby given or made, such devise, legacy, estate, interest, gift, disposition, or appointment shall, so far only as concerns such person attesting the execution of such will
why_relevant: A bedside execution tempts the notary to use family members present in the house as witnesses. This section makes any benefit under the will void as against an attesting witness or that witness's spouse, so the choice of witnesses is a substantive matter, not a formality.
temporal_note: Original 1840 section, not recorded as amended in the corpus; treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: Every notary shall be bound to have his office within the area specified in his warrant; and any notary infringing this provision shall be liable to have his warrant withdrawn by the Minister.
why_relevant: Context for the notary's residence at Battaramulla: where he lives is regulated only through the location of his office, and it is the area specified in the warrant, not his residence, that fixes where he may attest.
temporal_note: Original 1907 section, not recorded as amended in the corpus; treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: The taking of instructions for or signature to a deed or instrument shall not be a good cause for absence from office, unless the person whose instructions or signature is to be taken is believed to be on the point of death.
why_relevant: Background showing that the Ordinance contemplates a notary going out to a person who cannot come to him, while treating that as exceptional. It applies only to notaries who are not attorneys-at-law.
temporal_note: Part of the additional rules for notaries who are not attorneys-at-law; not recorded as substituted by any amending Act in the corpus; treated as in force in April 2019.

formal_title: Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance
relevant_excerpt: Every writing, deed, or instrument which by section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance is required to be executed in the manner therein mentioned in order to its validity, shall, if made after this Ordinance shall come into operation, be valid and effectual, so far as relates to the execution thereof, if the same be signed by the party making the same or by some person lawfully authorized by him, and by two or more witnesses present at the same time, in the presence of some District Judge
why_relevant: Recorded because it is the obvious alternative to look for and it fails: the substitute execution before a District Judge or authorised Justice of the Peace is offered only for instruments required to be executed under section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, not for wills under section 4 of that Ordinance.
temporal_note: Original 1852 section, not recorded as amended in the corpus; treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: It shall be lawful for any person who has reached the age of eighteen years and residing within or outside Sri Lanka to execute a will bequeathing and disposing any movable and immovable property
why_relevant: Background on testamentary capacity and the freedom to dispose. It confirms that the client's problem is one of execution, not of capacity to make a will at all.
temporal_note: The corpus text is the version repealed and substituted by Act No. 29 of 2022, which post-dates the matter date of 2019-04. The April 2019 wording is not in the corpus, so this provision is used as background only and is not relied on for any operative step.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim of the text substituted by Act No. 29 of 2022; the April 2019 text is not in the corpus, so the provision cannot support even a background statement about testamentary capacity as at the matter date.

relevant_excerpt: in the case of a will- (i) set out in the attestation of the will that the testator was in good and sound mind to execute the will; and (ii) enter in the deed register maintained by him, the number assigned to such will, the date and the name of the testator.
why_relevant: The will-specific content of a notarial attestation in the current law: a statement that the testator was of sound mind, plus a limited register entry.
temporal_note: Recorded in the corpus among the parts of rule (20) substituted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 and the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 6 of 2024, both later than 2019-04. It is therefore not treated as indispensable and is flagged for the verifier.
verifier_note: Wording verified and the temporal finding confirmed against 31-2022 s.16(11)(d), which inserted paragraph (h); because it was not in force in April 2019 it has been moved from supporting to background and its reasoning edge to PROV-M092-007 removed.

relevant_excerpt: Every warrant issued to a notary under the provisions of section 3* or section 4* authorizing him to practice as a notary in any judicial division in which he resides, shall be deemed to authorize him to practice as a notary in the judicial zone in which he resides.
why_relevant: Measures the area that rule (22) protects. Read with section 3(1) and section 4(2), which entitle a notary to a warrant for the judicial zone in which he resides, this section deems a warrant expressed for a judicial division to authorise practice throughout the judicial zone of the notary residence. It is therefore the provision that decides whether a warrant expressed as "Colombo", held by a notary residing at Battaramulla, reaches Mount Lavinia, and the researcher treated that question as a scenario fact instead.
temporal_note: Inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Law No. 20 of 1976 s.4 and not amended since; in force in April 2019.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked as a verbatim substring of 1-1907/s4A.

relevant_excerpt: Before any deed or instrument (other than a will or codicil) affecting any interest in land or other immovable property is drawn by him, he shall search or cause to be searched the registers in the land registry to ascertain the state of the title in regard to such land and whether any prior deed affecting any interest in such land has been registered
why_relevant: The only provision that speaks directly to what a notary must do before the deed is drawn: search the land registry registers for the state of the title and for prior registered deeds. It is the statutory core of the answer.
temporal_note: Rule (17)(a) was in force in April 2019. Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022, s 16(10) repealed and replaced only paragraph (b) of rule (17) and added new paragraphs (c) to (e); paragraph (a) was not touched by the 2022 or the 2024 amendment. The proviso allowing the parties to dispense with the search in writing was also in force.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument, other than a will or codicil, affecting land or other immovable property, unless the deed or instrument embodies therin or in a Schedule annexed therto an accurate and clear description of the said land or other property affected thereby, showing its boundaries, extent, situation specifying the district, pattu, korale, Divisional Secretary's Division, local authority division and the Grama Niladari Division
why_relevant: The notary cannot draft the schedule until he has the material for an accurate description of the land by boundaries, extent and situation. Gathering that material is a pre-drafting step.
temporal_note: In force in April 2019. Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022, s 16(9)(a) only substituted the closing words of rule (16)(a) to add condominium parcels; the words quoted here are the pre-2022 text (the spellings 'therin' and 'therto' are as printed in the corpus).

relevant_excerpt: if such property consist of a share of a land or other property, the deed shall state whether it is a divided or undivided share, and the fractional part which it is of the whole. If it be a divided share, such share shall be clearly and accurately defined by its particular boundaries and extent
why_relevant: Wimal is buying a portion, not the whole estate. Rule (16)(b) requires the deed to say whether the share is divided or undivided and, if divided, to define it by its own boundaries and extent, which in practice requires a survey plan of the portion before drafting.
temporal_note: In force in April 2019. The 2022 amendment (s 16(9)(b)) only deleted the proviso at the end of rule (16)(b); the sentences quoted here are unchanged.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and unaffected by the 2022 amendment, but 31-2022 s.16(9)(b) deleted a proviso at the end of rule (16)(b) that was still in force in April 2019 and is absent from the consolidated corpus text, so the April 2019 paragraph cannot be read in full.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: The transfer of ownership of a tea or rubber estate on or after the appointed day shall, subject to the provisions of subsections (2) and (3), be null and void unless- (a) a certificate of consent of the Board to such transfer has been previously obtained by the transferor, and (b) such transfer is effected in accordance with the conditions, if any, subject to which such consent has been granted.
why_relevant: If the land is a rubber estate within the meaning of the Act, the transfer of a portion of it is null and void unless the transferor has previously obtained the Board's certificate of consent. Checking whether the Act applies, and seeing the certificate, is an indispensable pre-drafting step.
temporal_note: In force since the appointed day, 11 December 1957 (s 2), and unamended as at April 2019.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: means a rubber estate of not less than one hundred acres in extent which, under the Rubber Control Act is or is deemed to be an estate registered under that Act
why_relevant: The consent requirement in s 3(1) only bites if the land answers this definition. The notary must therefore establish the extent of the estate and whether it is registered under the Rubber Control Act before he can know whether a certificate of consent is needed.
temporal_note: In force in April 2019. The corpus body of s 25 prints the defined terms in a separate list, so the definition reads as a bare 'means ...' clause; the term defined is 'rubber estate'. The recorded amendment events on s 25 relate to the coconut estate and local authority definitions dealt with in 2005.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: with reference to any tea or rubber estate, means the transfer of ownership of such estate or any portion thereof by sale, exchange or gift other than a gift by a testamentary disposition
why_relevant: This definition is what brings the sale of a portion of the estate, and not merely a sale of the whole, within s 3(1). Without it the Fragmentation Act would look irrelevant to a purchase of part of an estate.
temporal_note: In force in April 2019; the corpus body prints the defined term separately from the definition, as noted for PROV-M093-005.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: Where a certificate of consent to the transfer of ownership of a tea or rubber estate is issued by the Board, such certificate shall be attached to the deed by which such transfer is effected, and the notary attesting such deed shall in his attestation state that such certificate has been issued in respect of such transfer and specify the number, if any, and the date of issue of such certificate
why_relevant: The certificate has to be in the notary's hands before drafting, because it must be attached to the deed and its number and date recited in the attestation. Failure is an offence under s 5.
temporal_note: In force since 1957 and unamended as at April 2019.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: Every application for the consent of the Board to the transfer of ownership or the partition by deed of, or to the institution of a partition action in respect of, a tea or rubber estate shall- (a) be made in writing by the proprietor or any one of the proprietors of such estate or by the authorized agent of such proprietor or proprietors; (b) be addressed to the Chairman of the Board and transmitted to or delivered at the office of the Board
why_relevant: Tells the notary who must apply for consent (the proprietor, that is the vendor) and what the application must contain, so he can advise the parties on the step that has to be completed before the deed is drawn.
temporal_note: In force since 1957 and unamended as at April 2019.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: No officer of a local authority shall approve a blocking out plan of any land which is a tea estate, a rubber estate or a coconut estate, as the case may be, within the meaning of the Act, unless a certificate of consent under section 14 of the Act has been issued by the Board relating to such estate.
why_relevant: Carving a portion out of the estate needs a blocking out plan, and the local authority may not approve one without the Board's certificate. This fixes the order of the pre-drafting steps: consent first, then approval of the plan, then the deed.
temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 20 of 2005, s 9, so in force well before April 2019.

formal_title: Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act
relevant_excerpt: The Board shall grant its consent- (a) to the transfer of ownership of a tea or rubber estate which does not involve the division of such estate into a number of lots; (b) to the transfer of ownership of a tea or rubber estate which involves the division of such estate into a number of lots, or to the partition by deed of a tea or rubber estate
why_relevant: Background on the grounds on which the Board must consent, which lets the notary tell the client at the outset how the application for a divided block is likely to be treated.
temporal_note: In force since 1957 and unamended as at April 2019.
verifier_note: The excerpt stops at the opening words of paragraph (b) and omits sub-paragraphs (i) to (iii), which are the conditions that actually govern consent to a division into lots, so as quoted s 8(1) reads as an unconditional duty to consent; the excerpt should be extended before the answer relies on it.

relevant_excerpt: unless it is duly registered under this Chapter, or, if the land has come within the operation of the Land Registration Ordinance, 1877f, in the books mentioned in section 26 of that Ordinance, be void as against all parties claiming an adverse interest thereto on valuable consideration by virtue of any subsequent instrument which is duly registered under this Chapter
why_relevant: Explains why the pre-drafting search matters: priority turns on registration, so an unnoticed registered prior instrument can defeat the purchaser.
temporal_note: In force since 1927 and unamended as at April 2019 (the trailing 'f' is a footnote marker printed in the corpus text).
verifier_note: The excerpt is verbatim but begins mid-sentence and drops the subject ('An instrument executed or made on or after the 1st day of January, 1864 ... shall'), so it does not stand as a proposition on its own; the priority point it is cited for is correct.

relevant_excerpt: all duplicates and copies and all books and indexes kept under this Ordinance may be searched and examined by any person claiming to be interested therein or by his attorney-at-law or agent duly authorized thereto in writing, and certified copies of or extracts from any such duplicate, copy, or book may be obtained if required
why_relevant: This is the statutory right that makes the search under rule (17)(a) possible, and the source of the certified extract the notary should obtain.
temporal_note: In force since 1927 and unamended as at April 2019.
verifier_note: Section 42 confers a right, subject to the prescribed regulations, to search and to obtain certified copies or extracts; it imposes no duty on a notary. The duty to obtain a certified extract of the folio was created by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022, s 16(10)(a), inserting rule (17)(b)(i), and did not exist in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: Every instrument presented for registration shall be registered in the book allotted to the division in which the land affected by the instrument is situated and in the folio in which
why_relevant: Fixes the registry at which the search has to be made: the division in which the land lies, that is Ratnapura, not the notary's own district of Colombo.
temporal_note: In force in April 2019; the only recorded change is by Act No. 14 of 1974.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any area other than that in which he is authorized to practice, nor in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice nor authenticate or attest any deed or instrument drawn in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice.
why_relevant: The notary is licensed for Colombo while the land is in Ratnapura. Rule (22) restricts the area and language of attestation, not the situation of the land, so the notary must plan execution within his own area and in his own language before he starts drafting.
temporal_note: In force in April 2019; rule (22) was not touched by the 2011, 2022 or 2024 amendments.

relevant_excerpt: It shall be the duty of every notary to endeavour to ascertain the true and full consideration for the execution of any deed, and to insert and set forth the same in such deed.
why_relevant: Ascertaining the true consideration is an instruction-taking step that precedes drafting, and it feeds both the deed and the stamp duty computation.
temporal_note: Subsection (1) has stood since 1907. The 2005 and 2022 amendments changed only the fine in subsection (2).

relevant_excerpt: When a deed transferring any immovable property is executed or acknowledged before a notary, he shall use his best endeavours to obtain the title deed, if any, of such property
why_relevant: Calling for the vendor's title deeds is the practical first step that both supports the registry search and lets the notary trace the devolution of title before drafting.
temporal_note: In force in April 2019; rule (33) was not touched by the 2011, 2022 or 2024 amendments.
verifier_note: Rule (33) is triggered when a deed is executed or acknowledged before a notary, so on its terms it is a duty at execution rather than before drafting; it supports calling for the title deeds at the instruction stage only by inference.

relevant_excerpt: Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary in any other written law, the transfer of title of any land situated in Sri Lanka, shall be prohibited if such transfer is- (a) to a foreigner; or (b) to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act where any foreign shareholding in such company, either direct or indirect, is fifty per cent or above
why_relevant: Before drafting, the notary must satisfy himself that the transferee is not within the prohibition; an alienation in contravention of the Act is void under s 18.
temporal_note: In force from 2014 and in force in April 2019 as amended by Acts No. 3 of 2017 and No. 21 of 2018.
verifier_note: The quoted words of s 2(1) were in force in April 2019, but the temporal note is wrong on the amending Acts: the corpus records no amendment event on 38-2014/s2, and Act No. 3 of 2017 inserted s 5A while Act No. 21 of 2018 amended ss 3 and 5A.

relevant_excerpt: means a person who is not a citizen of Sri Lanka
why_relevant: Defines the class the notary has to exclude when he checks the purchaser's status, which is why proof of citizenship or identity is taken at the instruction stage.
temporal_note: In force in April 2019. As with other interpretation sections in this corpus, the body prints defined terms separately from their definitions.

relevant_excerpt: the maximum extent of agricultural land which may be owned by any person, in this Law referred to as the " ceiling ", shall (a) if such land consists exclusively of paddy land, be twenty-five acres; or (b) if such land does not consist exclusively of paddy land, be fifty acres
why_relevant: Rubber land is agricultural land, so before drafting the notary should check what agricultural land the purchaser already owns, since the ceiling limits what he may acquire.
temporal_note: In force since 1972; last recorded change by Act No. 39 of 1981, well before April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: Where after the date of commencement of this Law any person becomes the owner of agricultural land in excess of the ceiling, any such land owned by such person in excess of the ceiling shall as from that date- (a) be deemed to vest in the Commission
why_relevant: Shows the consequence of skipping the ceiling check: the excess vests in the Commission, so the purchase would not give the client what he is paying for.
temporal_note: In force in April 2019 as amended in 1981 and 1986.

relevant_excerpt: No plan or map or copy or tracing of a plan or map shall be receivable in evidence in any court in Sri Lanka unless such plan or map has been prepared (a)by or on behalf of the Surveyor-General by a registered surveyor duly authorised by him and certified by the Surveyor-General or by a registered surveyor duly authorised by him for such purpose
why_relevant: The divided portion has to be surveyed before it can be described under rule (16)(b); this section is why the plan should come from the Surveyor-General's department or a registered licensed surveyor.
temporal_note: In force since 2002 and unamended as at April 2019. The corpus body repeats paragraph (a); that is an artefact of the source text.
verifier_note: Section 13 governs the admissibility of a plan in evidence; it does not require a survey to be made. It supports the survey step only indirectly, and the requirement to define a divided share by its own boundaries and extent comes from Notaries Ordinance s 31 rule (16)(b), not from the Survey Act.

relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property, and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object
why_relevant: Background: this section is what makes notarial execution of a writing indispensable to a sale of land, and so explains why the notary's pre-drafting duties arise at all.
temporal_note: The requirement of a notarially attested writing has stood since 1840 and applied in April 2019, but the corpus text of s 2 is the version substituted by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Acts No. 30 of 2022 and No. 4 of 2024. Only the opening words, which those Acts did not change, are quoted, and nothing in the answer depends on the post-2019 wording.

relevant_excerpt: there shall be charged a duty (hereinafter to be called "stamp duty") at such rate as the Minister may determine by Order published in the Gazette on every "specified instrument"- (a) executed, drawn or presented in Sri Lanka
why_relevant: Stamp duty has to be quantified and provided for before the deed is engrossed, so the notary must obtain the value of the portion and compute the duty at the instruction stage.
temporal_note: In force since 2006 and unamended as at April 2019. The rate Order itself is not in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: Otherwise than in cases where there is an agreement to the contrary, stamp duty shall be payable:- (a) in the case of a policy of insurance, by the person effecting the insurance
why_relevant: Identifies who bears the duty in the absence of agreement, which the notary needs to settle with the parties before drafting.
temporal_note: In force in April 2019 as amended by Act No. 10 of 2008.
verifier_note: The quoted paragraph (a) concerns policies of insurance. The limb that carries the claim is paragraph (e), 'in all other cases, by the person drawing, making or executing such instrument', which is not in the excerpt.

relevant_excerpt: includes (i) the growing of rice, all field crops, spices and condiments, industrial crops, vegetables, fruits, flowers, pasture and fodder; (ii) dairy farming, livestock-rearing and breeding; (iii) plant and fruit nurseries; means land used or capable of being used for agriculture within the meaning given in this Law and shall include private lands
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. The ceiling in s 3(1) bites only on 'agricultural land', and the map relied on the unstated premise that rubber land answers that description. Section 66 supplies it: 'agriculture' includes the growing of industrial crops, and 'agricultural land' means land used or capable of being used for agriculture. Without this definition the ceiling limb of the answer rests on an uncited assumption.
temporal_note: In force in April 2019. The corpus records one change, by Act No. 39 of 1981 s 15, well before the matter date. As with the other interpretation sections in this corpus the body prints the defined terms separately from the definitions; 'agriculture' is the first defined term and 'agricultural land' the second, matching the order of the quoted clauses.

relevant_excerpt: No will, testament, or codicil containing any devise of land or other immovable property, or any bequest of movable property, or for any other purpose whatsoever, shall be valid unless it shall be in writing and executed subject to the provisions specified in subsection (2)
why_relevant: Establishes that a codicil, like a will, is invalid unless it is in writing and executed with the prescribed formalities; this is why the client's wishes must be reduced to a written, notarially executed codicil rather than a note or an alteration of the existing will.
temporal_note: The corpus text is section 4 as renumbered and amended by section 3 of the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 30 of 2022, which is after the April 2019 matter date. In April 2019 the section required the will to be in writing and executed 'in the manner hereinafter mentioned' and did not require a thumb impression. The pre-2022 wording is not in the corpus, so this provision is recorded as supporting only and is not treated as indispensable.

relevant_excerpt: No will, testament, or codicil, or any part thereof, shall be revoked otherwise than by the marriage of the testator or testatrix, or by another will, testament, or codicil executed in manner herein before required
why_relevant: The client wants to displace clause 5 of Last Will No. 3250. Part of a will can only be revoked by another will or codicil executed with the same formalities, which is the authority for effecting the change by a codicil containing an express revocation of clause 5.
temporal_note: In force from 1840; the corpus records no amendment event for this section, so the text applied unchanged in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: No obliteration, interlineations, or other alteration made in any will, testament, or codicil after the execution thereof shall be valid or have any effect, except so far as the words or effect of the will, testament, or codicil before such alteration shall not be apparent, unless such alteration shall be executed in like manner as herein before is required for the execution of the will
why_relevant: Explains why clause 5 cannot simply be struck out or written over on the 2009 will: any alteration after execution has no effect unless executed with will formalities, so a separate codicil is the appropriate instrument.
temporal_note: The section carries an amendment event by section 4 of Act No. 30 of 2022 (after the matter date), but that amendment inserted the thumb, finger and toe impression wording later in the section and in the proviso. The limb quoted here is the original 1840 wording and applied unchanged in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: If any person shall attest the execution of any will, testament, or codicil to whom or to whose wife or husband any beneficial devise, legacy, estate, interest, gift, disposition, or appointment of or affecting any immovable or movable property (other than and except charges and directions for the payment of any debt or debts) shall be thereby given or made, such devise, legacy, estate, interest, gift, disposition, or appointment shall, so far only as concerns such person attesting the execution of such will, testament, or codicil, or the wife or husband of such person, or any person claiming under such person
why_relevant: Constrains the choice of attesting witnesses for the codicil: none of the beneficiaries named in it (Himali, Hemal, Kumudu, Bandula, Karunadasa) or their spouses may attest it, or the gift to that witness is void. The two attesting witnesses named in the scenario take no benefit, so the rule is satisfied.
temporal_note: In force from 1840; no amendment event recorded in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: Whenever in this Ordinance the word 'will' is used it shall be construed to extend to a testament and to a codicil, and to any other testamentary disposition
why_relevant: Definition provision: everything the Wills Ordinance says about wills applies to the codicil to be drafted, including the republication rule in section 6.
temporal_note: The section carries an amendment event by section 6 of the Wills (Amendment) Act No. 29 of 2022, but that amendment substituted words in the definition of 'landed property' only. The limb quoted here is the 1844 wording and applied in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: Every will re-executed or republished, or revived by any codicil, shall for the purpose of this Ordinance be deemed to have been made at the time at which the same shall be so re-executed or republished or revived.
why_relevant: Supports the closing confirmation clause of the codicil. Because the client wants all other clauses of Last Will No. 3250 to stand, the codicil should confirm the will, and the confirmed will is then deemed to have been made at the date of the codicil.
temporal_note: In force from 1844; no amendment event recorded in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: Every testator shall have full power to make such testamentary disposition as he shall feel disposed
why_relevant: Background: the testator's freedom to redistribute his property among his wife, children, driver and servant by codicil.
temporal_note: The corpus text of section 2 is the version repealed and substituted by section 2 of the Wills (Amendment) Act No. 29 of 2022, after the matter date. Recorded as background only.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless one of the executants to the deed or instrument or the two attesting witnesses be known to notary or by the identity of the executants to a deed or instrument is established by such notary by inspection of the national identity card, bio-page of the passport or the driving licence of such executants; he shall satisfy himself, before accepting them as witnesses, that they are persons of good repute and that they are well acquainted with the executant and know his proper name, occupation, and residence
why_relevant: Governs the situation where the executant is not known to the notary: identification through the two attesting witnesses who are known to the notary. This is the rule the attestation must reflect.
temporal_note: This is rule (9) as substituted by section 16(6) of the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 and further amended by section 3(3) of Act No. 6 of 2024, both after the April 2019 matter date. The wording in force in April 2019 is recorded separately as PROV-M094-009. Not treated as indispensable.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless the person executing the same be known to him or to at least two of the attesting witnesses thereto;
why_relevant: The amending section recites verbatim the wording of rule (9) of section 31 of the Notaries Ordinance that it replaced, and that recited wording is the rule that was in force in April 2019: the executant must be known to the notary or to at least two of the attesting witnesses. It is the only corpus text of the April 2019 rule.
temporal_note: The amending Act itself dates from 2022 and was not in force at the matter date. It is cited only because its recital preserves the pre-2022 wording of rule (9), which was the wording in force in April 2019. Recorded as supporting, not indispensable.

relevant_excerpt: (11) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any case in which the person executing or acknowledging the same shall be or profess to be unable to read the same, or in which such person shall require him to read over the same, unless and until he shall have read over and explained the same, or caused the same to be explained, in the presence and hearing of such person and, except in the case of wills and codicils, in the presence of the attesting witnesses.
why_relevant: Reading over and explanation; the express carve-out for wills and codicils means the reading over of this codicil need not take place in the presence of the attesting witnesses, which affects how the attestation is worded.
temporal_note: Rule (11) is not among the rules substituted by the 2022 or 2024 amending Acts recorded in the corpus, so the wording is treated as in force in April 2019. The verifier should confirm this against the 2019 edition.

relevant_excerpt: (12) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless the person executing the same and the witnesses shall have signed the same in his presence and in the presence of one another, and unless he shall have signed the same in the presence of the executant and of the attesting witnesses.
why_relevant: The core execution requirement the attestation must certify: testator, both witnesses and the notary signing in the presence of one another.
temporal_note: Rule (12) is not among the rules substituted by the 2022 or 2024 amending Acts; wording treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: (15) If any deed or instrument executed or acknowledged before him be signed by any of the parties or witnesses thereto with a mark, or with a signature in a language other than that in which the notary is authorized to practice, he shall write over such mark or signature in his own handwriting and at the time of execution the words "This is the mark (or signature, as the case may be) of A. B."
why_relevant: Decisive for this attestation: the notary is licensed in Sinhala, but both attesting witnesses sign in English characters, so the notary must write over each of those signatures the words 'This is the signature of ...' and record that he did so.
temporal_note: Rule (15) itself was not substituted by the 2022 or 2024 amending Acts (Act No. 31 of 2022 inserted a new rule (15A) immediately after it); wording treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: (18) He shall correctly insert in letters in every deed or instrument executed before him the day, month, and year on which and the place where the same is executed, and shall sign the same.
why_relevant: The date and place of execution must be written in letters, not figures, in the codicil and carried into the attestation.
temporal_note: Rule (18) is not among the rules amended in 2022 or 2024; wording treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: (20) He shall without delay duly attest every deed or instrument which shall be executed or acknowledged before him, and shall sign and seal such attestation. In such attestation he shall state- (a) that the said deed or instrument was signed by the party and the witnesses thereto in his presence and in the presence of one another;
why_relevant: The operative duty to attest, sign and seal, and the first mandatory recital of the attestation.
temporal_note: The chapeau and paragraph (a) of rule (20) were not touched by the 2022 or 2024 amendments (which replaced paragraphs (b), (e) and (g) and added (h)); wording treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: (b) whether the executants of the said deed or instrument are known to him or whether he has identified them by the inspection of the national identity card, bio-page of the passport or the driving licence or whether the witnesses thereto are known to him and in the latter case he shall specify which of the executants or the person acknowledging are known to the said witness;
why_relevant: The recital that carries the decisive fact in this question: the executant is not known to the notary, the witnesses are, and the attestation must specify which executant is known to which witness.
temporal_note: This paragraph is the text substituted by section 16(11)(a) of the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022, after the matter date; the national identity card limb did not exist in April 2019. The pre-2022 wording of paragraph (b) is not reproduced anywhere in the corpus. Not treated as indispensable.

relevant_excerpt: (c) the day, month, and year on which and the place where the said deed or instrument was executed or acknowledged, and the full names of the attesting witnesses and their residences; (d) whether the same was read over by the person executing the same, or read and explained by him, the said notary, to the said person in the presence of the attesting witnesses;
why_relevant: Requires the attestation to state the date and place of execution, the full names and residences of the two witnesses, and whether the codicil was read over by the testator or read and explained by the notary.
temporal_note: Paragraphs (c) and (d) of rule (20) were not amended in 2022 or 2024; wording treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: (f) the number and value of the adhesive stamps affixed to or the value of the impressed stamps on such deed or instrument and the duplicate thereof;
why_relevant: Supporting recital about stamps. The scenario gives no stamp particulars, so the drafted attestation can only leave the values to be completed.
temporal_note: Paragraph (f) was not amended in 2022 or 2024; wording treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: (h) in the case of a will- (i) set out in the attestation of the will that the testator was in good and sound mind to execute the will; and (ii) enter in the deed register maintained by him, the number assigned to such will, the date and the name of the testator.
why_relevant: Under the current text the attestation of a will or codicil must state that the testator was of sound mind. It is recorded to warn the verifier that this recital is a post-2019 statutory requirement, whatever notarial practice may have been in 2019.
temporal_note: Paragraph (h) was inserted by section 16(11)(d) of the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022, after the April 2019 matter date. Not treated as indispensable.

relevant_excerpt: (21) Every such attestation shall be substantially in the form E in the Second Schedule, and shall be legibly signed by him in the language in which the deed or instrument is written, and also with his usual signature if the language or form of that signature be different from that in which such deed or instrument is written.
why_relevant: Fixes the form of the attestation and requires the notary to sign it legibly in the language of the instrument, which here is Sinhala.
temporal_note: The text of rule (21) was not amended in 2022 or 2024, but Form E of the Second Schedule was repealed and replaced by section 22 of Act No. 31 of 2022. The Second Schedule is not in the corpus at all, so the Form E in force in April 2019 cannot be reproduced.

relevant_excerpt: (22) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any area other than that in which he is authorized to practice, nor in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice nor authenticate or attest any deed or instrument drawn in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice.
why_relevant: The notary is licensed to practise in Sinhala, so the codicil must be drawn in Sinhala and the attestation written and signed in Sinhala. This also explains why the witnesses' English-character signatures engage rule (15).
temporal_note: Rule (22) was not amended in 2022 or 2024; wording treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: (8) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument to which at least two witnesses have not subscribed their signatures in letters.
why_relevant: Requires the two attesting witnesses; the scenario supplies exactly two, both of whom sign in letters (English characters).
temporal_note: Rule (8) was not amended in 2022 or 2024; wording treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: (23) He shall number with consecutive integral numbers the documents executed or acknowledged before him, including wills and codicils, according to the order in which they are executed or acknowledged before him.
why_relevant: The codicil takes the attesting notary's own next consecutive number; it does not carry the number 3250 of the original will, which was attested by a different notary.
temporal_note: Rule (23) was not amended in 2022 or 2024; wording treated as in force in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: (24) He shall carefully preserve as his protocol a draft or copy of every deed or instrument executed or acknowledged before him, to which shall be attached his signature and those of the party and witnesses to the original deed or instrument
why_relevant: Background on what happens to the codicil after attestation: a protocol copy is retained, and for wills and codicils only the number and date go into the register.
temporal_note: The 2024 amendment replaced Form F of the Second Schedule referred to in this rule; the quoted words of rule (24) are unchanged and applied in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: No instrument shall be deemed to be invalid by reason only of the failure of any notary to observe any provision of any rule set out in section 31 in respect of any matter of form
why_relevant: Background: departures from the prescribed form of attestation do not by themselves invalidate the codicil, although they expose the notary to the penalties in section 34.
temporal_note: In force from 1907; no amendment event recorded in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument, other than a will or codicil, affecting land or other immovable property, unless the deed or instrument embodies therin or in a Schedule annexed therto an accurate and clear description of the said land or other property affected thereby, showing its boundaries, extent, situation
why_relevant: A codicil is expressly excluded from the requirement of a full boundary and extent description, so the drafted codicil may identify the Moratuwa and Ratmalana properties by name, assessment number and street as the client described them.
temporal_note: Rule (16)(a) was amended in 2022 by the addition of condominium wording at the end of the paragraph; the opening words quoted here, including the exclusion of wills and codicils, are unchanged and applied in April 2019.

relevant_excerpt: Before any deed or instrument (other than a will or codicil) affecting any interest in land or other immovable property is drawn by him, he shall search or cause to be searched the registers in the land registry to ascertain the state of the title in regard to such land
why_relevant: Confirms that no title search is required before drawing a codicil, which is why the drafting can proceed on the client's instructions alone.
temporal_note: Paragraph (a) of rule (17) was not amended in 2022 or 2024 (those amendments replaced paragraph (b) and added paragraphs (c) to (e)); wording treated as in force in April 2019.

formal_title: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance No. 7 of 1840
relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property, and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object, or for establishing any security, interest, or incumbrance affecting land or other immovable property (other than a lease at will, or for any period not exceeding one month)
why_relevant: Every instrument any of the three brothers would need — a deed of transfer of Asanka's undivided share, a deed of partition between the three, a deed of release of the father's life interest, or the mortgage bond Sasanka must give for a housing loan — is a transfer or a security affecting immovable property, so it has no force in law unless it is executed and attested before a notary in the manner this section prescribes. It fixes the form of whatever route is advised, not the choice between routes.
temporal_note: In force since 1840; the notarial-execution requirement for transfers, mortgages and agreements affecting land was in force at 2018-10. The corpus body is the consolidated text carrying amendments by Act No. 30 of 2022 s.2 and Act No. 4 of 2024 s.2, both after the matter date; the excerpt taken is the opening words of subsection (1), which the 2022 and 2024 amendments did not introduce. The detail of paragraphs (a) and (b) (thumb impressions, transferee signature) reflects the post-2022 text and must not be applied to a 2018 matter.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: all instruments, including wills, decrees and orders of any court or authority, and awards, which purport or operate to create, confer, declare, limit, assign, transfer, charge, incumber, release, or extinguish any right, title, or interest, whether vested or contingent, past, present, or future, to, in or over land
why_relevant: Brings each of the candidate instruments within the registration Chapter: a deed of partition limits and assigns interests in the land, a deed of release extinguishes the father's life interest, a transfer of Asanka's share assigns it, and a mortgage bond incumbers it. Without this section, s.7's priority rule has nothing to bite on.
temporal_note: In force since 1927 with no recorded change year in the corpus; applicable at 2018-10.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: be void as against all parties claiming an adverse interest thereto on valuable consideration by virtue of any subsequent instrument which is duly registered under this Chapter
why_relevant: Whatever route the brothers take, the resulting deed must be registered in the land registry of the district, or it will lose priority to a later registered instrument taken for value. This is why the practical advice ends with registration, and it is what makes Sasanka's lender willing to accept the security.
temporal_note: In force since 1927 with no recorded change year in the corpus; applicable at 2018-10.

relevant_excerpt: The Law shall apply to any building- (a) erected on alienated land held as one Sand parcel and capable of being subdivided into parcels (hereinafter referred to as "Condominium Property")
why_relevant: Asanka's stated wish is to buy an apartment in Colombo. This section identifies when the Apartment Ownership Law governs the building he would be buying into, and so which statutory regime, rather than ordinary land law, describes what he acquires.
temporal_note: In force since 1973; last amended in the corpus by Act No. 39 of 2003 s.3, before the matter date. Applicable at 2018-10.

relevant_excerpt: after the registration of a Condominium Plan, or Semi Condominium Plan, any condominium parcel depicted therein together with the common elements appurtenant thereto may be held and dealt with in the same manner and form as any land.
why_relevant: Explains what Asanka would get for the proceeds of his share: a condominium parcel that can be owned, sold and mortgaged like land, rather than a further undivided share. It is the statutory answer to the apartment limb of the advice.
temporal_note: In force since 1973; subsection (4) as it stands reflects amendment by Act No. 39 of 2003 s.13, before the matter date. Applicable at 2018-10.

relevant_excerpt: No share in the common elements of a registered, Condominium Property or of a registered Semi Condominium Property shall be disposed of or otherwise dealt with except as appurtenant to a condominium parcel of such property
why_relevant: Qualifies the ownership Asanka would acquire: his share of the common elements is tied to the parcel and cannot be dealt with separately. Relevant to advising him on the difference between the co-ownership he is leaving and the apartment ownership he is entering.
temporal_note: In force since 1973; the text in the corpus reflects replacement by Act No. 39 of 2003 s.16, before the matter date. Applicable at 2018-10.

relevant_excerpt: No person acquiring an title or interest or benefit in any condominium parcel of a registered Condominium Property or of a registered Semi Condominium Property shall be entitled to such title or interest, or benefit, unless such title, or interest or benefit is registered under the provisions of Registration of Title Act. No. 21 of 1998.
why_relevant: Sets the registration step Asanka must take on the apartment purchase, and shows that the apartment side of the advice runs under the Registration of Title Act rather than the deeds registration Chapter that governs the Battaramulla land.
temporal_note: In force since 1973; the present text was substituted by Act No. 39 of 2003 s.15, before the matter date. Applicable at 2018-10.

relevant_excerpt: includes things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth, and any estate, right, or interest in or over land
why_relevant: Context for Sasanka's housing loan: for mortgage purposes 'land' extends to any estate, right or interest in or over land, so an interest short of full divided ownership is capable of being mortgaged. It does not by itself tell us whether a lender would accept his interest, and it is recorded as background only.
temporal_note: In force since 1949 with no recorded change year in the corpus; applicable at 2018-10. Note that the corpus text of this interpretation section has lost the defined terms themselves, so the excerpt reads as a bare 'includes' clause; the verifier should confirm from the source that it is the definition of 'land'.

relevant_excerpt: The Partition Law shall not apply to any land or building comprised in any registered Condominium Plan.
why_relevant: Recorded as background because it is the only place in the corpus that acknowledges the Partition Law, which is the enactment the answer to this question actually turns on and which the corpus does not contain. It also marks the boundary between the two regimes in play: the Battaramulla land and the Colombo apartment.
temporal_note: In force since 1973 with no recorded change year in the corpus; applicable at 2018-10.

relevant_excerpt: Where it is shown to the satisfaction of the Registrar-General that any error or omission has been made in registering any instrument, whether before or after the commencement of this Ordinance, the Registrar-General shall issue notice in writing in the prescribed form (a) in the case of a deed to the parties thereto; or (b) in the case of a will to the executor or administrator, as the case may be; or (c) in the case of any other instrument to the person who presented it for registration, and order such error or omission to be corrected
why_relevant: This is the operative correction power. It fixes the first three steps of the procedure: the error must be shown to the satisfaction of the Registrar-General, who then issues written notice in the prescribed form to the parties to the deed (Deed No. 351), and orders the correction. Registering the sub-divided Lot 3A in the parent folio Vol/Folio A 350/25 is an error or omission made in registering an instrument.
temporal_note: Subsection (1) was repealed and re-substituted by section 3 of the Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act, No. 50 of 1982; the consolidated corpus text is that substituted text and it is the text in force in October 2018. No later amendment in the corpus (Nos. 5 of 1990, 21 of 2013, 32 of 2022, 18 of 2024) touches section 35.

relevant_excerpt: and order such error or omission to be corrected and the correction shall then be made by the Registrar concerned in the prescribed manner, but shall not affect any priority accrued before the correction is made
why_relevant: Fixes the last two steps: after the Registrar-General's order the correction is made by the Registrar concerned (here the Registrar of Lands, Homagama) in the prescribed manner, and it does not disturb any priority that accrued before it. Without this the procedure is incomplete and the effect of the correction on priority is unstated.
temporal_note: Same 1982 substituted text as PROV-M098-001; in force at the matter reference date of October 2018.

relevant_excerpt: Provided that the Registrar-General may with like effect make such an order for the correction of any error or omission made in registering any such instrument if it is proved to his satisfaction by any person interested that by reason of the death or legal incapacity of any person or party to whom notice is required to be issued as aforesaid or for any other sufficient cause whatsoever, such notice cannot be issued.
why_relevant: Supplies the alternative route where notice to a party to Deed No. 351 cannot be issued. Supporting rather than indispensable, because the facts do not state that any party has died or is incapacitated, but a complete statement of the procedure should note it.
temporal_note: Same 1982 substituted text; in force at October 2018.

relevant_excerpt: Every instrument presented for registration shall be registered in the book allotted to the division in which the land affected by the instrument is situated and in the folio in which 1974] the first registered instrument affecting the same land is registered, or in another folio (whether of the same volume or of another volume) bearing a separate number, opened in continuation thereof, cross reference being entered in the prescribed manner so as to connect the said folios
why_relevant: Supplies the standard that was breached and so identifies what the error is. It is what makes the registration of the divided Lot 3A in the parent folio of Lot 3 wrong: the sub-divided lot should have been carried to a separate folio opened in continuation, connected by cross reference. Without it the assertion that there is an error in registering has no statutory support.
temporal_note: Amended by Act No. 14 of 1974; the corpus consolidated text carries the 1974 wording (the stray '1974]' marker is an artefact of the consolidated source). In force at October 2018.
verifier_note: Wording, role and 1974 dating confirmed, but the excerpt carries a stray '1974]' marker from the consolidated source that is absent from the substituting text in 14-1974/s.2, so the excerpt should not be reproduced as the clean statutory wording.

relevant_excerpt: (a) an instrument may, if the Registrar thinks fit, be entered in a new folio, cross references being entered in the prescribed manner so as to connect the registration with any previous registration affecting the same land or any part thereof
why_relevant: Shows the form the corrected registration should take: a new folio for Lot 3A with cross references back to Vol/Folio A 350/25. Supporting, because the corrective act itself is ordered under section 35.
temporal_note: Part of the section 14 text in force at October 2018.

relevant_excerpt: An instrument, whether registered before or after the commencement of this Ordinance, shall not be deemed to be duly registered under this Chapter unless it is registered in accordance with the foregoing provisions of this section.
why_relevant: Explains why the mis-folioed registration must be put right rather than left alone: registration otherwise than in accordance with section 14 is not due registration, so the chain of registration for Lot 3A is defective until corrected.
temporal_note: In force at October 2018.

relevant_excerpt: The Registrar-General may, if he thinks fit. exercise all or any of the powers possessed by a Registrar.
why_relevant: Identifies the officers named in section 35, the Registrar-General of Lands and the Registrar of the division (Homagama), and confirms the Registrar-General's own competence over registration acts. Contextual support for who the application is addressed to.
temporal_note: In force at October 2018; subsection (7) also permits a Deputy or Assistant Registrar-General to act.
verifier_note: Section 2(6) is verbatim and does allow the Registrar-General to exercise a Registrar's powers, but it is section 2(2), not 2(6), that constitutes the offices of Registrar-General and Registrar; the why_relevant over-reads the subsection.

relevant_excerpt: The Minister may make regulations, to be published in the Gazette, as to any matter which by this Ordinance may or is to be prescribed and generally for regulating the forms to be used and the procedure and practice to be observed in carrying this Ordinance into effect.
why_relevant: Section 35 twice defers to what is prescribed: the form of the notice and the manner of correction. This section is the source of that prescription, so it locates the detailed procedural steps outside the Ordinance itself.
temporal_note: In force at October 2018. The regulations made under it are not in the frozen corpus.

relevant_excerpt: The forms contained in the Second Schedule shall be used with such variations as circumstances may require
why_relevant: Background: the prescribed forms referred to in section 35(1) are those in the Second Schedule as altered by regulation. The Schedule text itself is not in the corpus.
temporal_note: The Second Schedule was amended by section 5 of the Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act, No. 32 of 2022, which post-dates the matter; only the pre-2022 position is relevant here.

relevant_excerpt: Any person aggrieved by an order of a Registrar refusing to register an, instrument may, within thirty days from the date of the order being communicated to him, appeal to the Registrar-General, who may vary or reverse the order.
why_relevant: Background only. The lease was refused registration, so if the Registrar makes a formal order of refusal there is a separate thirty-day appeal to the Registrar-General, and thereafter a District Court suit under subsection (2). It is not the route for correcting the folio error, which is section 35.
temporal_note: In force at October 2018.

relevant_excerpt: There shall be charged on- (a) every instrument relating to a transfer of situated in the immovable property Western Province
why_relevant: The charging provision for stamp duty on Deed No. 351. Lot 3A is at Homagama in the Colombo District, which lies in the Western Province, and the valuation was given by the Commissioner of Revenue of the Western Provincial Council, so the provincial statute is the charging law.
temporal_note: In force from 1990, subject to the Ministerial Order appointing dates under section 1; treated as in force at October 2018. The corpus text is garbled by the source layout ('a transfer of situated in the immovable property Western Province') but is legible.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim and the charge on transfers of Western Province immovable property is legible, but the corpus text is OCR-scrambled ('a transfer of situated in the immovable property Western Province') and nothing in the corpus records the section 1 Ministerial Order bringing the stamp duty Part into operation, so applicable_to_matter_date rests on an assumption.

relevant_excerpt: Where any property is conveyed by an instrument, the stamp duty with which such instrument is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property conveyed.
why_relevant: Settles the base of the calculation. The duty is computed on the value of Lot 3A, not on the Rs. 7,000,000 stated as the price, which is why the Rs. 7,500,000 valuation matters.
temporal_note: In force at October 2018.

relevant_excerpt: "value" with reference - (a) to any property (other than immovable property which is gifted) and to any date, means the price which in the opinion of the Assessor, that property would have fetched in the open market on that date
why_relevant: Defines the term on which section 48(1) turns. Because value is the open-market price in the opinion of the revenue officer, the Rs. 7,500,000 opinion of valuation displaces the Rs. 7,000,000 contract price as the base of the duty.
temporal_note: In force at October 2018.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim, but section 106 says 'in the opinion of the Assessor', defined in the same section as a Provincial Assessor of Revenue; the why_relevant's 'the revenue officer' blurs that. The Commissioner's opinion reaches the definition only through section 104(4), added as PROV-M098-901.

relevant_excerpt: means the Provincial Commissioner ofRevenue, and includes a Provincial Deputy Commissioner of Revenue appointed for the purposes of this Statute
why_relevant: Identifies the Commissioner of Revenue of the Western Provincial Council named in the facts as an officer of this Statute. The same section defines Assessor as a Provincial Assessor of Revenue, and it is the Assessor's opinion that the definition of value refers to, so the verifier should check whether a Commissioner's opinion of valuation counts for section 106.
temporal_note: In force at October 2018.
verifier_note: Verbatim and correctly identifies the Commissioner. The question it leaves open - whether a Commissioner's opinion of valuation counts for the section 106 definition of 'value' - is answered by section 104(4), added as PROV-M098-901.

relevant_excerpt: Except where there is an agreement to the contrary stamp duty shall be payable; (a) in the case of an instrument of transfer by the grantee
why_relevant: Identifies who bears the duty on Deed No. 351: Dininda Perera as grantee, absent an agreement to the contrary.
temporal_note: In force at October 2018.

relevant_excerpt: The Minister may make regulations in respect of all or any of the following matters: (a) any matter which is required or authorized by this Statute to be prescribed
why_relevant: Locates the missing element. Section 37 charges duty at the prescribed rate and the rate is fixed by regulation under this section, so the numeric rate schedule sits outside the Statute and outside the frozen corpus.
temporal_note: In force at October 2018; the regulations themselves are not in the corpus.

relevant_excerpt: the provisions of the Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982, relating to the Imposition of Stamp Duty (other than any instrument relating to the transfer of immovable property, the transfer of motor vehicles or documents filed in Court)
why_relevant: Background: confirms that the 2006 Act did not take over the stamping of transfers of immovable property, which are expressly carved out. That is why the deed of transfer is dealt with under the provincial statute and the Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982, and not under the 2006 Act.
temporal_note: In force at October 2018.

relevant_excerpt: The stamp duty with which any instrument is chargeable shall be paid before or at the time of execution of the instrument except as otherwise permitted in this Statute
