relevant_excerpt: the common elements shall be held by the owners of all the condominium parcels as tenants in common proportional to their respective share parcels
why_relevant: Fixes who owns the land on which a registered condominium stands: once the Condominium Plan is registered the land parcel outside the condominium parcels becomes common elements held by the parcel owners as tenants in common in proportion to their share parcels. Gihan owns no condominium parcel, so he can hold no share in that land.
temporal_note: In force from 1973; last amended by Act No. 39 of 2003 s.13, some fifteen years before the matter reference date of 2018-04. The consolidated text used here is the text in force in April 2018.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim in 11-1973/s9(1) and states what why_relevant claims; the section is in force from 1973 with amendment events in 1982 and 2003 only, so the consolidated text is the text in force in April 2018.

relevant_excerpt: each condominium parcel depicted therein together with the common elements appurtenant thereto shall be deemed to be absolutely owned by the person or persons described in the relevant plan as the owner or owners of the Condominium Property
why_relevant: Confirms that on registration of the Condominium Plan absolute ownership vests in the person described in the plan as owner. Rehan, being so described, is the absolute owner; a stranger's declaration cannot displace that deemed ownership.
temporal_note: In force from 1973; subsection (5) in its present form comes from Act No. 39 of 2003 s.13, well before 2018-04.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim in 11-1973/s9(5); the omitted tail, which saves the rights of mortgagees and compensation claimants, does not qualify the deeming of absolute ownership relied on here.

relevant_excerpt: No share in the common elements of a registered, Condominium Property or of a registered Semi Condominium Property shall be disposed of or otherwise dealt with except as appurtenant to a condominium parcel of such property
why_relevant: The central prohibition. A Deed of Declaration claiming a half share of the land on which the condominium stands is a dealing with a share in the common elements otherwise than as appurtenant to a condominium parcel, which this section forbids outright.
temporal_note: In force from 1973; last amended by Act No. 39 of 2003 s.16, before the matter reference date.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and s.11 does bar a share in the common elements from being held otherwise than as appurtenant to a condominium parcel, but it regulates dealings with a share that exists, so on these facts it reinforces rather than supplies the answer, which turns first on s.9(1) and s.9(5) leaving Gihan with no share at all.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: Registration of an instrument under this Chapter shall not cure any defect in the instrument or confer upon it any effect or validity which it would not otherwise have except the priority conferred on it by this section.
why_relevant: Answers the second half of the question. Even if the Registrar accepts the Deed of Declaration and enters it in the register, registration gives the deed no validity it does not already have; it cannot manufacture a half share for a person who has none.
temporal_note: In force from 1927 with no recorded amendment event in the corpus; applicable at 2018-04.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim in 23-1927/s7(4); the corpus edition is the 1990 consolidation, and the only pre-2018 amending Acts in the corpus, Nos. 48 of 2011 and 21 of 2013, amend ss.13, 22, 48 and the First Schedule rather than s.7, so the text is applicable at 2018-04.

relevant_excerpt: The provisions of this Law shall have effect notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any other written law, and where there is any conflict or inconsistency between the provisions of this Law and such other law the provisions of this Law shall prevail over such other law.
why_relevant: Resolves the clash the question sets up. Gihan wants to use the Registration of Documents Ordinance to achieve something the Apartment Ownership Law prohibits; this section makes the Apartment Ownership Law prevail over the Ordinance.
temporal_note: In force from 1973 with no recorded amendment event; applicable at 2018-04.
verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but s.25 operates only where there is a conflict or inconsistency and there is none on these facts, because s.7(4) of the Ordinance itself denies the registration any curative effect, so the role is corrected from indispensable to supporting.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: all instruments, including wills, decrees and orders of any court or authority, and awards, which purport or operate to create, confer, declare, limit, assign, transfer, charge, incumber, release, or extinguish any right, title, or interest, whether vested or contingent, past, present, or future, to, in or over land
why_relevant: Shows that a Deed of Declaration asserting a half share is on its face an instrument affecting land, so it falls within the class of documents the Ordinance accepts for registration. This is why the deed can be lodged at all, and why the answer has to turn on effect rather than on registrability.
temporal_note: In force from 1927 with no recorded amendment event; applicable at 2018-04.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim in 23-1927/s8(b) and a deed declaring an interest in land falls within it; none of the eleven provisos to paragraph (b) excludes such a deed.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: any person executing the instrument; (b) any person claiming any interest or benefit thereunder; (c) any person having any interest in or charge on any property affected thereby
why_relevant: Gihan, as executant of the deed and as a person claiming a benefit under it, is a person who may present it for registration. The Ordinance does not require the presenter to prove title first.
temporal_note: In force from 1927 with no recorded amendment event; applicable at 2018-04.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim in 23-1927/s26(1), whose paragraphs (a) and (b) cover an executant claiming a benefit under the instrument.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: A Registrar may, if he thinks fit, refuse to register an instrument- (a) where he has reason to suspect that the person presenting the instrument for registration is not a person who is authorized by this Ordinance to present it for registration
why_relevant: Sets out the grounds on which a Registrar may refuse registration. They are directed at authority to present, form and mode of execution, stamp duty and fees, not at the truth of the claim of title asserted in the deed, which confirms that acceptance for registration says nothing about the deed's validity.
temporal_note: In force from 1927 with no recorded amendment event; applicable at 2018-04.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim in 23-1927/s36(1)(a), but the why_relevant reasons from the whole of s.36, including s.36(1)(b) on form and mode of execution and s.36(2) on stamp duty and fees, which the quoted fragment does not itself set out.

relevant_excerpt: The owners of all the parcels may by a special resolution at a meeting convened by the management corporation direct the management corporation to transfer a part of the common elements.
why_relevant: Gives the only lawful route by which part of the common elements can pass to anyone: a special resolution of the owners of all the parcels, executed by the management corporation. A unilateral deed by an outsider is not that route.
temporal_note: In force from 1973; last amended by Act No. 39 of 2003 s.21, before the matter reference date.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim in 11-1973/s16(1), and subsections (2) to (4) confirm that the management corporation executes the instrument, so the route described is the statutory one.

relevant_excerpt: The Partition Law shall not apply to any land or building comprised in any registered Condominium Plan.
why_relevant: Closes off the obvious fallback. Having declared himself entitled to a half share, Gihan could not follow it with a partition action over the condominium land, because the Partition Law does not apply to land comprised in a registered Condominium Plan.
temporal_note: In force from 1973 with no recorded amendment event; applicable at 2018-04.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim in 11-1973/s23; the Partition Law itself is not in the corpus, so what it would otherwise have permitted cannot be checked from within the corpus, as the recorded corpus gap says.

relevant_excerpt: means so much of the land parcel for the time being not comprised in any condominium parcel shown in a Condominium Plan or Semi Condominium or Provisional Condominium Plan
why_relevant: The interpretation section's definition of 'common elements'. It is what makes the land on which the condominium stands, as distinct from the individual units, common elements, and so brings sections 9 and 11 to bear on Gihan's claim.
temporal_note: In force from 1973; last amended by Act No. 39 of 2003 s.41, before the matter reference date. The corpus text of this interpretation section has lost the defined-term lead-ins, so the excerpt reads as a bare 'means ...' clause; the verifier should confirm against the source that this clause is the definition of 'common elements'.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim and the clause is the definition of common elements: every other body in s.26 maps to a term in the corpus row's defined_terms list, this one does not, that list omits common elements, and paragraphs (b)(vi) and (b)(vii) of the same clause describe facilities as common elements; but the excerpt quotes only limb (a), limb (b) adding the built parts and shared installations.

relevant_excerpt: No person acquiring an title or interest or benefit in any condominium parcel of a registered Condominium Property or of a registered Semi Condominium Property shall be entitled to such title or interest, or benefit, unless such title, or interest or benefit is registered under the provisions of Registration of Title Act. No. 21 of 1998.
why_relevant: Background on which register governs interests in a registered condominium. Interests in a condominium parcel take effect through registration under the Registration of Title Act, not through the Registration of Documents Ordinance register Gihan proposes to use.
temporal_note: In force from 1973; replaced by Act No. 39 of 2003 s.15, before the matter reference date. Its practical operation depends on an order under section 1 of the Registration of Title Act extending that Act to the relevant division, which is why it is treated as background rather than as a load-bearing step.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim in 11-1973/s10(1), and the temporal_note correctly records that its practical operation depends on an order extending the Registration of Title Act to the relevant division, which is why it is background.

relevant_excerpt: the Registration of Documents Ordinance (Chapter 117) shall continue to apply to and in relation to, the registration in accordance with the provisions of this Act- (a) of a Condominium Plan, a Provisional Condominium Plan or a Semi Condominium Plan
why_relevant: Background on the residual role of the Registration of Documents Ordinance in condominium matters. Where the Registration of Title Act has not yet been extended, the Ordinance continues to apply to the registration of condominium plans and plans of amendment, re-division or amalgamation, a list that does not include a stranger's declaration of title.
temporal_note: In force from 2003, before the matter reference date of 2018-04.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim in 39-2003/s44 and the list it introduces is confined to condominium plans and plans of amendment, re-division or amalgamation.

formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
relevant_excerpt: any instrument registered under Chapters IE or IV is a forgery, or has been registered without due authority or in contravention of any provision of this Ordinance, or where any instrument registered as aforesaid is rectified or set aside by a competent court, the District Court may order the registration of the instrument to be cancelled or to be rectified in such manner as the circumstances may require
why_relevant: Supplies the authority for the last sentence of the gold conclusion, which says the registration would be open to challenge in the District Court. Where an instrument has been registered without due authority, the District Court may order the registration cancelled or rectified, so an interested party is not left without a remedy if the deed is entered in the register.
temporal_note: In force from 1927; the corpus edition is the 1990 consolidation and neither pre-2018 amending Act in the corpus, Nos. 48 of 2011 and 21 of 2013, touches s.39, so the text is applicable at 2018-04.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier because the gold conclusion asserted a District Court challenge with no provision behind it; the excerpt is verbatim, and 'Chapters IE or IV' is a transcription artefact for Chapters III or IV in the corpus text.

relevant_excerpt: (15) If any deed or instrument executed or acknowledged before him be signed by any of the parties or witnesses thereto with a mark, or with a signature in a language other than that in which the notary is authorized to practice, he shall write over such mark or signature in his own handwriting and at the time of execution the words "This is the mark (or signature, as the case may be) of A. B." (here insert the name of the person signing with the mark or signature);
why_relevant: This is the rule that governs the exact situation: an executant has signed in a language (Japanese) other than the language in which the notary is authorized to practise. It fixes the notary's positive duty - to write over the signature, in his own handwriting and at the time of execution, the words "This is the signature of A. B.", inserting the signatory's name.
temporal_note: Rule (15) dates from the 1907 Ordinance. Neither Act No. 47 of 2011, nor Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16, nor Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3 substituted rule (15); Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(8) only inserted a new rule (15A) immediately after it. Rule (15A) (compulsory thumb impression alongside the signature) came into force after April 2018 and is deliberately not relied on.

relevant_excerpt: Every appointment to the office of notary shall be by warrant granted by the Minister, and shall specify the area within which, and the language or languages in which, the person appointed is authorized to practice.
why_relevant: Rule (15) is triggered only by a signature "in a language other than that in which the notary is authorized to practice". Section 2 is what settles that authorized language: it is the language specified in the notary's warrant. Without it there is no way to say that a Japanese signature is in another language for this notary.
temporal_note: In force from 1907; the corpus records no amendment event on section 2, so the text stood as printed in April 2018.

relevant_excerpt: (22) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any area other than that in which he is authorized to practice, nor in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice nor authenticate or attest any deed or instrument drawn in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice.
why_relevant: Marks the boundary of the problem. Rule (22) bars the notary from attesting a deed drawn in a language outside his warrant, but it says nothing about the language of a party's signature. So a Japanese signature on a deed drawn in the notary's own language does not disable him from attesting; it only brings rule (15) into play.
temporal_note: Rule (22) is original to the 1907 Ordinance and was not among the rules substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16 or Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3.

relevant_excerpt: (11) He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any case in which the person executing or acknowledging the same shall be or profess to be unable to read the same, or in which such person shall require him to read over the same, unless and until he shall have read over and explained the same, or caused the same to be explained, in the presence and hearing of such person and, except in the case of wills and codicils, in the presence of the attesting witnesses.
why_relevant: An executant who signs in Japanese will commonly not read the language of the deed. Where he is, or professes to be, unable to read it, rule (11) adds a second duty on the notary: read over and explain the deed, or cause it to be explained, in the executant's presence and hearing and in the presence of the attesting witnesses, before attesting.
temporal_note: Rule (11) is original to the 1907 Ordinance and was not among the rules substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16 or Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3.
verifier_note: Wording and temporal note confirmed verbatim against 1-1907/s31 rule (11), which no post-2018 amendment touches; the role correction is that rule (11) is engaged only by synthetic decisive fact FACT-M110-Q01-005, so it is supporting to an enrichment-created issue rather than to the question as examined.

relevant_excerpt: and in the case of a mark he shall besides require such person to affix to the deed or instrument the impression of his left thumb and shall write over such impression at the time and in the manner aforesaid the words "This is the left thumb impression of A. B." (here insert the name of the person whose thumb impression it is).
why_relevant: CL-M110-Q01-003 asserts that the left thumb impression limb of rule (15) applies to a mark and not to a signature. The excerpt in PROV-M110-001 stops before that limb, so the claim had no cited text behind it. This entry supplies the limb verbatim: it opens with "and in the case of a mark", which is what confines it to marks.
temporal_note: Part of rule (15) as it stood in 1907. Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(8) inserted a new rule (15A) immediately after rule (15) but did not substitute rule (15) itself; Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3 amended rule (15A), not rule (15). The limb therefore read as printed in April 2018.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked verbatim with search_corpus.py check.

relevant_excerpt: (d) whether the same was read over by the person executing the same, or read and explained by him, the said notary, to the said person in the presence of the attesting witnesses;
why_relevant: Once rule (11) is engaged, the reading over and explanation is not the end of the notary's duty: rule (20)(d) requires him to state in the attestation itself whether the deed was read over by the executant or read and explained by the notary in the presence of the attesting witnesses. The map relies on rule (11) but stops short of the recording duty, so this completes the answer to "what is the duty of the Notary".
temporal_note: Rule (20) was amended after April 2018 by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(11) (paragraphs (b), (e), (g) and new (h)) and by Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(7) (paragraph (g)). Paragraph (d) was not touched by either, so the printed text is the April 2018 text.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier as a supporting provision the researcher missed; excerpt checked verbatim.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any area other than that in which he is authorized to practice, nor in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice nor authenticate or attest any deed or instrument drawn in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice.
why_relevant: This is the only rule in section 31 that limits where a notary may attest. It restricts the area in which the act of attestation is performed and the language of the deed; it says nothing about where the land affected by the deed is situated. It is therefore the provision that answers how Lal Peiris, whose warrant covers Colombo, may lawfully attest a deed relating to land at Matara.
temporal_note: Rule (22) is part of the original 1907 rules. It is not among the rules substituted, inserted or repealed by the amendments recorded against section 31 (Act No. 20 of 1976, Act No. 47 of 2011, Act No. 31 of 2022, Act No. 6 of 2024), so the text quoted stood in this form in April 2018.

relevant_excerpt: Every warrant issued to a notary under the provisions of section 3* or section 4* authorizing him to practice as a notary in any judicial division in which he resides, shall be deemed to authorize him to practice as a notary in the judicial zone in which he resides.
why_relevant: Fixes the extent of the "area ... in which he is authorized to practice" for the purposes of rule (22) of section 31. Without it the area is read as the judicial division named in the warrant; with it the notary may attest anywhere in the judicial zone in which he resides. It is the provision that tells us how far Lal Peiris's Colombo authority reaches.
temporal_note: Inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Law No. 20 of 1976 s.4 and in force from 1976. No later amendment is recorded against it, so it was in force in April 2018.

relevant_excerpt: Every notary shall be bound to have his office within the area specified in his warrant
why_relevant: Explains why Lal Peiris's office is in Colombo and anchors the area of his warrant. It is background: it constrains where he keeps his office, not what deeds he may attest.
temporal_note: Original 1907 text; no amendment recorded against section 9. In force in April 2018.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument to which he is a party.
why_relevant: The scenario stresses that the purchaser is a friend of the notary. Rule (13) is the only disqualification in section 31 based on the notary's own connection with the deed, and it is confined to his being a party. It is needed to show that friendship with an executant is not a statutory bar to attestation.
temporal_note: Original 1907 rule; not among the rules amended by Act No. 47 of 2011, Act No. 31 of 2022 or Act No. 6 of 2024. In force in this form in April 2018.

relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property, and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object
why_relevant: Supplies the reason a notary must attest at all: a sale or transfer of immovable property is of no force in law unless the deed is in writing and attested by a licensed notary. It frames the question of how Lal Peiris may attest this particular deed of transfer.
temporal_note: The opening words quoted are original 1840 text and stood in this form in April 2018. The detailed conditions in paragraphs (a) and (b) of subsection (1) and the whole of subsection (2), as they appear in the corpus consolidation, reflect the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Acts No. 30 of 2022 and No. 4 of 2024 and are NOT the April 2018 text; nothing in this map relies on them.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim, but it stops before the operative words "shall be in force or avail in law unless" and before paragraph (a), and it is paragraph (a) that imposes the writing-and-notarial-attestation requirement relied on by CL-M112-Q01-001; Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 30 of 2022 s.2 shows that the section as it stood in April 2018 ended with different words beginning "shall be of force", and that April 2018 text is not in the corpus, so this provision supports only the subject-matter of the section and not the operative requirement.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument, other than a will or codicil, affecting land or other immovable property, unless the deed or instrument embodies therin or in a Schedule annexed therto an accurate and clear description of the said land or other property affected thereby, showing its boundaries, extent, situation specifying the district
why_relevant: Requires the deed itself to state the district in which the land is situated. That statement is what makes the Matara District identifiable on the face of the deed, which is the trigger for the out-of-district duty in rule (29) and part of what Lal Peiris must do before he can attest.
temporal_note: Paragraph (a) of rule (16) was substituted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 47 of 2011 s.2, in force well before April 2018. The words quoted stop before the condominium wording added by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(9)(a), so the excerpt is confined to text that stood in April 2018.
verifier_note: Confirmed for the matter date from the corpus itself: Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 47 of 2011 s.2, which is in the corpus, sets out the substituted paragraph (a) in full and contains the quoted words "showing its boundaries, extent, situation specifying the district", so the excerpt is the text that stood in April 2018; Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(9)(a) only appended the condominium wording after "street in which it is situated".

relevant_excerpt: He shall deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which he resides the following documents, so that they shall reach the registrar on or before the fifteenth day of every month, namely, the duplicate of every deed or instrument (except wills and codicils) executed or acknowledged before or attested by him during the preceding month
why_relevant: The baseline monthly return every notary owes to the Registrar of Lands of his own district. Rule (29) operates "besides transmitting the duplicate in manner aforesaid", so this rule has to be read first to see what the out-of-district duty is additional to.
temporal_note: Rule (26) was amended by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 47 of 2011 s.3 (renumbering and the new subparagraph (ii)), which was in force before April 2018, so the text quoted stood in April 2018. The corpus records rule (26) as later repealed by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(12) although the consolidation still carries its text; that repeal is after the matter date and does not affect this provision. The consolidated body prints this rule without its rule number - the number (26) is taken from sections 32(1) and 34(2), which both refer to "rule (26) set out in section 31", and from Act No. 47 of 2011 s.3, which amends "subsection (26)".
verifier_note: Rule number confirmed independently: Act No. 47 of 2011 s.3, in the corpus, amends section 31 "in subsection (26)" by renumbering paragraph (a) as sub-paragraph (i), which is the renumbering visible in the consolidated body, so the unnumbered rule is rule (26). The researcher's caveat that the corpus records rule (26) as repealed in 2022 is a corpus mapping artefact: Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(12) reads "by the repeal of rule (27) thereof", so rule (26) was never repealed. In April 2018 the list form was the Form F, not the Form F 1 (Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(8)); the excerpt stops before the form reference.

relevant_excerpt: shall on or before the fifteenth day of the month next following that in which the same was executed (besides transmitting the duplicate in manner aforesaid) deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which such land shall be situated a copy thereof certified by him as correct
why_relevant: This is the duty asked about in question 2. It applies precisely where a deed other than a will or codicil affects land in a district other than that in which the attesting notary resides, which is this case: the notary resides in Colombo, the land is in Matara. It fixes both the act required (a certified copy plus a list in duplicate, signed by him) and the deadline (the fifteenth day of the following month).
temporal_note: Rule (29) is original 1907 text. The only change recorded against it is Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(9), which substituted "Form F 1" for "in the Form F" in the reference to the accompanying list; in April 2018 the rule referred to the Form F. The excerpt quoted stops before the Form reference, so it is unaffected by that 2024 change, but the verifier should note that the Form named in April 2018 was Form F, not Form F 1.
verifier_note: The April 2018 wording is directly available in the corpus and matches: Notaries (Amendment) Law No. 20 of 1976 s.10(1) substituted rule (29) and sets out the whole rule, including every word of this excerpt, with "in the form F in the Second Schedule". Added as PROV-M112-902 so that the temporal position rests on corpus text rather than on inference.

relevant_excerpt: any other rule set out in section 31, shall be guilty of an offence, and shall, on conviction after summary trial before a Magistrate, be liable to a fine not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, in addition to any civil liability he may incur thereby.
why_relevant: Shows that the rule (29) obligation is a penal duty and not merely directory, which is what makes it a "duty cast on" the notary. It is supporting only: the existence and content of the duty come from rule (29) itself.
temporal_note: Section 34 as quoted is the text substituted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s.17, which is AFTER the matter reference date. In April 2018 section 34 was in its earlier form with lower fines (the fines in the Ordinance having been raised by the Increase of Fines Act No. 12 of 2005). The pre-2022 text of section 34 is not in the corpus, so the penalty figure applicable in April 2018 cannot be stated from the corpus. This provision is used only to show that breach of a section 31 rule is an offence, a feature of the section both before and after 2022; the figure of fifty thousand rupees is not relied on.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim and the classification of a rule (29) breach under paragraph (1)(c) is right on the current text, because paragraphs (1)(a) and (1)(b) list rules (1), (31), (32) and rules (2), (3), (6), (7), (11), (18), (21), (23), (24), (30A) and do not include rule (29); but the section in the corpus is the text substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.17, the Schedules to the Increase of Fines Act No. 12 of 2005 are not in the corpus, and so neither the wording nor the penalty of section 34 as it stood in April 2018 can be established. Correctly kept applicable_to_matter_date=false and confined to supporting use.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless he has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided.
why_relevant: Links the notary's attestation duty to stamp duty: he may not attest until he is assured the duty is provided. It is why the stamp duty questions arise for Lal Peiris at all, and it is part of what he must satisfy before attesting.
temporal_note: Rule (6) is not among the rules substituted by Act No. 47 of 2011, Act No. 31 of 2022 or Act No. 6 of 2024, so the text quoted stood in April 2018. Note that rule (7A), which makes the notary himself the payer of stamp duty, was inserted by Act No. 31 of 2022 and amended by Act No. 6 of 2024 and was NOT in force in April 2018; it is deliberately not relied on anywhere in this map.
verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim, but the temporal note is wrong on one point: rule (6) WAS substituted, by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(4), which re-enacted it in exactly the words quoted. The pre-2022 wording of rule (6) is not in the corpus, so the April 2018 wording cannot be confirmed from the corpus even though the 2022 re-enactment reproduces it. The provision is supporting only in Q01, Q03 and Q04, so no question is blocked by this.

relevant_excerpt: a stamp duty at the prescribed rate. Different rates may be prescribed in respect of different classes or categories of instruments.
why_relevant: The charging provision for an instrument executed in Sri Lanka. It is also the reason question 3 cannot be answered from the corpus: the Act fixes no figure, it charges duty "at the prescribed rate", and no prescribing instrument has been extracted.
temporal_note: Section 2 is original 1982 text with no amendment recorded against it. It continued to operate in April 2018 for instruments relating to the transfer of immovable property because those instruments are expressly carved out of the displacement effected by Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 s.13.

relevant_excerpt: Where any property is conveyed by an instrument, the stamp duty with which such instrument is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property conveyed.
why_relevant: Fixes the base on which the duty is computed. It makes the Rs.1,000,000 market value in the scenario the relevant figure, and it is the step that would turn a prescribed rate into a money answer if the rate were in the corpus.
temporal_note: Original 1982 text; no amendment recorded against section 15. In force in April 2018.

relevant_excerpt: in the case of a conveyance or agreement to convey, by the grantee, or intended grantee;
why_relevant: Identifies the person on whom the duty falls on a deed of transfer: the grantee, here the purchaser Waruna Liyanage. It matters to both stamp duty questions, because it explains whose money the notary must see provided before he attests.
temporal_note: Original 1982 text; no amendment recorded against section 24. In force in April 2018. It is not displaced by Act No. 12 of 2006 s.6, because s.13 of that Act preserves the 1982 Act for instruments relating to the transfer of immovable property.

relevant_excerpt: the provisions of the Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982, relating to the Imposition of Stamp Duty (other than any instrument relating to the transfer of immovable property, the transfer of motor vehicles or documents filed in Court), Exemptions and any other provision in the aforesaid Act, shall, in so far as the same are inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, have no operation and the provisions of this Act shall prevail.
why_relevant: Decides which stamp duty regime governs this deed. Because the instrument relates to the transfer of immovable property, it falls within the express exception, so the Stamp Duty Act No. 43 of 1982 continues to apply to it rather than being displaced by the 2006 Act. Without this section the reasoning could not choose between the two Acts.
temporal_note: Original 2006 text; no amendment recorded against section 13. In force in April 2018.

relevant_excerpt: All stamp duty payable to a Provincial Council in respect of documents and instruments referred to in List I of the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution, shall be paid to the respective Provincial Council within whose limits the instrument was executed or the property situated as the case may be
why_relevant: The only provision in the corpus that addresses where stamp duty is to be paid when the duty is a Provincial Council levy. It is the starting point for question 4, but it is also the source of the difficulty: it offers two limbs, the place of execution and the place where the property is situated, and leaves the choice between them to be resolved "as the case may be" by reference to List I of the Ninth Schedule, which is not in the corpus.
temporal_note: Original 2006 text; no amendment recorded against section 9. In force in April 2018.

relevant_excerpt: The stamp duty with which any instrument is chargeable shall be paid before or at the time of execution of the instrument and such payment shall be indicated on such instrument by means of adhesive stamps or impressed stamps except as otherwise permitted in this Act.
why_relevant: Gives the time and the manner of payment under the 1982 Act: before or at execution, evidenced by adhesive or impressed stamps on the instrument. It is the part of the "where and how" of payment that the corpus does answer, and it is what the notary must see satisfied before he attests.
temporal_note: Original 1982 text; no amendment recorded against section 6. In force in April 2018. Note that the 1982 Act contains no provision equivalent to the prescribed-bank machinery found in provincial finance statutes, so the identity of the office or bank that receives the money for a Southern Province land transfer cannot be established from this section alone.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless the person executing the same and the witnesses shall have signed the same in his presence and in the presence of one another, and unless he shall have signed the same in the presence of the executant and of the attesting witnesses.
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. The Q01 answer concludes that the parties and the two witnesses must execute the deed before Lal Peiris at his Colombo office, but no provision in the map stated that requirement: rule (22) fixes only the area and the language, and rule (16)(a) only the description of the land. Rule (12) is the provision that requires execution in the notary's presence and in the presence of one another, and it is what ties the place of signing to the place of attestation on which rule (22) operates.
temporal_note: Rule (12) is original 1907 text. It is not among the rules amended by Notaries (Amendment) Law No. 20 of 1976 s.10 (rules (29) and (36)(b)), Act No. 47 of 2011 ss.2-3 (rule (16)(a) and rule (26)), Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16 or Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3, each of which enumerates the rules it touches. In force in this form in April 2018.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked verbatim against 1-1907/s31.

relevant_excerpt: together with a list in duplicate in the form F in the Second Schedule, signed by him, of all such deeds or instruments as relate to lands in such last-mentioned district.
why_relevant: Added by the verifier. This is the amending section that substituted rule (29) of section 31 in 1976 and sets the whole rule out in full. It is the corpus source for the wording of rule (29) as it stood in April 2018, and in particular it shows that the list accompanying the certified copy was then in the Form F, the Form F 1 having been substituted only by Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(9). It removes the need to infer the April 2018 text of rule (29) from the post-2024 consolidation.
temporal_note: Enacted 1976 and in force from 1976. The substituted rule (29) it sets out stood unchanged until Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(9), so it states the law in April 2018.
verifier_note: Added by the verifier; excerpt checked verbatim against 20-1976/s10.

relevant_excerpt: there shall be charged a duty (hereinafter to be called "stamp duty") at such rate as the Minister may determine by Order published in the Gazette on every "specified instrument"- (a) executed, drawn or presented in Sri Lanka
why_relevant: This is the charging provision for stamp duty on the lease to be executed in Sri Lanka. It is also the reason the sum cannot be computed from the corpus: the rate is not in the Act but in a Ministerial Order published in the Gazette, which the corpus does not hold.
temporal_note: In force from 2006; the corpus records no amendment to section 3, so the text applies as at April 2018.

relevant_excerpt: (i) a lease or hire of any property;
why_relevant: Brings the lease agreement within the definition of specified instrument for the purposes of the section 3 charge. Without this paragraph nothing in the Act would attach duty to a lease.
temporal_note: In force from 2006; the corpus records no amendment to section 4, so the text applies as at April 2018.

relevant_excerpt: (c) in the case of a lease, by the lessee;
why_relevant: Fixes the lessee, not Mr Perera as lessor, as the person liable for stamp duty on the lease, subject to the opening words of the section which allow the parties to agree otherwise. Those opening words are what make the incidence of stamp duty a proper subject for a mutual covenant in the deed.
temporal_note: In force from 2006; amended by Act No. 10 of 2008, which is before the matter date of April 2018. The consolidated text therefore applies.

relevant_excerpt: Stamp duty payable on any specified instrument relating to a mortgage or lease of any immovable property may be paid, prior to, or at the time of, the execution of the specified instrument, to a prescribed bank.
why_relevant: Governs when and how the duty on this lease is to be paid, and so bears on the notary's practical steps once the amount is known.
temporal_note: In force from 2006; substituted by Act No. 10 of 2008, which is before the matter date of April 2018.

relevant_excerpt: and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object, or for establishing any security, interest, or incumbrance affecting land or other immovable property (other than a lease at will, or for any period not exceeding one month)
why_relevant: A lease of the Dehiwala house for two years is outside the carve-out for a lease at will or for a period not exceeding one month, so the instrument must be notarially executed to be of force in law. This is why the client needs a notary and why a notarially attested deed, not a mere signed agreement, is the operative document.
temporal_note: In force from 1840. The corpus text is consolidated to 2024 and carries amendments by Act No. 30 of 2022 and Act No. 4 of 2024, both after the matter date. The quoted words are the carve-out for short leases, which long predates 2018, but the verifier should confirm the April 2018 wording against a point-in-time text before treating any part of section 2 as indispensable.

relevant_excerpt: shall be in force or avail in law unless - (a) the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary
why_relevant: States the form the lease deed must take: writing, signature by both lessor and lessee and the witnesses in the presence of a licensed notary and of one another, and notarial attestation.
temporal_note: The paragraph (a) and (b) structure quoted here was introduced by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act, No. 30 of 2022, which is after the matter date. The substance of the writing, witnesses and notarial attestation requirement was in section 2 well before April 2018, but this precise wording was not. Held as background only for that reason.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless he has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided.
why_relevant: Ties the stamp duty question to the drafting question: the notary retained by Mr Perera may not attest the lease until he is satisfied that the duty has been provided for, which is why the amount has to be worked out before execution.
temporal_note: Section 31 has been in force since 1907. The corpus text is consolidated to 2024 and carries amendments by Acts Nos. 47 of 2011, 31 of 2022 and 6 of 2024. Rule (6) is not among the rules the corpus records as substituted in 2022 or 2024, but the verifier should confirm the April 2018 wording. Held as supporting, not indispensable.

relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument, other than a will or codicil, affecting land or other immovable property, unless the deed or instrument embodies therin or in a Schedule annexed therto an accurate and clear description of the said land or other property affected thereby, showing its boundaries, extent, situation
why_relevant: Requires the lease deed for No. 96, Quarry Road, Dehiwala to carry, in the body or in an annexed schedule, an accurate description of the premises with boundaries, extent and situation. This is the one drafting requirement for this lease that the corpus does state.
temporal_note: The consolidated wording of rule (16) refers to Divisional Secretary's and Grama Niladari Divisions and to condominium parcels, features the corpus attributes to the 2022 and 2024 amendment Acts. The core duty to describe the land accurately in the deed or an annexed schedule predates 2018. Held as background pending a point-in-time check.

relevant_excerpt: (xi) any instrument if the only interest in land created or dealt with thereby is a tenancy at will or for a period not exceeding one month or determinable by the landlord by not more than one month's notice.
why_relevant: A two-year lease falls outside this exclusion, so the lease is an instrument deemed to affect land for the purposes of the Ordinance and is registrable. That in turn is why the deed needs the description required by the Notaries Ordinance and why the parties commonly covenant about who bears the cost of registration.
temporal_note: In force from 1927; the corpus records no later change to section 8, so the text applies as at April 2018.

relevant_excerpt: the provisions of the Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982, relating to the Imposition of Stamp Duty (other than any instrument relating to the transfer of immovable property, the transfer of motor vehicles or documents filed in Court)
why_relevant: Settles which enactment governs. A lease is not a transfer of immovable property, a motor vehicle transfer or a court document, so the carve-out in section 13 does not apply and the 1982 Act gives way to Act No. 12 of 2006 to the extent of any inconsistency.
temporal_note: In force from 2006; the corpus records no amendment to section 13, so the text applies as at April 2018.
